about: Machine-readable changelog of @origingame/engine (docs/release.md §3). kind: patch (0.x.y, compatible) or minor (0.x.0, has breaks). simulation: changed when a game's world can step differently (the golden replays' hashes moved, scripts/replay-gate.ts), else unchanged; versions before 0.6.1 were not measured and say changed. breaking: what a game may have to edit, each with the fix; find lists the identifiers og upgrade searches the game's sources for, codemod a mechanical rewrite it applies. Merges record changes as fragments in changelog/unreleased/, folded in by scripts/release.sh fold and bump; release notes are generated from this file.

breaking.change: The reflected records add radius, default 0.
breaking.fix: Re-cook scenes against the updated schema; leave radius zero to preserve punctual lights.

breaking.change: The field is now Option<ParticleBlend>; None retains the per-kind default.
breaking.fix: Wrap explicit Rust blend values in Some and read the resolved value with emitter.blend(). Effect files and the TypeScript API need no changes.

breaking.change: Closed transmissive volumes refract at both interfaces and use their measured entry-to-exit distance for absorption. Authored thickness and its map now approximate both only where no geometric exit is captured; zero thickness remains a thin wall.
breaking.fix: Review closed glass volumes for the corrected bending and tint. Use attenuationDistance to set absorption in world units; keep thickness and thicknessMap as the fallback for open, off-screen or occluded exits.

breaking.change: The face is redrawn: a frame cut at two corners and rimmed in its type's colour, the art window over its rarity's glow, the name on a plate, a tinted type line, the rules text in a recess (up to four lines, fewer on a short face, each ending whole with an ellipsis) and a hexagon cost gem. CardFace.headline, .label, .caption, .figure, .well and .picture are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardFace.headline dresses CardFace.name; .label and .caption dress CardFace.type; .figure dresses CardFace.cost; .well and .picture dress CardFace.art.

breaking.change: An unplayable card dims its art and frame and says why on a tag at its head instead of a lock badge. CardHand.badge is gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardHand.badge dresses CardHand.reason; a game passes its reason on each row.

breaking.change: A pile is a stack of card backs (one when empty) with its icon on top and the count on a cut tag at its corner. CardPiles.cell, .figure and .badge are gone; CardPiles.stack is new.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardPiles.cell dresses CardPiles.pile; .figure and .badge dress CardPiles.count.

breaking.change: Each card shows its owned count on its corner, In deck ×N or Not in deck under it and, when the game will not add it, the reason under that; the selected card wears brackets; an unowned card is hatched and dimmed while its name keeps its ink. The filters are an underline strip that scrolls with a fade. CardCollection.badge is gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardCollection.badge dresses CardCollection.owned, .deck or .reason.

breaking.change: A row carries its card type as a rail on the leading edge, the cost in a hexagon, ×copies and square steps; the size is a leaning bar. CardDeckList.figure, .label, .cell, .caption, .track, .fill and .caption are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardDeckList.figure dresses CardDeckList.copies or .cost; .track and .fill dress CardDeckList.size.

breaking.change: Offers sit in one row with brackets on the one looked at; a relic is a gold plate with its mark in a diamond. On a phone one offer shows at nearly full width with its text whole and the next peeking at a faded edge, scrolling sideways. CardReward.cell, .well, .headline and .caption are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed CardReward.cell dresses CardReward.choice or .relic; .well dresses CardReward.mark; .headline dresses CardReward.name; .caption dresses CardReward.kind or .text.

breaking.member: DataGrid, Chart, Carousel, NodeGraph, SplitView, table, data-list, tree, pagination, calendar, card, creator-tools
breaking.change: The data and tool panels are redrawn in the HUD's language: each stands on a cut smoked-glass plate with a lit top edge, headings are small tracked capitals over a faint rule, figures are condensed and tabular, and a chosen row is washed in the accent from its leading edge, which carries a lit bar. DataGrid's numeric columns read as figures, and in a shell narrower than 480 px each row becomes a two-line card (the first column and the last on one line, the others as a caption under them) instead of cutting every column to an ellipsis; its Retry is the primary button. Chart's bars lean and are lit along their top, its line series is gold, and a long category name wraps under its bar. Carousel shows one page at a time with the next beyond its edge, its place as leaning pips between 44 px cut arrow keys. NodeGraph's well is the plate under a faint dot grid with accent links and a lit current node. SplitView's grip is lit in the accent. The table's first column is a name and the others are end-aligned figures. data-list rows start-align their words. tree rows carry indent guides, and the selected row is washed in the accent instead of being a primary button. pagination and calendar use cut keys and 44 px targets; today is lit in the accent, and a marked day carries a gold diamond instead of a bar at its foot. card is a pressable plate whose body is no longer clamped to three lines. creator-tools' tools are a segmented switch lit in the accent, and on a portrait phone its panel tabs are one strip that scrolls sideways with 44 px targets instead of wrapping. Parts, props and strings are unchanged.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed these panels through their row, cell, frame or band roles sets the --data-* and --hud-plate-* tokens instead. A style that dressed a tree's selected row through `#Item[variant="primary"]` dresses `.row[aria-selected="true"]`. A game that relied on card clamping its body keeps its body short.

breaking.change: Cancel is no longer the quiet variant (it is a default button with class plate), and the dialog sets its own panel fill, edge and backdrop from the --dialog-* roles.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the quiet Cancel dresses #Cancel or ::part(confirm.actions) button; one that dressed the panel sets --dialog-fill, --dialog-edge and --dialog-scrim.

breaking.change: The menu's frame is no longer bare: it draws its own plate, and its rows are type, not row-role strips.
breaking.fix: A game that stood Menu in a panel of its own removes that panel's fill, or sets --dialog-fill to none on the menu.

breaking.change: screen.tutorial.Step now reads "Tutorial · {step} / {steps}" and stands at the card's head, not beside the actions.
breaking.fix: A game that wants the bare count overrides screen.tutorial.Step in its string table.

breaking.change: A rarity no longer draws the frame's rim through --frame-rim and --frame-rim-width. The card sets --frame-fill and --frame-shadow (a lit top edge and a tinted head) and the socket's --well-fill and --well-shadow from --rarity; --title-ink is still the rarity's colour.
breaking.fix: A style that recoloured a rarity sets --rarity on ::part(TooltipCard.frame), or the palette's rarity colours; one that drew its own rim on the card sets --frame-shadow there.

breaking.change: The choices' panel is bare (no HUD plate behind them). A chapter or ending card is no longer a raised panel, and one not reached draws part lock (a well and a lock icon) in place of its thumb art.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the choices' panel dresses ::part(film-choices.shade); one that dressed a locked card's thumb dresses ::part(film-chapters.lock) or ::part(film-gallery.lock).

breaking.change: The entries are no longer framed buttons: Continue is no longer the primary variant, the .large class is gone, and the save line is inside the Continue entry. The menu's first focus is MenuMenu/Entries/Continue (was Menu/Continue). The key art draws only when keyArt is set; without it the screen is the style's dark ground.
breaking.fix: Pass keyArt (og.load.texture) for the key art and logo or name for the mark. A style that dressed the buttons dresses ::part(main-menu.entry); a style that sized .large sets --front-entry-size.

breaking.change: A mode's tag is a <span part="mode-select.tag"> on the card's art, not a <badge>; a locked mode's reason is a lock line (part mode-select.lock). Play is a lit cut plate rather than the primary button's face. The card's cut corners and rim moved from mode-select.cell to the new mode-select.plate inside it; the cell carries the lift and the chosen card's glow.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the badge dresses ::part(mode-select.tag); one that dressed Play's base sets the --front-play-* tokens. A style that cut or ringed ::part(mode-select.cell) does so on ::part(mode-select.plate).

breaking.change: The key art draws only when keyArt is set; without it the screen is the style's dark ground. The logo comes from the logo prop.
breaking.fix: Pass keyArt and logo (og.load.texture handles) on Title and Credits, or name on Title for a wordmark.

breaking.change: The places gained are named by one plural string each: racing.lap.up and racing.lap.down are now ICU plurals ({n, plural, one {Up # place} other {Up # places}}), and the racing.lap.upOne and racing.lap.downOne strings are removed.
breaking.fix: A game that overrode racing.lap.upOne or racing.lap.downOne puts its one-place wording into the one branch of its racing.lap.up or racing.lap.down plural instead.

breaking.change: RacingTelemetry is one tachometer standing bare over the scene: a white rev arc with its red zone (lit once the revs reach it) round a dark glass face holding the shift lights, the speed, the units and the gear on a lit tag beside the gearbox's mode. New props mode, scale (keyed rows of { id, value, label }: the dial's figures and ticks) and lights (the share of the shift lights lit; negative hides them). The bar form and the boost ring are gone: props dial, boost, boostMax and boosting are removed. The Shift cue is a word beside the gear. Its parts are RacingTelemetry.frame, .dial, .track, .fill, .redline, .tick, .mark, .face, .lights, .speed, .units, .gear, .mode and .badge; .plate, .figure, .label and .caption are gone, and the frame's data-dial and data-boosting are gone.
breaking.fix: Drop dial, boost, boostMax and boosting from the RacingTelemetry tag and show boost with RacingBoost (value, max, firing). Pass scale for the dial's figures and lights for the shift lights. A style that dressed .plate or .figure dresses .gear or .speed; .label dresses .units; .caption is gone. Set the --hud-rev-*, --hud-redline* and --hud-dial-* tokens for the dial's look.

breaking.change: RacingLapHud stands bare over the scene as the race HUD mockup draws it: the place large and slanted over the field's size, the lap on a lit plate and the places gained beside it (new prop gained), then the current, last and best lap times and the split delta on a green or red tag beside the split's name (new prop sector). The split's sense is read with the delta, no longer a word drawn beside it, and the final lap reads on the lap plate. Its parts are RacingLapHud.frame, .place, .of, .lap, .gained, .times, .row, .label, .time, .delta and .badge; .readout, .title, .figure and .caption are gone. The Time label reads Current and the position's label Position.
breaking.fix: Pass gained (places gained since the start; 0 hides it) and sector (the split's name). A style that dressed .readout or .figure dresses .place, .lap or .time; .title and .caption dress .label.

breaking.change: RacingStandings is the position tower: one leaning glass row per car without a heading band, the place in a box, the car's colour on a stripe (new row field color), the name and the gap; the leader's empty gap reads Leader; the player's row is lit in the HUD's accent and no longer carries a You word; a retired car's tag reads DNF and its row dims. On a phone the tower keeps the leader and the rows either side of the player. title is now only read, not drawn. Its parts are RacingStandings.frame, .row, .place, .car, .name, .gap and .badge; .band, .title, .label, .figure and .caption are gone.
breaking.fix: Add color (a CSS colour, or empty) to each row. A style that dressed .band or .title drops it; .label and .figure dress .place or .gap; .caption (You, the empty line) dresses .row[data-player=true] or .badge. Name the player's row as the game wants it read (You).

breaking.change: RacingBanner's plate is the HUD's smoked glass with a lit top edge in the accent and the call in widely set capitals. New kind call shows the game's own words (new prop text: Final lap next, Sector best). The plate part is RacingBanner.plate alone (it no longer also wears RacingBanner.frame).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the plate as RacingBanner.frame dresses RacingBanner.plate. Pass kind call with text for a call the kit does not word.

breaking.change: RhythmScoreHud is the score alone, set against the screen's end: score, accuracy, a new grade and the player's best with the gap to it. The life, danger, failed and progress props are gone, and its parts are RhythmScoreHud.frame, .legend, .score, .accuracy, .grade, .best and .delta.
breaking.fix: Show life with <RhythmGauge kind="life" value danger failed> and the song's progress with <RhythmSongProgress value elapsed length>; pass grade and best for the new readouts. A style that dressed the old parts dresses the new ones.

breaking.change: The combo stands above the judgement as the hero figure, and the word is drawn in its judgement's lit gradient. Its parts are RhythmJudgement.frame, .combo, .count, .legend, .mark, .call, .word, .timing and .offset (the old .plate, .title, .badge, .figure and .caption are gone). New props offset (+4 ms) and mark (fullCombo, allPerfect).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RhythmJudgement.plate dresses RhythmJudgement.call, .title dresses .word, .badge dresses .timing, .figure dresses .count and .caption dresses .legend.

breaking.change: BossBar stands bare over the scene as the action HUD mockup draws it: a Boss tag, the name and a new epithet; a long leaning bar in a burning orange with a warm ghost (new prop ghost) and a diamond at each phase boundary; under it a stagger gauge cut into cells (new props stagger, negative hides it, and staggerCells), the elements the boss is weak to (new prop weaknesses, keyed rows of { id, name, icon, glyph }) and health's share in figures. The health figure (value / max) is now the meter's spoken value only, and the list of phase chips is gone (phases are diamonds on the bar). Its parts are BossBar.frame, .kind, .boss, .epithet, .health, .ghost, .threshold, .stagger, .weakness, .share and .state; .figure, .fill, .notch, .phases, .phase, .label, .headline, .card, .caption and .dot are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed BossBar.headline dresses BossBar.boss; .fill dresses .health (its fill is the --hud-boss-fill token) or .ghost; .notch and .phase dress .threshold; .caption on a state dresses .state. Set --hud-boss-fill for the bar's colour. A game that showed the phase names words them itself.

breaking.change: The tracker stands bare over the scene: a heading in gold (new prop label; empty is Main quest), the quest's name with the distance on a tag, then each step with a diamond, the done ones struck through, the first not done lit as the one in play and the rest dim; a step's new field tag shows its progress on a tag (1 / 3). A phone shows the step in play alone. Its parts are RpgQuestTracker.frame, .legend, .quest, .distance, .step, .marker, .text and .progress; .title, .row, .caption and .figure are gone, and a step no longer draws a check or flag icon.
breaking.fix: Give each step a tag field (empty for none). A style that dressed RpgQuestTracker.title dresses .quest, .row dresses .step (still on data-done), and .caption or .figure dresses .distance.

breaking.change: AmmoCounter stands bare over the scene as the mockup draws it: the reserve weapon's line, the magazine as the HUD's largest figure, a leaning tick per round and the fire mode as pips beside the weapon's name. New props secondary, secondaryAmmo and secondaryKey. Its parts are Ammo.frame, .alternate, .swap, .count, .reserve, .rounds, .magazine, .modes, .weapon, .mode, .reload and .prompt (the old .track, .label, .figure, .well, .fill and .caption are gone).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed Ammo.track dresses Ammo.rounds, .label dresses .weapon or .mode, .figure dresses .count and .reserve; Ammo.magazine is now the loaded rounds' ticks.

breaking.change: A killfeed row draws the weapon as a glyph by its class (new row field kind: rifle, smg, pistol, shotgun, sniper, launcher or melee; empty keeps the name in words), names in their side's colour on a glass that fades toward the middle, a headshot tag (HS) and a lit edge for the player's rows. Killfeed.label is gone and Killfeed.headshot is a tag, not an og-icon; new parts Killfeed.glyph and Killfeed.edge. An upright phone shows the newest row (it showed three); a phone on its side still shows three.
breaking.fix: Give each row a kind to show its glyph. A style that dressed Killfeed.label dresses Killfeed.weapon; one that inked og-icon[part="Killfeed.headshot"]::part(image) sets the tag's color.

breaking.change: The arcs are drawn in the HUD's danger red with a glow (the shield's blue for a shield hit); the part DamageDirection.fill is gone and an arc no longer takes data-tone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed DamageDirection.fill dresses DamageDirection.arc (its ink is stroke).

breaking.change: The reticle is white with a dark keyline and its hit marks red with a glow for a headshot or a kill and blue for a broken shield. The circle shape's ring is a masked fill: its ink is its background, not its border-color.
breaking.fix: A style that set border-color on Crosshair.ring sets background.

breaking.change: The compass is a strip with ticks every 15 degrees, large cardinal and dim intercardinal letters on a dark band fading at its ends, the heading on a tag in the HUD's accent over it (three digits, 042°) and a caret under the ticks; a poi with no icon is a diamond. The strip shows 120 degrees across its width (it showed 180).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed Compass.badge, .notch or .window keeps the same parts; set --hud-accent for the heading's tag and caret.

breaking.change: StrategySelection is the RTS selection panel drawn bare over the scene: the portrait in a lit tile with its health as a bar and in figures, the name large with how many are selected, its class line, a status tag and stats on tags (new props name, count, kind, line, status, portrait, icon, health, healthMax, stats keyed { id, label, value }), and every unit selected as a card with a health bar green, gold or red (data-tone), the focused card lit. The command card moved to StrategyCommands: the commands prop and the command intent are gone. Props title and summary are gone; a unit row's line and status fields are no longer read. Cards show only for two or more units. Its parts are StrategySelection.frame, .portrait, .health, .fill, .vital, .name, .count, .line, .status, .stat, .roster, .cell, .art, .meter and .badge; .band, .title, .detail, .grid, .command, .key, .reason, .picture, .well, .plate, .label, .headline, .caption, .figure, .track and .sweep are gone.
breaking.fix: Pass the focused unit's or subgroup's name, count, line, status, portrait or icon, health, healthMax and stats to StrategySelection, and its commands to StrategyCommands (rows { id, name, icon, glyph, key, action, enabled, affordable, cost, costIcon, cooldown, time, active, detail, cooldownText, readyText, reason }; label becomes name, hotkey becomes key, cooldownText the tile's figure becomes time). Drop title and summary. A style that dressed .detail or .headline dresses .name; .caption dresses .line or .status; .well, .track and .fill on a card dress .meter.

breaking.change: StrategyQueue is one bare row, as the selection panel's barracks queue: what produces in small capitals, the order in production as a larger tile with a dark sweep for what is still to run and its time, the orders waiting as smaller tiles, the free places up to the limit as empty tiles, the count over the limit on a tag (Queue full 5 / 5 when full), and Paused, or Blocked with the reason, as words after it. Tapping a tile reports cancel; there is no separate cancel button and no progress bar. New item field picture (a texture; 0 draws icon). The waiting word and the per-order name line are gone (the name is the tile's accessible name). The capacity reads 3 / 5. Its parts are StrategyQueue.frame, .title, .slot, .art, .sweep, .time, .badge, .open, .count, .state and .reason; .band, .row, .cell, .name, .headline and .caption are gone.
breaking.fix: Pass picture on each item (0 keeps the icon). A style that dressed .row or .cell dresses .slot; .band and .headline dress .title; .caption dresses .reason or .state. A page that set the queue on its own plate keeps the plate: the frame is bare.

breaking.change: StrategyWave is the wave plate at the top right: smoked glass with its edge lit in danger while a wave comes or fights, its picture (new prop icon), Wave n (of N) and its name (new prop name) in red capitals, the countdown as figures with a bar of the wait still to run, or Under attack or All waves cleared, the Final wave tag; the enemies under it as feed rows; Call early on a lit plate with its reward in gold. It no longer uses HudTimer: the countdown is a role=timer group, near its end it turns red (data-near). The Get ready word is gone from the countdown. Its parts are StrategyWave.frame, .plate, .icon, .label, .time, .bar, .fill, .state, .badge, .row, .mark, .name, .count, .call and .reward; .readout, .title, .figure and .caption are gone.
breaking.fix: Pass name and icon (both optional). A style that dressed .readout or .figure dresses .label, .time or .count; .title and .caption dress .label or .reward; HudTimer's parts inside the wave dress .time and .bar.

breaking.change: StrategyTower is dressed as the strategy HUD's plates: smoked glass with a lit top edge and two corners cut, the portrait in a lit tile, the name large, its stats on a dark well, each path a feed row edged by its state (accent, red, gold), its tier on a leaning bar, the buy plates and Sell on glass (an affordable buy lit). Names stay on one line and scroll when they overflow (a path's name no longer wraps). Its props and parts are unchanged.
breaking.fix: None needed; a style that dressed the tower's surfaces through the frame, band, card and badge tokens dresses its parts directly.

breaking.change: The bag is redrawn: its frame is cut at two corners with a lit top edge, the title sits under a kicker beside the purse chip, the tabs are an underline strip between the category actions' key caps that scrolls and fades before the next cap, and the carried weight is a leaning bar across the footer (the bag icon and the purse beside it are gone). An item cell no longer paints itself: it holds a tile cut at two corners that wears the rarity's cell fill and rim with a lit bar along its foot, its stack, Equipped (E), Locked and New in its corners and, when selected, corner brackets. Broken is now said on the tile (Broken). Equipped is RpgBackpack.state, not .badge; the locked mark has no part.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgBackpack.cell's background or rim sets --cell-<rarity>-fill and --cell-<rarity>-shadow, or the --inv-slot-* tokens. A style that dressed the equipped badge through RpgBackpack.badge dresses RpgBackpack.state. Pass kicker and capacity, and a count per tab, to show them.

breaking.change: Each row is a glass row with the item's rarity on its leading edge and its icon in a socket; the count sits on the name's line and the reason a row is refused replaces its description, in red. The band reads Loot · n items over the title, and Close carries the back action's key cap. RpgLoot.name no longer also wears the headline role: the RpgLoot.headline part is gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgLoot.headline dresses RpgLoot.name. Pass rarity on each item to colour it.

breaking.change: The station is two columns: the recipes as rows (rarity edge, socket, name, why it cannot be made), and the selected recipe with its art large over a glow of its rarity, its name, what it does and how many the player holds, the ingredients as have / need chips (a short one tinted and named Missing ingredients), then the batch stepper with the cost and Craft. The batch and Craft sit at the foot of the selected recipe, under what scrolls, so Craft is always in view; on a narrow panel the recipes sit over it. The selected recipe is no longer a well, and the quantity reads as a figure between − and +. The RpgCrafting.headline part is gone (the ingredients' heading is a kicker).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgCrafting.headline dresses RpgCrafting.ingredientsTitle; one that dressed the detail's well dresses RpgCrafting.detail. Pass rarity and held on each recipe to show them.

breaking.change: The merchant's band holds the title under a kicker, a Buy / Sell switch (RpgTrade.mode, role switch, checked on the sell side) and the purse. Each good's row shows its price, a discount struck before it; the selected good's total, the balance after and Buy or Sell sit in a footer under the list instead of a well. The mode button no longer reads Browse goods to buy / Browse items to sell: those words are its accessible name.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgTrade.detail's well dresses RpgTrade.detail; one that dressed the price in the detail dresses RpgTrade.total. Pass was, after and rarity on each good to show them.

breaking.change: The card is redrawn: its frame is cut at two corners with a lit top edge; the art sits over a glow of its rarity; kind is a kicker in the rarity's colour over the name; the headline figure is large with its change as a chip (an arrow in the trend's colour) and what is equipped beside it, headed Equipped (it read Your current); the other figures are rows of this, change and equipped under This / Equipped headings, and drop under the label when the line is short; the lore hangs from a rule of the rarity; the art and the name scroll with the figures while the buttons sit side by side at the foot, the main one carrying the details action's key cap. On a phone or a short screen the art sits in a socket beside the name and the rows drop the equipped column. RpgItemCard.title and RpgItemCard.well are gone: the name is RpgItemCard.name only and the lore is RpgItemCard.lore.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgItemCard.title dresses RpgItemCard.name; one that dressed the lore through RpgItemCard.well dresses RpgItemCard.lore. Pass line and reason to show them.

breaking.change: The loading screen is redrawn in the HUD's language over its key art: an eyebrow (Now entering) over the place in large condensed bold, the tip on a cut smoked-glass plate with a Tip tag and a Next tip button (Tab on a key cap; a 44 px target on a touch screen), and the progress as the HUD's leaning bar with a white lead edge, a spinner while it is not ready and the figure, which turns to the accent once ready. Continue is a lit bevelled button (Enter on a key cap; Tap to continue on a touch screen). The tip is no longer clamped to four lines, and a shade rises behind the words and grows with them, so a long place name stays readable over bright art. Without key art the style's placeholder is a dark wash lit by the accent instead of a picture glyph. The `<progress>` control is replaced by the bar: the screen now uses the Spinner component and no longer uses control:progress. New prop status (what the wait is for, beside the figure). New parts loading.eyebrow, .label, .next, .bar, .fill, .figure and .status; loading.scrim, .frame and .title stay, and .frame is the tip plate (no longer a panel). New string keys screen.loading.busy, .continueKey, .entering, .next, .nextKey and .tapContinue.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the loading screen's `progress` element dresses loading.bar and loading.fill (or sets the --loading-fill, --bar-well and --bar-rim tokens). A style that gave loading.frame a panel's look sets the --hud-plate-* tokens instead. A game that translates the screen adds the six new string keys to its tables.

breaking.change: RpgWorldMap draws no panel: the map art is the screen. Each kind of marker is its own pin shape with its icon, names sit white on cut plates, the chosen marker is ringed, danger is marked red on its triangle while its name stays white, and the legend draws the markers' own marks (stacked in a corner on a narrow screen). The parts RpgWorldMap.cell and RpgWorldMap.dot are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgWorldMap.cell or .dot dresses RpgWorldMap.marker; the name is RpgWorldMap.plate. Set the --map-marker-*, --map-name-* and --map-legend-* tokens for the map's look.

breaking.change: RpgPlaceCard is a bare card: the picture fading into it, the name scrolling when long (text-overflow: -og-scroll), a gold rule, the about line, and Mark and Travel buttons. The part RpgPlaceCard.headline is gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed RpgPlaceCard.headline dresses RpgPlaceCard.name. Set the --map-card-*, --map-picture-*, --map-go-* and --map-ghost-* tokens for the card's look.

breaking.change: MinimapView is a bezel round smoked glass with a north badge on its rim and a zone plate; markers keep a shape per kind (objective diamond, ally and enemy discs, loot square) sized from the type scale, so they stay told apart at any text size. The parts MinimapView.plate, .cell, .frame, .dot, .gridline and .tag are gone.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed MinimapView.frame dresses .bezel, .plate dresses .glass, .gridline dresses .grid, .dot or .cell dresses .marker and .tag dresses .badge. Set the --map-bezel-*, --map-glass-* and --map-pip-* tokens for its look.

breaking.change: CardRunMap draws no board over the act's art: a room is a disc, or a diamond for an elite or the boss, its kind in its icon; the path taken is solid gold over the faint paths ahead; the legend draws each kind's mark as its rooms do, from a legend row's new shape. added.summary: Limit near-camera outline growth without losing the distance falloff. Defaults to the existing 4× growth; anime-cel-3d uses a 1× cap so its 2.5 px character lines stay thin up close.

Attach an entity to an animated node, including non-joint glTF socket helpers. Parent selects the skeleton, node indexes Animation.nodes (not skin.joints), and Transform remains the bone-local offset. Attachments and descendants follow the final pose after IK, interpolate with the skin, survive snapshot/restore, and place lights, audio and kinematic colliders at the socket on both hosts. Dynamic rigid bodies under a socket are refused.
`uncooked` or `bundle`; each kind numbers its requests from 0. A journal without kinds is read as uncooked loads, as before.

Which version of a content catalog is current: `{ catalog, version, manifest, published }`, a platform answer journaled with its tick. The answer pins that version's manifest integrity, so og.load.data reads it against it. Natively `og run --content <dir>` (and playtests' PlaytestDesc.content) answer it from `<dir>/<catalog>/head.json`; on a page without a Player, from the content base's head.json; `unavailable` without a content base (guide saves §11).

A hint that a catalog may have a new version (`{ catalog, version, manifest }`); it pins that version's manifest as an answer does. Best effort: a host may send it late, twice or never, so a game polls og.platform.catalogHead.

`@origingame/engine/provider`: a provider may name the game's content base (`content: { base() }`), over the build's `--content`. `catalog.head` joins CORE_METHODS and `catalog` the notice kinds; `staticCatalog(base, { inner, read })` answers catalog.head from the static layout; checkPlatformProvider checks a head's shape. PROVIDER_VERSION stays 1.

A grounded environment's ground (groundHeight above 0) takes the shadows of what stands on it, as a real floor would, so props sit on the photographed ground instead of floating over it: the map's light they hide from it, within 32 m of groundCenter, and the sun's shadow from a DirectionalLight with castShadow (three.js ShadowMaterial, Unity's HDRI backplate, Unreal's HDRI Backdrop). groundShadows sets how dark, 1 by default; 0 draws the ground as photographed, as before. A grounded scene's ground darkens round its props unless it sets 0.

A leaf's material states how its species follows the year: `season` (0 evergreen, 1 deciduous), `autumnColor` and `autumnColor2` (linear) and `seasonShift` (days late, negative early), in a plant's `leaves` block, a `material` block or glTF extras.ogFoliage. The oak, birch, willow, shrub, fern and reed kinds have `season 1` and their own autumn colours. The cook stores them in og.ModelMaterial (version 5), so a project's models cook again; nothing drawn changes yet.

Opt-in aerial perspective thins hatch stroke width and ink strength with view depth in screen, surface and object space, leaving the sky bare without changing the wash or contour weighting. Zero retains the existing look.

added: PointLight.radius and SpotLight.radius set a spherical source size in metres. Near-source illumination uses distance² + radius², and specular highlights use Karis's energy-normalized representative point. The default zero preserves punctual lights; shadow softness is unchanged.

added.summary: Read one file of a content catalog by catalog, version and path (CatalogEntry, DataDesc), as JSON or bytes, up to LoadBudget.bytes (32 MiB by default). Files come from the host's content base, never a URL in game code: `og run --content <dir>`, `og replay --content <dir>` and PlaytestDesc.content natively, `og build --content <url>` or project.ogt `publish { content }` on the web. Each file is checked against its version manifest's sha384 integrity. A failed load says why first: not_found, unavailable, failed, timeout, integrity, too_large or invalid (guide loading §14).
The value of a ready og.load.data file read as JSON.
The bytes of a ready og.load.data file read as bytes.

og.load.completions journals data loads (`kind` `data`) with the tick they were put in place and the integrity of the bytes read; og.load.replayCompletions puts each in place at that tick and fails it when the bytes differ. Absent for other kinds, so existing journals stay valid.

Open a cooked bundle a content catalog's version lists by name (its manifest's `packs`, `{ name: { integrity } }`), from `<base>/<catalog>/packs/<name>/cooked/` under the host's content base. Its `.cook.ogt` is read against the integrity the version lists; once ready it is a runtime bundle as og.load.bundle opens (bundleInfo, groups and cells, og.load.release). Journaled as a `bundle` completion with its manifest integrity, which a replay requires again. A failed open says why first, as og.load.data's (guide loading §14).
Also set for an og.load.pack `bundle` completion: the integrity of the pack's cooked manifest.

Opt-in logarithmic depth bands fitted to the full visible non-sky depth range each drawn frame. A GPU min/max reduction covers every depth pixel; false preserves the existing absolute linear depthBandsNear/depthBandsFar fit without reduction passes.

A model LOD whose source charts prevent its triangle target can receive an xatlas parameterisation and a switch-footprint surface projected from LOD0, with aligned albedo, tangent-space normal, occlusion, roughness, metalness, opacity and emission maps and dilated gutters. Derived corners share source attributes on disk and store their own 16-bit atlas UVs. Derived normal and material maps use linear ETC1S, with two-channel normal sampling or XYZ reconstruction on fallback devices; source textures and LOD0 keep their encoding and density. Runtime instances, crowds and terrain scatter select the material with the geometry; levels that reach their target retain source UVs and add no maps. Physical-extension and material-variant surfaces retain their existing path.

The moon's light scatters in the physical sky as the sun's does, by its phase and height (Jensen et al. 2001): a moonlit night is a dim blue sky, brightest round the moon, over land lit as the sky lights it; the fog and the image-based light take it. A new moon leaves the night as it was.

On a page a Player hosts, the Player's hello may name the content base (`content`), over the build's `og build --content`. The page starts the engine with its base to come (CreateOptions.contentLater, host call og_engine_set_content); data loads stay pending until the hello settles the platform, then read from the named base, or fail `unavailable` when there is none.

The most the puddles fill (default 1, as before): steady rain fills them to it and no further, the ground draining what more falls, so a street keeps its water in the joints and hollows instead of one sheet. Lowered below the fill, the puddles drain down to it at drainTime's rate. A game that stopped the fill by raising puddleTime sets the limit instead.

A streamed model fades in instead of appearing whole: every entity a cell spawned (og.CellMember), and a model or HLOD proxy that was hidden while its textures were prepared, is dithered in over 0.4 s in the lit, prepass and shadow passes, on both hosts. og.render.reveal(world, entity, seconds) sets the length for one entity or for everything a cell spawns; 0 draws it whole at once. A model taking over from its HLOD proxy never fades. Presentation only: no world state, event or hash changes. StreamStatus.ready and og.loading.idle stay false until the fades have finished.

A light a cell spawns (og.PointLight, og.SpotLight, og.RectLight) no longer switches on whole on the cell's load tick: its intensity ramps over the same fade as the cell's models (0.4 s by default, held and started with them). og.render.reveal on the light or its cell sets the length; 0 lights it at once. Presentation only: world state and hashes are unchanged; og.loading.idle waits for the ramp.

Close an unused runtime bundle and reclaim its cached models, proxies and BVHs. Calls inside systems wait for the next boundary; status/error distinguish refused closes from completed releases without changing world state or events.

Deciduous leaves follow the year: with og.Season enabled each leaf of a species whose leaves material has season above 0 grows from its bud, turns to a colour between autumnColor and autumnColor2, browns and drops on its own day (trees of a species about 10 days apart, leaves of one tree about a week), its shadow with it; the wood stays. The crown drawn is og.atmosphere.season's leafOut times what has not fallen. Needs compute and indirect draws (RenderCapabilities.caps); the GL tier, scattered copies and impostor cards draw the leaves as modelled.

Shared worlds (guide shared-worlds): visitors of one large world see each other in real time through an `og world-server`, near them only. The game marks its avatar with og.SharedAvatar and moves it as always; og.shared.join asks the host's session provider for a connection (the game names no URL or token), and every other visitor in sight is an og.RemoteAvatar entity the engine spawns, draws 100 ms behind the newest server time between the states around it, and despawns. og.shared.shape adds the game's own avatar fields and an event component (og.shared.send, og.shared.events); og.shared.teleport jumps past the server's speed rule; a refused move comes back as og.SharedCorrected with the avatar put back. og.SharedJoined, og.SharedLeft, og.PresenceEntered and og.PresenceLeft tell the session's life, og.shared.status and og.shared.remote describe it. What the session delivers is host input, applied at a tick's start and kept in og.platform.journal (kind `shared`, without the token), so a session replays without the server. A world that names none of the records keeps its type table and hash.

`og run --shared ws://host:port/ [--shared-token-file f]` gives a native run a static session provider for og.shared: one world server endpoint and the token sent as it is (a self-hosted `og world-server`, or any host's). Without it og.shared.join ends with og.SharedLeft `unavailable`. The run paces itself in real time while a session is open, and its summary carries og.shared.status as `shared`.

A page's `sessions` provider hosts og.shared on the web: a SessionProvider (`host`, `connect({ world, reconnect })` answering `{ ok, url, token? }`), `staticSession({ url, token? })` for a fixed world server, `tokenEndpoint(url)` for a game's own endpoint that signs short-lived tokens for an `og world-server --auth hs256`, or a world server's URL in `window.__OG_PROVIDER.sessions`. The engine Worker opens the WebSocket itself. A page without one ends og.shared.join with og.SharedLeft `unavailable`. Additive: PROVIDER_VERSION stays 1.

A SessionAnswer (and staticSession, tokenEndpoint) may name `webtransport: { url: "https://…", certHashes? }`: a browser that has WebTransport carries og.shared over it and falls back to the answer's WebSocket when it fails to open. og.shared.status's `transport` says `wt` or `ws`. Additive: PROVIDER_VERSION stays 1.

`og run --shared https://host:port/ [--shared-cert-hash HEX]` carries a native run's og.shared session over WebTransport (`og world-server --wt-listen`), checking a self-signed certificate by its SHA-256; a `ws://` URL is a WebSocket as before.

`og world-server --wt-listen ADDR --cert F --key F` also serves WebTransport beside the WebSocket: snapshots and proposals cross as datagrams, so a lost packet delays only itself, and every other message crosses one stream. `og world-server cert` writes a self-signed ECDSA certificate (14 days at most) and prints the SHA-256 a page passes. `og world-server load --url https://… --cert-hash HEX` drives bots over it, and `--latency MS --loss PCT` shapes either transport and reports delivery (delivered fraction, added delay, gaps). The WebSocket protocol is unchanged.

The shared-world server (docs/design.md §2.12), standalone on any host and tied to no platform: it holds every visitor's avatar, checks each proposed move against its kind's top speed and the world's bounds, and sends each client only the avatars within two 128 m cells of it, at most 64, nearest first, as deltas over what the client acknowledged (about 8 bytes for a walking avatar). Tokens are checked offline: --auth hs256 (a secret shared with the game's own token endpoint) or --auth jwks (EdDSA or ES256 keys of an issuer's JWKS, chosen by kid), with --issuer and --max-lifetime to hold iss and exp − iat; --auth none only with --dev. GET /healthz, Prometheus text on --metrics, and SIGTERM drains (clients are told to move). The game API (og.shared) follows in a later release.

A bot swarm of real WebSocket clients against a world server: it measures each client's bytes down and up at the socket, the avatars in sight and the server's tick time (--metrics), and with --gate holds the run to the design's budgets (8 KiB/s down and 1 KiB/s up at p95, tick p99 10 ms).
Sign an HS256 token for a self-hosted world server, as a game's own token endpoint would.

added: The probe's dump_stream `terrain` block counts only the terrains loaded now and adds `fieldBytes`, the whole fields they hold on the CPU (world §2).

added.summary: --alert-* roles for the notifications family: a toast's cut glass plate and rim, its rail width, one hue per tone with a wash from the leading edge (warn a deep amber apart from a reward's gold), the gold rule under a banner, the shade and near-opaque stroke that hold subtitles and a banner over a bright sky, the inbox's open message and reader, and the family's type steps (a banner's title, a level's figure, a subtitle line, each with a phone step). A style pack restyles the family by setting them.

A notification is a glass plate with two corners cut, a rail and a wash in its tone, the tone's mark in an octagon socket, its title in small capitals of the tone and its body in white; each tone has its own hue. A toast is the compact plate with the tone's mark before its words. Under reduced motion they fade in place instead of sliding. New parts notifications.title, notifications.mark and notifications.toast.

HUD type over the scene with no plate: the headline large and balanced over a lit gold rule, the line under it in gold small capitals, with a near-opaque stroke so it holds over a bright sky; a phone type step; it fades in place under reduced motion. New part banner.rule.

HUD type at the foot of the screen inside the HUD's safe edges: the speaker in gold small capitals over the words in white with a near-opaque stroke, on a soft dark shade that holds them over the brightest sky. Lines wrap balanced, so no word is left alone; an older line steps back smaller.

The level up is HUD type: the word in gold small capitals, the level a large white figure lit gold inside a ring of light that settles and stays lit; it no longer draws the style's tag halo of stacked shadows. Under reduced motion the ring, word and figure appear in place.

Messages are cut cards, an unread one with a gold rail and the open one washed gold; the count sits on a dark cut tag; the open message is in a sunken reader; attachments are dark cut chips with their amount as a gold figure; Claim is the reward's gold face; an expired state reads in the danger colour, a claimed one in the success colour. On a narrow inbox the list sits over the reader in one column.

Articles are cut cards, a pinned one with a gold rail; the kind is a chip in the info hue, Pinned and Unread gold tags; the headline is a figure-sized title on a quiet toggle; the picture is cut to match.

--tcg-* roles for the card family (CardFace, CardHand, CardPiles, CardCollection, CardDeckList, CardReward): each type's colour and its type-line ink, the face's cut, glass, wash and rim, the art window over its rarity's glow, the hexagon cost gem, the name plate and text recess, dimming for unplayable and unowned cards (art and frame only), the reason tag, card backs and count tags, the deck list's type rail and steps, the relic plate and the fade of a strip that scrolls sideways.
New prop dim: dims the art and the frame of a card that cannot be played or is not owned, never its words.
New row field cards.reason: the game's words for an unplayable card (No energy), shown on a tag at the card's head, above any Play plate; empty reads Cannot be played. New part CardHand.reason.

New row field filters.count (shown beside the filter's label) and string card.collection.notInDeck; card.collection.inDeck reads In deck ×{count}. New parts CardCollection.count, .owned, .deck, .reason.
New prop kicker (a small line over the title). New parts CardReward.kicker, .mark, .kind, .name, .text, .bracket. A relic's kind line shows its typeLabel when the game gives one.
Contained world labels can opt out of edge fading with contain-fade=none, keeping off-screen boss plates readable without changing distance, occlusion or declutter fades.

--data-* roles for the data and tool panels: the heading ink, the rule between rows, a row's hover, pressed and selected fills and its lit leading edge, the recess a day, node or well sits in, the indent guide, a chart bar's fill, gloss, rim and lean, a marked day's diamond and glow, and a divider's fill and lit grip, which a style pack sets to restyle DataGrid, Chart, NodeGraph, SplitView, Carousel and the table, data-list, tree, pagination, calendar, card and creator-tools screens.
Marks intentional overlap with space-separated full probe paths (or * for all), covering each declared subtree without changing layout or paint.

added.member: Default style dialog and film tokens
added.summary: --dialog-* roles for confirm, tutorial, Menu, Breadcrumbs and TooltipCard (the scrim, the dense plate and its accent or red top edge, the red confirming plate, the title, body, label and row type steps with a larger label step for Chinese, Japanese and Korean, the key chip's rim, the tooltip card's rim, tint and socket well) and --film-* roles for the film screens (the shade behind the choices, a chosen and an unavailable choice, the quick-time bar, a hotspot's brackets and wash, a locked chapter's well, the card widths and name steps). A style pack restyles these documents by setting them.

A dense smoked plate over a dark scrim, lit along its top in the accent; when danger is set the edge is red and a "Cannot be undone" kicker stands over the question. Cancel is a glass plate and the confirming action the lit plate, red for a destructive one. New part confirm.kicker; new string table confirm.en.ogt with screen.confirm.undone.

The step card is an accent-lit plate: the step count as a kicker beside a thin progress line, the title, the text (never clamped: the card grows), Skip in type and Next as the lit plate. New parts tutorial.track and tutorial.fill.

Draws on its own smoked plate. A row is type, washed in the accent from a lit leading edge under the pointer or the focus; a shortcut sits on a dark key chip, a check is drawn in the accent, the chosen radio is a lit diamond, a disabled row is faint and a destructive one red. A long command wraps between its words; rows keep 44 px targets under a coarse pointer.
Dim links, faint chevrons, the current page bold on a lit underline. The trail wraps between crumbs and a long name wraps between its words; crumbs keep 44 px targets under a coarse pointer.

The item's card is a smoked plate lit along its top and tinted at its head in its rarity's colour, the icon in an octagon socket; figures are condensed and tabular, a change carries its triangle and sign in green or red, an added or removed stat a chip. What is equipped stands beside it on a plainer plate, and under it on a narrow screen. Long names and stats wrap between words.

The choices dock at the foot over a shade, under a thin lit line that drains with the time left. A choice is a cut smoked plate whose words wrap whole; the chosen one is ringed and washed in the accent, an unavailable one flat and dim but readable (4.5:1), a quick-time one carries a gold bar. A hotspot is four lit brackets round a faint wash. New part film-choices.shade.

Over a veil: chapters and endings are cut stills with the name under the picture, where a long name wraps whole. The selected one is ringed and lit; one not reached is a hatched dark well under a lock. An ending found carries a gold diamond. The grid fills whole columns and scrolls. New parts shade, plate and lock on both, and film-gallery.mark.

Over a veil; the picked node sits on an accent-lit plate under a "Selected" kicker, its words whole beside Play from here, which drops under them on a narrow screen. New parts film-flowchart.shade and film-flowchart.kicker; new string screen.film-flowchart.selected.

New props keyArt, logo and name: the key art under a vignette, the game's logo (or its name set as a wordmark when there is no logo) and the call between two lit rules, breathing unless motion is reduced. On a touch screen the call reads Tap to start. New parts title.shade, title.rule and title.name.

New props keyArt, logo and name. The entries are type on the key art: dim until pointed at or focused, then washed in the accent from a lit leading edge with a chevron; Credits and Quit are smaller under a divider. News is a cut glass plate in the far corner (above the entries on a phone). New parts main-menu.shade, main-menu.entry, main-menu.news and main-menu.name.

New prop keyArt. The modes are full-art cards with two cut corners: the chosen one has a lit rim and glow, the others are dimmed, a locked one is grey and dark with its reason on a lock line. Play is a lit cut plate. On a phone held upright the title takes its own row under Back and the cards are one column that fades at its foot. New parts mode-select.plate (the cut plate inside a card, which carries the rim), mode-select.shade, mode-select.foot, mode-select.tag and mode-select.lock.

The marks are paged with dots, the boot bar is a slanted lit track with the status and a percentage over it, and a skip hint shows the key on a desktop and Tap to skip on a touch screen. New parts splash.dots, splash.dot, splash.boot, splash.track, splash.fill and splash.skip.

New props keyArt and logo: the roll runs over the key art under a veil, its window fading at both edges; headings sit between lit rules, roles under names, and a key hint says how to roll faster. New parts credits.shade, credits.rule and credits.role.

--front-* roles for the title, splash, main menu, mode select and credits: the dark ground and the shades and veils over key art, the inks and the call's glow, the lit rules, the main menu's entry wash and lit edge, the mode cards' rims, foot and dimmed, chosen and locked art, the tags and the lock's ink, the cut corners, Play's lit plate and glow, the boot bar, the splash's dots and the type steps (with phone steps). A style pack restyles the front end by setting them.

--hud-* roles for ink on the accent, the player's row in the position tower, a place's box, a car's stripe, the best lap's violet, a delta's ink, the tachometer's rev arc, its well, red zone and glass face, the shift lights' green to red ramp, a pedal's keyline, the track map's road and line, a call's tracking, the racing HUD's place, time and speed type steps, and the tachometer's and the track map's sides on a phone, which a style pack sets to restyle the racing HUD.

The track map at a top corner: the circuit as a light line over a dark road, the lap driven lit in the HUD's accent, the start line, the other cars as dots in their colours and the player's car as an arrow turned to its heading; the track's name and length under it. Smaller on a phone, without the length.
A boost meter (nitro, ERS): its picture, its name with the key that fires it, and a leaning bar cut into cells that glows while it fires.
Throttle and brake as two leaning upright wells filled from the foot, green and red, each named under it.

The car's condition: the tyres as tags two to a line inked by their wear (good, worn, bad), the fuel as a thin bar with the game's words that turns to danger with Fuel low, and a Box this lap tag when the team calls the car in.
Feedback over the road: a meter (the slipstream) as a word over a bar in the HUD's accent, and the points a drift or a chain earns, large and slanted, with what earns them in gold.

A tall gauge at a screen edge, cut into ten cells and leaning toward the play field: the run's life (Danger and Failed in words, a pulsing danger rim) or its fever charge (Ready and the key cap that spends it).
The song in play: the jacket in an octagon with a lit edge, title, artist and tempo, the chart's chip in its tier's colour with its level, and the modifiers on tags.
The song's progress as a thin lit line along the screen's top edge, with the time played over the length riding under its played end.
The score chain: a lit plate with the multiplier and the steps to the next one as leaning pips; the plate pops when the multiplier rises.
The judgement tally so far, each judgement in its colour, over a timing scale from Early to Late with the beat at its centre and the latest hits as ticks that fade with their age.
The lanes' key caps under the judgement line, spread across the field, each lit while the player holds it.

--hud-* (stroked HUD type, condensed figures, tracked capitals, cut plates, tag plates, key caps, pips, the HUD accent), --judge-* (a lit colour and gradient per judgement), --gauge-* and --chart-* role tokens, which a style pack sets to restyle the HUD.

added.member: Default style action RPG HUD tokens
added.summary: --hud-* roles for the vitals' life, mana and stamina fills, the boss's health, the stagger gauge, the experience line, a fill in the HUD's accent, the hexagon, slot lift, ready glow, sweeps and their lit edge, the no-mana veil and its word's size, the ultimate's gold, effect edges, feed rows and rarity, blips and the round map, the lock-on ring, a critical's slant, a burn's ink, a quest step's marker and struck line, and the HUD's RPG type steps, which a style pack sets to restyle the RPG HUD.

The party leader's vitals at a top corner: a large octagon portrait, name and level, health as a figure over its most, a fat health bar with a warm ghost that turns to danger when low, a mana bar and a stamina bar cut into cells.
Buffs and debuffs as cut tiles under the leader, green for a boon and red for a harm, the time left as a dark radial sweep over the art and the time or stacks on a tag.

The companions' plates: an octagon portrait, the name, a thin health bar with its ghost over a thinner mana bar and the key that switches to them; a fallen companion dims with a Fallen tag. Side by side on a phone.

A round minimap over a map texture with a lit ring, a sweep and range rings: allies, foes, a boss and the objective as blips of their own shape and colour, the player's arrow turned to the heading, N on its top, and the place with its time of day on a tag under it.
The lock-on reticle a page centres on the locked target: four lit arcs with a glow in the HUD's accent.

Damage and healing figures beside the fight: a critical largest, gold and slanted under its call, older figures stepping down and away, a burn in an ember ink with its word, a heal in green with a plus.
The combo counter: the hits as a large slanted figure with its word, the chain's window as a decay bar and the damage multiplier it gives.
The loot feed: icon, name, the rarity on a tag and the count gained on a fading glass row with an edge tinted by rarity; old rows fade; a phone shows the newest.
What the player can do now over the ability bar (a finisher): a key cap and the action in words, dimmed with its reason when it cannot be done.

The action RPG's ability bar: consumables in smaller octagons with their counts, skills in octagons with a radial cooldown sweep, a lit leading edge and the seconds left, a No mana state, charge pips over a slot and the ultimate in a hexagon inside a gold ring; key caps under every slot. A phone drops the consumables.
Input hints at the screen's foot: a key cap and what it does in small capitals; hidden under a touch screen.
The experience line across the screen's foot, lit violet to the share of the way to the next level, with the level and that share over its start.

--hud-* roles for the sides' inks, the vitals' fills, feed rows, rarity, the radar, the compass band, the reticle, hit marks, incoming damage arcs, slot lift, ready glow, sweeps and the HUD's type steps, which a style pack sets to restyle the shooter HUD.

The player's vitals at a bottom corner: the portrait in an octagon with a lit edge, name and level, health over its most, a shield bar cut into cells over a fat health bar that leaves a warm ghost when it drops and turns to danger (pulsing) when low. The name and level take the row first; the health figure goes under them when they need its room.

The squadmates' plates: portrait, name, a state in words (Reviving, Down), a thin cut shield bar over a thin health bar with its ghost; compact on a phone, with the state on a tag under the name and bars.
The objectives under a heading in the HUD's accent: the one in play lit with its progress on a tag, the others dimmed with theirs. A phone shows the one in play alone.

A round radar over a map texture with a lit ring, a sweep and range rings: allies, foes and the objective as blips of their own shape and colour, the player's arrow turned to the heading, N on its top.
The round and its time left on a lit plate, the score with the player's side in blue against the other's red; urgent turns the plate and clock to danger.
The pickup feed: icon, name and the count gained on a fading glass row with an edge tinted by rarity; a phone shows the newest.
Damage the player deals beside the reticle: the newest figure largest with Headshot or Eliminated over it, older ones stepping down and away.
The interaction prompt under the aim: a key cap and the action in words, dimmed with its reason when it cannot be done.
The effects on the player as cut tiles, green for a boon and red for a harm, the time left as a dark sweep over the art and the time or stacks on a tag.

The ability bar: octagon slots with a cooldown sweep and its seconds, charges on a tag and key caps under them, a ready slot lit; the ultimate in a larger hexagon inside a ring filled by its charge, with its share in figures.

--hud-* roles for a plate whose edge is lit in danger, a surface that wears nothing, an empty slot in a queue or a command card, a unit's health fill green, gold when hurt and red when low, the minimap's camera frame and an alert's red ring on it, and the strategy HUD's readout and unit-name type steps with their phone steps and a cooldown's figure and a tile's key cap each held to a share of its tile, which a style pack sets to restyle the strategy HUD.

The resource bar at the top left: each stockpile's picture in a cut tile, its amount large with a ceiling after it (the population's), and its income under it, green while it grows and red while it drains, or the game's word (Near cap) in gold at a limit; the age or tier on a lit tag. On a phone it takes the width on one or two compact rows.
The match clock at the top right: what it counts (Day 3), the time large and the game's speed on a tag, or Paused.
Alerts and notices as feed rows lit from their start edge, newest first: a mark and an edge in danger, done or info, the game's words and the key that jumps to it; an older notice set back.

Control groups and quick picks (the idle villagers, the army) as small plates with their key caps and counts, the group selected now lit and one that wants the player in gold. Reports pick with the group's key.

The RTS minimap: the whole map square in a lit-edged tile, your units, your allies' and your foes' as dots in their colours (a base larger, a resource a gold diamond), the camera's view as a white frame and each alert a red ring. Smaller on a phone.

The command card: abilities, orders and buildings as square tiles four to a row with their pictures, hotkeys in the corner, a cooldown as a dark sweep with its seconds, a command that cannot be paid for greyed with its price on a red tag, empty cells, the order in hand lit, and the info card of the command in focus over the grid (name, key, what it does, price, cooldown, when it is ready or why it cannot be used). Reports command with the tile's key; a disabled or unaffordable tile sends nothing. On a phone the grid takes the width, eight to a row, without the info card.

--inv-* roles for the inventory family (bags, loot, crafting and trade): the frame's cut corners and lit edge, the kicker over a title, the purse chip and its coin, the tab strip's line, counts and fade, an item tile's cut, hover and selected rims, its rarity bar's glow, the selected tile's corner brackets, the corner tags (stack, Equipped, Locked, New) and Broken's ink, a row's glass, hover and chosen fills, a short ingredient's tint and the alert strip; inv-accent is the HUD's accent unless a pack names another. A style pack sets them to restyle the family.

New props kicker (a small line over the title) and capacity (how full the bag is, as the game words it); a tab row may carry a count, shown beside its label above 0. New parts RpgBackpack.kicker, .purse, .count, .capacity, .state and .bracket. Overburdened (load above 1) is also said in words under the bar.

An item row may carry rarity (common to mythic): its leading edge, its icon's socket and its name take the rarity's colour. RpgCrafting recipes may carry held (how many of the result the player holds); RpgTrade goods may carry was (a struck price before a discount) and after (the balance once paid). New parts: RpgLoot.band, .kicker, .socket; RpgCrafting.band, .kicker, .socket, .hero, .result, .held; RpgTrade.band, .kicker, .socket, .former, .total, .after.

New props line (a line under the name as the game words it, such as One-handed · Item level 60) and reason (why the main button is refused, as the game words it: Requires level 40, shown in red over the buttons while canPrimary is false). New parts RpgItemCard.hero, .band, .kicker, .line, .delta, .current, .stats, .lore, .actions and .reason.

--icard-* roles for the item card: the hero's height and art size (they follow the screen and give way to larger text), the rule under the hero, the name's glow, the headline figure's size, a change's up and down ink and fill and its arrow, the figure columns' widths, and the lore's rule and style. The card otherwise wears the inventory's --inv-* roles.

--loading-* roles for the loading screen: the shade behind its words and at its side, the placeholder without key art, the progress fill and its glow, the bar's lead edge, and Continue's fill and glow, which a style pack sets to restyle the loading screen.

--map-* roles for the world map's marker pins per kind, name plates, chosen and focus rings and legend marks, the place card's fill, picture fade, rule and buttons, the minimap's bezel, glass, grid, north badge, cone and kind colours with pip sizes from the type scale, and the run map's rooms (fill, rim, open, current, done check) and paths (taken, ahead, width), which a style pack sets to restyle maps.

added.member: Default style character and party tokens
added.summary: --party-* roles for the pages around a match and a character's own pages: the smoked cut card and its rules, a tile's or a row's glass, its hover, chosen (an accent ring with a white lip and a wash from its foot) and focus rims, a portrait's shade, the grey of what cannot be picked and a ban's art, an open seat's hairline octagon, ready's green and a refusal's red as ink, tag, glow and a row's edge, the button plate and the accent action's ink, a team's plate on the round HUD and the second side's mirrored row on the versus, the versus seal, the garage's picture shades and ground, the character figure's glow, and the family's type steps and sizes (a name, a side's title, a player's name held to its side, the seal, a round's verdict, a score, the clock, a roster tile, a portrait, a ban, an equipment slot, a garage tile), which a style pack sets to restyle the family.

Two pinned Lucide vectors join the last-resort icon set: tree (Lucide tree-pine) and wheat, so wood and farms have their own icon instead of borrowing leaf, whose outline reads as a speech bubble at chip size. IdleResources, IdleOffline and IdleGenerators fixtures use them.

added.member: Default style puzzle and idle tokens
added.summary: --play-* roles for the puzzle and idle families (PuzzleGoals, PuzzleBoosters, IdleResources, IdleGenerators, IdleOffline, IdlePrestige): the counter's cut well and its low rim and ink, a goal's socket, met check and dimmed art, the score's star bar and marks, the booster socket, its armed ring and lift and an out booster's gold tag, the resource chip and its full rim, a generator's level hexagon, yield ink, Auto and boost tags, locked art and cycle bar, the haul's gold glow, Double's gold and prestige's epic purple.

New props progress and stars: the score toward the level's top star on a leaning bar under it, with the game's star marks, lit up to the progress. A goal shows its name under what is left. New parts PuzzleGoals.socket, .name, .track, .fill and .star.

A generator's level sits on a hexagon at its socket's foot and its cycle is a leaning bar with the time left beside it; a locked row says Locked with what unlocks it (its rate) on one tag. The kicker Producers heads the list. New parts IdleGenerators.kicker, .socket, .level, .owned, .track, .fill, .time and .tag.

The time away is shown large, the panel's status naming the whole sentence; the haul is a row of sockets with the amount and the name under each; Double is dressed in the game's gold. New parts IdleOffline.kicker, .away, .haul, .socket and .amount.

The currency sits in a socket glowing epic purple, what is held beside what a reset gives; each bonus row reads now, an arrow, after; the requirement's tag reads Ready with a check once met over a leaning bar; Prestige is washed in the epic purple. New parts IdlePrestige.kicker, .socket, .label, .tag, .track and .fill.

added.member: Default style quest and reward tokens
added.summary: --quest-* roles for the quests and rewards family: an entry's cut card and its gold wash while a reward waits, the gold Claim face, an icon's octagon socket (gold while its reward waits), a prize's dark well, a medal's hexagon in its tier's colour, a tier's chip, the login calendar's day, today, milestone, missed and taken tiles with the taken stamp and the milestone's ribbon, the journal's quest marks and selected row, the quest page's scenery banner and the family's type steps. A style pack restyles the family by setting them.

New props label (the quest's kind over its name, Main quest), tracked, canTrack and canLocate. With canTrack a primary Track button reports track, and once tracked a quiet Stop tracking button reports track; with canLocate Show on map reports locate. The actions stay at the frame's foot while the body scrolls and fades above them. The scenery is a banner under the title, shaded into the frame's glass; objectives hang from their stage on a rail with the stage in play lit gold; rewards are cut chips with an octagon socket, a reward with a detail lit gold. New parts RpgQuestDetail.actions and RpgQuestDetail.fade, and a long fixture.

Groups are gold small capitals behind a short gold rule, a finished group quiet; the tracked quest's diamond is lit gold, a finished quest's filled; the selected row is washed gold from its leading edge with a chevron toward the detail; a fresh update carries a New tag (new part RpgQuestLog.fresh). An overflow fixture.

HUD type over the scene with no plate: the quest in gold small capitals, a gold diamond per objective (filled once done, its words struck) and a thin leaning bar in a dark well, cut into cells when an objective's new steps field is above 1. On a phone only the objective in play shows.

Day tiles with two corners cut: a header strip, the reward large, its amount and a foot with its state. Today is lit gold with a Claim foot, a taken day carries a check stamp over its dimmed art, a missed day is hatched, a milestone is violet with a ribbon (string general.rewards.milestone). Three across on a phone, a last day alone taking the whole row.

--result-* roles for the screens after a match or a level: the dimmed scene under them, a win's gold and a loss's red verdict fills and glows, the rule and its lit diamond, the grade's hexagon face, a best stat's gold rim, the tabs' rule and accent mark, the top three places' gold, silver and bronze, the player's own lit row, a league's promote and demote edges, a team's ink, rule and row wash on a scoreboard, the revive's and Next's faces, and the verdict, grade, score, title and star type steps with their phone steps, which a style pack sets to restyle the results family.

Opt in to text-overflow: -og-scroll <travel-time> <hold-time> for overflowing single-line titles and native labels. Motion-token durations drive deterministic start/end holds and linear return, with alpha edge fades; fitting text stays still and reduced motion uses an ellipsis. Review distinguishes explicit overflow choices from undeclared cuts.

added.member: Default style song and level select tokens
added.summary: --select-* roles for the song list's cut plates (rest, hover, chosen and focus), its tags and buttons, a difficulty tile's lean, tier strip, chosen fill and rim and each tier's ink, the select's type steps, and the level path's discs (done, open, current, locked, chosen, focus), road, star capsule and chapter meter, which a style pack sets to restyle song and level select.

--shop-* roles for the shop family (Shop, ShopConfirm, PassTrack, Reveal, IdlePurchases): the offer tile's cut, fill and rims, its art well and the rarity's glow behind the art, the ruled foot and price sizes, corner tags (a discount on gold) and refusal tags (owned, short, sold out), the confirmation's ledger and socket, the pass's level hexagon, premium gold (button, lane rule, tile wash and rim) and ready ring, the reveal's sealed glow and reward sockets, an upgrade's refused Buy. The family otherwise wears the inventory's --inv-* roles.

New props kicker (a small line over the title) and, on rows, tabs.count, offers.rarity (the light behind the art) and offers.badgeTone (success puts a badge such as New on green). New parts Shop.kicker, .count, .art, .detail, .featured, .foot, .bracket.

New props rarity (the socket the icon sits in), reason (why the purchase is refused when no price says it) and, on prices rows, missing (how much more a short currency takes, shown as Not enough Gems · 1,600 more). New parts ShopConfirm.art, .detail, .ledger, .after, .missing, .reason, .actions.
New prop level (on a hexagon beside the bar to the next tier). New parts PassTrack.kicker, .level, .track, .fill, .art.
New props kicker and icon (the sealed prize). New parts Reveal.band, .kicker, .socket, .dot.

--social-* roles for chat, friends and a conversation: a chat line's chip and the player's own gold wash, the shown channel's fill and gold foot, another player's name colour, how far an away or offline friend's avatar dims, a conversation band's glass and gold-lit rim, the speaker's gold plate, a reply key's keyline, narration's style and the line's type steps (with a phone step). --alert-level-shade fills a level up's ring. A style pack restyles the family by setting them.

Channels are cut tabs, the one shown washed and lit gold along its foot, an unread count a gold cut chip; the log sits in a dark cut well (Chat.plate and Chat.well now name the well around the scrolling Chat.log, so a scrolled line clips inside its rim); each line is a cut chip, the player's own washed gold at the far side, another player's name in the info colour, a system line bare and quiet beside a gold bolt; the notice reads in the warn amber.

Section headings are gold small capitals; a request is a cut card washed gold with its avatar in a gold socket and Accept on the reward's gold face; a friend is a cut row, the chosen one washed gold with a gold bar; presence is a diamond in its tone at the avatar's foot and the status reads in that tone. Away and offline dim the avatar and its mark, never the name. The title keeps its words whole and Add friend wraps under it when both do not fit.

The band is cut glass lit gold along its top; the speaker sits on a gold plate in small capitals over the line in a larger white type step (a phone step under 720 px); each reply is a cut row with its number in a gold keyline, the one in focus washed gold with its number filled and a lit gold diamond, a used reply grey; Auto when on is lit gold. The reply number no longer carries a trailing full stop.

Lines are cut cards with the speaker in gold small capitals, narration quiet and in italics, and the line replaying washed gold with a gold bar; the title keeps its words whole and Close wraps under it when both do not fit.

An earned star is drawn filled in the style's star gold under a lit edge, with a soft glow; an unearned star is a faint outline over a dim well. Each star keeps its star icon under the drawn glyph. New parts star-rating.star and star-rating.glyph, and the --star-* role tokens, let a style pack recolour both. The landing animation is unchanged.

Document each blocks can iterate string-list props, writable values and literal defaults using the string itself as the stable key. Distinct nonempty strings retain their controls and focus across reorder; duplicate and empty strings are rejected. Repeated labels still use object rows with distinct keys.

Beside the slots, a cut glass plate shows the chosen slot: its shot, chapter, place, time and date, the game's preview under them and the actions at the plate's foot (the main one on its own row when the plate is too narrow for all three). With no slot chosen there is no plate. A phone held upright keeps only the actions at the foot. New parts save-load.detail and save-load.shot.

The brightness step draws its own test in the well: three marks on black, from one a well set screen barely shows to one it shows clearly, lifted as the slider moves. A game's test snippet replaces it.

added.member: Default style pause and settings tokens
added.summary: --system-patch-ground, --system-patch-faint, --system-patch-mid and --system-patch-clear: the calibration brightness patch's black and its three marks.

added.member: Default style pause and settings tokens
added.summary: --system-* roles for the pause, settings, save and load and calibration screens: the shade over the paused game and the veil under the full screens, their title and entry type steps (with phone steps), a disabled and a dangerous entry's ink, a settings row and its lit state, the page tabs' rule and lit bar, a save slot's lit rim and an empty slot's well, and the calibration steps' rings. A style pack restyles these screens by setting them.

The game stays in view under a shade from the leading side; the menu is a column of type down that side, washed in the accent from a lit edge when pointed at or focused, Quit to menu and Quit game smaller under a divider (Quit game in red). The objective and the time played sit in a cut glass plate. Every entry keeps a 44 px target. New parts pause.shade, pause.status and pause.entry; new string screen.pause.objectiveLabel.

Over a veil: the pages are a strip of type tabs with a lit bar under the chosen one, which scrolls sideways and fades at its edges when the pages outrun it (the keys that change page shown at its ends on a desktop). The settings are glass strips, the focused one lit; its description shows in a plate beside the list on a wide screen and under its row on a narrow one. Revert and Apply are cut plates. New parts settings.shade, settings.tabs, settings.tab and settings.description.

Slots are cut glass strips (thumb, chapter, place, time and date, an Auto tag), the chosen one ringed and lit; an empty slot is a well. The preview and the actions sit beside them, the actions at the foot on a phone held upright, as cut plates; on a phone the Auto tag sits on the thumb. New parts save-load.shade, save-load.tag, save-load.preview and save-load.actions.

One cut glass plate: the steps as a numbered track, the current one lit and the finished ones filled; the game's test in a well; the hint and the control; Back and Next as cut plates. New parts calibration.step and calibration.test.
HudEditor's hint sits on a cut glass plate like the pause menu's status. KeyValues reads names in dim ink and values in front ink with tabular figures.
