breaking.member: UI: text on a path in a vertical element
breaking.change: Text on a path (`-og-text-path`) in a `vertical-*` or `sideways-*` writing mode is set as a vertical line along the path: upright clusters stand one vertical advance long with their tops back along the path, and sideways runs lie along it. It was set as horizontal text. Its box is unchanged (the path's extent).
breaking.fix: Text that should read as horizontal along a path sets `writing-mode: horizontal-tb` on the path text.

breaking.change: Layout change: a document's flex item that declares no flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink or flex-basis is CSS's initial `flex: 0 1 auto`, so an item with a definite width or height now shrinks with its siblings when its line overflows, as in a browser. It used to keep its size and overflow the line. An or with a px size shrinks no smaller than that size (its natural size). The built-in main menu and carousel keep their sizes.
breaking.fix: Give an item that must keep its size along an overflowing line `flex-shrink: 0` (or `flex: none`).

breaking.member: UI CSS position: absolute and fixed (top, right, bottom, left, inset)
breaking.change: Layout change: an absolute or fixed box's insets and percentage sizes are measured from its containing block's padding edge, inside the holder's border, as in CSS. They were measured from the holder's outer (border) edge, so a box at top: 0; left: 0 sat on the holder's border.
breaking.fix: Where an inset made up for the border (top: 2px under a 2px border), set it back to the intended distance from the padding edge (top: 0).

breaking.member: UI CSS white-space, white-space-collapse, tab-size and text-wrap
breaking.change:
Text change: a text's white space is processed from its computed white-space at build time, for bound text ({$value}, {expr}) and text with inline elements as for literal text. Before, the parser collapsed every text's spaces and line breaks HTML's way unless it was plain literal text, so pre, pre-line, pre-wrap, break-spaces and tab-size did nothing to a bound string, and a bound string under normal kept its runs of spaces and newlines as written. A
stays a line break under every value.
breaking.fix: A text that relied on a bound string's newlines or repeated spaces showing under the default white-space gives the element `white-space: pre-line` (newlines) or `white-space: pre-wrap` (spaces and newlines).

breaking.change: A block whose children lie in lines (it holds an inline-level box) beside a float is no longer narrowed whole as if it started its own formatting context: its lines are shortened one by one and those below the floats take the full width, and a float inside it now reaches the boxes after it.
breaking.fix: Give the block display: flow-root to keep it narrowed whole beside the floats and holding its own floats.

breaking.change: @font-face font-weight and font-stretch (font-width) default to auto, as CSS Fonts 4 says: a variable font's wght or wdth range, else 400 and 100 %. og_ui::css::FontFace's weight and stretch are Option (None: auto).
breaking.fix: Declare font-weight or font-stretch on an @font-face whose variable font should keep one weight or width; read FontFace.weight and .stretch as Option.

breaking.change: ui-monospace and ui-rounded no longer stand in for a style without a mono or rounded face of its own (ui-rounded used to take the display face), and ui-serif and math no longer take the body face ahead of later families: each matches nothing there and the next family in the list draws. FontFamily gains a Ui variant.
breaking.fix: End a family list with the generic that should stand in (monospace, sans-serif, fantasy), as in a browser.

breaking.change: In a grid, justify-content aligns the tracks (CSS Box Alignment) instead of each item in its cell, and justify-content: normal leaves auto tracks to stretch into the free room.
breaking.fix: To align items in their cells, write justify-items (or justify-self on the item).

breaking.member: UI document scoped CSS (the root element's auto width)
breaking.change: A document's root element with width: auto now fills the column or stack it is mounted in, as CSS's root block fills the initial containing block, instead of shrinking to fit its content. A wider child's min-content no longer widens the whole document past the viewport, so max-width: 100% and aspect-ratio below it hold to the viewport (a 640px card with max-width: 100% in a 16px-padded root at a 390 viewport is 358×201, not 640×360).
breaking.fix: Where a component should size to its content, give its root element `width: fit-content`.

breaking.change: CSS easing keywords in transition now use the CSS curves (ease-out is cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)), not the style's own curves. animation no longer requires forwards, a missing 0% or 100% keyframe takes the element's value, and conditional animations are allowed.
breaking.fix: Recook documents. For the style's curves write the motion token, for example transition: opacity var(--motion-ui), or an explicit cubic-bezier(). Add forwards (or both) where an animation should hold its last keyframe.

breaking.change: Beam.tile (texture repeats per metre) is uvTile, metres per repeat, as og.Trail.uvTile and RibbonDesc.uvTile: one tiling for every strip. 0 now stretches the texture once from the entity to `end`; the default stays one repeat per metre. A saved og.Beam keeps its look (version 3 and a save step take the reciprocal).
breaking.fix: Rename tile to uvTile and give it 1 / the old value (tile 2 becomes uvTile 0.5).

breaking.change: SpriteBlend and StripBlend are one enum, Blend: alpha 0 and additive 1 everywhere (StripBlend had additive 0). og.Trail, og.Beam and RibbonDesc still default to additive, sprites to alpha; the variant strings are unchanged, so `blend: "alpha"` means what it did. A saved og.Trail or og.Beam keeps its blend (og.Trail and og.Beam take version 2 and a save step).
breaking.fix: Rename the type SpriteBlend or StripBlend to Blend where game code names it.

breaking.change: SpriteBlend is now Blend (see StripBlend).
breaking.fix: Rename SpriteBlend to Blend.

breaking.change: A composed effect's `flash` element is `glow` from `type vfx` version 2, so it no longer shares its name with og.tween.flash and PostEffects.flash; VfxInfo.elements reports it as `glow`. Version 1 files still load, their `flash` read as `glow`; a version 2 file that says `flash` is refused with the new name. og vfx import and the cook's Effekseer conversion write version 2.
breaking.fix: Write `glow { ... }` and `version 2` in a type vfx file (og upgrade rewrites a version 1 file's top-level flash elements).

breaking.change: og.Wind is the world's wind and `strength` is removed: `speed` is how fast the air moves (m/s, 0 by default: still), and vegetation leans 0.05 of its height for each m/s of it. `speed` used to be how fast the gusts travelled (3 by default) beside a separate lean.
breaking.fix: Set `speed` to the old `strength / 0.05` (a strength of 0.3 is 6 m/s) and drop `strength`. A save restores that way by itself.

breaking.change: Both are added to og.Wind (the clouds take it at twice its speed) and default to no drift of their own: clouds were carried at (12, 0.4, 4) and rain and snow at (1.5, 0, 0.5) whatever og.Wind said.
breaking.fix: Set og.Wind's direction and speed for a world whose clouds, weather and vegetation move together; for the old motion without it, set og.Clouds.wind to (12, 0.4, 4) and og.Weather.wind to (1.5, 0, 0.5).

breaking.change: og.Wind now pushes every rope, cloth and garment (its velocity in m/s as an acceleration), and each one's `wind` is added to it. They ignored og.Wind before, so a world with both moves differently.
breaking.fix: Nothing where the two should agree. For one that must hang still in a wind, set its `wind` to the opposite of og.Wind's velocity.

breaking.change: With followRotation the offset is x to the entity's right, y up and z behind it. It was turned by the entity's rotation as it stood, which put the default offset (0, 2, 6) six metres in front of an entity facing its +Z (a vehicle, a nav or motion agent), looking at its face.
breaking.fix: Where a game set followRotation and chose an offset by hand, negate the offset's x and z; a game that left the default now gets the camera behind the entity.

breaking.change: followRotation now turns followOffset with the followed entity (x to its right, y up, z behind it), and a shot with no lookAt keeps its own og.Transform rotation. Both read a rotation that was always the identity, so the offset stayed in world axes and such a shot looked down world -Z.
breaking.fix: Nothing where followRotation is off and the shot's entity is not rotated. A shot that set followRotation, or a rotated shot with no lookAt, now does what its fields say; re-record replays and pinned hashes of worlds with one.

breaking.change: SaveEdit.types answers a Result, as the host always did: { ok: true, value: SaveType[] }, refused once the save is closed. It used to be typed as the bare list, and the runtime answered [] for a closed save.
breaking.fix: Check `.ok` and read `.value`: `const t = edit.types(); if (t.ok) for (const type of t.value) ...`.

breaking.change: og.render.display is typed DisplayInfo | null: it answers null when the world has no engine or its renderer cannot be read at that moment, which it always did but the type did not say.
breaking.fix: Check for null before reading the answer: `const d = og.render.display(world); if (d) save(d.settings);`.

breaking.change: The inspector's panel is a built-in document now, styled only by tokens, so dump_inspector names its elements by the document's ids: a component's or resource's header is Inspector/Detail/Group#C:<Component>/Section (Group#R:<Resource>/Section), a field's row Inspector/Detail/Group#…/Field#<target>/Row and its text boxes …/Row/Part#<target>%23<n>, a hierarchy row Inspector/Tree/Row#<bits>/Entry#<bits>/Label. The toolbar keeps its paths (Inspector/Bar/Save, Inspector/Tools/Undo, Inspector/View/Strip/Track/Item#1).
breaking.fix: Find a field's text box by its set target: Inspector/Detail/F:Score.best/P0 is Inspector/Detail/Group#R:Score/Field#Score.best/Row/Part#Score.best%230, and Inspector/Detail/S:Score is Inspector/Detail/Group#R:Score/Section.

breaking.change: The style catalogue is twelve looks, every one offered to a new game: cinematic-realism, anime-cel-3d, inked-comic-3d, painterly-3d, faceted-low-poly, low-resolution-3d, pixel (was 16bit-pixel), minimal-geometric, neon-vector, toy-3d (new), cartoon-2d (new) and pixel-3d-hybrid. The look.frozen mark and the refusal of a frozen look are gone. Removed presets, previews and catalogue entries, with nothing resolving them: 16bit-pixel (now pixel); folded into a kept look's variant: muted-cinematic-3d (cinematic-realism muted), bold-comic-illustration and heavy-ink-shadows (inked-comic-3d bold-comic, heavy-ink), lush-painted-worlds, luminous-layered-painting and expressionist-painting (painterly-3d lush, luminous-layers, expressionist), monochrome-dither-3d (low-resolution-3d monochrome-dither), 8bit-pixel, monochrome-pixel, detailed-pixel, luminous-pixel, coarse-pixel and topdown-tile-pixel (pixel 8bit, monochrome, detailed, luminous, coarse, topdown), layered-silhouette (minimal-geometric layered-silhouette), voxel-worlds, sculpted-clay, miniature-diorama and paper-craft (toy-3d voxel, clay, diorama, paper), watercolor-wash, decorative-storybook and rubber-hose-animation (cartoon-2d watercolor, storybook, rubber-hose); deleted outright: illuminated-manuscript, black-figure-pottery, classical-painting-collage, gothic-contour, detailed-doodle and pencil-hatching. An old slug is an unknown look: extends, create and presetLook refuse it as any unknown name. painterly-3d and pixel-3d-hybrid now name ui "fantasy", neon-vector ui "scifi" and draws on a black sky, toy-3d and cartoon-2d ui "cartoon"; neon-vector's support is content (its line art is authored).
breaking.fix: Extend one of the twelve. For a removed style, extend its kept look and name the variant: `extends "pixel"` with `variant "8bit"`, `extends "toy-3d"` with `variant "voxel"`; for 16bit-pixel, `extends "pixel"`. For a deleted one, pick the nearest look (cartoon-2d for the manuscript, pottery, collage, gothic and doodle styles, inked-comic-3d for pencil-hatching).

breaking.change: A game file's module-scope let or var written from a function, or a module-scope container ([], {}, new Map, new Set, a typed array) mutated from one, is now an og check error (OG9101) instead of a warning in the first log: state in a JS module is outside the world snapshot and the presentation checkpoint, so a restore, a rollback or a fork does not bring it back. og run, og test and og build stop on it as on a type error. The check parses and resolves names (a local shadowing a module name is its own; a write as the module loads is not state); playtests and tests are not checked.
breaking.fix: Keep the state in a component or a resource, or derive it again where it is needed (og.load answers the same handles for a path loaded before). --no-check runs anyway.

breaking.change: A font's shaped forms (ligatures, joined letters, OpenType features' alternates) are keyed by glyph id past Unicode (0x110000 + id) instead of as the private-use characters U+F0000 + id, which collided with fonts that map characters there (icon fonts): such a character drew another glyph or failed to cook. The font blob is version 2; one cooked by an earlier engine is refused when it loads. A saved UI state of the previous version upgrades, its frozen texts' shaped forms read as glyph ids.
breaking.fix: Cook the project again (`og cook`). Every font recooks with the same charset, glyphs, pages and run-time mode; only the keys of its shaped forms move.

breaking.change: Each screen and component document is typed from its contract: `og ui types` writes `.og/types/ui/<name>.d.ts` (its props, the events it can send, its slots) and og check, run, build and dev write them before they check. These functions take the document's name as a type parameter, so for a declared name the viewmodel or props must match the contract (every prop given, of its type; a list's items as its fixtures show them) and og.ui.screenVm answers that type. A partial viewmodel or a prop of the wrong type no longer type-checks. A name no document declares stays untyped, as before. The wire is unchanged.
breaking.fix: Pass the whole viewmodel the document's `props` block declares (or declare the prop `any` there). A game made before this release adds ".og/types/**/*.d.ts" to its tsconfig's include to get the types.

breaking.change: og.Fluid2D steps with the solver og.Fluid3D uses: neighbours come from the spatial hash in its pair order, a particle pushed out of a solid loses its velocity into it and a little of its slide (as in 3D), and its spawn jitter differs. A 2D fluid settles to the same shape but not to the same particle positions, so the world hash of a world with one, and a snapshot or replay recorded on an earlier version, no longer match.
breaking.fix: Re-record replays and pinned hashes of worlds with an og.Fluid2D; restore no snapshot holding one across the version. No field changed.

breaking.change: An aligned follower now faces along the path as every object does: its +Z along the tangent. It used to be turned as a camera, -Z along the tangent, so a model travelled backwards. `offset` is unchanged (the path's right, up and backwards).
breaking.fix: Remove any half-turn a game added to its model or its children to face it along the path. For a camera riding a path, sample the path and set og.transform.lookAt(position, position + tangent).

breaking.change: A playtest file (`tests/*.og.ts`) is a bun:test file: describe, test and expect from "bun:test", each test awaiting `runPlaytest({ commands, ... })`, which plays the script in fresh processes of the game og test built and resolves to the PlaytestRun. `playtest()`, the default export, `PlaytestDesc.name` and `check(run, t)` with t.ok, t.equal, t.near and t.frame are removed. The script's expect: steps, invariants and require are one assertion: runPlaytest rejects with each failure. A test with no assertion fails. A frame read without a renderer outside `run.frame` now fails the test (FrameUnchecked) instead of ending the check.
breaking.fix: Write `test("what it proves", async () => { const run = await runPlaytest({ commands }); expect(run.quit).toBe(true); })`. t.ok(x) becomes expect(x).toBe(true) or a matcher on the value; t.equal compared JSON text, so use toBe for a primitive and toEqual or toStrictEqual for a structure; t.near(a, b, tol) is an absolute tolerance, `expect(Math.abs(a - b)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(tol)` (toBeCloseTo takes decimal places); t.frame(files, f) becomes run.frame(files, f). A game's tsconfig maps "bun:test" to `.og/engine/vendor/bun-types/test.d.ts`, as the template's does.

breaking.change: A publish build no longer writes the plain-name copies `origin-engine.js` and `origin-engine_bg.wasm`, nor the one-line `play.js` loader: `index.html` loads `./play.<hash>.js` directly, and every bundle, engine module and decoder exists only under its content-hashed name (docs/web-export.md §Content-hashed names; platform ask 18). A dev build keeps every plain name. A game's code is unaffected; a host, deploy script or check that reads a publish build's files by a plain name finds nothing.
breaking.fix: Read the served names from the build's og-build.json: `worker` (the engine Worker), `wasm`, `lanes.glue`/`lanes.wasm`, and `names` (each plain name to its served file, such as `names["play.js"]`).

breaking.change: Ease columns store a canonical 20-byte tag and parameter payload, not a named-only u32 enum index. Camera blendEase, soloEase and blendCurve accept the full shared timing vocabulary.
breaking.fix: Use Ease strings for every field; rebuild cooked scenes and start new recordings/snapshots containing Ease columns. Raw Uint32Array views have stride 5.

breaking.change: Removed: HDR is no longer opt-in. RenderOptions.output (left out `best`) presents extended range and Display P3 wherever the surface offers them, and the tone curve the game chose extends to the headroom instead of the LPM mapper replacing it. On an SDR display or surface nothing changes.
breaking.fix: Delete `hdr: true`. To keep a game at SDR on HDR displays, set `render: { output: "wide" }` (Display P3, standard range) or `output: "srgb"` in GameDesc.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `orthonormal_basis(n: vec3<f32>) -> mat3x3<f32>` (Duff et al.'s branch-free basis about a unit vector) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares its own `orthonormal_basis` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader (material, post and UI shaders) now has `srgb_encode`, `srgb_decode`, `luma` and `const LUMA` (Rec.709 weights) in scope, from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's (it is the standard sRGB curve and Rec.709 luminance), or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `is_sky_depth(d)` and `const SKY_VIEW_DEPTH` in scope, and lit material shaders `toward_eye(p)`, from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `hue_rotate(rgb: vec3<f32>, a: f32) -> vec3<f32>` (the colour's hue turned by `a` radians about the grey axis) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares its own `hue_rotate` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `hg_phase(cos_t, g)` (the Henyey-Greenstein phase function) in scope, and lit material shaders `range_window(light, d2)` and `spot_cone(light, l)` (a local light's windowed falloff and a spot's cone), from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `face_dir(face: u32, uv: vec2<f32>) -> vec3<f32>` (a cube face's direction at its NDC point) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares its own `face_dir` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every module a game shader is compiled into now starts with the engine's shader library, so a game shader that defines a function named pcg, hash_lowbias, hash_to_unit, hash_unit, lattice3, oct_encode, oct_decode, fullscreen_clip, view_point or ign no longer cooks: the cook refuses it with the redefinition error.
breaking.fix: Rename the function in the game's shader, or delete it and call the engine's: pcg(u32) and hash_lowbias(u32) hash an integer, hash_unit(u32) gives a number in [0, 1), oct_encode(vec3) and oct_decode(vec2) map a unit vector to and from the octahedral square, ign(pixel) is interleaved gradient noise.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `value_noise2(p: vec2<f32>, layer: i32)`, `value_noise3` and `value_noise3_at` in scope from the engine's one copy (value_noise3 was already there in material shaders; sprite, post and UI shaders get it now); a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `oklab_encode` (linear light to Oklab) and `oklab_decode` (back) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `const PI` in scope from the engine's one copy (material and UI shaders had one already; post shaders did not), so a post shader that declares its own `PI` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own `PI` and use the library's (write a turn as `2.0 * PI`), or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `quad_corner(i: u32) -> vec2<f32>` (corner i mod 6 of a unit quad drawn as two counter-clockwise triangles) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares its own `quad_corner` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every material shader now has `world_normal(model, n)` (a normal through a transform's inverse transpose) and `skin_matrix(joints, weights, palette)` (a vertex's blended joint matrix) in scope from the engine's one copy, and `custom_skin` is gone (it was `skin_matrix` under another name); a shader that declares `world_normal` or `skin_matrix`, or calls `custom_skin`, no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, and call `skin_matrix` where you called `custom_skin` (the same arguments), or rename yours.

breaking.change: RenderCapabilities.tier is now the feature set the renderer was made for (RenderTier: `full`, `miniGame` or `gl`, `full` without a renderer), as og-render's tier is. The backend it used to name (`webgpu`, `vulkan`, `vulkan-cpu`, `metal`, `dx12`, `none`) is the new RenderCapabilities.backend, typed RenderBackend, the former RenderTier type; the probe's hello still names it `tier`.
breaking.fix: Read `og.render.capabilities(world).backend` where you read `.tier` for the backend, and the type `RenderBackend` where you named `RenderTier`.

breaking.member: Engine components and resources (og.*) read by the engine
breaking.change: The engine now reads the og.* components and resources it uses as their IDL types. Two cases a well-formed game never meets behave differently: a NaN float field (written from a failed computation) reaches the engine as NaN instead of being replaced by the field's default, so whatever it drives (a camera's fov, a transform, a timeline's speed, a post-effect value, a world origin's step) goes NaN too, except where NaN would crash, which keeps the old fallback; and a row with an enum field set past its variants (for example PostEffects.aoMethod 7) is skipped as unreadable, or refused by the system that reads it, instead of being clamped to the first variant while the rest of the row still applied.
breaking.fix: Write finite numbers and a declared variant (by name, or an index within the enum) to og.* fields; check a computed value with Number.isFinite before writing it.

breaking.change: Removed the CSS style-check command and its contrast pass, which timed out on the built-in documents.
breaking.fix: Use og ui sheet and og ui review to inspect packs; og style check-project remains the game's art-contract checker.

breaking.change: A declaration outside a :root rule may no longer write a literal colour (#hex, a named colour, rgb()/hsl()/… without var()), a length other than 0, a duration or a url(); the check fails with <file>:<line>: <property>: literal … for each. Keywords, 0, unitless numbers, percentages and angles stay allowed, and @font-face src and -og-sound may name url()s anywhere. og style new writes packs that pass.
breaking.fix: Move each value into a :root (or :root[data-scheme=…]) custom property and name it with var() in the rule: button::part(base) { border: 2px solid #8f7650 } becomes :root { --line-strong: #8f7650 } and button::part(base) { border: var(--stroke-regular) solid var(--line-strong) }.

breaking.member: Word and line breaking in Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese
breaking.change: ICU's word dictionaries for these scripts left the engine (about 3 MB of wasm) and ship in the font packs: the cook packs one only when a string table's locale takes that language and an installed font pack names it, and og.i18n installs it with the pack. A game with such a locale but no pack for it now breaks that text by the Unicode rules alone (a run of these scripts is one word) and is warned of at cook.
breaking.fix: Install the locale's font pack: og font add japanese, chinese-simplified, chinese-traditional or thai (og create --lang does it).

breaking.change: A caption track draws nothing. The engine used to draw the showing key itself, white on a black plate over everything, at the track's anchor and type step. The keys showing are now the UI's $captions store, and the track's and keys' style and anchor entries are refused: a caption is text only.
breaking.fix: Load and push the built-in subtitles screen once (og.load.document(world, "@ui/screens/subtitles.svelte"), then og.ui.push(world, "subtitles", { lines: [] })): it shows $captions after the game's own lines, dressed by the style pack. Delete style and anchor from caption tracks; to place or size captions differently, iterate $captions in a document of your own.

breaking.change: AssertRecord.condition is required: a record without one (or with a condition that is not true or false) is refused, so it counts as neither true nor false and the call answers the epoch. It used to count as false, so an always or each record without a condition was reported as a violation. AssertRecord.kind left out is always, as the IDL says. og.assert.always, sometimes, reachable, unreachable and each send a condition and are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Send condition (true for reachable and unreachable) in every record a tool passes to og.assert.record.

breaking.change: DisplaySettings.frameCap, quality and powerPreference are read by name only: an index (frameCap: 1, quality: 2, powerPreference: 1) used to pick the variant at that position and is now refused with the field and the names, such as `settings.frameCap: expected a FrameCap name (auto, display, ...), got 1`.
breaking.fix: Pass the variant's name (frameCap: "fps30", quality: "high", powerPreference: "lowPower"), as og.render.display(world).settings answers them.

breaking.change: RenderTargetDesc.format is read by name only: format: 1 used to mean hdr and is now refused (`desc.format: expected a RenderTargetFormat name (...), got 1`).
breaking.fix: Pass format: "hdr" or "ldr".

breaking.change: CurveDesc.kind is read by name only: kind 0, 1 or 2 used to pick catmullRom, bezier or linear and is now refused (`desc.kind: expected a PathKind name (catmullRom, bezier, linear), got 0`).
breaking.fix: Pass kind: "catmullRom", "bezier" or "linear".

breaking.change: TweenDesc, TweenFromDesc, TimelineTweenVars and TweenKeyframe are read whole by the generated types, `to` and `from` included: a lane list holding something other than a number is refused with its index (`desc.to[1]: expected a number, got "a"`) instead of a message without the path; a desc that is not an object is refused as `desc: expected an object`.
breaking.fix: Pass `to` and `from` as one number or a list of numbers.

breaking.change: ShapeGeometryDesc.shapes, ExtrudeGeometryDesc.shapes and SweepGeometryDesc.section are read by the generated types: a point whose x or y is not a number used to read as 0 and is now refused with its path (`desc.shapes[0].holes[0][2].y: expected a number, got "1"`). The uvRepeat of cylinderGeometry, coneGeometry, capsuleGeometry, torusGeometry, ringGeometry, circleGeometry and tubeGeometry is read the same way: a component that is not a number used to be 1 and is refused.

breaking.fix:
Write the box in a document: the portrait an ``, the speaker a ``, the line a `

` with `-og-reveal: 40` (characters a second) and `onrevealed` when it is whole, and a `

breaking.member: @origingame/engine/ui-parts/hud: slot, statusGrid, statBar, minimapView; @origingame/engine/ui-parts/screen: STAR_GOLD, speechBubble
breaking.change: The kit helper modules no longer re-export the removed components.
breaking.fix: Use the component documents (`og ui eject <name>`) in a kit's screens; for the star gold write `#ffc93c` or the style's `--gold` token.

breaking.change: Every built-in component and screen takes its colours, sizes, spacing, radii, strokes, shadows and timings from tokens and names its frames, bands, titles, rows, cells, wells, badges, figures and labels as parts, so the default style's role rules dress them. Their own panel fills, borders, radii, glass and text shadows are removed, colours written in markup (SVG fill and stroke attributes, colour fallbacks) moved to CSS, and sizes moved to the nearest token, so their appearance changes.
breaking.fix: Restyle them from a style pack: set the role and semantic tokens in :root, or write a ::part rule on the part the component names. A game that needs the old look of one document copies it with og ui eject and edits its own copy.

breaking.change: Core elements take HTML's names wherever HTML names the role, with HTML's attributes: (type text, password, number, email, url, tel, search) and
breaking.fix: Write as (or its type) and a multi-line one as

breaking.change: `modal` is refused when bound (`modal={$x}`): a modal's content is built in the top layer, under `<id>/Panel`, so it is fixed when the document is written, as HTML chooses showModal() or show() per opening.
breaking.fix: Write `modal` as a literal; for a dialog that is sometimes modal, write two dialogs or put one in `{#if}`.

breaking.change: The built-in components are filed by what they do instead of flat or by genre kit: base/ (small parts: Spinner, Ribbon, SkeletonGroup, Avatar…), hud/ (screen-space play: AbilityBar, StatBar, ProgressBar, Crosshair, Killfeed, CombatLog, QuestTracker, AmmoCounter, RadialMenu, TouchControls…), world/ (pinned to the scene: Compass, Nameplate, Minimap, Waypoint, SpeechBubble, Telegraph…), panels/ (whole screens and panes: Backpack, ItemCard, QuestLog, Conversation, Menu, DataGrid, TooltipCard, Chart…) and meta/ (the former general/: Shop, Friends, Chat, Achievements, DailyRewards…). Genre kits (rpg/, shooter/, racing/, …) keep only their genre's own pieces; a piece any genre uses moved out of its kit with its strings in a `<name>.en.ogt` beside it. Component names are unchanged; their ids, import paths and eject names gained the folder. RpgCompass merged into Compass, and RpgActionBar into AbilityBar, whose slot takes a count (a quick item's stack).
breaking.fix: Import `@ui/components/<folder>/<file>.svelte` (for example `@ui/components/panels/backpack.svelte`) and eject with `og ui eject panels/backpack`; `og api find` lists each component's folder. Write `<Compass heading pois units="m">` for RpgCompass. For RpgActionBar, use one `<AbilityBar slots>` for skills and a second for quick items with each slot's `count`.

breaking.change: The og-kit layer is renamed og-components, ordered og-default, og-components, og-pack, og-game; it holds the rules of the engine's built-in component documents (sources under @ui/): a style pack's rule dresses a built-in component over its own rule of any specificity, and a game's own rules beat both.
breaking.fix: Write og-components where a stylesheet named og-kit in an @layer rule.

breaking.change: og style check reports contrast as facts about what is drawn instead of root-token ratios: the core-control sheet's pages and every built-in document (from its fixture:default) are built under the pack in both schemes without a GPU, and each text is read on what is drawn under it (fills, gradients and images where the text is, glass, layer opacity; a ground the UI covers only partly over black and over white, called scene), with its WCAG 2 ratio, APCA Lc and, with a text-shadow or stroke, its ratio on that halo, read a pixel out from the glyphs' edge on their weakest side as the renderer covers it (a blurred shadow covers at most half there; an offset one, one side only). It also reports how far apart (ΔEOK) the team and state colours stay under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. It takes a pack by name (fantasy) or default for the core style. Nothing is graded; the bars are in the screens guide's §5. The --json report's rootTokenContrast is gone; contrast and colorVision replace it.
breaking.fix: Read --json's contrast (sheet, scheme, text, path, ink, ground, over, disabled, halo, ratio, apca per text) and colorVision (scheme, set, vision, pairs with deltaE) where a script read rootTokenContrast.

breaking.change: Removed -og-control-size and the small/medium/large size attribute on document buttons, switches and tabs. Rust descriptor sizes are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Use standard CSS dimensions and padding on hosts and exposed parts. Shipped screen sizes use rem and pointer media queries, with (-og-input: pad) for gamepad density.

breaking.change: <input type="checkbox"> without switch draws HTML's check box, not a switch.
breaking.fix: Add switch to a checkbox that should stay a switch: <input type="checkbox" switch>.

breaking.change: Ui installs default.css and resolves parts through the document CSS cascade. DressSet, Dressing, the legacy Selector, set_dressings, theme_dressings, default_dressings, v1_dressings and style-file dress blocks are removed. Hover and press appearance uses CSS transitions; CSS keyframe animations and transitions replay with presentation state.
breaking.fix: Write lowercase markup hosts, classes and attributes before ::part(name), with standard state pseudo-classes after it. Use background, border, color, box-shadow, border-image and transition instead of dressing declarations. Select HTML controls by their authored input type, select or textarea. The -og-material property supplies glass weight and elevation; unknown -og-* properties are errors.

breaking.change: CSS var() resolves only through the cascade, without a Theme lookup fallback. Theme::length is removed. Theme palette, spacing, radius and typography mutations write root custom properties, and widgets read their resolved values. CSS font-family accepts ordered lists of quoted names, unquoted names and generic families.
breaking.fix: Declare tokens on :root and use var(--name). Supply installed font families in fallback order. Retain CSS across UI reconstruction with inherit_part_css; it preserves root overrides at every breakpoint. The TypeScript og.ui theme API keeps its existing shape.

breaking.change: Style generation emits metadata only; it no longer emits legacy appearance or dress blocks. The dressing form of -og-frame is removed; its unrelated rive(...) form remains.
breaking.fix: Author appearance in CSS. Pure-CSS pack generation follows in phase C. Existing font, icon, sound and ornament metadata generation remains available between phases.

breaking.change: Part resolution takes the placed [width, height] and returns a CSS ElementDraw or diagnostics instead of a merged legacy dressing.
breaking.fix: Supply standard CSS with Ui::set_part_css and select lowercase markup hosts with ::part(name), such as button.primary::part(base):hover or input[type=range]::part(track). Pass the part's placed size when resolving.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary image crop property; it is no longer accepted.
breaking.fix: Use object-view-box: inset(top right bottom left), with percentages v0*100, (1-u1)*100, (1-v1)*100, u0*100. The shipped minimap uses the standard property.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary list marker properties and the internal --og-list-style-* custom-property channel.
breaking.fix: Use inherited list-style-type, list-style-position and list-style-image. Only list items draw inherited markers.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary centering and anchoring declarations and their reflected attributes; no aliases remain.
breaking.fix: Center with left/top: 50% and translate: -50%, or standard flex/grid alignment. Use anchor-name, position-anchor and anchor() with translation for asymmetric self-alignment. Existing rotate and scale still compose with translation. Implicit popover anchoring is unchanged.

breaking.change: Removed implicit scene ink and separation shadow styling.
breaking.fix: Declare color and text-shadow. The shipped shooter controls use text-shadow: 0 max(1px, 0.04em) max(1px, 0.08em) #000000, with their scene ink declared as color. Font-relative shadow lengths now use the element's winning font size rather than the body default.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary skew declaration and skew-x/skew-y reflected attributes without aliases.
breaking.fix: Use transform: skew(x, y). To preserve a legacy rotation/skew/nonuniform-scale combination, move rotation and scale into the same transform list in rotate(...) skew(...) scale(...) order. Animate transform instead of -og-skew.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary texture tint property and reflected tint attribute without aliases.
breaking.fix: Use filter: url(#id) referencing an SVG feColorMatrix with type=matrix, color-interpolation-filters=linearRGB, the tint's linear-light RGB and alpha on the diagonal, and zero elsewhere. This preserves RGBA multiplication, unlike an approximate CSS filter-function chain. Without a texture, use background-color.

breaking.member: og style art, og style pack and style cooking
breaking.change: The cook no longer recolours part slices or injects their measured tones. og style art packs only corner, divider, flourish, crest and edge ornaments; it reports other requests as skipped. For version 2+ styles, og style pack no longer writes part dressing blocks. Style summaries no longer count dressings.
breaking.fix: Author part appearance in standard CSS. Ornament packing and recolouring remain available until the style.ogt pack format is replaced by CSS tooling.

breaking.change: Fit-min takes literal reflected type-step names, not a custom-property namespace shortcut. CSS spring timing is reflected with grammar and an extension reason; unresolved motion variables no longer name engine timing presets.
breaking.fix: Use -og-fit-min: caption (or another reflected step), and transition-timing-function: -og-spring(350ms, 0.3). Author variables can substitute these values normally. Spring duration must be non-negative and bounce finite. Material and sound remain reflected CSS extensions with their existing grammars and reasons.

breaking.change: Style packs are directories of CSS and assets. style.ogt, its parser and writers, atlas recolouring, and the clean pack are removed. The cook stores CSS sources and cooks external SVG images as textures.
breaking.fix: Pass a directory such as styles/my-pack to og.load.style. Direct-child CSS files load in lexical order in og-pack; nested CSS uses @import. URLs resolve beside their CSS source. Use :root variables, @font-face, images, masks, border-image, media queries, transitions and keyframes. Interaction audio uses -og-sound with event sample sets and volume/pitch ranges. CLI pack authoring and migration replacements follow in phase C. Core widget host rules and inheritance land with parts-as-nodes.

breaking.member: Progress and meter track CSS boxes
breaking.change: Progress bars, meters and HTML meters have a persistent CSS track box. Its CSS width, height, margin, padding and border now lay it out, and the fill, trail, separators and label are drawn over that box. The default frames are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Style the track through progress::part(track) and meter::part(track). The host keeps the progressbar or meter role and value; fills, trails, separators and labels are still dressed through their ::part rules.

breaking.change: og style new writes an editable CSS directory with both palettes, core-control states, finish treatments and shared interaction sounds. og style check validates that directory; the project art-contract checker moves to og style check-project. Legacy upgrade, art and pack commands are removed.
breaking.fix: Author main.css and companion assets under assets/styles/<name>, without extension.json or style.ogt. Use standard CSS images, border-image and mask-image instead of atlas conversion. Load the directory with og.load.style and select it with og.ui.configure. Use check-project for game art-contract measurements.

breaking.change: Removed behavior declarations from CSS and their old reflected attributes, without aliases.
breaking.fix: Use data-fill-origin and data-min-gap on input type=range, data-cycle on select, data-detents and data-edge on dialog, and data-hit-slop on any element. Bindings, events, pointer priority, sheet drag/snap state and checkpointing are unchanged.

breaking.change: Removed the proprietary number-input styling and reflected attributes. Number inputs use the editable field with spinner buttons, not the f32-only stepper widget.
breaking.fix: Use input type=number with min, max, step, data-wrap and data-large-step. Data-format affects only unfocused presentation. Raw text, selection, validation, readonly focus and the pad keyboard remain available.

breaking.change: Resolve lexical custom properties per mounted element with computed-value inheritance, recursive var() fallbacks, cycle diagnostics, !important, parsed selectors and CSS specificity. Text ::part styles share the cascade. Ancestor interaction predicates carry the matched document node identity.
breaking.fix: Recook documents. Use scoped --name declarations and var(--name, fallback); invalid winning values no longer revive lower-priority declarations. :has() and unsupported selector syntax fail cooking.

breaking.change: CSS image and cursor URLs name files relative to their stylesheet, never atlas icon names or numeric texture handles. Numeric URLs now name numeric files.
breaking.fix: Replace icon-name URLs with SVG files through mask-image and a background colour. Replace numeric texture-handle URLs with the texture's file path.

breaking.change: Inherited standard declarations and bound inline styles no longer use --og-* custom properties. Reserved --og-* names cannot enter the computed custom-property map or be read through var().
breaking.fix: Use standard inheritance and style:prop={expr}. Use author custom properties without the reserved --og- prefix; style:--name={expr} remains supported.

breaking.change: Parse CSS dimension, aspect-ratio, orientation and reduced-motion queries with boolean composition and nested intersections. Replace named engine breakpoints with standard conditions.
breaking.fix: Recook documents. Replace @media phone with @media (width < 600px), (height < 600px); use explicit dimension/orientation conditions for other size classes. Unsupported features fail cooking.

breaking.member: Button and choice widget CSS boxes

breaking.fix: Style the visual box with ::part(base), ::part(box), ::part(track) or the registered part name. Keep host dimensions, events and accessibility on the host. Host color and font size inherit into labels.

breaking.change: Removed -og-enter and -og-exit, including their reflected enter/exit attributes.
breaking.fix: Use @starting-style with standard transitions for entrances. Exit with opacity and display transitions using allow-discrete, keeping the element mounted until its display becomes none. Svelte in:/out:/transition: directives retain their existing lifecycle behavior.

breaking.change: The two properties that dialog::backdrop { background } and select::picker(select) { max-height } lowered to are gone, with the dialog's `backdrop` and the select's `pickerMaxHeight` document props. The pseudo-elements are now boxes of their own.
breaking.fix: Write `dialog::backdrop { background: … }` and `select::picker(select) { max-height: … }`.

breaking.change: A range's reach, track, fill, ticks, knobs, core and value bubble have persistent CSS layout and paint boxes. Their CSS width, height, padding and border now size them; the bubble's border takes part in its width. The default frames are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Style the visual box through input[type=range]::part(reach|track|fill|tick|knob|core|bubble). Input, focus and the slider role stay on the host; a knob's :active follows the press.

breaking.member: Select list and group CSS boxes
breaking.change: Select lists, suggestion lists and group headings have persistent CSS layout and paint boxes. List border widths participate in layout; the default frames remain unchanged.
breaking.fix: Style list interiors through select::part(list) and headings through select::part(group). The popup host still owns its focus scope and dismissal.

breaking.change: Select triggers and options, and tab tracks, indicators and tabs, have persistent CSS layout and paint boxes separate from their event owners.
breaking.fix: Style the visual box through its registered ::part selector. Keep events and accessibility on the host. Address the selected tab with tabs::part(tab):checked.

breaking.change: A number stepper's minus and plus buttons and its value have persistent CSS layout and paint boxes. Their CSS width, height, padding, border and state rules now lay them out and paint them; a border with no CSS padding sits inside the widget's own inset, so the default frames are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Style the boxes through stepper::part(button) and stepper::part(value). Input, focus, adjust and the spinbutton role stay on the hosts; stepper::part(frame) is still drawn by its host.

breaking.member: Text field, textarea and number spinner CSS boxes
breaking.change: input::part(frame) and textarea::part(frame) are persistent CSS layout and paint boxes over the control's padding box that draw its text; the reveal, clear and number spin buttons (input::part(reveal), input::part(clear), input[type=number]::part(button)) are boxes filling their buttons. Frame width, height and transforms now size and move the frame box, not the control. Undressed controls draw unchanged.
breaking.fix: Size and place the control through its host (input, textarea); style the frame's padding, border, background, radius and states through its ::part selector. A frame without its own padding keeps the control's inset with its border inside it. Focus, editing, presses and accessibility stay on the host.

breaking.change: Removed -og-select-filter without an alias. Native select behavior remains available; author-controlled filtering uses an input linked to a datalist.
breaking.fix: Use <input list="Maps" placeholder="Find a map" bind:value={$map}> and <datalist id="Maps"><option value="map-17" i18n="map.bay">Bay</option></datalist>. Suggestions filter values and localized labels, skip disabled options, and write the selected option value.

breaking.change: Document events include a separate rowKey field for the innermost collection row.
breaking.fix: Keep rowKey when forwarding document events; use an empty string for events outside collection rows.

breaking.change: Removed -og-emitter without an alias. Particle emission is a reflected og-emitter element behavior, not a style declaration.
breaking.fix: Move the former value to <og-emitter effect="confetti 70 burst 110 for 1.4s">. Keep position, dimensions and visibility in standard CSS. The effect attribute supports expressions; keyed insertion starts a new emitter. Presets, rates, one-shot bursts, timing, seeded replay and reduced-motion suppression are unchanged.

breaking.change: FilterUse no longer has images; an feImage's element is built as children of the filtered element whose ElementDraw::element_image numbers it.
breaking.fix: Drop images from FilterUse literals; set element_image: None on ElementDraw literals that list every field.

breaking.change: UiFilter has a space (its map to CSS px, UiFilter::CSS the identity), and its primitives' subregions, lengths, positions and lights are in that space instead of CSS px. UiFilterOp::Lighting and UiFilterOp::Convolve take kernel_unit, and UiFilterOp::Layer is new.
breaking.fix: Build a UiFilter with ..Default::default() or space: UiFilter::CSS, and add kernel_unit: None to Lighting and Convolve.

breaking.change: UiLayer has backdrop: a layer that draws nothing and filters what is under its composite.
breaking.fix: Add backdrop: false to UiLayer literals.

breaking.change: BeginLayer takes a role (LayerRole: Draw, Backdrop, Image).
breaking.fix: Add role: LayerRole::Draw to BeginLayer literals.

breaking.change: The hold-to-confirm builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<button data-hold="1200" onhold={confirm}>Delete save</button>` in a document (its fill is `button::-og-hold { background: … }`) and read the hold from og.ui.docEvents, or eject the `hold-button` component document.

breaking.change: The action bar builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write a row of `<button onclick={press}><kbd data-action={h.action}></kbd> {h.hint}</button>` over og.ui.actionBar's hints (a hold one with `data-hold` and `data-action`, so the action's hold fills it), or eject the `action-hints` component document. Place it with CSS (`position: absolute; inset-block-end: 0`): a screen's root already keeps out of the safe area.

breaking.change: The switch builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<label><input type="checkbox" switch data-on="On" data-off="Off" bind:checked={$music}> Music</label>` in a document; the caption's side is its source order in the label.

breaking.change: The number stepper builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<input type="number" min="1" max="8" data-format="{value, number} players" bind:value={$players}>` with `-og-stepper: buttons` (and `-og-stepper-wrap: wrap`, `-og-stepper-large-step: 10`) in its `<style>`.

breaking.change: The framed text field builders are removed.
breaking.fix: Write the field as markup: `<label for>` above, a row of `<icon>`, `<input class="bare" maxlength="20" bind:value={$name}>` (`appearance: none`, the row styled with `:focus-within`) and a `<span>` suffix, then `<small>{$name.length}/20</small>` for the count and a `<small role="alert">` for the error; `<input type="search">` draws the clear button; `<textarea rows>` for several lines.

breaking.change: The bare text input builders are removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<input bind:value={$name}>` or `<textarea rows="4" bind:value={$note}>` in a document (`type`, `inputmode`, `autocomplete`, `maxlength`, `placeholder`, `readonly` as in HTML).

breaking.change: The dropdown builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<select bind:value={$lang}>` with `<option>`s (under `<optgroup>`s) in a document; `-og-select-filter: on` and `data-filter-placeholder` give its open list a filter, `select::picker(select) { max-height }` bounds it.

breaking.change: The tab bar builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `<tabs items="Gear Quests" icons="sword shield" badges={$unread} bind:selected={$tab}>` in a document with the selected tab's panel under it in an `{#if}`; tabPrev and tabNext step it, and `<kbd data-action="tabPrev">` shows a bumper's glyph.

breaking.change: The accordion builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write a `<details name="faq" summary="Rules">` per section in a document; one name keeps one open at once (single), no name lets several open.

breaking.change: The badge builder is removed: the tab bar and accordion were the last components that built one.
breaking.fix: Write `<badge tone="primary">3</badge>` in a document.

breaking.change: The screen helpers no longer export the removed builders.
breaking.fix: Build those controls in the kit's screen document: `<input>`, `<select>`, `<button data-hold>`.

breaking.change: name on a <details> is its exclusive accordion group, no longer its accessible name.
breaking.fix: Name a disclosure for a screen reader with aria-label; keep name for the group.

breaking.change: The ambient particle emitter builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `-og-emitter: sparkles` (or confetti, embers, snow, bubbles, dust, sparks, fireworks) on the element in a document's `<style>`; a rate, `burst <n>`, `for <time>`, `life <time>`, a speed (`120px/s`), a shape, a size and colours override the preset. `none` stops it.

breaking.change: The per-element particle builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `-og-emitter` in a document: `-og-emitter: 40 burst 30 for 1.6s life 1.2s 80px/s 220px/s diamond 6px #ffd166` throws a burst when the element first stands, emits for 1.6 s, each particle living 1.2 s.

breaking.change: The rays-and-sparks builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write `-og-burst: <count> [<radius>px] [<colour>] [<time>]` in a `@keyframes` step of the element's animation (`@keyframes land { 60% { -og-burst: 24 48px #ffd166 600ms; } }`); a delay is the animation's `animation-delay`.

breaking.change: The celebration builder is removed.

breaking.change: The zoomable picture builder is removed.

breaking.change: The framed turntable viewport builder is removed.

breaking.change: The modal builder is removed.
breaking.fix: Write a `<dialog>` in a document (shown modal with its `open` bound to a store), or a screen document with data-layer="modal" pushed with og.ui.push; Back and a press outside close it.

breaking.member: og.ui.props, og.ui.setDraw, og.ui.semantics, og.ui.ElementProps, og.ui.DrawDesc, og.ui.SemanticsDesc, og.ui.Fill, og.ui.Stroke, og.ui.Effect and the element model's other types
breaking.change: Setting an element's props, draw and accessibility by call is removed, with the types only they used (Edges, GridSpec, Track, StateGroup, DragSpec, GestureSpec, TextEffectsDesc, DrawShape, UiTransform and the rest).

breaking.change: The UI's numeric memory for immediate builders is removed.
