breaking.change: The kit helper entries for TypeScript components are removed with the components.
breaking.fix: Write a kit's components as documents and register code-side helpers with @origingame/engine/ui-extensions.

breaking.change: Backdrop sampling is off by default, including glass panels, tooltips, HUD frames and standalone backdrop-filter chains; floating surfaces keep readable near-opaque fills.
breaking.fix: Opt in once with the style root --glass-backdrop: auto or UiDesc.glassBackdrop. Explicit none overrides the style and null inherits it. Use @media (-og-glass-backdrop: auto) for thinner on-state fills. Reduced transparency always disables sampling.

breaking.change: The health bar is no longer a <meter>: it is a BossBar.health track holding BossBar.fill parts and BossBar.notch gates, with role meter and the same name and values. The BossBar.heading part is gone (the name is BossBar.headline).
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the meter's parts dresses BossBar.health and BossBar.fill; one that dressed BossBar.heading dresses BossBar.headline.

breaking.change: The ProgressBar.well part is gone: the track is the bar's well.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed ProgressBar.well dresses ProgressBar.track.

breaking.change: The StatBar.well part is gone: the track is the bar's well.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed StatBar.well dresses StatBar.track.

breaking.member: UI icon markup and color styling
breaking.change: Removed <icon>, -og-cue and -og-secondary-tint without aliases. The reflected <og-icon> tag preserves the internal icon kind and exposes separate image and secondary parts.
breaking.fix: Write <og-icon cue="danger"> for a semantic cue, or set its icon attribute explicitly. Use og-icon::part(image) and og-icon::part(secondary) with standard color declarations for independent layer colors. Rename inline icon tags to og-icon too.

breaking.change: A text's inline markup is elements: `<span>`, `<a href>`, `<b>`, `<i>`, `<ruby>`, `<rt>` and the other formatting tags inside a text are `inline` elements that class, id, attribute, structural, child and state selectors (`a:hover`) match, and every inherited text property, `vertical-align` and `display` styles their words. A document or pack rule such as `span { … }` or `.gold { … }` now reaches them, and HTML's formatting comes from the UA sheet, which rules override.
breaking.fix: Check rules whose selectors name span, a, b, i or a class that inline markup now carries; a box property (padding, background, width) on an inline element is ignored until its fragments are boxes.

breaking.change: `padding`, `border` and `margin` on a `<span>`, `<a>` or another inline element of a text were ignored; they now move the words after them and can change where its lines break.
breaking.fix: Drop inline padding or margin you did not mean to apply, or move it to a block around the text.

breaking.change: Forced Touch and Mouse density now override pointer/hover media features. Auto continues to report the device. Gamepad mode is exposed by the reflected (-og-input: pad) media feature.
breaking.fix: Use standard pointer: coarse and hover: none queries for touch, pointer: fine and hover: hover for mouse, and (-og-input: pad) for gamepad styles. Express control dimensions in rem/em. No density environment variables are provided; Rust control descriptors are unchanged.

breaking.change: A document's rule no longer reaches a component instance. A rule whose subject names one (#Mine, .loud, Badge, [data-tone] on <Badge id="Mine" class="loud"/>) is refused when the document is parsed; a rule that only sweeps over one (*, #Root > *) passes it by.
breaking.fix: Pass a prop, set a custom property on the instance (<Badge --width="66px"/>), or dress a part the component declares from the style pack ([part="Badge.frame"]).

breaking.change: Genre kits are removed: extension.json's kind "kit" and its entry, types and components fields are refused, og ui add no longer installs a kit into assets/ui-kits/, nothing discovers assets/ui-kits/, og ui eject no longer takes <kit>/<document>, and documents under assets/ui-kits/ no longer land in a cascade layer of their own. The rpg and shooter documents are built-in components.
breaking.fix: Use a component by the name its document declares (<RpgBackpack/>, <Killfeed/>); the screen that uses it loads it. Delete assets/ui-kits/ and the og.load.document calls naming it, or keep a document you edited as the game's own (it then replaces the built-in one of its name); og ui eject <group>/<document> (rpg/backpack) copies one to edit.

breaking.change: registerUiExtension, uiExtensionNames and the @origingame/engine/ui-extensions and @origingame/engine/extensions/* exports are removed, with the tsconfig paths og check and the project skeleton wrote for them.
breaking.fix: Delete the import; a component is a document used by name, and TypeScript helpers live in the game's own modules.

breaking.change: The materials pack is a resource pack of its own kind (extension.json kind "materials"): og ui add materials installs it into assets/materials/materials/, so its presets' ids are materials/materials/<preset>.ogt instead of ui-kits/materials/<preset>.ogt.
breaking.fix: Run og ui add materials again and write -og-material: "materials/materials/foil.ogt" (holo, burn, rarity) where a style named "ui-kits/materials/…"; delete assets/ui-kits/materials/.

breaking.change: Default separators and compact units now follow the active locale and CLDR precision, instead of hard-coded English grouping and three significant digits. Calendars use CLDR headings and weekday labels by default.
breaking.fix: Set decimals for fixed precision, group/point for explicit custom separators, or monthNames/weekdayNames/weekdayShort for game-authored calendar names. Omit these overrides to follow locale switches.

breaking.change: Mass elements use the shared Ease type instead of MassEase.
breaking.fix: Use none, power1.out, power1.in, back.out and steps(1,end) in place of linear, out, in, back and step. Other shared curves are now supported.

breaking.change: Returns Result<number> and reports invalid timing text instead of silently substituting linear.
breaking.fix: Check ok before using value, or use massTemplate for managed templates.

breaking.change: Removed -og-meta. A full-screen vignette, tint or material overlay is now its own element, <og-overlay effect="…">, with the same grammar; its strength is still the element's opacity.
breaking.fix: Replace an element styled with -og-meta: <value> by <og-overlay id="…" effect="<value>"></og-overlay> and keep its opacity (and any opacity animation) in CSS. A material parameter that came from var() comes from a bound attribute instead: effect={$fx}, the store holding the whole value.

breaking.change: Removed -og-overlaps. og.ui.overlaps and og ui check's overlap finding now list every overlap between elements except those the engine places on purpose (a badge on its item); a document can no longer hide one.
breaking.fix: Delete -og-overlaps declarations. Move an overlap that is a defect; keep one the design means and treat its finding as a measurement, not a failure.

breaking.change: A screen pushed without a prop now holds that prop's default (its <meta name="prop:…"> data-default, or its type's zero value), so og.ui.screenVm answers every prop where it answered null for one the push left out, and ScreenValues<S>'s fields are all present. A {#each} over a list prop left out iterates no rows instead of failing.
breaking.fix: Code that tested a screen value for null to learn the push left it out: give the prop a data-default the game never passes (such as -1 or "") and test for that, or pass the value explicitly. A prop every user must pass gets data-required, and a mount or push leaving it out is then refused with an error naming the instance and the prop.

breaking.change: A screen is on the stack once: pushing a screen that is already on the stack is refused with an error, where it stacked a second copy.
breaking.fix: Pop the screen before pushing it again, or use og.ui.replace.

breaking.change: A list a pushed screen iterates with {#each} has rows that each carry the key the each names ((row.id): a unique nonempty string id). A screen iterating any other list reports "each over '$rows' needs a keyed list; give each of its rows a unique string id" and is not drawn. A list the screen only reads whole is unaffected.
breaking.fix: Give each row of an iterated list a unique string in the field the each keys it by.

breaking.change: A pushed screen whose component instance leaves out a prop the component declares data-required is refused with "<file>:<line>: <Component> leaves out its prop '<name>', which it requires (data-required); pass it", as a mounted document already is; the push used to build it with the prop unset. A prop without data-required reads its default (ui-props-have-defaults).
breaking.fix: Pass the props your own components mark data-required. The built-in components require none.

breaking.change: A document whose root is a block ({#if}, {#each}) is refused with "a document's root is one element; put the block inside it".
breaking.fix: Wrap the block in one root element.

breaking.member: og.ui.anchor, og.ui.openAnchor, og.ui.label, og.ui.close, og.ui.AnchorDesc, og.ui.LabelDesc, og.ui.Response, og.ui.UiBuild, og.ui.Size, og.ui.Direction, og.ui.Align, og.ui.Cross, og.ui.FontRole, og.ui.StylePart
breaking.change: The last immediate-mode UI builders and the types only they used are removed: a HUD group is a document now that its CSS insets clear the host's controls.
breaking.fix: Write the HUD as a component document mounted with og.ui.scope(world, id).mount(...) and its values in stores. Place each corner with `position: fixed` and insets read from env(): `left: calc(env(-og-hud-inset-left) + 24px); top: calc(env(-og-hud-inset-top) + 24px)` (right and bottom alike), which keep it clear of Back and inside the HUD band on an ultrawide; a label is a `<span>` styled with `font: var(--text-display-sm)`, `font-family: var(--font-mono)` and `color: var(--ink-muted)`, the group's look `background: var(--panel); border-radius: var(--radius-panel); -og-frame: card`.

breaking.change: An absolutely or fixed positioned box sizes and places as CSS 2.1 §10.3.7 and §10.6.4 say. With an auto width and one inset or none it shrinks to fit its content, at most the room its inset and margins leave, instead of filling its containing block. Between two insets a definite size or a max-width now holds, and auto margins centre it. Its margins now hold it off the insets it is placed by.
breaking.fix: A positioned box that should span its containing block takes both insets (`left: 0; right: 0`, `inset: 0`) or `width: stretch`. Drop `width: max-content` workarounds on HUD corners: an auto width now fits its content.

breaking.change: The readouts that were named as `cell` parts, and so wore the default style's tile (fill, rim, shadow), are named for what they show and wear no role dressing: ArenaLobby.cell → ArenaLobby.state, ArenaScoreboard.cell → ArenaScoreboard.stat, IdlePrestige.cell → IdlePrestige.readout, RacingLapHud.cell → RacingLapHud.readout, RacingResults.cell → RacingResults.place, RacingStandings.cell → RacingStandings.place, RhythmDifficulty.cell → RhythmDifficulty.rating, RhythmResults.cell → RhythmResults.readout, RhythmScoreHud.cell → RhythmScoreHud.readout, RhythmSongSelect.cell → RhythmSongSelect.fact, StrategyWave.cell → StrategyWave.readout, table.cell → table.entry. A `cell` is now only a tile the player picks (an item, a card, an ability, a slot).
breaking.fix: Rename the selectors in your style pack or game CSS (`[part="RacingLapHud.cell"]` → `[part="RacingLapHud.readout"]`, `::part(RacingLapHud\.cell)` → `::part(RacingLapHud\.readout)`), and drop any rule that only undid the tile on them. To keep a readout's tile look, give its new part the `--cell-*` fill, rim and shadow yourself.

breaking.change: Removed the 15 old genre kits and their documents, sheets, fixtures, and pack-only tests. The nine replacement kits are not yet built. The materials extension and VFX packs remain available.
breaking.fix: Compose with core UI controls and game-owned documents until the replacement kits are available. See docs/ui.md for the authoring and acceptance contract.

breaking.member: creation ui and bundled style packs
breaking.change: Removed the 14 old style packs. Creation ui accepts only default; all 37 look presets select the asset-free core default. Shared and CJK assets remain available for game-owned styles.
breaking.fix: Use ui default for creation, or author a game-owned style with og style new and select its asset path in the look. Do not select a removed built-in pack.

breaking.change: Removed the codemod that rewrote game code to the deleted genre kits. Its dispatcher reports manual review rather than writing imports to missing kits.
breaking.fix: Compose the required UI from core controls; there is no automatic rewrite to the replacement kits.

breaking.change: Removed -og-reduced-motion (fade, none, keep). An element's transitions under the player's reduced motion now follow standard CSS: a transition written under @media (prefers-reduced-motion) plays as written; any other keeps the engine's fallback (movement jumps, opacity and colour fade quickly).
breaking.fix: For none, write @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .x { transition: none; } }. For keep, repeat the element's transition inside that block. Drop fade: it is the fallback for every transition not written for reduced motion.

breaking.member: url() cross-origin() and referrer-policy(); <iframe> crossorigin and referrerpolicy
breaking.change: A remote url() takes only integrity(). cross-origin() and referrer-policy() are refused, as are a remote <iframe>'s crossorigin and referrerpolicy attributes: the engine fetches without cookies, credentials or a referrer of its own on both hosts, so they protected nothing. A document or style pack that names one fails to load and says why. Natively the engine no longer emulates the browser's CORS check; in a browser the engine Worker still reads another origin's image only when the server allows the game's origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin).
breaking.fix: Delete cross-origin(…) and referrer-policy(…) from url() values, and crossorigin and referrerpolicy from remote <iframe>s. Keep integrity("sha384-…") where it is.

breaking.change: UI stores, collections, document state, interaction state and motion clocks are presentation checkpoints, no longer hashed ECS state blocks. Simulation hashes therefore change even for games whose UI has not changed. Saves require og-save:3 with a separate UI checkpoint; earlier formats are refused, never converted. GameDesc.ui registers named presentation state after start and on hot reload, never per tick; gameplay writes during registration are refused. UI feedback plays outside the ECS and snapshot. Pause layers emit og.PauseIntent through the general reflected intent path, applied at the next tick boundary.
breaking.fix: Regenerate simulation hash baselines for the new engine version. Keep gameplay initialization in start and named scope store registration in ui. Declare gameplay actions with defineEvent and deliver them through input.intent. Record with input.takeIntents and replay with input.replayIntent; mismatched layout hashes are refused. Document mounts, models, actions and snippets require the separate Svelte document API head.

breaking.change: Removed -og-frame: rive(...) without an alias. Rive loading and playback are semantics of the reflected og-rive element, not CSS decoration.
breaking.fix: Write <og-rive src="ui/chest.riv#Chest"> and use standard CSS for its dimensions and visibility. Source IDs remain relative to assets/. Playback, hot reload, picking, dependency loading and checkpoint replay are unchanged; probe edits replace the src attribute.

breaking.change: The built-in components' parts named for what they show now also name their role, as a part list (`part="ArenaRoster.portrait ArenaRoster.picture"`), so they wear the role rules and tokens: ranks, states, tiers, places and the like are labels; scores, prices, counts, times and stats are figures; portraits, avatars, jackets and art are pictures; skill, item, tile and choice buttons are cells; team, round, banner, grid and board panels are plates; tracks, magazines, meters and trails are wells. A selector written `[part="ArenaRoster.portrait"]` no longer matches those parts, and their default look follows their role.
breaking.fix: Reach a part with `::part(ArenaRoster\.portrait)` or `[part~="ArenaRoster.portrait"]`; restyle it through its role's tokens (docs/ui.md §3.2).

breaking.change: Every built-in rpg component names its frame, bands, titles, tabs, cells and rows as parts (RpgBackpack.frame, RpgBackpack.cell, RpgQuestLog.row…), listed in its <meta name="parts">, and the classes those elements carried (.rpg-backpack, .rpg-band, .rpg-title, .cell, .tab, .quest…) are gone; data-* state attributes are kept.
breaking.fix: Dress them through their parts, RpgBackpack::cell[data-rarity=epic] in place of .rpg-backpack .cell[data-rarity=epic]; a game that needs the old classes ejects the component (og ui eject rpg/backpack) and keeps them in its copy.

breaking.change: UiDesc.primaryColor is gone. The default style's whole palette is derived from seed colours (packages/design/tokens/seed.css): grounds, surfaces, lines and inks from `neutral`; the primary fill and its hover, pressed and soft tones and the ink on it from `primary`; the highlight ink, the accent role and the focus ring from `accent`; the status colours from `danger`, `warn`, `success` and `info`; the eight team colours from `team`. Each scheme keeps text at 4.5:1 and focus rings, rims and team marks at 3:1 whatever the seeds. The primary's tones are no longer mixed in Rust: they follow the seed through the stylesheet, so a style pack's `--primary-hover` or `--on-primary` stays the pack's.
breaking.fix: Give the colour as UiDesc.seeds.primary: og.ui.configure(world, { seeds: { primary: color.fromHex(0xc8102e) } }). Add `accent` for a second accent and `neutral` to tint the grounds.

breaking.change: Selectors are parsed and matched by Servo's `selectors` crate, as Firefox's are. An unquoted number as an attribute value is refused (`[level=3]`). Inside `:is()`, `:where()` and `:not()` an argument that does not parse is an error, not a dropped alternative. A document's rules see its own tree, as a page's styles see its light tree. Content passed into a component has its nearest ancestor in the document as its parent, not the component's element that holds it. A component's own elements stay out of the document's rules.
breaking.fix: Quote numeric attribute values (`[level="3"]`), and correct a selector the error names.

breaking.change: Removed count attributes on ordinary text and the -og-count-duration, -og-count-decimals, -og-reveal and -og-spotlight CSS properties. These semantics use reflected og- tags without legacy aliases.
breaking.fix: Use <og-counter value={$score} duration="900" decimals="0">, <og-typewriter rate="20" onrevealed={done}>, and <og-spotlight target="Target" bind:open={$tour}>. Typewriter rate counts extended grapheme clusters, preserving combining marks and joined emoji. Tick timing, checkpoints and completion events remain supported.

breaking.change: Tween state blocks use version 2 to preserve parameterized easing payloads.
breaking.fix: Start a new recording or snapshot; version 1 tween state blocks cannot be restored.

breaking.change: A document's generated declaration no longer exports a `<Name>Slot` type or a `slots` member in its UiScreens or UiComponents entry, and og.ui.document's answer no longer has a `slots` list. Documents refuse `<slot>` (content is passed with `{#snippet}` and placed with `{@render}`), so the type was always `never` and the list always empty.
breaking.fix: Remove references to `<Name>Slot`, `UiScreens[name]["slots"]`, `UiComponents[name]["slots"]` and the `slots` field of og.ui.document's answer; nothing replaces them.

breaking.change: `stretch` is now CSS Sizing 4's stretch-fit size (CSS Sizing 4 §3.1): the containing block's size less the box's margins, as browsers lay it out. It used to be the house meaning, the room the parent leaves. That made it a flex share along a flex line (`flex: 1`), and in a block it turned the block into a column whose `stretch` children shared what their siblings left. Now a `stretch` along a flex line is the container's whole inner size and neither grows nor shrinks. A `stretch` in a block is the block's height, overflowing below its siblings. Across a flex line it fills the line, as `align-self: stretch` does. A zero minimum (`min-width: 0`) is now a bound of its own, so it lifts a flex item's content floor as in CSS. The built-in components, screens, sheets and inspector say what they meant (`flex: 1` with `min-width: 0` or `min-height: 0` where siblings share a line, `display: flex; flex-direction: column` where a block shared its height), and their layout is unchanged. A bound `Size` given as a string reads `stretch`, no longer `grow`.
breaking.fix: Where siblings shared a row or column through `width: stretch` or `height: stretch`, write `flex: 1; min-width: 0` (or `min-height: 0`) instead. Where a block's child took the height its siblings left, make the block `display: flex; flex-direction: column` and give the child `flex: 1; min-height: 0`. Keep `stretch` where a box should fill its containing block or its flex line.

breaking.change: Replace the OGT screen/component dialect with scriptless .svelte documents: HTML core tags, metadata contracts, scoped CSS, keyed each blocks, named-store expressions, explicit two-way models, actions, snippets, translations, and typed text spans with ::part rules. The old reader and migrator are removed. Cooked documents carry a new version and track string-table dependencies.
breaking.fix: Author screens and components in .svelte using the screens and components guides, then recook. Core screens and CLI discovery/eject use the new format; eject also copies base messages.

breaking.change: A <tabs> element's parts are Tabs.track, Tabs.indicator (the mark that slides to the selected tab) and Tabs.tab[selected], the names the core default and og style new already dress; they were Segmented.track, Segmented.thumb and Segmented.item since og.ui.tabBar went, so every Tabs.tab dressing was ignored.
breaking.fix: Rename a style's Segmented.track, Segmented.thumb and Segmented.item[selected] selectors to Tabs::track, Tabs::indicator and Tabs::tab:selected.

breaking.change: A toast draws nothing itself. The engine used to stack its own toast plates at UiDesc.toastAnchor; the toasts up are now the UI's $toasts store, shown by the built-in notifications screen. UiDesc.toastAnchor is removed, and so is the style pack's toast::part(indicator).
breaking.fix: Load and push the notifications screen once: og.load.document(world, "@ui/screens/notifications.svelte"), then og.ui.push(world, "notifications", { items: [] }). To place or dress toasts, style [part="notifications.frame"] in the style pack or iterate $toasts in a document of your own. og.ui.toast and og.ui.dismissToast keep their signatures.

breaking.change: The built-in tutorial screen takes input as all, not menu: the documents under it stay live and gameplay sees input while it shows. Under menu the HUD was inert, so a waiting step could not be done and a lit element could not be pressed.
breaking.fix: Where a step must be read before play goes on, hold gameplay input in the game until the screen reports next or skip.

breaking.change: A style pack is refused when it names a part of `chip`, `skeleton`, `spinner`, `cooldown`, `minimap`, `dialogue` or `actionbutton`, or `meter::part(trail)`, `meter::part(separator)` or `meter::part(label)`. No document element drew these parts, so the rules never dressed anything.
breaking.fix: Delete those rules. The components that replaced them are dressed through their own named parts: `[part="Cooldown.cell"]`, `[part="Minimap.frame"]`, `[part="SkeletonGroup.line"]`, `[part="Spinner.ring"]`, `[part="ActionButton.disc"]`, `[part="SpeechBubble.frame"]`.

breaking.change: A reflection probe's box and fade are the og.Volume on its entity, as every region's: `size` and `blendDistance` are removed. The fade lies past the box's faces, not inside them, so surfaces on the faces take the probe whole. The box follows the entity's scale and, turned, is the box around it. A probe without an og.Volume reaches everywhere and reflects as at infinity.
breaking.fix: Add `og.Volume` to the probe's entity: `world.add(e, og.Volume, { size: <the old size, 10 10 10 when it was omitted>, fade: <the old blendDistance, 1 when it was omitted> })`, or in a scene a `Volume { size …  fade … }` row on the entity, and drop the two fields from og.ReflectionProbe. Bake again (`og bake probes`).

breaking.change: A light volume's box is the og.Volume on its entity, as every region's: `size` is removed. Baked and realtime volumes now share one edge: whole up to the box's faces, fading out over og.Volume.fade past them (a baked one faded in over its outer spacing, a realtime one out over one spacing). The box follows the entity's scale and, turned, is the box around it. A light volume without an og.Volume has no box: nothing is baked or relit.
breaking.fix: Add `og.Volume` to the volume's entity: `world.add(e, og.Volume, { size: <the old size, 4 4 4 when it was omitted>, fade: <the spacing> })`, or in a scene a `Volume { size …  fade … }` row on the entity, and drop `size` from og.LightVolume. Bake again (`og bake lightmaps`).

breaking.change: og.ReverbZone has no `size`, `radius` or `fade`: the og.Volume on its entity shapes it. A zone without an og.Volume has no bounds and is heard everywhere; before, a bare zone was a 10 x 4 x 10 m box with a 2 m fade. A snapshot or save holding an og.ReverbZone does not restore across the version.
breaking.fix: Add og.Volume beside each og.ReverbZone with the zone's old size, radius and fade: `world.insert(e, og.Volume, { size: { x: 10, y: 4, z: 10 }, fade: 2 })` keeps the old default.

breaking.change: og.StreamCell has no `size`: the og.Volume on its entity is its box (or sphere), and the entity's scale now applies to it. A cell without an og.Volume is a point at the entity's position, as a zero size was. A snapshot or save holding an og.StreamCell does not restore across the version.
breaking.fix: Move `size` from the entity's StreamCell block to a Volume block beside it (`Volume { size 20 10 20 }` in scene text, or `world.insert(e, og.Volume, { size })`).

breaking.change: Replace the bounded Yarn profile with released Yarn Spinner 3.2.2, including typed expressions, smart variables, enums, once content, dynamic transfers, node groups, saliency strategies, pure registered functions and localized markup. Dialogue text now retains the Speaker: prefix and carries typed scalar-offset spans. Cooked dialogue schema is 3 and story saves checkpoint offered and selected option values.
breaking.fix: Declare #og-profile:yarn-spinner-3.2.2 and re-cook all .yarn assets. Keep explicit #line: ids and stable node/subtitle/continuation identities. Consume text and spans together without parsing markup or adding a second speaker prefix. Register pure typed functions in project.ogt before cooking. Quests remain engine data.

breaking.change: Dialogue authoring now uses the declared yarn-3.0-og-1 Yarn syntax profile. type dialogue .ogt and its cooked schema are removed; story saves now use stable continuation ids and checkpoint detour stacks.
breaking.fix: Convert dialogue assets to .yarn, declare #og-profile:yarn-3.0-og-1 and #og-name, put base text on lines and options with explicit #line: ids, update load paths and re-cook. Keep node, line, option and pending detour identities for new saves. Old dialogue-format saves are not migrated. Quests and DialogueView/QuestView retain their contracts.

added.summary: A `type vfx` effect may play a pixel effect (`type vfx2d`) or any flipbook sheet with `flipbook "<id>"`: a camera-facing og.Sprite with og.Flipbook from its `at`, sized by `size` and the frame's shape, tinted by `color` and the effect's tint, for `life` or its clip's length; the sheet's og.FlipbookEvent events (the impact frame among them) reach the game as the effect's og.VfxEvent of the same name.

The IDL takes an `aliases "..."` line on functions, records, structs, enums, unions and interfaces: synonyms and other engines' names (Unity, Godot, Unreal, three.js). The wiki prints it as `Also known as:` and `og api find` scores it as a fifth BM25F field; field lengths now average over the entries that have the field. 94 entries carry aliases, and a few one-line docs gained their purpose (defineSystem, og.SensorEntered). On the 160-query evaluation set recall@1 goes from 53 to 62 and recall@5 from 100 to 132; on a 40-query held-out set written before any alias and never tuned against (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-heldout.tsv) recall stays at 9 to 10 @1 and 21 @5: aliases fix the entries they name, not others.

`og api find` fuses BM25F with static word embeddings by reciprocal rank (k 20, embedding weight 0.7), so a query worded by purpose finds entries none of its words names. The model is minishlab/potion-base-8M (model2vec, MIT, third_party/potion-base-8M) cut to 128 dimensions and int8 (crates/og-api/search/words.bin, 4.1 MB, compiled into og); each entry's vector is built at `og api gen` and shipped in wiki/search.tsv. CPU only, no service. On the evaluation set, grown to 160 queries (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-queries.tsv), recall@1 rises from 46 to 53 and recall@5 from 90 to 100 over BM25F alone. The line output is unchanged; `--json` adds each entry's `bm25` and `cosine` beside the fused `score`.

Identical cooked outputs share the filename of the lexicographically smallest asset id. Bundle source lookup uses a map, and web preloading fetches shared files once. Cook stamps changed: the first cook after upgrading rebuilds everything. Content hashes no longer include the source pathname; actions that resolve relative references or embed asset names retain their path dependency. The same inputs and cooker still produce byte-identical cooked files. The blob format and FNV stamp algorithm are unchanged.

added.member: probe pickUi (wire pick_ui), PickResult.source and PickResult.ui
added.summary: pickUi(x, y) answers the UI element under a point: the topmost that shows something or takes input (a layout container that draws nothing lets the point through), with its id, path, kind, text, rect, layer, the document line that built it (source), the style part it is drawn as and the style rules that dress it, each with its file and line in the order they apply (rules; rule the most specific). pick keeps its scene answer; its source now names the scene line that declares the entity (scenes/main.ogt:12), and outside a publish build it carries the UI element over the point as ui. dump_ui's elements carry part and rules too.

`og assets` queries the unshipped cooked/.assets.ogt metadata and reference graph by text, --kind, --group and --unused. --refs lists dependencies, --by lists referrers, --dupes finds identical outputs and --dupes --near N compares texture dHashes and sound loudness-envelope hashes at the caller's Hamming threshold. --json returns structured results. Game TypeScript is parsed with OXC; computed og.load paths retain their static prefix, or everything without a prefix, and are reported. `og api find` discovers the assets guide.

og assets mv <from> <to> moves a source and its import settings, rewriting matching static asset-id literals in OGT documents and game TypeScript. Computed loads are reported, not rewritten. Destinations must be absent; parsing and path checks precede staged writes with rollback backups. Source-relative dependencies inside models and maps still need review when moving across directories. Run og cook afterward to refresh outputs.

Native cooks share BLAKE3 action keys and authenticated contents under ~/.cache/origingame/cook-v1/{ac,cas}, including texture and content-keyed prefracture results. A per-project .og/cook-index records file stats and content hashes and skips source reads on unchanged cooks. The store defaults to a 10 GiB cap, configurable with OG_COOK_CACHE_MAX_BYTES; og cache gc [--max-bytes N] [--json] trims it on demand. Cache eviction never deletes source assets or cooked outputs. FNV world/schema hashes and in-blob stamps, streaming packs and service-worker SHA256 remain unchanged.

Publish exports omit unreachable cooked outputs and list omitted ids, removed files and computed-load retention in og-build.json's pruning field. Project asset references, placed scenes, TS literals and publish { keep "path/**" } patterns are roots. Computed loads retain their static prefix or all assets; escaped loaders and runtime-keyed baked probes are kept conservatively. Needed streaming packs keep every member without changing pack bytes. Shared files survive while any retained id names them. Source assets and development cooked files are never deleted by export pruning.

Effect materials: one parameter set for particles (billboards, velocity-stretched and mesh), trails, ribbons and beams, as an `.ogt` of `type effect` an emitter names with `effect "<id>"`. A main texture through a channel and an optional gradient ramp, a mask, noise erosion over life with a soft border and a glowing edge, a flow map, a fresnel rim or soft silhouette and a soft depth fade; each texture with its own tile, offset, scroll, turn and polar coordinates. Intensity, alpha, the uv offset, the erosion and eight custom numbers are constants, random ranges per particle or curves over its life. A material shader in hooks mode runs its surface_color and surface_emissive last, reading effect_life(), effect_random(), effect_custom1() and effect_custom2(). Visual only: evaluated from the particle's life and random value and the tick's clock, nothing read back. Trails, ribbons and beams drawn with one are soft across their width unless the material has a mask (then their cross-section), and a beam fades in over its width at each end. Emitters without one draw as before.

added.member: og.load.vfx, og.vfx.spawn, og.vfx.info, og.Vfx, og.VfxEvent, type vfx
added.summary: Composed effects: an `.ogt` of `type vfx` is one effect as a timeline of emitter, mesh, trail, beam, light, decal, flash, shake and sound elements, each with `at`, `offset`, `rotate` and `life` or `until`, with `duration`, `loop`, `event <s> "<name>"` and `impact <s>` lines shared with `type vfx2d`. og.vfx.spawn plays one in a call, at a position or following a parent, with a scale, a tint and a seed; og.Vfx is the component it adds. The engine's og.vfx system sends og.VfxEvent on the tick each event lands (the impact is named `impact`), adds shakes, plays sounds and despawns ended effects; the visuals are expanded by the renderer from (asset, seed, startTick, tick) alone, so replays and restores draw the same. `og cook` refuses a vfx that names an asset not in the project.

Pixel-art 2D effects: an `.ogt` of `type vfx2d` is a Pixel VFX Forge recipe (Scenario's JSON, its 22 layer types keyed by their own `type`, unchanged), inline or named with `recipe "<file>.json"`, with the `duration`, `loop`, `event <s> "<name>"` and `impact <s>` lines of `type vfx`. The cook renders it with the Forge's renderer ported to Rust (the Forge's frames byte for byte, the same on every host) into an ordinary flipbook sheet: its texture `<id>#sheet` (pixel art), one clip named after the file with the recipe's fps and loop, and an og.FlipbookEvent `impact` on the impact frame (the `impact` line, the recipe's, or the frame with the largest jump in coverage). An effect pack (`kind vfx`) may ship them: `og vfx add` installs the recipe files with their `.ogt` files. `og api show pixel-vfx` has the format and the 22 layer types.

added.member: og vfx add, extension kind vfx
added.summary: An effect pack is an extension of `kind vfx` (no code): `og vfx add <name|directory> [project]` installs an editable copy into assets/vfx/<name>/, where its effects name their emitters and materials as `vfx/<name>/<file>`; `og ui list` names installed and bundled packs.

added.member: og vfx add: minEngine, tags, keywords, preview/
added.summary: A vfx pack's extension.json may carry `minEngine` (x.y.z), `tags` ({style: stylised|realistic|pixel, dim: 2d|3d, category: [...], element: [...]}) and lowercase `keywords`, the asset library's catalog fields. `og vfx add` refuses a pack whose minEngine is newer than the engine (`--any-engine` installs it anyway) and leaves the pack's `preview/` (review sheets, clips, cost files) out of the game.

added.member: dump_render draws, transparent, transparentDraws, spriteDraws, particles, strips, stripSegments
added.summary: The render dump reports what the last frame submitted besides its triangles: draw calls across every pass (`draws`), blended instances and their draws, sprite draws, the particle systems with their slots and the live particles of CPU-simulated ones (`particles`: systems, capacity, cpu), and trail strips and segments. Effect previews and cost sheets read them.

added.member: og.load.emitter speedOverLife, spinOverLife, rateOverTime, attractor, field, shape spline, inheritVelocity
added.summary: Emitter expressiveness: curves over life for the speed (`speedOverLife`, against the velocity) and the angular velocity (`spinOverLife`, the rotation its integral), a curve over each cycle for the rate (`rateOverTime`); up to four attractors (`attractor <x> <y> <z> <strength> [<radius>]`, negative pushes); a vector field, curl noise (`field curl`) or a grid the cook bakes from a texture (`field "<texture>" <strength> <size>`); emission along a Catmull-Rom spline (`shape spline ... [closed]`); and a share of the emitter's own velocity (`inheritVelocity`). Compute and the CPU path agree on all of them. Emitters without them simulate as before.

`og api find` ranks with BM25F over each entry's name, summary, member names and body (camelCase, snake_case and dotted names split, plurals and -ing/-ed stemmed, a word one or two edits off still matching), from an index `og api gen` ships beside the wiki (wiki/search.tsv); a query takes milliseconds with no service. On the 96-query evaluation set (crates/og-cli/tests/fixtures/api-find-queries.tsv: queries by purpose, partial name and typo) recall@1 rises from 18 to 30 and recall@5 from 38 to 56. `--json` prints the entries with their scores; the line output and `og api show` are unchanged, and `og api show <module>` lists the module's members after its overview. The wiki is split: a module page keeps its overview, values, constants and a contents table (signature and one sentence per item), and every function, record, interface and type has its own page under wiki/<module>/ (ui.md 1.1 MB to 116 KB, render.md 0.6 MB to 54 KB).

Guides beside the IDL (crates/og-api/guides: start, testing, determinism, looks, models, art-review, screens, animation, three-to-og) are generated into the wiki as guide-<name>.md: `og api show <guide>` prints one, `og api find` returns their numbered sections (`testing §2`) beside the API entries, and `--kind guide` selects them. They hold the workflow, thresholds and pitfalls no signature states.

A jump goal whose arc the simulation owns: after `prepare` it takes off in the tick through an og.CharacterController's jump (jumpSpeed set for `height` under the controller's gravity, so ceilings and ledges are the controller's) or, without one, a fixed ballistic arc back to the takeoff height; the goal ends `recover` seconds after the landing tick, and the jump's state is in snapshots and the hash, with the landing each tick predicts from the controller's arc and the ground along it (og.motion state MOTION4; MOTION3 and MOTION2 saves still load). The motion model only draws it, its generated clip retimed onto that flight (docs/design.md §2.7, Jumps).

Check-bearing commands accept --require-checked to exit 1 when GPU checks remain unchecked; the default stays a warning. JSON summaries consistently expose uncheckedCount. og test retains its aggregate unchecked field as a deprecated alias; per-playtest unchecked remains a file list.

added.member: og test resident runs and failureCaptures
added.summary: Playtest files, repeats and then steps share a worktree's running og session, preserving fresh-world isolation and ordered --jobs output. Room peers remain dedicated processes. Failed playtests retain the actual final world dump, snapshot and last drawn frame under .failure, reported in failureCaptures; passing suites discard them. PNG encoding happens only on failure, with no extra draw or replay. Missing frames remain explicitly unavailable. Resident retirement flushes its final reply before exiting.

Per-tick properties after Antithesis's assertions: og.assert.always, sometimes, reachable, unreachable and each (one bucket per key), identified by name and the call's place, recorded beside the world and never in it (hashes unchanged); default invariants from reflection checked after every tick outside publish builds (no NaN or infinity, every number inside its field's min..max, no Entity field naming a despawned entity, roots inside og.WorldBounds), incremental from change ticks; the probe's assertions member (take starts a new report) and og run --json's assertions; the invariant: command action; playtests' invariants and require, and a list of every sometimes, reachable and each bucket that never fired.

og.ui.layers lists active (the layer that takes Back, pop and focus), and a layer's events gain `activate` and `deactivate` as it becomes and stops being the active one (CommonUI's OnActivated and OnDeactivated), so a screen refreshes what it shows when the player returns to it.

The design language's motion.timing (packages/design) names what hover, press, enter, exit, cascades, toasts and screen transitions move on; og-ui's widgets read it (theme::TIMING), and a style's motion block overrides a row with the new `toastHold <ms> [<error ms>]`, `screen <ms>` and `magnet <0–1>` lines beside the existing hoverSpring, pressSpring, eases and stagger. The defaults are the numbers the widgets used before, so no frame moves. VirtualCursorDesc.magnet 0 now takes the style's magnet.

A style's `recolour "<colour as painted>" <role>` lines (and a dressing's own, or `recolour none`) make its painted art follow the palette: when the role's colour differs from the one the art was painted in, og cook recolours every authored slice and ornament in Oklab (hue turned, chroma and lightness moved by the accent's, other hues and greys kept) at each atlas density, beside the style (`<style>#atlas.png`), and measures the frames' tones again. Every painted built-in pack names its primary, so a game's copy with its own accent recolours its painted buttons and frames; an unchanged copy cooks nothing extra (docs/art.md §2.7).

`og ui add materials` installs per-element shader presets as `type ui-material` assets with tunable parameters: foil, holo, burn and rarity glow, each usable from a style dressing (`material "ui-kits/materials/foil.ogt" 0.7`) or an element's layer; `og ui sheet materials` reviews them.

A label asks for uppercase in the UI's locale: the same ICU casing a type role with case upper uses (Turkish i, Greek final sigma), applied before measuring; the probe keeps the source text. Components ask for it instead of String.toUpperCase; the bundled kits do.
An icon set that draws the names the atlas (the game's icons, else the style's) lacks, for og.ui.icon, rich text, action glyphs and art placeholders; a pack keeps the icons it paints.

added.member: FieldDesc and TextAreaDesc tight, component; document field tight, component
added.summary: tight lays a field with no inset at its text's line height (rows lines for a text area; on a touch screen at least the 44 CSS px target), with or without bare, for a field inside a box the caller draws. component dresses it as <component>.frame, .text and .placeholder instead of Field, keeping its focused, invalid and disabled states.

added.member: Style dress keys ink and step
added.summary: A text part (a field's text or placeholder) takes ink <colour> and step <type step>, so a style sets a field's text size and colours without per-field members.
The scroll kind in .ogt documents takes fade and fadeInto, as og.ui.scrollArea does, so a cut row reads as more content, not a clip.
Each takes disabled and dresses as a disc. Each keeps the finger that went down on it; the joystick's vector rises from 0 past its dead zone; the d-pad reads eight ways by angle.

added.member: og.destruction (og.Destructible, og.Chunk, og.Fractured, og.Destruction, damage, explode, fracture, info, capabilities)
added.summary: Destructible props. A model's fracture { } block (type model or import settings) is cut by the cook into chunks by a fracture profile per material (style voronoi, concrete, brick along its mortar, wood along its grain, glass radial from its impact) with an interior material and its maps, optional children and anchors (bottom, ends), written beside it as <model>#fracture (og.Fracture). og.Destructible breaks it in the tick from impacts, og.destruction.damage, explode and fracture; NVIDIA Blast's stress solver (BSD-3, third_party/blast), with Mohr–Coulomb friction (og.Destructible.friction), brings down what loses its support; loose islands become rigid bodies, og.Fractured reports each break, each material's breakFx and hitFx and GPU-only debris burst through particle emitters, and og.Destruction budgets loose chunks. Deterministic and in snapshots; lazy, so a world without destructibles keeps its hash.

added.member: UI kits: documents and open tiers
added.summary: The racing kit ships race-results.ogt, a type screen document (place, best lap and points, the classification as a for block, rewards, a Podium slot; emits continue, restart and replay) that a game edits as text. Gacha featured units and pull items take a tier { label, rank, color } over Rarity for a game's own tiers. og ui sheet installs a kit into its sheet's working copy, so pages load the kit's documents as a game does.

Selector-addressed painted parts, per-dressing ornamentTint, paint token alpha and gradients, selection/onSelection/accent/sceneInk/scenePlate/sceneShadow roles, per-role tracking/cjkTracking and locale-aware case upper, hero typography, document tabs, IconDesc.secondary/secondaryTint and LabelDesc.onScene. og ui sheet renders pack or kit baseline pages on demand at desktop and phone, 100% and 150%, outside the gate. MSDF overlap resolution handles negative bearings before sign/error correction.

Format-1 extension.json, og ui add/list/eject and og style add install editable kits and data packs. Typed kit namespaces use @origingame/engine/ui-extensions on both hosts without changing frozen og.ui. Pack-owned choices, skills and nested assets ship beside style.ogt; the UI kit scans its look documents at build time. Style check also finds GameDesc.look without starting a world. Paint-style retries rate_limited 429 responses with bounded backoff. Pack acceptance no longer measures contrast or compares authored data to generator output.

Missing model skin data and incompatible palette counts, joint order or inverse bind matrices warn and appear in probe dumps as render.skinIssue. Equivalent rigs from different asset paths remain valid. Draw behavior and simulation are unchanged.

added.member: DebugView.terrain, terrainLayers, terrainMip; dump_entity terrain diagnostics
added.summary: Terrain projection weights, clipmap cells and morph bands, strongest raw layer and normal-map mip footprint estimate. Entity dumps report the renderer's clipmap regions, triangle spacing, seams and material rules. No simulation or default beauty change.

added.member: timeline tracks property, light, visibility, post, blendshape, material and timeline (nested); camera keys roll, focus, focusOn and focusRange; TimelineTrackInfo.kind and target name them
added.summary: Cinematics, R10 batch 1: a timeline eases any reflected field of a component or resource (`track property "lamp" { field "og.PointLight.distance" ... }`), an entity's light, what it draws' visibility (stepped), og.PostEffects, og.Blendshapes weights and a material's parameters, nests other timelines (from a key, at a speed, looping or held, at most four deep, their markers named `<file>/<marker>`), and rolls and focuses the camera (depth of field on a distance or an entity). Every value is read from the timeline's time, so a seek lands where playing does. The cook checks each field against the engine's records and refuses nesting cycles; an unknown track kind is refused naming it and the engine's version. Material tracks are presentation, applied every frame from the time and put back at the end, so a restore mid-way draws the right material on its next frame. No blob change: the og.Timeline blob keeps its text payload, version and type hash, and a timeline from before cooks to the same bytes; the og.timeline state block grows only for a run whose camera track focused.

added.member: og.VirtualCamera, og.CameraBrain, og.CameraCut; the column Ease
added.summary: Cinematics, R10 batch 2: virtual cameras with priorities and blends. og.VirtualCamera is a shot (its own position or follow an entity with smoothing, lookAt, fov, roll, focus, and collide: a sphere kept clear of colliders between the look point and the camera, pulled in at once and eased out over damping). The resource og.CameraBrain makes the solo shot, else the enabled one with the highest priority (ties: the later enabled), live and blends og.Camera to it over the incoming shot's blendTime by its blendEase, from the blended pose when a blend is interrupted; og.CameraCut reports each change. Registered only when a game names one of them, so other worlds keep their type table and hash; the brain's state is record fields, so a snapshot or a restore mid-blend continues the blend. Collision reads the colliders as the tick started and moves no body. The column Ease lets a record hold og.tween's curves.

added.member: og.story (load, parse, start, view, history, conversations, advance, choose, stop, get, set, reset, startQuest, progress, setStage, completeQuest, failQuest, quest, quests, track, markSeen, mark), og.Story, og.DialogueShown, og.DialogueEnded, og.DialogueCheck, og.QuestUpdated, og.StoryEvent, DialogueView, QuestView, StoryLine
added.summary: Dialogue and quests as data (G2-8): dialogues (`type dialogue`: speakers, lines, choices with conditions, reasons and passive or d20 checks, variables, weighted picks, tick timers) and quests (`type quest`: stages of objectives, rewards, conditions), cooked into the new og.Dialogue and og.Quest blobs and validated with each error's line and fix. Every line, choice, reason and title is an og.i18n key, checked against the base string table at cook and resolved when viewed. The story is a state block saved by ids, so saves survive edits that keep them; renaming the node a save stands on warns naming it and falls back to the start. Picks and checks draw from og.Rng's fork "story". og.Story and the events are lazy records: a world that never loads a story keeps its saves and hash.

added.member: og.story.bark, og.story.ambient, og.story.barks, og.BarkSaid, BarkDesc, AmbientDesc, BarkView, DialogueView.voiceTicks, DialogueView.voiceLeft; og i18n extract
added.summary: og.story completed (G2-8 batch 2). Barks: a dialogue's `bark` blocks (topic, lines in cycle or random order, a `when` that may read the world as Record.field or self.Component.field, priority, weight, per-entity and shared cooldowns, duration, once), asked for with og.story.bark or every so often with og.story.ambient, listed by og.story.barks and announced by og.BarkSaid; the higher priority wins, equal ones draw by weight on the story's stream, and a speaker mid-bark is interrupted only by a higher priority. Voice-over: a line's `voice` clip plays through og.audio on its own og.AudioSource entity, and DialogueView.voiceLeft counts the ticks to its end. A quest objective with `on <Event>` and an optional `where` (reading event.<field>) counts that og event with no game code. dump_story writes the whole story state. og i18n extract lists every key the dialogues and quests show with their arguments, checks each locale's table for missing keys and unpassed arguments (--check exits 1), and --write adds the missing keys to the base table. The story state block's save version is 2; version 1 saves still load.

added.member: og.StreamCell, og.StreamAnchor, og.CellMember, og.CellEvent, the scene `scene "<id>"` line
added.summary: Sub-scenes and world cells (G3-3): an entity's `scene "<id>"` line places another scene under it as its own blob; with og.StreamCell { scene, size, load, unload, pin, loaded } the entity is a cell whose sub-scene's entities (colliders and bodies included) spawn as each tick starts while an og.StreamAnchor { reach } is within `load` of its box and are despawned past `unload`, decided from world state only, in entity order, so replays and restores spawn the same ids. og.CellEvent { cell, loaded, entities } is sent in that tick; every spawned entity carries og.CellMember { cell }. Without anchors the og.Camera position loads cells, refused in an og.net session. All four records are lazy: a world without cells hashes and saves as before.

added.member: BackdropEffect.glass, BackdropEffect.elevation, BackdropEffect.edge, BackdropEffect.edgeColor, BackdropEffect.solid, BackdropEffect.cssMix, GlassWeight, Elevation
added.summary: Flat glass (docs/ui.md §5.3): a backdrop effect takes one of three weights (thin 10 px, regular 22 px, thick 32 px of CSS blur, 200 % saturation, a light tint in the theme's scheme, a 0.5 px hairline inside the edge, mixed as CSS mixes), an elevation (raised, float, lift: soft shadows outside the shape only), its own hairline width and colour, solid (the tint opaque, nothing under it read) and cssMix. Under reduced transparency a weighted glass is the solid raised surface; under high contrast solid with a strong 1 px edge. Thin glass carries icons and play discs only, never text; regular and thick hold the scheme's text at 4.5:1. A style writes `effect backdrop … glass thick elevation lift`. Backdrops without these draw as before.

added.member: SystemDesc.changed, SystemDesc.added, SystemDesc.removed, ArchetypeView.rows, QueryDesc.changed, QueryDesc.added, QueryDesc.removed, World.removed
added.summary: Change detection: a system's change filters narrow its query to the rows whose component changed or was added since the system last ran (ArchetypeView.rows; columns still hold every row), and world.removed lists the entities that lost one. A change is a value that differs from the one last compared, compared after each system and hook for what it writes and as each tick begins for what was written between ticks; a write of the same value is not one. Change ticks count system runs, never a clock, and are world state: saves, the hash and replays carry them, so a restored world filters tick for tick as the original. A component is tracked once a system filters on it; a world that tracks nothing and has no state machine saves and hashes exactly as before.

added.member: og.defineHook, HookDesc, HookEvent, HookRun, Hook, GameDesc.hooks
added.summary: Add and remove hooks per component: a hook runs after its component is added to an entity (spawned with, or inserted) and before it is removed (removed, or despawned, so it reads it), wherever the change comes from (a system's structural changes as they apply, a call between ticks), in GameDesc.hooks order; its own changes apply when it returns and may run hooks in turn, 16 deep at most. Restores run none.

added.member: GameDesc.states, StateDesc, SystemDesc.state, SystemDesc.value, SystemDesc.when, StateWhen, SystemDesc.runIf, RunCondition, World.state, World.setState
added.summary: Game states and run conditions: a state machine (GameDesc.states) holds one of its values; world.setState moves it as the next tick begins, which runs the systems leaving the old value (when: exit), then those entering the new one (enter), each exactly once, then the tick's systems, those bound to a value (during) only while it holds. The first tick enters each initial value. A run condition (runIf) is asked before each run with the system's access read only; a skipped tick is not a run. The states are world state, saved and restored with it.
world.children(entity) lists the entities whose og.Parent is it, in entity order; any system may ask.

A spatial hash for entities without colliders: world.spatial({ with, without, cell }) places every entity with an og.Transform at its position, and the index answers within(center, radius) and nearest(center, count), nearest first with equal distances in entity order, the same on both hosts (positions read as stored, distances in f64).

added.member: GameDesc.saveVersion, GameDesc.migrations, SaveMigration, World.openSave, SaveEdit, SaveType
added.summary: A game's own save version (GameDesc.saveVersion or project.ogt's `saveVersion`, 1 when absent) is written into every save, and its migrations run on a restore from the save's version to the current one, in order: each `{ from, migrate(save) }` edits the save as a SaveEdit (renameField, renameType, transform with the old record, split, dropType, setRecords, spawn) before the world sees it. A step that refuses or throws refuses the restore with its reason and leaves the world as it was; a save of a newer version is refused. The migrated world is the one the new version builds from the same state. world.openSave opens a save for the same edits outside a restore.

Selective saves: world.snapshot({ with: [tags], resources: [chosen] }) saves only the entities carrying every tag and the chosen resources (50 tagged entities of a 5,000-entity world: 1.9 KiB), and world.restore of it replaces those entities and sets those resources, leaving the rest of the world as it is.

added.member: og style eject, og style list
added.summary: og style eject <slug> [<name>] [--project <dir>] [--force] writes a built-in UI style (style.ogt, atlas, icons, fonts with their import settings, licences), byte for byte from the copy og carries, into the game's assets/styles/<name>/ (default the slug), refusing to overwrite without --force, and prints the look's ui "styles/<name>/style.ogt" line; the ejected style cooks to the built-in's blobs, and its cjk fonts stay the shared @styles/cjk/ built-ins. og style list names the built-in slugs with their signatures. The og-ui and og-taste skills use it in place of copying templates/styles/, which the installed package does not have.

og api show with a module's name as written (input, physics) prints the module's overview from its wiki page (what the module is for and how its parts fit, without the IDL); og.Input and og.physics.raycast still print the entry. The skills name `og api show <module>` where they pointed at a wiki page.

The UI draws with analytic shapes (docs/ui.md U1): og.ui.setDraw gives the element added last a shape (rect with four radii and round, squircle, bevel or notch corners; ellipse; polygon and star; arc and ring; a path of lines or Béziers), layered fills (colour, linear/radial/conic/diamond gradients mixed in OKLab and dithered, images with cover/contain/none, a focal point, nine-slice and scrolling patterns, cooked vectors), strokes with their own paint, alignment and dashes, drop and inner shadows, glows, layer blur and backdrop glass, opacity and blend modes, a clip to its shape or a mask, an offscreen layer composited through a built-in UI material (dissolve, shine, hologram, glitch, ripple, pixelate, colour adjust, outline, blur) or a custom `type ui-material`, and text outline, gradient fill and shadows. Colours given as theme tokens follow the style. og.load.vector loads a cooked `type vector` (an SVG subset), og.load.uiMaterial a `type ui-material` (WGSL compiled at cook for every back end). Existing UI draws as before; circles and rings are now exact rather than atlas-sampled, so their antialiased edges move by a few levels.

Prompts read each action's glyph on the device used last (keyboardMouse, xbox, playstation, switch, gamepad, touch), and an og.ui action follows a gameplay action through UiActionDesc.action. og.input.rumble shakes a pad (output only, the frame answer's rumble). og.Gamepad holds eight pads (MAX_GAMEPADS 8, was 4) and each pad's family in devices. The web shell no longer drops pads whose mapping is not "standard" (Firefox, Linux, third-party pads): it maps them through a table by vendor and product with a generic fallback and tells each pad's family. A save from a four-pad build restores without migrate: og.Gamepad is the host's after a restore, so World.restore maps a save whose only differences are in the input it keeps (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock, og.Audio).

This differs from setDisplay as first merged (G1-4, unreleased), where omitted fields went back to their defaults; og.render.resetDisplay is now the explicit way back to them.

The player's sensitivity and inversion of an axis action per device class (keyboardMouse, the pads, touch): scale multiplies the action's analog bindings (mouse movement, wheel, stick, touch stick), invertX and invertY turn the value over (keys are inverted, never scaled). Kept in og.input.saveBindings text; a world with none set hashes as before.

Glyphs show what the player's keyboard layout prints while bindings stay on physical keys (KeyboardEvent.code): og.input.glyph reads Z Q S D for KeyW KeyA KeyS KeyD on AZERTY. The web shell sets it from navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap (Chrome, Edge) and elsewhere learns each key from its first unmodified press.

Raw mouse input while the pointer is locked (pointer lock's unadjustedMovement, on by default) where the browser grants it; mouse().rawUnsupported where it refuses (Firefox, Safari, Linux), whose lock is the plain one. The web shell's pointer lock re-arms on Escape, focus loss or a refused request and locks again on the next click. Host state, never in the world.

On an ultrawide surface anchored groups (og.ui.anchor, the HUD templates) and toasts lay out in a centred band at most hudMaxAspect times its height wide (21/9 by default; 0 is the whole safe area); og.ui.viewport().hud is the band for a HUD placed by hand. Dialogs, scrims and world-space markers keep the whole surface. A HUD on a screen wider than 21:9 moves inward.

The ui-kit settings screen's Graphics tab is the PC graphics page when GameSettings.display holds og.render.display's settings: preset, render scale, frame-rate limit, a fixed V-Sync row, adaptive quality, battery saver, fullscreen and the GPU with "Applies after a restart". The Controls tab sets the mouse's sensitivity and inverted look on SettingsDesc.lookAction and raw mouse input.

The probe's memory report and the web shell's field telemetry carry the GPU devices lost and recovered, beside the GPU memory.

A window moved to a monitor of another scale (or a page zoom) resizes the canvas and og-ui before the next frame, through a (resolution: <dpr>dppx) query re-armed at each ratio, so no frame is drawn blurry.

A bus graph: user buses 4 to 15, each an og.AudioBusNode with a parent (a built-in bus or a lower user bus) and a volume multiplied down the chain to master, so a footsteps bus under sfx is turned down with sfx. AudioSource.userBus routes a source into one; an og.AudioBusFx with userBus puts effects on it. The graph reaches the mixer as commands in the stream, only what changed, so it is in the world hash.

Mixer snapshots (combat, underwater, paused): per-bus volumes, low-passes and high-passes the mix blends towards while `active` and back from when not, over `fade` seconds; `weight` is written each tick, and the gains ramp linearly across each tick, so a blend is a straight line to the sample. Several snapshots multiply their volumes and take the lowest low-pass and highest high-pass.

added.summary: Bus effects: a three-band equaliser (low shelf, peak, high shelf), an echo with feedback and mix (its delay to the sample) and a tanh waveshaper, on any bus, built-in or user.

Audio events: one of up to eight sounds per trigger, chosen weighted-random, round-robin or shuffled, with volume (dB) and pitch (semitone) jitter, a cooldown and a voice limit that steals the oldest voice or ignores the trigger. The og.audioEvents system draws on the engine's seeded stream for audio (forked from og.Rng's seed, kept in the world, never Math.random), so a seed and the same triggers play the same sounds at the same pitches on every host and replay, and the game's og.Rng never moves for a sound. Each play is a voice entity parented to the event's, despawned when it ends.
PCM a game computes in TypeScript (a Float32Array of interleaved samples, its rate and 1 or 2 channels) becomes a sound that plays, loops and pitches as a loaded one; og.load.soundInfo reports it.

The blob is og.Sound version 3 (a `codec` field; cooked bundles re-cook). The runtime decodes its 0.48 s blocks beside the tick on both hosts and streams a long track through the frame cache, sample for sample its whole decode; on the web the engine Worker decodes a few packets after each frame's audio, never inside a tick. The decoder adds about 82 KB brotli to the wasm.

added.member: og.load.prefab, og.PrefabLink, World.prefabOf, World.instantiate (prefabs), og cook (type prefab), og prefab check/show/extract
added.summary: Prefabs (docs/design.md §2.5, G2-1): an .ogt of type prefab holds one entity tree; an entity with a `prefab "<id>"` line is an instance of it, its block holding only what differs: component blocks over the root's fields, `override "<node>" { ... }` over a descendant's, `remove "<node>" [Component]`, added child entities. Prefabs nest, a `base "<id>"` line makes a variant (variants chain), and a cycle is refused naming the chain. The cook flattens instances into the scene blob depth first in text order (a scene re-cooks when any prefab it reaches changes) and names a placed descendant `<instance>/<node>`; a generated name taken by another entity is refused naming both. An override whose node, component or field the prefab no longer has stays in the text: a dev cook warns, og prefab check exits 1, a publish cook (og build --publish) refuses it naming the instance, node and field. Each placed entity carries og.PrefabLink { prefab (the prefab's asset handle), node, root }; world.prefabOf reads it; og.load.prefab and world.instantiate place one at run time, unnamed. Simulation: a world that places a prefab hashes differently from the same entities written by hand (the links are world state) and stably across a re-cook that changes nothing it spawns; og.PrefabLink is registered only when a prefab entity first spawns (or a save holding one is restored), so a game without prefabs keeps its type table, saves and hash, and no save migration is needed.

added.member: probe (protocol 5, additive): apply_prefab, revert_prefab actions; dump_entity.prefab; save_scene keeps instances
added.summary: Strictly additive to probe protocol 5: two new command-channel actions, apply_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]][:base] (an instance's overrides, or a value set at run time, moved into the prefab's .ogt at the entity's node and out of the scene, so every instance takes them; :base writes a variant's through to its base) and revert_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]] (the overrides dropped and the live values set back to the prefab's); dump_entity gains an optional `prefab` ({ prefab, node, root, overrides }) for entities placed from one. save_scene writes a placed entity's tuned field as an override of its instance, only when it differs from the prefab's value, and removes one back at it. No member, field or answer that exists changes shape; publish builds serve neither action.

added.member: og.NavFilter, og.nav.setArea, NavAreaDesc, PathDesc.areaCosts, PathDesc.excluded; type navmesh `area` (G2-4)
added.summary: Navmesh area types and costs: spans under an area's shape take an area id (0 is ground, up to 63), set at run time with og.nav.setArea (rebuilding only the tiles it touches) or baked; regions never mix areas, so every polygon has one. An agent's og.NavFilter weighs each polygon's length by its area's cost (areaCosts, at least 0.01; past the list 1) and keeps out of its excluded areas; og.nav.findPath takes the same two fields. A* stays admissible (its heuristic at the cheapest cost). og.NavFilter is registered with the world only once a game inserts it, declares it in a system or hook, or restores a save holding it, so a world without it keeps its type table, saves and hash; run-time areas are in the og.nav state block's trailer (og_ecs::trailer, tag 2), written only when a mesh has one. Cooked navmeshes keep their blob version: areas are optional sections a blob without them loads as all ground.

Obstacle shapes beyond boxes: a box turned about +y (orientedBox), an upright cylinder and a convex prism, carved into a navmesh by id like og.nav.setObstacle (which stays the axis-aligned box and carves exactly as before). A shape blocks the cells whose centres it covers, grown by the agent radius, and rebuilds only its tiles; the shapes are in the og.nav state block's trailer, so a save restores them.

added.member: og.nav.setLink, og.nav.setLinkOpen, og.nav.finishLink, NavLinkDesc, NavLinkKind, NAV_ON_LINK, og.NavLinkReached, NavPath.links; type navmesh `link` (G2-4)
added.summary: Off-mesh links: a jump, a ladder, a door or a teleport from one point of a navmesh to another (both ways unless bidirectional is false), baked from a navmesh asset's `link` lines or set at run time by id. A* crosses an open link where it is cheaper than walking (cost in metres, 0 its length); a shut one (og.nav.setLinkOpen) is never planned and agents re-plan when it opens or closes. An agent reaching a link reports NAV_ON_LINK and sends og.NavLinkReached; the engine animates the crossing (an arc for a jump, half speed on a ladder, walking through a door, a teleport at once, or the link's duration), and a link with game (`traverse game`) holds the agent until og.nav.finishLink. og.NavLinkReached is registered only once a mesh has a link (or a save holding one is restored), so a world without links keeps its type table, saves and hash. Run-time links (where they moved from the baked ones) and agents crossing them are in the og.nav state block's trailer (tags 1 and 3); cooked links are an optional `links` section, so the navmesh blob keeps its version.

added.member: og.nav.load(world, path, profile?), NavMeshInfo.profile; type navmesh `agent <name>` (G2-4)
added.summary: Agent profiles: a navmesh asset may hold several agent blocks, each `agent <name> { radius height climb slope }` baked into its own mesh over the same geometry, areas and links, so a small body walks a doorway a big one cannot. og.nav.load takes the profile's name (omitted: the first agent block, the unnamed one if any) and refuses an unknown one naming those the asset has; NavMeshInfo.profile says which was loaded. The first profile fills the blob's own tables and each other is a whole navmesh blob in an optional `profile.<name>` section, listed in `profiles`: a navmesh of one unnamed agent cooks byte for byte as before and the blob keeps its version. A second unnamed agent, a repeated name or a name other than letters, digits, '_' and '-' is refused naming its line.

Crowd avoidance (ORCA, RVO2's construction): an og.NavAgent with og.Crowd { neighbours 8, horizon 2, obstacleHorizon 0.5, weight 0.5 } moves each tick at the velocity nearest what its path and steering want that keeps it clear of its nearest agents (G2-2's spatial hash: by distance, then entity) for horizon seconds and of the navmesh's boundary edges for obstacleHorizon, each pair of crowd agents sharing the avoidance by weight and an agent without og.Crowd avoided wholly. Deterministic by construction: every agent solves from the tick's start-of-tick state (a Jacobi step, so solving order does not matter) with + − × ÷ and sqrt only, and a symmetric jam (eight agents swapping across a ring lock still under plain ORCA) is broken by a per-agent margin of up to 5% of its radius from a hash of its entity id, the same on every host and run. og.Crowd is registered only once a game uses it (or a save holding it is restored) and adds no state block or trailer: an agent without it moves exactly as before (og.Steering separation), so existing nav games keep their hash. New projects start with it: create-game's templates that use nav (game's guard, third-person's sentinels, topdown's slimes) insert og.Crowd, which moves the game-3d golden replay from tick 84 (the guard keeps clear of the yard wall's edge); game-2d is unchanged. tower-defense keeps separation: its maze waves file in line, and ORCA let visitors pass each other beyond the towers' reach.

added.member: og.Collider on a child of an og.RigidBody (compound colliders), RaycastHit.body
added.summary: A Collider without a RigidBody whose og.Parent chain reaches a RigidBody is part of that body, placed at its transform relative to it, so a body is built from several shapes on child entities (a table, a ship, a character's limbs). Children join in entity order; a changed child rebuilds the body; events and queries name the collider, and RaycastHit.body names its body. A world without such children steps and hashes exactly as before.
Every collider along a ray, nearest first (ties in entity order, alike on every host), at most maxHits (256).
The nearest point on any collider to a point within a reach, with its collider, body, outward normal, distance and whether the point is inside (solid or onto the surface).

added.member: Physics.sleepTicks, Physics.sleepSpeed, RigidBody.canSleep, RigidBody.sleeping, BodySlept, BodyWoke
added.summary: Sleep (G2-3): a dynamic body slower than sleepSpeed for sleepTicks ticks in a row sleeps, together with every dynamic body it touches (contacts and joints, transitively), and costs nothing until something wakes it: a body landing on it, a push, a joint, a moving kinematic body, a write to its components, its support going away, or sleepTicks set to 0. RigidBody.sleeping is written (write false to wake); BodySlept and BodyWoke are sent in entity order. Counted in ticks and saved with the world, never a clock. sleepTicks 0, the default, keeps every existing world stepping as before; og.RigidBody and og.Physics are version 2, and saves of 0.7.7 restore with the new fields at their defaults. Simulation: a world without sleep steps as before and its portable hash (og replay's, the golden replays') is unchanged; the raw world hash moves once for every engine world, because og.RigidBody's and og.Physics's new layouts are in the type table it covers. og.BodySlept, og.BodyWoke, og.JointBroken and og.ContactHook are registered with a world only once a game names them (a system or hook that declares one, an insert, a read of the events, a save holding one), like G2-4's lazy records: a world that never does keeps their absence from its type table, saves and raw hash, and the events are not sent to a world that cannot read them.

Breaking joints (G2-3): a joint whose solver load through a step passes breakForce, or whose torque about its anchor passes breakTorque, breaks: it is removed in joint entity order, its `broken` is written and og.JointBroken { joint, body, other, force, torque } is sent; writing broken false mends it where its bodies are. The load is what the solver holds through the step (a weight, gravity, what rests or presses on it); a lone impulse, applyImpulse or applyForce, is absorbed before it counts. 0, the default, never breaks; og.Joint is version 2 and saves of 0.7.7 restore with the new fields at their defaults. og.JointBroken is registered only once a game names it; a joint breaks (and `broken` is written) either way.

Contact hooks (G2-3) on a collider's entity: oneWay (solid only from one side, within 45°, what came in from elsewhere passing until clear: a platform jumped through from below), surfaceVelocity (a conveyor), friction and restitution in place of the pair's mean (negative keeps them), and ignore (up to eight entities, colliders or their bodies, it never collides with). The solver reads them from a table frozen at the start of the step, on its worker threads, so they are data rather than game callbacks, the same on both hosts and in replays. A world without hooks steps as before. og.ContactHook is registered only once a game inserts or names it; until then physics reads no hooks.

added.member: og.ai game actions, subtrees and utility (G2-4)
added.summary: Behaviour trees gain three nodes. `action <name> args` hands a long action to the game: og.ai sends og.AiActionStarted { entity, node, name, args } and the node stays running until og.ai.finish(world, entity, success, action?) answers it at the next think; when the tree leaves it first (a higher branch, a machine transition, og.ai.restart) og.AiActionStopped carries result AI_INTERRUPTED (new constant, 4). `use "<path>"` inlines another cooked behaviour's tree, its keys and routes joined (a differing route of one name, a machine, and a cycle are refused naming the chain; the cook's stamp covers every subtree reached, so editing one re-checks the trees using it; BehaviourInfo.subtrees lists them). `utility { inertia x; option <name> { score ...; nodes } }` runs the option whose score lines multiply highest (constants, or an input mapped by linear, inverse, quadratic, sqrt, smooth or step over a range), the running one gaining inertia, ties to the first written, failing when none scores above 0. Hash and save: the two events are lazy records, registered only once a behaviour with an action is loaded (or a save holding them restored); a finished action's pending result is og.ai's trailer section 1 (og_ecs::trailer), written only while one is pending. A game using none of this keeps its type table, saves and hash (the yard pin is unchanged).

added.member: Vehicle.model, VEHICLE_ARCADE, VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN, Vehicle.gears, reverseRatio, finalDrive, idleRpm, maxRpm, torqueCurve, automatic, shiftUpRpm, shiftDownRpm, clutchTime, gear, rpm, handbrake, handbrakeGrip, driftGrip; og.VehicleWheel; WheelPose.entity; unit rpm (G2-3)
added.summary: A drivetrain car (G2-3): model VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN drives the wheels with an engine whose torque curve (N·m at evenly spaced speeds up to maxRpm, 0 past it) goes through a gear's ratio and the final drive; the engine's speed follows the wheels while a gear is in and free-revs in neutral and while the clutch is out (clutchTime). An automatic gearbox shifts at shiftUpRpm and shiftDownRpm and into reverse when throttle is negative at a standstill; a manual one takes the game's gear. gear and rpm are written for a tachometer and an engine sound; the gearbox is in the og.physics state block's trailer (tag 4).
