Both models gain a handbrake that brakes the rear wheels and loosens their grip (handbrakeGrip), and driftGrip, their sideways grip while they slide. og.VehicleWheel children (up to 16, entity order) replace the four implicit wheels with wheels of their own radius, suspension, grip, steering share (negative for rear steering) and drive, brake and handbrake flags; vehicleWheels lists them with their entity. og.VehicleWheel is registered only once a game names it. og.Vehicle is version 2; saves of 0.7.7 restore with model VEHICLE_ARCADE, and an arcade car on its implicit wheels steps and saves exactly as before (tests/unchanged.rs).

added.member: SoftBody, SOFT_SPHERE, SOFT_BOX, SOFT_MESH, og.physics.softBodyPoints, SoftBodyPoints (G2-3)
added.summary: PBD soft volumes (G2-3): og.SoftBody is a closed surface of points (a sphere, a box or a closed mesh; 2D a ring) held by distance constraints along its edges (stiffness) and one constraint on the volume it encloses (pressure, volumeStiffness; 2D its area), dropped under gravity and pushed out of every solid collider with thickness and friction, so it lands, squashes and springs back; pinTop hangs it from its entity. It moves nothing, like og.Cloth. volume (now over rest) and center are written; its points are in the og.physics state block's trailer (tag 5), softBodyPoints reads them with the surface's triangles, and the renderer draws it with material. og.SoftBody is registered only once a game names it.

Weighted picks and shuffles on the engine's seeded streams: `weighted(weights)` draws an index with probability weight / sum (zero, negative and non-finite weights never picked; -1 when none is positive), `permutation(n)` is 0 to n - 1 in a Fisher-Yates order (n - 1 draws). A shuffled copy is `rng.permutation(a.length).map((i) => a[i])`. On og.Rng itself both need og.Rng among the system's writes.

added.member: og.procgen.noise, og.procgen.noiseGrid, og.procgen.poissonDisk, og.procgen.bsp, og.procgen.wfc, NoiseKind, FbmDesc, NoiseGridDesc, PoissonDesc, CellRect, BspDesc, BspResult, WfcTile, WfcCell, WfcDesc, WfcResult
added.summary: Procedural generation (G2-6): Perlin and simplex noise in 2D and 3D with fractal octaves, Poisson-disk points (Bridson), BSP rooms joined by corridors, and wave function collapse (the simple tiled model, with rotations, fixed cells and wrapping, retried on forks of the seed). Each is a pure function of its desc: it takes a seed (`world.resource(og.Rng)`'s value `.fork("label").seed`, a u32 as og.Rng's own) and draws only from og.Rng streams of it, in integer and IEEE f32 arithmetic with no host libm, so equal descs give bit-identical results on both hosts. They need no world and touch no state.

Writes a row-major block of cells at once (a generated grid mapped to tile ids): checked whole before any cell is written, a terrain layer re-tiled and the colliders rebuilt once, cells past the map's edge skipped.

`og relay` can play a bad network to test netcode against (G2-7): every frame to a peer held the latency plus up to the jitter in milliseconds, in order, and a send marked unreliable (lockstep's inputs) dropped the loss percentage of the time and free to overtake others, the draws from one seed.

Rollback netcode (G2-7): with mode `rollback` a tick runs on predicted inputs (each missing player's last input) up to maxPrediction ticks (default 8) past the last tick whose inputs are all in, and when a real input differs the world is rewound to the engine's own snapshot of that tick and re-simulated within the frame. A peer also predicts no further than it can re-simulate in half a frame. The zero value (`lockstep`) keeps today's behaviour; the confirmed world, which every peer agrees on, is the same as lockstep's for the same inputs.

resimulating(world) tells a system that the running tick is a rollback's re-run, so a game's own presentation (a shake, a haptic) fires once; finalHash(world, tick) is the shared hash of a tick's final world, run on real inputs only, kept for the last 1024 final ticks.

added.member: og.net.status: rollback, maxPrediction, confirmedTick, finalTick, acknowledged, predicted, rollbacks, resimulatedTicks, snapshotBytes
added.summary: The status reports the rollback state: how far the world runs ahead of its confirmed inputs, how many rewinds and re-simulated ticks it took, and the bytes the rewind ring holds.

A re-simulated tick plays each sound once: a play already sent for the same voice and sound is dropped, a new one is kept only if at most 100 ms late, and a voice the re-run no longer plays is stopped. Wall-clock presentation only: never in the tick or the hash.
og run's summary gives the confirmed (final) hash of its last tick in a room; in rollback the run continues past --ticks until that tick is final and acknowledged by every peer.

Tilemap orientations (G2-6): a map is orthogonal, isometric, staggered (odd rows shifted) or hexagonal (pointy- or flat-top, odd rows or columns shifted, sides half a tile), from a tilemap `.ogt`'s `orientation` line or a Tiled map (Tiled's isometric, staggered and hexagonal maps in that layout now cook; another stagger is refused naming the Map Properties to change). cellAt, cellCenter and the new neighbours follow it; an isometric or staggered tile's image stands on its cell's bottom (taller tiles overlap those behind, drawn back to front); solid tiles off the orthogonal grid collide as one collider per connected solid region (see TileLayerInfo.cellColliders), or one diamond or hexagon per cell on request (new Collider shapes 7 and 8, both profiles, also for game code); terrain layers need an orthogonal or isometric map. Cook: the orientation is an optional `orientation` section of the og.Tilemap blob, so an orthogonal map cooks to the same bytes under the same type hash and nothing re-cooks (pinned).

Run-time tilemaps (G2-6): create makes an empty map in code (size, tile pixels, unit, orientation, tileset asset ids, layers), with a handle from the world's own counter; resize grows or crops a map (a loaded one too), moving its cells, every placed copy's edits and its objects by (x, y), refusing an odd shift along a staggered or hex map's shifted axis. Both are world state: the og.tilemap block's og_ecs::trailer holds the maps made or resized whole (section 1, tilesets by asset id) and the counter (section 2), written only once a map was made or resized, so a world that only loads maps saves and hashes as before (pinned: tests/tilemap_runtime.rs). A save restores them in a session that never made them; an earlier save puts a resized loaded map back as loaded.

Merged tilemap colliders off the orthogonal grid (G2-6): each connected region of solid cells (sharing sides) is one static collider, a generated triangle mesh whose shape is saved with the world (a restore needs no mesh): in 2D its outline, a hollow polyline with holes as their own loops, in 3D the closed prism over it. A static map now costs physics per region, not per cell (256 × 256 hex, half solid: 1,264 colliders instead of 32,631; steady tick 0.26 ms against the merged orthogonal map's 1.73 ms, release). A layer's `cellColliders true` (`.ogt` layer line, Tiled bool property, TileLayerDesc) keeps one diamond or hexagon per cell. SHAPE_TRIMESH now works in 2D for game code too: the outline of the mesh's triangles. Cook: a layer flag bit, clear for every map cooked before, so nothing re-cooks.

Stall timeout, drop and rejoin (G2-7): a peer silent for a second is reported (og.PeerStalled, this peer's own), and past stallTimeout (5000 ms; 0 never drops) or on leaving the room its seat is dropped at a tick every peer agrees on (og.SeatDropped, hashed), with empty input from then on. With rejoin (default true) a dropped player that comes back, or a newcomer of the same name, takes its seat back from the authority's world (og.SeatRejoined, at one tick on every peer). The seat events are registered only once a world runs lockstep in a room.
The status lists the silent peers and counts the drops; each seat hold says whether it ended because its peer left the room or stalled.
og run's summary carries the game's facts (og.game's `facts`), as the probe prints them.
Coin Duel notes the seats changing hands (Duel.droppedAt, rejoinedAt, drops, rejoins), shows "Waiting for peer n" while a peer is silent, and takes `stall:<ms>` for og.Lockstep.stallTimeout.

added.member: og.i18n.formatCompact, og.i18n.formatCurrency, og.i18n.formatDate, og.i18n.formatTime, og.i18n.formatDuration, DateStyle, TimeStyle, DateFormat, TimeFormat; MessageFormat `{n, number, compact}`, `{p, number, currency/EUR}`, `{d, date[, style]}`, `{t, time[, style]}`
added.summary: Locale formatting (G2-6): compact numbers (`1.2K`, `1,2 Mio.`, `1.2万`), currency amounts with the currency's own symbol and fraction digits (`$1,234.50`, `1.234,50 €`, `￥1,235`, Indian grouping in hi), dates in four styles and times in two, and clock-face durations, in the active locale's digits and separators. The data is a CLDR 49 subset built into the engine (crates/og-i18n/src/cldr.rs, generated by scripts/cldr.ts): the 45 languages og-i18n's plural rules cover plus zh-Hant, and 40 currencies; another language is written as en. A date or time is seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC that the game passes in, with an offset for formatDate and formatTime; nothing reads a clock, so the text is the same on both hosts and in a replay. A message's tables now format with their full tag (zh-TW writes Traditional), and `{n, date}` and `{n, time}` parse instead of being refused; `{n, number}` keeps its form.

added.member: og.TimeGroup, og.TimeGroups, og.time.setGroupScale, og.time.groupDt, og.ParticleSystem (time groups)
added.summary: Time groups (G2-6): og.TimeGroup puts an entity in one of 16 groups and og.time.setGroupScale sets a group's scale on top of the global one (0 freezes it); og.anim, flipbooks, 2D skeletons, the entity's scaled tweens and its og.nav agent advance by scaledDt times that scale, groupDt answers it for game code. An og.ParticleSystem on a grouped entity spawns, ages and moves its particles at the group's scale, read as the frame is extracted (the renderer keeps a piecewise clock per system, re-anchored where the scale changes; at scale 1 it steps exactly as before, so existing particle frames are unmoved); particles still ignore the global scale and hit stop. Physics stays on the global scale (one solver steps every body), as do timelines and the UI. Both types are registered only once a game names either, so a world without them keeps its type table, saves and hash (pinned: og-runtime tests/time_groups.rs); a save of a grouped world restores its scales in a session that never named them.

added.member: og build --publish: content-hashed names and the service worker's incremental update
added.summary: A publish build serves its shell, engine Worker, audio worklet, engine glue and wasm (single-threaded and lanes) and the Basis transcoder as <stem>.<12 hex of sha256>.<ext>, cached for a year (_headers). The page finds them through og-config's files, and og-build.json gives them in worker, wasm, lanes, names and each source map's file. A new build's service worker copies every file, packs included, whose content its previous cache holds, and fetches only what changed (docs/web-export.md §Content-hashed names, §The shell). For the platform's checks the build keeps index.html's ./play.js, now a one-line loader of play.<hash>.js, and plain copies of origin-engine.js and origin-engine_bg.wasm. These aliases go away only once docs/platform-asks.md #18 has landed, in a later minor version with its own breaking entry; until then nothing a game or host reads changes.

added.member: og.load.imageData, og.load.gltfData, og.load.release, og.load.imageInfo, og.load.completions, og.load.replayCompletions, the dump_memory command, LoadBudget, ImageDataDesc, GltfDataDesc, ImageKind, ImageInfo, LoadCompletion
added.summary: Uncooked images and models at run time (G3-4): a PNG or JPEG, or a glTF 2.0 (.glb, or .gltf with data: URIs), that a player made or a generator wrote, loaded from bytes and drawn like a cooked texture or model (world.instantiate, og.Model, og.load.gltfInfo). Its size, a model's triangles and each image's dimensions are read from the headers and checked against LoadBudget (32 MiB, 500,000 triangles, 4096 texels, at most 8192) before anything is decoded; a load over a limit is refused at the call, naming the limit and the fix, and so is what the reader does not decode (Draco, meshopt, Basis, WebP, sparse accessors, another file). Natively a thread decodes images; on the web the browser does (createImageBitmap in the engine's Worker), so the engine thread never waits, and a model's primitives are converted a LoadBudget.frameMs at a time. Completion is host input: it is applied at a tick boundary, within LoadBudget.frameMs a frame, and journaled (og.load.completions), and og replay --record keeps the journal so --compare and og.load.replayCompletions put each load in place at its recorded tick. In a lockstep or rollback room a completion stays local to each peer: the game shares the bytes with og.platform.roomSend and agrees on the tick the simulation uses them through og.net.submit. og.load.release frees an uncooked asset: a pending load is dropped unjournaled, a ready one's textures and meshes are emptied under their handles (what still names them draws nothing), giving back their GPU memory and CPU copies; the command channel's new dump_memory[:path] writes the probe's memory report, the GPU figures included.

added.member: TransitionKind glitch; a style's motion `enter glitch <strength>` and `toast glitch <strength>`
added.summary: A glitch transition (the owner, for cyber): the content draws through the existing glitch layer material (slices pushed sideways, colours split) as it fades in or out, over 150 to 180 ms whatever the style's base duration, weakening as it settles. Any style or transition can name it. Its slices come from the element's id and the tick-counted UI clock, so a captured frame is the same every run; under reduced motion it is a plain fade.

added.member: og.StreamCell persist and budget, og.StreamAnchor maxSpeed, a scene's `stream "<name>" { cell }` group; dump_stream's hold and holds
added.summary: World cells, G3-3 batch 2: a `persist` cell keeps its entities as they are through an unload, in the og.cells state block (snapshots, saves, the hash and rollbacks carry it), and `budget` spreads a large cell's spawn over ticks (a 5,000-entity cell's worst tick 41/28/19 ms at budgets 1000/500/250, its one-tick load 153 ms). A sub-scene can declare a cell group, `stream "<name>" { cell; asset ... }`: its blob leaves the boot bundle for the group's pack, fetched ahead of each anchor by 2 s at its StreamAnchor.maxSpeed. A tick that would load a cell whose blob has not landed is held, never skipped or reordered, with each hold and its length in the engine's log and dump_stream's hold and holds; natively a read completes at once, so a native run never holds. A room session over anchorless cells is refused at its start. The og.StreamCell and og.StreamAnchor layouts grew, so a world with cells hashes and saves differently; a world without them is unchanged.

added.member: og.WorldOrigin, og.OriginShifted; the IDL attribute worldspace
added.summary: Large worlds, R12: a world that names og.WorldOrigin shifts as a tick starts once its focus (WorldOrigin.focus, else the first og.StreamAnchor, else og.Camera.position) strays past `step` from the zero, by the multiple of `step` nearest it, so every place stays near zero however far the world goes; the zero is kept in f64 and og.OriginShifted carries the delta. What moves is the schema's: fields marked `worldspace world`, `root`, `hook` or `none` with their axes (og-idl refuses an unmarked Vector2/Vector3 record field named as a place); every state block shifts, rapier's bodies in place with their contacts, warm starts and sleep kept, navigation by a frame offset, streamed cells with their subtrees; VirtualCamera.eased and CameraBrain.fromPosition are marked world. The render origin is laid on the absolute world's grid, so a shift draws nothing different. 2D worlds shift on plane xy. A world without og.WorldOrigin keeps its hash and frames.

added.member: texture { stream true }, model { stream_textures true }; the probe's mip_stream and dump_stream's mips
added.summary: Texture mip streaming, G3-3 batch 3: a texture cooked with `stream true` ships its mip tail (levels at most 256 px, byte for byte the whole chain's) in the boot bundle and its whole chain as `<id>#mips`, fetched on demand. Before each frame the engine measures how many pixels each streamed texture covers, loads the whole chain of the most magnified within a 128 MiB mip budget, swaps it in under the same handle and puts the tail back once the texture has been small for 120 frames; texture size reports the whole chain's throughout. Presentation only: a world's hash never depends on it. The probe's `mip_stream:resident` shows every streamed texture whole before each frame, for reproducible captures; `mip_stream:stream[:<MiB>]` streams within that budget. Textures without `stream true` cook and draw as before.

added.member: og.Decal normalMin, normalMax and normalScale; decals past 32 per frame
added.summary: Decals, R7 batch 1: a decal can carry a tangent-space normal map from a region of the decal atlas (normalMin to normalMax, strength normalScale as three.js normalScale) that bends the surface's normal; a frame draws up to 65,536 decals (they were capped at 32), binned into the light clusters so each pixel walks only the decals that can cover it, at most 255 in one cluster (the newest kept). Existing decals draw as before; off by default (an empty normal region).
Up to 64 blendshapes: weights of targets 9…64, carried with the previous frame's weights for motion vectors.
An emitter's events (birth, death, collision) as an event gameplay reads; its systems are simulated in the tick. Emitters gain render mesh, lit, distortion, subEmitter and events lines.
Cloth on a skinned model's mesh, posed by the skin and simulated in the tick (R9).
An og.Garment's simulated points after the last step, in the world (R9).
Plays a clip on a model on the GPU from a shared baked clip, for crowds (R9).
An open sea: Gerstner waves of a fully developed sea for the wind, with swell and choppiness, whitecaps on the crests; og.physics.waterHeight reads the same surface in the tick (R5).
three.js Water2's flow map: the flow's direction per point, for the normal map's layers or the travelling waves (R5).

Floats a dynamic body on og.Water (a lake or a sea's waves) and og.WaterSurface by its voxelised hull: each cell under the surface lifts by the water it displaces at that cell, so hulls right themselves and pitch and roll with the waves, computed in the tick; submerged is written. Lazily registered: a world without it hashes as before.

A notice from the page that frames the game, outside any platform service: Player protocol 2 `platform` `{ notice: { kind: "host", data: { name, ... } } }`, applied at the next tick's start as og.PlatformNotice like the others. The engine gives it no meaning of its own; the game and its page agree what each name means (engine.origingame.ai's hero switches scenes with it). An appended variant: a game that never reads notices runs as before.

added.member: the built-in styles wasteland and foundry
added.summary: Two built-in UI styles of the sixteen packs (docs/ui.md §12.5), each painted from its approved sheet: wasteland (rusted riveted plate, duct tape, safety orange, a stencil display face; survival, crafting and extraction) and foundry (iron in brass rims, rivets, furnace orange, wide serif capitals; city builders, factory and 4X). A look names them with ui "wasteland" or ui "foundry"; og style list names them and og style new starts from them for their look families. Every other built-in style is unchanged.

New command: og frame measure <png> [--region x,y,w,h] [--against x,y,w,h] [--units px|fraction] [--metric contrast,highpass,mean,ramp] [--rows N] [--json] measures a region of any captured frame the same way on every machine, so a reviewer's numbers reproduce without image scripts: WCAG contrast (the ink, the region's darkest or brightest 5 %, against the median ground of --against or of the region), high-pass energy (the mean |grey - its σ 2 px Gaussian blur|, with its ratio to --against), the mean colour and grey, and the grey per band of --rows rows with the largest step. Reads the PNG's 8-bit sRGB values only; exit 2 on a usage error, 1 when the image cannot be read or the region lies off it.

project.ogt's screens {} takes any screen name: title, play and results are captured first, then the block's other screens in order, then the ui { screen } entries it does not name (before, a name other than title, play or results was refused, so nothing a game declared beyond them was captured). --sizes desktop,phone (also phoneLandscape, phonePortrait, tablet or WxH; phone follows publish { orientation }) captures every screen at each size into og-out/style/<screen>@<viewport>/; --size and the default (desktop 1280x720) keep og-out/style/<screen>/. --json adds to each frame its viewport, label (<screen>@<viewport>), size and the renderer tier that drew it; to contract its extends chain, the look's flattened art blocks (art, colours as sRGB hex), the palette's colours (palette.hex) and the catalogue style's checks and intended (style); and a coverage block (screens, viewports, uncoveredScenes: each scenes {} entry with no screen of its name, the start scene covered by play). --critic adds the style's intended traits and each frame's label (JSON: intended, shots); its frames list is unchanged. Additive: existing fields keep their meaning.

Each finding carries value, bar and unit where its rule measures a number (contrast's ratio against 3, 7 or the 4.5 warning bar; a text's size against its floor; a touch target's side against 44; an overlap's or overflow's area or px against 0) and at, one UiFindingAt per cell: the cell, its viewport, the box in CSS px (the overlap's rectangle, the text's line box, else the first path's element) and the cell's captured frame. check.json and --json list every cell's frame (frames), and --json names check.json (report). mergeFindings keeps every cell's place. Optional fields: findings built by older code still merge and print.

Every style entry has intended: one sentence, never naming the style, saying which traits of its frames look like defects and are the style (hard one-pixel steps, dither, broken edges, crushed-looking blacks), read by every critic beside the three checks (og-taste §12); the validator requires it. An added field: readers of the catalogue that ignore it read it as before.

The skill gains §5, the art bar a frame that passes every check is still held to (hierarchy, art, numerals, selection, depth, spacing, motion: each worded relative to the game's own look and decided by a number og frame measure, og ui check or og style check reproduces), and §6, verdicts: approve or hold, every hold a frame, a region, a criterion (style-check-N, bible:, contract:, measure:, bar:<item>), the measured value and what passes; a preference is a note, contrast is judged at the bar the engine's check states and never stricter, and a resubmission is judged on the held notes and regressions only. The skill keeps its name; its body is a new pack version. og-build §8, og-ui §8 and og-taste §12 describe the new measures.

Places the scatter's chunks with a compute pass when they come into range, by the same rules as the CPU (layer weight, holes, noiseThreshold, avoidWater, the footprints of the scatters placed before it) from the terrain's finest tiles, with nothing per copy on the CPU: on a moving camera over three chained scatters, 60.3 ms of CPU a frame drops to 14.3 ms for 0.21 ms of GPU. On by default; gpuPlacement: false places every chunk on the CPU. Where the renderer has no compute, or a footprint chain is too long or too wide, the CPU places them. The copies match the CPU's placement but for the last bits of the arithmetic: every scatter scene's reference frame (terrain-grass, terrain-grass-wind, terrain-hidden, terrain-scatter-unshadowed, impostor-scatter, probe-outdoor) holds within its tolerance, so a game draws as before. Visual only; the simulation is unchanged.

A `type flipbook` sheet takes animated GIF, WebP and APNG files (`source "hero_run.gif" { clip "run" mode loop fps 12 event 3 "step" align feet }`, a clip per file) instead of a texture: the cook decodes and composites the frames, keeps their delays as clip durations (10 ms or less shown as 100 ms, as browsers do), keys a flat background (`key auto|"#rrggbb" [tolerance]`, only what the border reaches, the edge ring unmixed), aligns the frames (`align feet|bbox|centroid|none`) in whole texels, resamples (`scale`), crops every frame to one size with the pivot at the anchor (`padding`), shares identical frames (`dedupe`) and packs them into the texture `<sheet>#sheet`, writing the same canonical sheet an Aseprite atlas makes.

`og sprite inspect <file.gif|.webp|.png|sheet.ogt> [--key auto|off|#rrggbb] [--tolerance T] [--out frames.png] [--json]` measures an animated sprite source, or a sheet built from them: frame count and delays, each frame's drawn bounds, centroid and coverage with their drift from the first frame, duplicate frames, the loop seam (last to first) beside the mean and largest frame-to-frame step, alpha levels and the edge fringe (edge and partial texels, the colour step to the interior and the distance to the background). Numbers only, no thresholds.

added.member: GraphDesc.sprite, og.AnimationGraph on og.Flipbook and og.Skeleton2D
added.summary: og.anim.graph(desc) with `sprite: true` builds a graph whose states name flipbook or rig2d clips; an og.AnimationGraph beside an og.Flipbook or og.Skeleton2D then drives it with the same states, parameters, transitions, interrupts and layers as a 3D skeleton. A flipbook cuts hard, only when the frame on screen ends (a transition's fade is ignored), keeping the phase within one state or sync group; a 2D skeleton cross-fades and blends its two heaviest leaves. The graph runs in the tick, its state is saved with the world and restored by snapshot. Off unless a graph is attached; existing games are unchanged.

A second clip sampled beside `clip` and mixed in by `blend` (0 to 1, slot draw order and attachments from the heavier clip); a graph sets them, a game may too. Defaults 0: the skeleton plays one clip as before.

A sprite draws through a material shader's hooks: og.Sprite.material takes a material from og.render.shaderMaterial, the same shader asset, material and og.render.setShaderParam a mesh uses. vertex_offset moves the quad's corners, surface_color changes its colour before the 2D light (an alpha of 0 cuts it: a dissolve), surface_emissive adds light after it. A shader of the new `mode sprite` runs on sprites only and may call `sprite_texel(uv)` to read its texture anywhere (distortion, chromatic splits); the cook validates it against the sprite module. Sprites of one material, texture and blend are one draw. A hooks shader that calls a lit-only helper draws its sprites plain and is named in dump_render's new spriteShaderErrors. 0 is none: existing sprites draw as before.

Destructible 2D ground of cells (Worms, Noita style): filled at its first tick (bedrock rows, then ground), collides chunk by chunk as its smoothed outline (static SHAPE_TRIMESH colliders on generated meshes), drawn as one sprite of its cells.
Ground an og.PixelTerrain lost (cut loose, thrown by a blast, broken off): a dynamic body colliding as the convex hull of its cells, drawn as its cells.
Sent for each piece of an og.PixelTerrain that breaks loose: its terrain, its og.PixelPiece (0 when under minPiece), cells, centre and cause.
Empty a round hole in an og.PixelTerrain this tick; what it cuts loose falls.
Make a round patch of an og.PixelTerrain solid (ground or bedrock) this tick.
A blast on every og.PixelTerrain in reach: a hole, the ring round it thrown as Voronoi pieces, loose pieces pushed outwards.
Break an og.PixelPiece (or an og.PixelTerrain's non-bedrock cells) into Voronoi pieces.
The og.PixelTerrain cell under a world point (0 empty, 255 bedrock, other ground).
PixelDetached.cause for ground carve2d cut loose.

A `.riv` under assets/ (format 7) is converted at cook time, never by the Rive runtime: each artboard its `<file>.riv.ogt` import settings choose (role, name, fit, align, state-machine) cooks to an og.RiveArtboard blob, id `<file>.riv#<Artboard>` (docs/ui.md §11.2). Phase 1 converts artboards, groups, shapes (points paths, rectangles, ellipses, triangles, polygons, stars), fills by both rules, centred strokes, solid, linear and radial paints, six blend modes, linear animations (hold, linear, cubic and value keys; loop, ping-pong, work areas), nested artboards and a state machine whose entry plays one animation. Luau, images, text and other state machines are cook errors that name the feature and object. og_ui::rive::Player plays one on the tick, draws it as UI paths, lists its objects as elements and saves and restores its state.

added.member: Effekseer import (og cook, og vfx import)
added.summary: An Effekseer effect (`.efkproj`, or the `.efkefc` that wraps the same project) is an asset: the cook converts its node tree into the engine's own `type vfx` with the `type particles` emitters, `type effect` materials and meshes it needs (sprites to emitters with their counts, spawn times, life, size and colour over life, fades, blend, texture, flipbook and UV scroll; rings to ring meshes with Effekseer's UVs and colours across; ribbons and tracks to trails; `.efkmodel` models to meshes), and loads under its own path (`og.load.vfx(world, "fx/slash.efkproj")`). `og vfx import <file> <out-dir>` writes the same conversion as `.ogt` text with copies of its textures, to edit. What the engine cannot express (triggers, force fields, f-curve paths, camera-facing rings, nested generation, ...) is a finding per node: a warning of the cook, a line of the import. No Effekseer runtime is embedded; the formats are read as Effekseer's MIT source writes them (third_party/effekseer).

How fast the air carries a dynamic body (per second, 0 by default: not at all): its velocity closes on the air's where it is, og.Wind and every og.WindMotor reaching it. A leaf, a balloon, a paper lantern or a 2D feather drifts on the wind and is thrown by a fan without game code; in still air it slows the body like linearDamping.

A motor now pushes in the tick as well as leaning vegetation: every og.Rope, og.Cloth and og.Garment hanging within its radius is blown by it, away from it (omni), along the entity's forward (directional, now with its vertical part: an updraft) or around it (vortex), and a body with RigidBody.airDrag is carried. Deterministic, in both profiles (a 2D vortex turns about z), and it needs neither og.Wind nor RenderCapabilities.compute. A game that kept a motor beside a rope or a cloth sees them move in it.
The enum of og.Collider.shape and ShapeDesc.shape: box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, convex, trimesh, heightfield, diamond, hexagon.
The enum of og.SoftBody.shape: sphere, box, mesh.
The enum of the simulation field of og.Cloth, og.Garment, og.SoftBody and og.Fluid3D: gameplay, visual.

The 2D half of the facing calls. face2d(position, target) is the rotation about +Z that turns a 2D thing's +X towards the target (their xy; the same point twice gives no turn), where og.transform.face points +Z at it and turns a sprite out of the plane. forward2d(quaternion) is the way a 2D thing faces: its local +X, as a unit vector.

The 2D heading of a rotation (radians about +Z from +X towards +Y, so half pi faces up) and the rotation of one. They replace math.atan2(forward.y, forward.x) and og.transform.fromAxisAngle({ x: 0, y: 0, z: 1 }, angle).

The heading an object faces (radians about +Y from +Z towards +X, so half pi faces +X) and the rotation of an upright object facing one: the pair the 2D calls are named after. They replace math.atan2(forward.x, forward.z) and og.transform.fromAxisAngle({ x: 0, y: 1, z: 0 }, heading).

One guide states the rules every member follows, once each: units (metres, kilograms, seconds; a time is seconds unless its name ends in Ms or Ticks), angles (radians but for fov, slopes, the sky, camera roll, post effects, styles and the art contract; a fov is the full angle and a cone its half), names (quaternion and rotation, layers and masks, damping, the input words), which way each grid's rows run, where an anchor and a pivot count from, colours and handles. Read it with `og api show conventions`.

The wheel's sign is stated in the fields' docs and in facing §3: Input.wheel and og.Wheel's deltaX and deltaY are the browser's, positive scrolling right and down (the wheel rolled towards the player), while an action's wheel.y control is up-positive, +1 a notch. The facing guide's input table also gains og.PointerMove's movementX and movementY (down positive).
The enum of og.Joint.kind: fixed, revolute, prismatic, spring, rope, ball.
The enum of og.Joint.motor: none, velocity, position.
The enum of og.Vehicle.drive: rear, front, all.
The enum of og.Vehicle.model: arcade, drivetrain.

The names the conventions guide states are kept by a test over every field of the API: a field in milliseconds is named ms or ends in Ms, one in ticks has Tick in its name, a Quaternion is named quaternion or ends in Quaternion, a rotation, heading or yaw with a unit is in radians, a fov and a slope are in degrees, and damping is a decay rate per second. The members that differ are listed there with their reasons: tick stamps (LockstepSeat.since and until, LockstepStatus.acknowledged, WorldRestored.from), ArtCamera.yaw (the art contract is in degrees), and the spring and reverb dampings (SpringBone.damping, Joint.damping, ReverbZone.damping).

A module lists its core members (the ones game code uses), `--all` every member; `--guide` shows a guide named like a module (physics, input, camera, audio, render); `og api show "saves §2"` prints one guide section.

New task guides: saves (and og.platform), physics (and character control), input, camera, audio, networking, render, loading, world and localization; start §5 is now a map from a task to its guide and functions.
Descriptions are shorter: workflow, sizes, timings and caveats moved to the guides, each entry ending "See `<guide> §N`."; large desc structs and records show their fields under group headings.
Reports descriptions over budget (600 characters for modules, functions and types, 300 for fields and the rest); `--budget` lists them.
Explicit starting values and tween timing; destination is captured at the call.
Captures the current destination before the delay; writes the explicit starting value at the first tween tick, not synchronously.
Starts a tween with explicit from/to endpoints, rejecting a missing from.
Typed cubic-bezier() and steps() strings share the deterministic timing parser on both hosts. Invalid tween text returns an error value; invalid timeline text is refused by the cook.

String enums support documented pattern alternatives with ${string} holes, emitted as TypeScript template literals and JSON Schema patterns. Numeric enum columns and explicit defaults retain fixed variants only.

With normals flat, neighbouring faces within this angle of their facet's normal shade as one facet, with one normal and one baked colour, so a gently curved ground reads as a few broad planes instead of a pattern of triangles. 0, the default, keeps every triangle its own facet.

Where a person would change a spawned entity (`src/enemies.ts:42`). Outside a publish build the runtime fills it with the game's own TypeScript line that called world.spawn (bun's mapping natively, the dev bundle's map in the web Worker), and pick and marks answer it as the entity's source. A given value wins.
capture takes fit (the longest side, 0 to keep it) and region (a box of the play surface in CSS px, cut at full resolution as its own image).

Set-of-Mark: the frame with a numbered box over each UI element and scene entity it shows, and a map from each number to its path, kind, text, box, a point to pick it at, the document or scene line that made it, and an element's style part and rule. Both hosts, og probe marks.
The run's events since the last read, each with its tick: inputs, command steps, screen changes (UiTree.screens), assertion events and expectations.

og render keeps the frames where something happened (the start, the end, each probe timeline event, a mean FLIP change from the last key frame) as keyframes/<index>.png fitted to 1280, a labelled sheet keyframes.png and timeline.json synced to ticks.
og api show captures: frames for a model, crops, marks, key frames and FLIP diffs.

og compare also measures NVIDIA's FLIP (a port of the reference LDR-FLIP, BSD-3-Clause, third_party/flip) of the render as compared against the reference: mean, p50, p95, p99 and max per pixel at --ppd pixels per degree (default the reference's observer, 67.02), a magma heat map (--flip, default <render>.flip.png) and up to --regions (default 4) worst regions, one per change and framed to its extent, each written as reference | render | heat enlarged to about 256 px a panel (<heat>-<n>.png). --json carries them as `flip`.

A frame that fails its reference also writes <scene>.flip.png (the FLIP heat map) and <scene>.flip-<n>.png (its three worst regions, reference | actual | heat enlarged) beside .actual.png and .diff.png, and the failure prints FLIP's mean, p95 and max with each region's box.

A character with og.Buoyancy wades and swims without a mode switch. Its `move` is slowed towards `waterSpeed` (0.5) of itself by how much of it is under, and `move`'s y is its stroke in the water: down it dives at that speed against any lift, up it rises to where it floats (or, where it sinks, to its head out of the water) and no higher. Wading is `grounded` with og.Buoyancy `submerged` above 0; swimming is not `grounded` with it above 0. A character with og.Buoyancy therefore moves slower in water than before: set `waterSpeed: 1` for the speed it had; a game that swam it with `gravityScale` 0 can leave gravity on and set `move`'s y instead.

`og check` names each material shader under assets/ whose mesh surface does not take something a scene can put on it: local lights, weather, decals, blending, the planar reflection, the screen AO or a lightmap. It reads the shader's lit module as the renderer builds it, the way the engine's own surface table is checked, so a `mode full unlit` shader lists the lights, weather and decals, and a `mode full lit` one the planar reflection and the lightmap. A warning (`--json`: a `shader-capabilities` event); the check still passes.

The cumulus casts its shadows on the world: on every lit surface, the water and the volumetric fog, along the sun's ray, drifting with the clouds. On by default: a scene with og.Clouds now stands in the sun or in a cloud's shadow as they pass, and its sun between the clouds is no longer dimmed by the share they hide. Set `shadows: 0` for the light as it was.

The cook times each of its stages (index, project, scan, import, resolve, contract, group, plan, execute, assemble, write, pack, finish, diagnose, save): `og cook --json` gains `stages`, a list of `{ name, ms }`, the Markdown report (`--report out.md`) a stages table, and `--report` prints them on one line. A cook that found nothing changed lists only `index`. Existing fields, cook-report.json and the slowest-assets lists are unchanged, and cooked output is byte-identical.

CSS 2 floats: float (left, right, inline-start, inline-end) and clear (left, right, both, inline-start, inline-end) in a block's flow. A float shrinks to fit and is shifted to its side as high as it fits, beside earlier floats or below them; the lines of a text beside it are shortened (a line no word fits moves below it); a box that starts a formatting context of its own (flow-root, flex, grid, an image, a scroller) is narrowed beside it or moved below it; clear places a box below the earlier floats on its sides; a flow-root holds its floats, a plain block does not and its floats reach the boxes after it.

added.member: UI: CSS writing-mode, text-orientation and text-combine-upright
added.summary: Document elements take `writing-mode` (`horizontal-tb`, `vertical-rl`, `vertical-lr`, `sideways-rl`, `sideways-lr`), `text-orientation` (`mixed`, `upright`, `sideways`) and `text-combine-upright` (`none`, `all`, `digits`), inherited. An element whose writing mode differs from its parent's lays out in a frame of its own, so block flow, flex, grid, tables, columns, floats and `clear`, insets, scrolling and the logical properties follow its axes; to its parent it is an orthogonal flow. Vertical text breaks and measures down its lines, stands CJK upright by the font's vertical metrics and forms and lays Latin sideways, and combines a short text into one em.

added.member: UI: vertical text selection, effects and justify; rich text down vertical lines
added.summary: Vertical text takes the player's selection (`user-select`), `::selection`'s color, decoration and shadows, the style's text glow and drop, and `text-align: justify` (at spaces, else between upright clusters). Rich text in a vertical writing mode runs down its columns with its spans' fonts, inks, outlines, pictures, icons and decorations, where it was a horizontal box.

added.member: UI: selection of vertical rich text
added.summary: Rich text in a vertical writing mode takes the player's selection (`user-select`): presses, drags and copies down its columns, its fill and `::selection`'s color.

added.member: UI: CSS background-color, background-position-x and -y, background-clip: border-area, and light-dark() images
added.summary: background-color sets an element's colour alone; background-position-x and background-position-y set one axis of each layer's position (an edge keyword with its offset, a length or a percentage), background-position resetting both; background-clip: border-area paints a layer only under the border (the border box less the padding box); a colour with a box in the background shorthand (#123 padding-box) is clipped by it; and light-dark(<image>, <image>) picks a background, mask or border image by the element's colour scheme.

added.member: UI: CSS object-fit on , object-position and image-rendering in documents
added.summary: object-fit takes fill, contain, cover, none and scale-down on (none and scale-down on too); object-position places the image as background-position is written, edge offsets included, and replaces 's focal point; image-rendering pixelated and crisp-edges (inherited) sample every image an element draws at the nearest texel.

added.member: og-render: UiImage offset and nearest, UiFit::ScaleDown
added.summary: UiImage.offset adds CSS px to where focal places a cover, contain or none image, UiImage.nearest samples the nearest texel of the top level whatever the texture's filter, UiFit::ScaleDown contains without scaling up, and a zero UiImage.size reads the region's own pixels from the texture.

added.member: UI: CSS contain, content-visibility and contain-intrinsic-size in documents
added.summary: contain takes size, inline-size, layout, style, paint, strict and content: size containment sizes a box as if empty or by contain-intrinsic-size, layout and paint make it a formatting context, paint clips its subtree, style scopes counters and quotes. content-visibility hidden skips its contents; auto skips them while far from the screen with no focus inside, sized by contain-intrinsic-size (auto: its last laid-out size).

added.member: UI: CSS resize and will-change in documents
added.summary: resize (both, horizontal, vertical, block, inline) on an element whose overflow is not visible puts a grab handle in its bottom end corner whose drag sets its width or height; will-change naming a property that makes a stacking context draws the element on a layer of its own.

added.member: UI: CSS cursor url() images shown on both hosts
added.summary: cursor: url(<icon or texture>) [<x> <y>], …, <keyword> now shows the first image that loads at its hotspot (an atlas icon by name or a texture by its asset handle, at most 128x128), the keyword where none does; images over auto stop the parent's keyword. og.ui's frame answer carries cursorImage when it changes and the web shell sets the canvas's CSS cursor from it. UiFrame gains cursor_images.

A window that sends {"CursorSubscribe":{"version":1}} after Hello hears {"Cursor":{"version":1,"keyword","image"}} once and whenever the UI's cursor changes; FrameLink::set_cursor hands it over. Nothing changes for a window that does not subscribe.

Every line box wraps around floats (CSS 2.1 §9.5): the lines of a block's inline-level boxes (inline-block, images, inline-flex and inline-grid boxes, texts) are filled one at a time into the room beside the floats, and a rich text's lines (::part runs, mixed inline elements) are broken one at a time at that room; a line whose first box or word does not fit moves below the floats. A block laying its children out in lines now takes part in its parent's formatting context, so a float inside it reaches the boxes after it.

overflow (clip, hidden, scroll, auto; overflow-x, overflow-y and the logical longhands) on ::view-transition-group() and ::view-transition-image-pair() clips the old and new images to that pseudo-element's box, turned with its transform. Unset, the images stay unclipped as in the spec's UA stylesheet.

Nested view-transition groups (CSS View Transitions 2): view-transition-group (normal, contain, nearest or an ancestor's view-transition-name) puts a shared element's group in an ancestor's ::view-transition-group-children(), drawn over that group's image pair. A nested group moves from where it was in the old parent's padding box to where it is in the new one, and its parent's box, transform, opacity and overflow carry it. ::view-transition-group-children() takes overflow (a clip to the group's padding box) and its own animation (nothing inherits into it).

Transitions and @keyframes animate every animatable property, interpolated by the CSS rules for its value types (lengths and calc(), colours through color-mix(), shadows, filters, transforms through decomposed matrices, gradients); discrete values flip halfway. Adds transition-behavior: allow-discrete, animation-composition (replace, add, accumulate, also per keyframe) and the reversing shortening of CSS Transitions. @starting-style is now the before-change style of an element's first style for every property a transition covers, not only the motion channels.

animation-timeline takes scroll(), view() and named timelines from scroll-timeline and view-timeline (with -name, -axis and view-timeline-inset longhands), seen across a subtree with timeline-scope; animation-range (-start, -end) takes normal, length-percentages and the named ranges cover, contain, entry, exit, entry-crossing and exit-crossing. A scroll-driven animation's time is its timeline's progress, so it moves with the scroller and costs nothing while the scroller rests. The animation shorthand now resets animation-timeline and animation-range, as in CSS.

added.member: UI: CSS alpha() and system colours
added.summary: alpha(from <colour> [/ <alpha>]) keeps a colour's channels in its own space and sets its alpha, `alpha` the origin's (alpha(from var(--panel) / calc(alpha / 2))). The CSS system colours are the style's palette roles: Canvas the backdrop, CanvasText, ButtonText, FieldText and MarkText the ink, AccentColor and AccentColorText the primary and its ink, ButtonFace and Field the control fill, ButtonBorder the strong line, GrayText the faint ink, Highlight and SelectedItem the selection, LinkText, VisitedText and ActiveText the highlight, and Mark the soft primary.

added.member: UI: CSS direction and unicode-bidi per element
added.summary: Document elements take `direction`, `unicode-bidi` and HTML's `dir` attribute (`ltr`, `rtl`, `auto`), inherited down the tree. A right-to-left element lays its flex rows, grid columns, columns and lines out from the right and aligns its start text there; logical margins, padding, borders, radii, insets, sizes and axes name the sides of each element's own direction. A declared direction sets its text's paragraph direction; `plaintext` and undeclared text keep the first strong character's, and the overrides lay text out unreordered.

@font-feature-values (CSS Fonts 4 §6.9) names values for font-variant-alternates' stylistic(), styleset(), character-variant(), swash(), ornaments() and annotation(), which set salt, ssNN, cvNN, swsh and cswh, ornm and nalt for a text whose family the rule lists.

Variable fonts: a face whose file has fvar and renders at run time is drawn at an instance (CSS Fonts 4 §7.2): wght from font-weight and wdth from font-stretch, each clamped to the face's declared range, opsz from the font size under font-optical-sizing: auto (the initial value), then font-variation-settings, inherited, which overrides them. The instance is measured, shaped and rendered at its location in pages of its own, from the frame after it first appears.

@font-face declares named font families: the cook bundles each url() source, and font-family (or the font shorthand) draws text in the first declared family, matched by font-style, font-weight range and unicode-range per CSS Fonts 4, falling back to the generic family's font role.

FontRole::Family(Family) names a document's @font-face family with a fallback role; Fonts::families holds its faces (FamilyFace, FaceStyle) and FontMetrics::with_range limits a face to its unicode-range.

font-family's optional generic families follow CSS Fonts 4 §2.1.3: system-ui and ui-sans-serif take the style's body face, ui-monospace and ui-rounded its own mono and rounded faces, and where the style has no face that suits one (always for ui-serif and math) the family list goes on to its next family.

Text is shaped in its language (CSS Fonts 4 §6.13): the element's lang attribute, inherited, or the OpenType language system font-language-override names, so a face's locl forms apply (Romanian Ș for Ş in Noto Sans), in Parley-laid paragraphs as well. Features carries the language (Features::with_language, Features::language), and og_text::shape::language_of_tag maps an OpenType language tag to the BCP 47 language HarfBuzz shapes in it.

@font-face size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override (CSS Fonts 5 §11.3, §11.4) apply to the face: size-adjust draws it that much larger with its advances, extents and x-height, ascent and descent overrides replace its extents (where its baseline sits), and any override sets line-height: normal in it to ascent + descent + line gap (1.2 otherwise). FontMetrics gains normal_line, scaled() and with_overrides(), at_rules::FontFace the four descriptors and metrics(), TextCss step_in().

font-palette takes palette-mix() (CSS Fonts 4 §9.1), mixing palettes entry by entry as color-mix() mixes colours, and font-palette transitions and @keyframes interpolate through it in OKLab. An instance (a variable location or a palette) whose font the host has not made yet draws with the nearest one made instead of blank, so an animated palette or axis stays on screen.

font-palette and @font-palette-values (CSS Fonts 4 §9): a run-time colour font (color true, runtime true) is drawn in the CPAL palette font-palette picks: light, dark, or a named @font-palette-values rule for the text's family with its base-palette and override-colors. The text is drawn with an instance of the font whose colour glyphs the host paints in that palette from the frame after it first appears.

font-size-adjust (CSS Fonts 5 §2.5) draws each face of a text at the size where its x-height, or the cap-height, ch-width, ic-width or ic-height named, is the given number of the text's size; from-font matches every face to the first's own value, so a fallback face is drawn to match its text. Advances scale with the face in plain and rich text. FontQuery gains size_adjust (FontQuery::with_size_adjust, og_text::text::SizeAdjust), FontMetrics a per-face scale and aspect(), and Piece a scale its text is drawn at, which a draw command's size multiplies.

font-stretch and font-width pick an @font-face family's face by width (CSS Fonts 4 §5.2: at or under normal the narrower faces first, over it the wider), from the @font-face font-stretch or font-width descriptor (one width or a range), before style and weight; the text is measured in the face it draws.

font-variant-emoji (CSS Fonts 4 §6.12) picks the face an emoji character both a text face and a colour face have is drawn in: emoji the colour face, text the text face, unicode and normal by its Emoji_Presentation (⌚ as emoji, © as text). A variation selector in the text wins: U+FE0F draws the character before it as emoji, U+FE0E as text. FontQuery gains emoji (FontQuery::with_emoji) and FontMetrics an emoji presentation (EmojiStyle).

font-variant-caps and font-variant-position are synthesised where the face lacks their forms (CSS Fonts 4 §6.3, §6.5): a small capital is drawn as its capital at 80 % of the size, letter by letter, and a super- or subscript run whose face lacks the form of any of its characters is drawn whole at 82 % (two-thirds from 45 px) and raised a third or lowered a fifth of the size. font-synthesis-small-caps and font-synthesis-position: none turn it off. Synth gains small_caps and position (Synth::ALL), og_text's FontFile has_variant().

added.member: UI: CSS opacity percentages, clip: rect(), SVG paint-order and mask-type
added.summary: opacity takes a percentage (opacity: 40%). CSS 2's clip: rect(<top>, <right>, <bottom>, <left>) cuts an absolutely positioned element to that rectangle of its border box (edges from its top and left, auto the box's edge; clip-path wins over it). paint-order on an SVG shape, set or inherited, draws its stroke and markers in the order given (paint-order: stroke draws the stroke under the fill). A <mask>'s mask-type="alpha" cuts by its content's alpha rather than its luminance.
::selection takes color, text-decoration and text-shadow beside background-color: selected text in labels and fields is drawn in the selection's ink, lines and shadows.

Document CSS nests rules and takes @layer, @supports, @scope, @import (cooked into the document blob), @starting-style, @property, @font-face, @counter-style and @position-try; inherit, initial, unset, revert and revert-layer work on every property.

Document CSS takes ::before, ::after, ::marker, ::first-letter, ::first-line, ::placeholder, ::selection and ::file-selector-button, generated content (content with strings, attr(), counter(), counters() and quotes), counter-reset, counter-increment, counter-set, quotes, @counter-style counter styles, and list-style-image.

Document @media takes prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, prefers-reduced-transparency and resolution (from the theme and viewport) and answers forced-colors, color-gamut, dynamic-range, display-mode, update, scripting and color for the play surface. @container takes style() and scroll-state() queries, container-type takes scroll-state and anchored, and the cqw, cqh, cqi, cqb, cqmin and cqmax units size against the nearest container.

Document CSS selectors: :has(), :nth-of-type()/:nth-last-of-type(), :first-/last-/only-of-type, :lang(), :dir(), :state(), the form, open, popover and :target states, :defined, :scope, :any-link, and the ~= |= ^= $= *= attribute operators with i and s flags. lang, dir, data-* and state:name are selector attributes.
@keyframes may be nested in @media and @container. The last definition of a name whose conditions hold plays; switching to another definition restarts the animation, as an animation-name change does.

Container queries: container-type (size, inline-size), container-name, the container shorthand and @container conditions on width, height, inline-size, block-size, aspect-ratio and orientation. They settle before paint on the first frame and on resize, for pushed and mounted documents, and can change display, list and grid boxes and Rive frames. Unsupported container features, style queries and container units fail at cook with the name.

The CSS box model. width and height take auto, min-content, max-content and fit-content(<length>), and the logical inline-size and block-size map to them. min-/max- bounds (and their logical forms) take lengths, percentages, math functions and content sizes on any size, and a bound alone no longer turns a block into a fit-content box. aspect-ratio takes a / b and auto, box-sizing takes content-box (border-box stays the default), and padding takes its longhands and the logical padding-block and padding-inline.

CSS Display: every display value, single and multi-keyword. inline, inline-block, inline-flex, inline-grid and inline-table lay an element out in its parent's lines (baseline-aligned, by text-align, vertical-align top, middle or bottom), each block-level sibling on a line of its own; flow-root keeps its children's margins inside; contents drops the box and hands its children to its parent's layout. display: table and its parts (row groups, rows, cells, captions with caption-side, columns) lay a table out by CSS 2 §17 and HTML's table model, reading colspan and rowspan. New vertical-align and caption-side properties. display on an element that is not a box now takes block, inline, inline-block and flow-root as well as none; flex, grid, table and contents stay a box's.

CSS Flexbox: flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis and flex-flow lay items out by the CSS flex algorithm; row-reverse, column-reverse and wrap-reverse, and wrapping columns; every justify-content, align-items and align-self keyword with safe and unsafe; align-content (normal stretching a wrapping box's lines), justify-items, justify-self and the place-* shorthands; order; row-gap, column-gap and a two-value gap. flex is no longer refused; width: stretch keeps working.

CSS Grid: track lists with line names, repeat() and repeat(auto-fill | auto-fit); min-content, max-content, fit-content() and minmax() of any two sizes, sized by the CSS track sizing algorithm; subgrid and masonry; grid-auto-columns and grid-auto-rows; the grid, grid-template and grid-area shorthands; grid-column-start, -end and grid-row-start, -end with line numbers, negative lines, line names, area names and named spans, and implicit tracks on either side. justify-content and align-content align a grid's tracks, and justify-items, justify-self, align-items and align-self align its items in their areas.

CSS Position 3: position: relative and sticky; the physical insets left and right, the inset, inset-block and inset-inline shorthands and every logical inset, each in px, % of the containing block, auto or anchor(). CSS Anchor Positioning 1: anchor-name, position-anchor (else the implicit anchor), anchor() and anchor-size() (alone or in calc()), position-area, position-try-fallbacks with flips, @position-try rules and position-areas, position-try-order, the position-try shorthand, and position-visibility. The house -og-anchor, -og-anchor-at and -og-anchor-self stay valid.

CSS Values 4 and 5 units and math: the physical units (cm, mm, Q, in, pt, pc), the small, large and dynamic viewport units (svh, lvw, dvmin and the rest, with vi and vb), the small and large ones read from the web shell's measure of the page's 100svh and 100lvh (new optional Viewport.smallWidth, smallHeight, largeWidth and largeHeight; the surface's own size on native hosts), the font-relative units ch, ex, cap, ic, lh and rlh with their root forms, and em in every length (not only margins). round() with its strategies, mod(), rem(), abs(), sign(), the trigonometric functions, pow(), sqrt(), hypot(), log() and exp(), with e, pi, infinity and NaN. grad joins the angles. env() takes the safe-area insets (a safe-area change re-resolves what reads them), and attr() reads an element's attribute, with HTML data-* attributes now kept for it and for attribute selectors. min(), max(), clamp(), round(), mod(), rem(), abs() and hypot() over % mixed with px are evaluated at layout.

transition and animation follow CSS Transitions and Animations Level 1: transition-property lists with per-property duration, delay and timing function, all, several animations per element with delay, iteration-count (including infinite), direction, fill-mode and play-state, and @keyframes with percentage stops and per-keyframe animation-timing-function. Rules choose animations through selectors, state and media. Motion runs on presentation ticks, is saved outside world_hash and restores exactly; reduced motion shows a finite animation's end and stops endless ones.

CSS Multi-column Layout 1: columns, column-count, column-width, column-gap, column-fill (balance, balance-all, auto), column-span: all and column-rule with its longhands. The flow breaks between children and between a paragraph's lines (two kept on each side); break-before, break-after and break-inside (and page-break-*) control the breaks.

Sibling combinators (+, ~) and structural pseudo-classes (:first-child, :last-child, :only-child, :nth-child(an+b [of S]), :nth-last-child(an+b [of S]), :empty) match the instantiated element tree after {#if}, keyed {#each}, snippets and components. Retained mounts invalidate only the affected sibling interval; virtualized rows restyle when they materialize. :has() still fails cooking with the selector named.

A decal now marks the scattered copies (og.TerrainScatter), their far cards, a crowd's far cards and the grass (og.Grass) that stand in its box, as it marks a mesh and the terrain: a scorch mark or a painted zone no longer stops at the plants. A blade of grass takes the decal of the ground it stands on.

Snow, wetness and puddle gloss now lie on scattered copies (og.TerrainScatter), their far cards and a crowd's far cards as they lie on a mesh, so rocks and trees placed by scatter whiten and darken with the ground around them.

The design tokens are authored as CSS: packages/design/tokens/*.css, custom properties on :root named by their path (--motion-duration-fast), one file per surface, with a :root[data-scheme=dark] block for what the dark scheme changes. tokens.json is now generated from them (same keys, values and group notes as `_doc`, the notes taken from the comments over each group's tokens; keys sorted; new tokens added) and the package ships both.

The determinism lint runs for every game, not only one that sets og.Lockstep, and reports more: Math.random and crypto.randomUUID, Date.now, performance.now and new Date(), setTimeout, setInterval and requestAnimationFrame (OG9006), Math's approximated functions and ** with a non-integer exponent, and what reaches outside the host ABI: fetch, WebSocket, XMLHttpRequest, EventSource, navigator.sendBeacon, localStorage, sessionStorage and indexedDB (OG9005). Each is a warning naming its replacement (og.Time, og.Rng, math, og.platform, og.load) and never fails the check; a line that only draws keeps it with // og-ok (// lockstep-ok still works). The JSON event is still lockstep-lint and gains lockstep: whether the game sets og.Lockstep.

A material shader's hooks read og.Wind as the frame draws it: `h.wind`, xyz where it blows (horizontal, normalised), w its strength (0 without og.Wind). It is the same in the lit, prepass and shadow passes, and the previous drawn frame's where the prepass evaluates the previous position for motion vectors. A game whose own shaders sway with one wind sets og.Wind once instead of a shader parameter on every material. A garden of 1072 cells while it gusts, per 10 s: setShaderParam calls 328,860 -> 54,327, writeBuffer calls 279,918 -> 5,640, Renderer::sync 341 -> 25 ms.
RenderOptions.without can leave out the caustics a water surface casts on what lies below it (og.Water.caustics), which every lit shader carries.

A list of optional lit features (LitFeature: surfaceWeather, gi, areaLights, decals) to build no lit shader with. Empty, the default, builds every one as before. Each one left out is in no lit pipeline the renderer makes, on native and on the web: its code, which every lit and prepass pipeline compiled behind a runtime test whether or not a scene used it, is folded away, so those pipelines compile faster and draw a little faster. It is not drawn: a scene that uses it draws as if it did not, and the log says so once.
The optional lit features RenderOptions.without can leave out: the weather on surfaces, the probes of GlobalIllumination, rect lights and decals.
The lit features the renderer was made without (RenderOptions.without); empty by default and without a renderer.

Cooks no meshlet clusters into the models: the blobs keep neither the `clusters` table nor the second index stream (`cluster_indices`). For a game whose frames are never culled on the GPU (under the default culling, below 16,384 instances), which never draws them. Such a model draws on the per-instance path in every frame, under any culling, with the same levels and the same simulation mesh. `clusters true` is the default and leaves every cooked byte as it was; turning it off re-cooks the models. A garden of 1072 cells: about 36 MB (brotli) fewer to download.

Tilt-shift depth of field, the miniature look: above 0 the sharp band is a strip across the middle of the image, this fraction of its height above and below the centre line, instead of a range of depths, so it holds whatever the camera's distance; the blur grows above the strip as far and below it as near, to dofMaxBlur at dofTiltShift times (1 + dofFalloff) past its edge. 0 focuses by depth as before.

Composed effects (og.load.vfx) og.destruction plays as an og.Vfx where each island breaks loose and at each hit that damages the prop, beside breakFx and hitFx: dust, grit, a sound and a shake in one file, each ended by og.vfx. 0, the default, plays none.
Called outside a system, it registers og.Vfx and og.VfxEvent (as naming them would), so what plays the effect for the game, such as og.destruction's breakVfx, may write og.Vfx.

A component that draws a mesh (a geometry handle) with an effect material (og.load.effect) at its entity: a shield dome, a portal's swirl, a slash arc. The material's curves run on its `life` (0 to 1, which the game or a tween drives); `color`, `opacity`, `seed` and `blend` as a composed effect's mesh element. Without a geometry or a material it draws nothing.

New guide effect-files: every line an emitter (`type particles`), an effect material (`type effect`) and a composed effect (`type vfx`) takes, with its arguments, default and the elements that take it, written from the tables the parsers read, so the guide and the parsers never disagree. loading §5 and §11 point to it instead of their partial tables; the emitter's `events` line is documented for the first time.

An emitter's `forceFields <0..1>` makes its world-space particles take that share of the og.ForceField acceleration where each one is (1: as a body does), on the GPU and CPU paths alike: smoke lifted by an updraft, sparks swirled by a vortex, embers drawn to a radial pull. Only bodies, ropes, cloths, fluids and characters felt the fields before. Default 0, so existing particles do not move.

New guide effects, the entry for effects: which tool to use for what (an effect pack, a pixel effect, a composed effect, one emitter, a trail, a beam, a decal, a screen effect, a hit stop and a shake, and which of the several sprite-sheet, dissolve and distortion paths), a composed effect written from nothing with its emitter and effect material and previewed with og vfx preview, how to choose elements, and the budget an effect is held to (a one-shot effect's peak 0.5 ms, a looping one 0.2 ms, everything on screen 1.5 to 2 ms on the reference host).

A converted Effekseer one-shot effect (by `og vfx import` or by the cook, from an `.efkproj` or `.efkefc` in assets/) now has an `impact`: the frame in its first 60% where the most is added to the picture at once, so it sends og.VfxEvent `impact` where it hits. `og vfx import --hit` also adds a light in the colour of what starts there and a camera shake by its size. Looping effects get neither.

The 323 Effekseer effects of the starter and the ten contributor packs are converted again with the new particle lines: uneven sizes, upright, flat and velocity-aligned sprites, camera-facing rings, two-colour random colours, per-particle trails, subtractive and multiply blends. What the conversion could not carry fell from 5765 findings to 3305. Every one-shot effect now sends an `impact` og.VfxEvent where most of it starts; the hit-spark, explosion and magic-impact ones also flash a light and shake the camera there. Reinstall a pack (`og vfx add`) to take them.

An emitter's `align upright [<x> <y> <z>]` stands its particles on an axis of the emitter, turned about it to face the eye (flames and pillars that do not tip over as the camera pitches), and `align facing <x> <y> <z>` lays them across one whatever the camera (`facing 0 1 0`: a shockwave flat on the ground); their rotation and height turn within that plane. Both simulation paths and mesh particles take them; sprite mode, which is 2D, faces the camera as before. `og vfx import` writes them for Effekseer's y-axis and fixed sprites and `align velocity` for its directional ones, all of which it drew facing the camera (1241 of the packs' conversion notes).

added.member: og.EffectMesh.billboard, type vfx mesh face camera
added.summary: A `face camera` line on a `type vfx` mesh element, and `og.EffectMesh.billboard`, turn an effect mesh to face the eye with its scale and spin kept (a glow ring seen from any side). `og vfx import` writes it for Effekseer's billboard rings, which it drew in their own plane (150 of the packs' conversion notes).

added.member: particles and effect materials: blend subtractive, blend multiply
added.summary: A `blend` line in a particles, effect or vfx mesh file takes `subtractive` (its colour taken away from what is behind at its alpha: dark smoke over a bright sky, a void) and `multiply` (what is behind tinted by its colour, mixed towards none as its alpha falls: scorch, a shadow under a spell). Both are order independent and draw on billboards, mesh particles and effect meshes on both simulation paths; sprite mode refuses them and a trail, ribbon or beam blends them as alpha. `og vfx import` keeps Effekseer's subtractive and multiplicative sprites, models and rings, which it drew alpha blended.

An emitter's `collision` line takes `die` (`collision 0.3 colliders die`): a particle dies where it first hits, on both simulation paths and in sprite mode, with a death event there that a `subEmitter death` splash or gameplay reads. Rain that stops at the ground, sparks that go out where they land. Without it particles bounce as before.

An emitter's `heightOverLife` curve scales a particle's height alone over its life (along its own up, or the velocity when stretched; a mesh particle's y), on both simulation paths and in sprite mode: a flame tall and narrow, a shockwave flat and wide. Left out, the height is the width, so existing emitters draw as before. `og vfx import` writes it for Effekseer sprites scaled unevenly, which it drew square at their mean (840 of the packs' conversion notes).

An emitter's `randomColorOverLife { key ... }` is a second colour curve: each particle's colour lies between it and `colorOverLife` at a share of its own (Unity's random between two gradients), on both simulation paths and in sprite mode: embers from orange to deep red, confetti. Left out, every particle takes `colorOverLife` as before. `og vfx import` writes it for Effekseer's random colours, from each channel's least to its most, which it drew at their mean (728 of the packs' conversion notes).

An emitter's `trail <seconds> [<width>] [only]` draws a trail behind each particle: the path it took over the last <seconds>, remembered at eight points, a camera-facing strip in the particle's colour (and effect material) narrowing and fading to its tail, its width a share of the particle's; `only` draws the trails without the particles (a spark's streak, a comet). Billboards and mesh particles on both simulation paths; not sprite mode or sub-emitters' particles.

A quality field: every particle system's emission times this (0 to 1, default 1), each emitter kept above it where it would otherwise have fewer than 8 particles alive at once, so a flash, a ring or a handful of embers stays whole. The low preset (og.render.applyQuality) now writes 0.5, so low draws busy effects with about half their particles; medium and high write 1, and frames at the default do not change. Drawing only: particle events and collisions are the full emitter's.

The engine bundles a third vfx pack, realistic-starter: seven realistic type vfx effects for 3D games written for the engine (a muzzle flash, a bullet impact, an explosion, the dust of something breaking, a water splash, a looping torch fire and looping dust in the air), on greyscale Kenney Particle Pack textures (CC0). Their smoke and dust are lit, blend alpha, fade into the scene and drift with og.Wind; sparks, chips and droplets bounce off or die on the drawn depth; each one-shot sends its impact at its first frame. `og vfx add realistic-starter` installs it; `og api show effect-packs` lists it.

captures §6 says how to capture an effect (its preview sheet, or og render's frames around the moment it plays) and which three moments to look at; art-review §7 says what to look for in an effect's frames: shapes that show the quad, blown-out colour, timing, scale and reading, and agreement with the game's other effects.

Loads an effect material from a cooked `.ogt` of `type effect` (the files emitters and composed effects name with `effect`), with its textures and hook shader, once per path. Its EffectMaterial handle goes in og.Trail.effect and og.Beam.effect.
A trail or beam drawn with an effect material (og.load.effect) instead of its texture: scrolling, eroding and fresnel strips such as a sword's slash. 0, the default, draws as before.
An entity the beam's far end follows each frame instead of `end` (a tether, a laser on its mark). 0, the default, uses `end`; a beam whose target is despawned is not drawn.

An emitter's `shape mesh box | sphere | tetrahedron | "<model id>"` births its particles on a mesh's surface (a model's first mesh, in the emitter's space), area weighted and moving along its normals: a statue crumbling to embers, a glow over a sword. The renderer had the shape; particles files could not name it. The model is checked and loaded as `render mesh`'s is.

A particles file's `sheet <columns> <rows> <frames> life <cycles> | fps <n> blend` cross-fades each flipbook frame into the next as it plays, so a 16-frame smoke or fire sheet rolls smoothly instead of stepping; a sheet played once holds its last frame rather than fading back to the first. Billboards on the GPU and CPU paths; refused with `off`, `random` or sprite mode. Without `blend`, sheets draw as before.

A `track vfx` keys composed effects: `effect "fx/hit.ogt"`, optional `at "<entity>"` (played as its child), `position`, `scale` and `seed`. From its key the effect plays as an og.Vfx the timeline owns; a seek into it joins it mid-way without resending the events, shakes and sounds already passed, and a seek out of it, og.timeline.stop and the timeline's end remove it. The cook refuses a vfx track naming an effect the bundle lacks.

RenderSettings.maxVfx and maxVfxParticles cap the composed effects (og.Vfx) drawn at once and the particle slots among their emitters: 64 and 65536 by default, 32 and 32768 on the low preset, 128 and 131072 on high. Past either, the oldest one-shot effects are left out first, then the oldest looping ones; the probe's dump_render reports `vfx: { drawn, dropped }`. Drawing only: the effects' events, shakes and sounds still come, and their entities stay. Scenes within the limits draw as before.

A model that says `conform effect` (an effect's mesh, in its import settings or `type model` text) is held to no face budget: the cook neither simplifies it nor warns of it, and og style check skips its faces. og vfx import writes it beside every mesh it makes, and an Effekseer project in assets/ gives its meshes the same.

A vfx `mesh ring` element takes its own shape: `inner <radius>`, `band <0..1>`, `height <outer> <inner>` (a cone, a tube), `arc <start> <length>`, `segments <n>` and `colors <outer rgba> <band rgba> <inner rgba>`, built at load with u along its arc and v across it. A plain `mesh ring` draws as before. og vfx import writes Effekseer rings this way instead of a .glb per ring node.

`subEmitter life "<emitter id>" [<inherit velocity>]`: each particle runs the other emitter's own emission (its rate, bursts, duration and looping) from its birth while it lives, born where the particle is at each tick (Unity's Birth sub-emitter, Niagara's particle-spawned emitters). It runs on the CPU path like the other sub-emitters and is deterministic per tick.

Every vfx element takes `move <x> <y> <z>` (metres per second) and `accelerate <x> <y> <z>`, which carry it from its offset from its start. An emitter spawns along the path, and a mesh, trail or light goes with it.

A cooked environment with `sun extract` in its .ogt has the image's sun taken out of the map and stored as a light: og.load.environmentSun answers its direction, colour and intensity for the og.DirectionalLight that puts it back, so the sun is counted once, casts shadows and leaves no speckle in rough reflections. Without the key a map cooks with its sun in it, as before.

Rain and snow bring their sky: og.Clouds closes to the weather's cover as `intensity` builds, and under a procedural sky with no og.Clouds the weather draws a deck of its own, so it no longer rains from a clear sky with sharp sun shadows. `dim: 0` keeps the sky and the light as they were. The deck costs what og.Clouds costs.
Ramping `intensity` builds or clears a weather smoothly: it changes the share of the particles born and keeps those in the air. A change used to restart the particles.

One wind for the world: vegetation, clouds, rain and snow, and ropes, cloths and garments all move in og.Wind's direction and speed, so a game sets the wind once instead of keeping five fields in step.

The command channel's `intent:<Event>[:<fields JSON>]` sends a gameplay intent through og.input.intent's recorded input path for the next tick, its fields from the JSON and the rest at their defaults: a script (a playtest, og explore's repro) plays what a UI button sends.

probe.observe(records?, types?) reads the game's resources and components (by default every record the game declared; at most 256 entities a component, named ones by name) as plain values, with their reflected field types on request: one cheap read of the state, for a tool that abstracts it (og explore's cells).
GameDesc.explore (ExploreDesc: cells, ignore, actions, intents) tells `og explore` what a cell reads and which inputs it presses; the engine and the world never read it.
The rotation that turns an object to face a target (its +Z towards it), beside og.transform.lookAt for cameras and lights.
