og.transform.forward, right and up give an object's directions from its rotation; og.transform.cameraForward and cameraRight give a camera's or a light's.
A two-axis action as a horizontal world vector seen from a camera: W walks into the screen wherever the camera has orbited. The `facing` guide states the axes once.

A built-in screen for og.film's choice window: the choices, a bar of the time left, the one taken outlined (also once the window locks), stacked on a phone. Write its stores open, choices, left and locked from og.film.view; its choose action reports the choice's index as the row key.

A film choice tagged `#hotspot:<id>` is also taken by clicking that hotspot on the picture: a segment's `track hotspot` gives each `id` a `rect x y width height` (fractions of the video frame) that moves between its keys, or `off true` to end it. FilmView.hotspots gives the hotspots of the window's enabled choices. A choice tagged `#qte:press:<action>`, `#qte:hold:<action>:<ms>` or `#qte:mash:<action>:<presses>` is taken by that og.input action in the window (one press, held that long, or that many presses; a hold let go starts again); og.film counts it and FilmView.qtes gives each one's progress. Only a node's first 8 choices may be a QTE. The cook refuses a `#hotspot` id its segment has no key for, a `#qte` that is none of the forms, and a QTE past the eighth choice.

`track hotspot { key <t> { id "<id>" rect <x> <y> <w> <h> } }`: from its key the hotspot `id` covers `rect` (fractions of the video frame from its top left), moving linearly to the same id's next key and held after its last until a key `off true`. Nothing draws it; og.film offers a `#hotspot:<id>` choice there. The kind joins TimelineTrackInfo.kind.

Skips the playing segment to its window's open (film.open) when that is ahead, else to its cut, which takes the pending or default choice: for replaying a seen segment. Command film:skip. Refused once the film has ended.

A film node headed `og-film-dissolve: <seconds>` (0 to 5) dissolves its segment in over the one before, which plays on under it for that long: og.Film.previous, dissolve and dissolveLeft, FilmView.previous (the old picture) and mix (the new one's opacity over it). Without the header the cut is hard.

A prepared dialogue's film nodes laid out as a flowchart: FilmChart.nodes (each with its depth, the fewest film nodes from the start, and an x and y in NodeGraph units) and links (where each node may lead, through logic nodes, with the choice index and an SVG curve). The built-in film-flowchart screen draws it.

added.member: UI: film-flowchart, film-chapters and film-gallery screens
added.summary: film-flowchart draws og.film.chart with the built-in NodeGraph (the story so far, seen nodes marked). film-chapters lists og.film.load's chapters as cards to play from, locked until reached. film-gallery lists its endings the same way. film-choices now draws a choice's hotspot over the picture and a quick-time event's progress under its choice.

Interactive film (guide film): a Yarn dialogue whose nodes headed `og-film: <timeline>` each play a segment, a timeline with one video track of its own. og.film.load prepares a loaded dialogue, og.film.start plays it on up to three decks (one plays, the others hold the segments the current node may lead to on their first frame), og.film.view answers the picture, the choices and the window, og.film.choose takes a choice between the segment's `film.open` and `film.lock` markers, and at `film.cut` (else its end) the choice, else the `#default`, is taken. Snapshots carry it all. Events og.FilmSegment, og.FilmChoice, og.FilmChapter, og.FilmEnded; commands film:choose:<index>, film:play, film:pause.

The cook refuses a dialogue og.film plays when a film node's segment is missing, has other than one video track of its own or its markers out of order, two of a node's choices are #default, a film node says Yarn lines, or a node without a segment offers choices.

Fog of war. og.SightMap lays a grid over the og.Volume on its entity (the ground's x and z, or x and y with plane flat in a 2D world); og.Sight is a team's eyes and og.SightBlocker beside an og.Volume stops them, by symmetric shadow casting. The map is cast as each tick starts and is world state: saved, restored and hashed. og.sight.visible and og.sight.explored answer for a team and a point, og.sight.reveal and og.sight.forget change what is explored, and the renderer draws the same cells over the lit frame for og.SightMap.team: seen ground as it is, explored ground dimmed, the rest covered. A world that names none of them keeps its type table and hash.

Fog inside the og.Volume on its entity: mist in a hollow, smoke in a room, the haze a lamp's shaft shows in, lit by the sun through its shadows and by the point, spot and rect lights. It needs no og.Fog and adds to a volumetric one; the 16 nearest the camera are drawn.

An acceleration on what is inside the og.Volume on its entity, whatever its mass: a low-gravity room, a jump pad, a gravity well, a whirlpool. Dynamic bodies, ropes, cloths, garments, soft bodies and fluids take it and a character controller takes its vertical part, the same on every run.

`key auto <tolerance> holes` also keys enclosed pockets of the background colour that the border flood does not reach (the magenta inside a slash arc); `og sprite inspect --holes` measures the same and its report counts texels near the key that are still drawn (`nearKey`).
A `source` block takes `scale`, multiplied by the sheet's, so a clip drawn larger than the others is brought to their size.

`crop each` cuts every source to its own drawn bounds and shelf-packs the cells into one atlas, each with its own pivot: loose PNGs become one sheet. The cook note reports the packed size and the drawn share.

Snow and sand lying on a terrain (og.Weather) keep a track where an og.GrassPusher walked: packed darker, its sides shaded as a hollow, filling in over four minutes. Bare ground and a pusher passing above the cover keep none. Drawn only, where the renderer has compute.

Hair on the physical material: `hair: 1` shades the surface as strands running along v (roots at the top of the image, turned by `anisotropyRotation` and `anisotropyMap`) in place of the glossy and the diffuse lobe. A white highlight lies in a band across the strands, a second in the hair's `color` nearer the tips, and `roughness` is how wide they are. With a `thickness` the light behind comes through, once through every strand on its way: all over a card drawn from both sides, at the rim of a closed head of hair. The sun, point and spot lights take it, in the lit pass on every backend.

Eyes on the physical material: `irisRadius` (the iris's radius in uv, round the centre of the uv square) puts the base colour within it under the cornea, `irisDepth` radii deep at its middle. It is seen refracted by `ior`, so the iris has depth, shifts against the white of the eye as the eye turns and stays in view from the side. The cornea's reflection is the clear coat.

A scene with an `hlod { size error texels }` block has its `static` models merged by the cook into a tree of simplified, textured proxies, and the frame draws a proxy in place of every model under it once its measured error is under a pixel (the rule a model's own levels follow, moved by RenderSettings.lodBias): a distant town is a handful of draws. Presentation only: the models stay in the world, and one that is despawned, hidden, moved, tinted or flashed returns its node to its models. A cell's sub-scene draws its proxies at the cell while it is not loaded. Skinned, impostor, cut-out, fractured and GPU-instanced models keep drawing themselves, counted by reason in `og cook --report` (cook-report.json's `hlod`, with the tree and each proxy's triangles, texels and error). `dump_render` gains `hlod` (proxies drawn, models replaced) and `dump_entity` `render.hlod`; `debugView lod` tints the proxies the regular path draws blue. The world guide, §5.

`impostorBelow true` beside `impostor true` bakes the impostor's views from under the model's horizon too (the atlas twice as wide), for a model seen from below: on a cliff over the camera, hanging, flying.
A swaying model drawn as its impostor sways too, in the wind every vegetation tier reads; its card was still.

An expect: or invariant: comparison's value may be `$<path>`, another path of the same source read when it is evaluated (`state:coins<=$total`, `entity:hero:Health.hp<=$Health.max`); a plain value is still taken as written.

The assertions' per-tick stream: each site's first firing, each each-bucket's first holding and each site's first violation, with its tick, since the last read (assert.AssertEvents). `og run --json` prints them as `{"event":"assert","outcome","tick",...}` lines as they happen, before the summary.

A plant's leaves and petals thin with distance: the cook gives leaf cards two more levels of a half and a quarter of the leaves, each kept one larger so the crown covers as much (an oak's leaves are 34 000, 17 000 and 8 500 triangles). Plants and glTF leaf cards cook again; a model with fewer than 16 leaves is unchanged.

A scattered mesh draws its coarser levels with distance: the coarsest whose error is under 2 pixels on screen, under 8 in shadows, reflections and probes, moved by RenderSettings.lodBias as a model's are. A wood drawn as meshes to 200 m took 7.1 ms of GPU a frame at 720p on an M4 Pro against 10.9, and 4.9 against 9.4 with impostors from 30 m.

Scene changes with their assets fetched first: og.scene.preload loads a scene (a GameDesc.scenes name or an asset id) and asks for every streaming group it declares, og.scene.progress answers how much of them has arrived (bytes, received, fraction, ready, the groups still waiting), og.scene.change puts it in place as the next tick starts (the scene before it despawned with its descendants, what the game spawned kept) and sends og.SceneChanged, and og.scene.current names the scene in place. A change asked for is og.SceneState, world state: a save taken between the call and the tick carries it. A world that never changes scene registers nothing.

The loading screen as one API on every host: project.ogt `publish { loading engine | game | page }` (written by og build) says who draws it, og.loading.stage reports a stage with a fraction and a label, og.loading.idle says the renderer has nothing left to compile or upload, og.loading.done ends it once, and og.loading.status reads it back. With `game` the engine's splash covers only its own boot and the game's first frames are its loading screen; with `page` the canvas stays hidden and the page draws its own loader.

A published page sends og:progress, og:stage, og:first-frame, og:loaded, og:ready and og:failed as window events, and, when framed, as postMessage({ source: "origin-engine", type, detail }) to the parent, so any page hosting the game can draw its own loader without the platform (docs/web-export.md §Loading events). `publish { loading_labels { fetch "…" } }` renames the splash's stages.

The bytes of a group's pack received so far (its size once resident), with StreamStatus.progress, the fraction: a pending group's download is readable for a loading bar, on the web as the fetch streams in.
How much of a pending bundle (og.load.bundle) the host has received: bytes received, total when known, and the fraction.

While a segment plays, the first chunk of every segment a choice may cut to (and of the next segment) is read ahead, on one deck as on two, so a cut to any option starts without waiting for its video.

The determinism report gains OG9007 (a warning, as the others): localeCompare, the toLocale... methods and Intl order and format by the host's locale and its Unicode data, and WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry observe the garbage collector, so a sort, a string or a branch built on them differs between peers and on the other host. `// og-ok` keeps a line that only draws.

Outside a publish build, the engine's first log warns of each module-scope `let`/`var` a game's own files write and each module-scope container they mutate, by file, line and name (`src/main.ts:2: module-scope let 'ticks' is written; ...`): that state is outside the world snapshot, so a restore, a rollback or a capture fork does not bring it back. Keep it in a component or a resource. A run report that expects no warnings sees them.

A look's `variant "<name>"` draws the preset its extends chain reaches another way: templates/looks/variants/<slug>/<name>.ogt is laid over the preset before the mood and the game's own fields. Each variant has its catalogue entry under its look's `variants` (title, checks, intended traits, palette, specs, art bible), which artBrief reads in place of the look's; presetLook takes `{ variant }` and BriefLook carries `variant`.
The creation ui choice is default, cartoon, fantasy or scifi, and a look's own pack is the suggestion; creationLooks(styles?) lists the twelve looks.

Chooses where the motion model runs for a world: `gpu`, the default, beside the renderer, or `cpu`, on the CPU across the lanes, each generation spread over the ticks before it is due (about 21 ms of CPU a generation natively, 23 ms in wasm, so it suits a few characters). The probe takes it as the action `motion_backend:<gpu|cpu>`.
New variant, reported by og.motion.capabilities and `dump_motion`'s `state` when the model runs on the CPU.
`late` reports how far the Presenter is behind the world now, the ticks the world ran while it was behind and the most it was.

`og explore [project]` searches the game's states from snapshots (Go-Explore: an archive of cells from the reflected fields and the time, returns by restore, bursts of the game's actions, intents and waits) for invariant violations, systems that throw and the sometimes, reachable and each sites it reaches. Each finding is shrunk to the fewest presses, replayed from tick 0 to the same world hash in-process, in a fresh og run and on the web host, and written as a repro and a bun:test playtest beside report.json. Budgets: --seconds, --ticks, --memory, --horizon; --jobs N worker processes; --first stops at the first violation or error and reports only those as findings. The explore guide covers the workflow.

COLR colour glyphs (emoji): a font that asks draws its COLR v0 and v1 glyphs in colour (solid, linear, radial and sweep gradients with every extend mode, transforms, clip boxes and glyph clips, all composite modes). The cook paints each cooked character's graph into an sRGB image at `color_px` (default 64 px/em) on colour pages of the font's blob, and og-ui text draws them as sprites beside its distance-field glyphs on both hosts. Only fonts with the setting change; one without colour glyphs, or with `runtime true`, refuses it (docs/design.md, crates/og-cook/README.md §Colour glyphs).

Colour glyphs draw a text's shadows, glow and outline (overlay text) and its outline (world text), under their images. The cook adds each colour page's silhouette as a signed distance field (`color-field.<n>`, `foreground-field.<n>` in the font blob, about a tenth of the colour pages' bytes); og-runtime draws it as a font page of its own before the colour pages. A font cooked before has no fields and draws its colour glyphs without effects, as before.

A colour glyph in the text's colour (COLR palette entry 0xFFFF) is drawn as the mix of its black and white paints by the text's colour, exact where its paint is affine in that colour. The cook paints each such glyph again at mid grey, a darker grey and one colour, and the font's note warns, naming the characters and the worst error in 8-bit levels, where the paint routes the text's colour through a blend that bends the mix: a separable blend branching on it (overlay as backdrop, hard-light as source, soft-light, darken, lighten, dodge, burn, difference), it multiplied or screened by itself, a clamping plus, or a hue, saturation, colour or luminosity blend.

A COLR colour font cooks its glyphs in the CPAL palette it names: an index (`palette 2`), or `light` or `dark`, the first palette the font marks for that background. A palette the font lacks is refused, naming how many it has; without the setting palette 0 is used, as before (crates/og-cook/README.md §Colour glyphs).

The component catalogue: every element kind a screen or component document can use, one guide section each, with its props as the document writes them (the CSS property and its value forms, or the attribute) and its states. Generated from og-ui's document schema by og api gen and checked by og api check, so og api find returns the kind's section.

rune-kit's keyboard model (MIT, third_party/rune-kit): inside a focus group Home and End go to its first and last member and PageUp and PageDown as far as one view reaches; in a group whose role is a list's (listbox, menu, list, tree, tablist) letters typed under a second apart pick the first member whose name starts with them, and the same letter again cycles. A dropdown's options are one wrapping group, and Up or Down on its closed trigger opens it. The UI state is version 17 (the typed letters); og.ui saves migrate 16 to 17.

og ui review <kit> [--style <pack>]... [--states a,b] renders every page of a kit's review sheet × state fixture (state:<name>) × style at 1920×1080 and on a phone portrait and landscape, 100 % and 150 % text, in the game's locale, Chinese, Arabic and the pseudo-locale: labelled contact sheets per page, state and style, review.json with every measure and review.txt with each one's count, minimum, median and maximum. Beside og ui check's measures it reads text drawn past its box (overflow), text its clip cuts (clip), edges off the grid (grid, --grid default 4) and the gaps in each row and column (gap). Measures only, no verdicts (docs/ui.md §16.6).

A container's `-og-frame: rive("<file>.riv#<Artboard>")` (the `rive` prop) plays that cooked Rive artboard in its box over its background (docs/ui.md §11.2). og.load.document loads the artboards its document names and refuses one that is missing or malformed; og dev reloads an edited .riv. Each element's player advances once per tick in og-ui's state and is saved with it (UI state version 18; og.ui saves migrate 17 to 18); a restored player is rebuilt from its bytes when its element next builds, and bytes that do not fit the artboard are reported and kept, not reset. The artboard's drawn objects are dump_ui, describe and pick elements of kind rive, their detail.source `<file>.riv#<artboard>/<object>`. An element's draw (paint::ElementDraw) carries the player as `rive`.

Each art slot is a whole generation spec: mask, transparency, tiling, legible size, nine-slice insets, multi-cell split, states and its set, with the first member whose art is set as the reference to match.
`itemCells` is an item icon's grid cells (it sets the aspect when no `ratio` is given), `slice` a nine-slice's insets, and `artSet` the set the slot is generated with (the kind's name by default).

Lists the style values a kit or document writes itself instead of taking from the style (colours, corner radii, font families), each with its file, line and the token to use. It reports and exits 0 when it ran; `style-literal-ok` on a line skips it.

Brush strokes in the paint, sized by paintRadius: each colour mass the filter flattens is laid in strokes that run along the image's structure where it is coherent and along a slowly turning lay over flat ground and sky, lighter and darker along their length with fine bristle streaks, and the masses meet with ragged edges. 0 is none (the paint as before); 0.5 to 0.7 reads as paint at a glance; 1 is bold. In a profile 2d project the cook paints the same strokes in each texture's texels.

An emitter's `wind <0..1>` line makes its `drag` close on that share of the air where its system is (og.Wind and the og.WindMotors in reach) instead of on rest: smoke, dust and sparks drift downwind and into a fan's stream, the same on the CPU and GPU paths and in the tick for an emitter that sends events. The default 0 is as before.

templates/styles/clean is a dark, restrained pack. Display and numeric text use Barlow Semi Condensed with tabular figures, radii are small, and the HUD sits on low-alpha plates. It dresses every core control part and the shooter kit's parts. It is in art review and not yet a creation choice.

packages/engine/extensions/shooter holds Crosshair, AmmoCounter, DamageDirection, Killfeed, Loadout (select, equip and back intents with row keys) and a CombatHud over core StatBar, as documents with a review sheet and behaviour tests. It is in art review.

A kit names the library component documents its documents compose (`"components": ["stat-bar"]`), and `og ui add` ejects each the game does not already have into assets/ui/, so a kit's `<StatBar>` resolves without a separate `og ui eject`.

A document's text element that names its part (`<span part="Killfeed.name">`) takes the part's `-og-ink` and `-og-step`, qualified by its classes like any part, so a pack sets a kit's text colours (`Killfeed::name.ally { -og-ink: var(--team1) }`). Before, only a field's `text` and `placeholder` parts took them; now only the core box parts (`frame`, `base`, `track`, `fill`) refuse them.

New text parts `Killfeed.name`, `Ammo.mode`, `Loadout.detail` and `Loadout.price`; the team colours of the killfeed's names and the muted ink of the weapon, reserve, fire mode and slot figures moved from the kit into the clean pack's dressings.

A `plant` block takes `kind`: oak, birch, willow, pine, palm, bamboo, cactus, shrub, fern, reed, daisy or tulip. `plant "palm" { kind palm }` is a whole plant, and the keys beside it change only what they name (a colour, a seed, a trunk's length). The models guide (§3) lists each kind's height and triangles.

A plant's leaves take `rows`: 2 puts them in two rows to the sides of their branch, level with the ground (a palm's or a fern's frond, a conifer's flat spray); 0, the default, anywhere round it as before.

A `plant` block grows a tree, a shrub or a flower from numbers and a seed: a trunk and up to three levels of branches, leaves and flowers in any colours, cooked with the wind's pivots and anchors so og.Model.sway bends it under og.Wind. The models guide (§3) gives the keys and four kinds to start from.

A material's `translucency` and `domeNormals` make it a leaf's: drawn from both faces, with light through it and shading by its canopy's dome. A glTF material states them as KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission and extras.ogFoliage.domeNormals; cooked models draw with both, so a project's models cook again.
One test can play several runs (each a fresh world) and compare them; `og test --json` reports each file's `tests`, its failures by test name and every expect() as `checks`.

A probe snapshot keeps the presentation state beside the world as a presentation checkpoint, outside world_hash: each particle system's per-tick emitter history and the renderer's adapted auto exposure. Its hash is reported as `SnapshotInfo.presentation`, per host and backend. A restore brings the checkpoint back, so the frames after it are the frames the saved run drew (docs/design.md §2.4).
Draws no display frame, only the captures the commands ask for, each from the tick-stepped presentation state, so its PNGs equal a run that draws every frame. Refuses --realtime, --watch and --port.

With --commands, takes N snapshots at evenly spaced ticks of the script and, after the run, plays each to the run's last tick with the steps still queued at it, writing no files; any fork whose world hash on a tick, screenshot bytes or end presentation hash differs from the run's is listed under `forks` in the JSON summary and fails the run. Refuses --realtime, --watch, --port, --room and --handoff.

A directory's import settings: assets/<dir>/import.ogt, a type import document of match "<pattern>" { … } blocks, gives every file under the directory that a pattern names what a settings file of its own (<file>.ogt) would. A file takes the matching blocks from assets/ down to its own directory, then its own settings file, a later entry replacing an earlier one key by key and two blocks of one key joining. The cooked bytes are those of the same settings written per file; an edit recooks only the files whose settings it changes. Before, a directory of files with the same settings needed one identical settings file each, and an import.ogt was an error.

A cooked navmesh stores its walkable heightfield as two meshopt vertex streams (a column's span count, then the spans) instead of two plain tables, and no longer writes each column's first span, which is the sum of the counts before it. The third-person sample's navmesh goes from 1,397,804 to 40,220 bytes on disk (70,207 to 13,100 after brotli). `og.NavMesh` is schema version 2: the next cook rewrites every navmesh, and the baked mesh and what `og.nav` answers are unchanged.

og fmt [path…] [--check] [--json] rewrites .ogt files in the canonical layout and keeps their comments: two spaces per level, one space between tokens, a trailing comment two spaces after its tokens, one blank line where there were several. Entries keep their order. A path is a file, a directory, or a project (its project.ogt and assets/; the default is the current directory); styles, UI documents, 2D effects and installed packs are skipped. --check writes nothing and exits 1 when a file would change. The cooked output of a formatted file is unchanged. Before, the only canonical writer dropped comments, so hand-written and generated files drifted apart in layout.

An `.ogt` asset may say its type in its name, `<name>.<type>.ogt` (`level1.scene.ogt`, `hero.flipbook.ogt`), so a glob finds every file of a type without opening one. The name is optional and decides nothing: the `type` line does, and the asset id is the path as written. The cook now warns when the last part of a name is a type the file does not cook as ("named as a prefab (.prefab.ogt) and cooked as a scene"); any other last part is free. Existing names keep working unchanged; `og assets mv` renames one and rewrites its references. The assets guide's section 7 describes the convention.

The host side of og.platform as a public, versioned contract (PROVIDER_VERSION 1): PlatformProvider and RoomProvider with PlatformCall, PlatformAnswer, PlatformNotice, PlatformLink, RoomOp and RoomEvent; the vocabulary as data (CORE_METHODS, HOST_EXTENSIONS, ERROR_CODES, RETRYABLE_CODES, kept equal to platform.ogt's); the helpers ok, failure and unavailable; and checkPlatformProvider, a conformance check for a provider author's tests. PlatformHost and RoomHost remain as the same types. Game code is unchanged.

added.member: Web page: play({ provider }) and window.__OG_PROVIDER
added.summary: The page that hosts a game names its providers, { platform?, rooms? }: where no Player answers, the page's platform provider answers og.platform instead of the browser's storage and its rooms provider carries the rooms. rooms may be an og relay URL. A Player framing the page still answers what it answers, and in a publish build a local provider answers the platform services unavailable (docs/web-export.md §Providers).

Rooms for a self-hosted web page through an og relay over the browser's WebSocket, as og run --room connects natively: og.platform.roomInfo's host reads relay. A lost relay is a left event; a later create, join or quick, and one sent to a relay that never answered, is refused offline.

Rain rings water as it rings a puddle: og.WaterSurface draws raindrop rings where the sky is open over it, and from afar the rings' spread dulls its mirror and widens its glitter. Before, a lake or a sea in the rain took the rain's sky and light and kept a dry surface.
Bezier controls and step count/position survive ECS hashes, snapshots, scene cook/save, probe edits and both hosts. The shared parser/evaluator now lives in og-core and remains exported by og-tween.

og run --room reaches a relay behind TLS: `wss://<host>/<room>` (port 443 unless named) beside `ws://`. The certificate is checked against the public roots the engine carries (webpki-roots), not the system's store, so a self-signed or private-CA relay is refused; og relay itself still serves ws:// and wants a TLS proxy in front.

A lost connection to an og relay is mended instead of ending the room: og run --room and relayRooms connect again for 30 s (250 ms, then twice as long up to 4 s) and join the room again, so the engine hears og.RoomJoined once more with a new peer number, the others og.RoomPeerLeft and og.RoomPeerJoined, and with og.Lockstep.rejoin the player takes its own seat again (og.SeatDropped, then og.SeatRejoined), named or not. What roomSend sent meanwhile is lost; only when the 30 s pass or the room refuses does the engine leave the room. relayRooms(url, { reconnectMs }) sets the window (0 never tries again).

og relay and its clients notice a dead connection themselves: either end pings one silent for 3 s and gives up one silent for 10 s, where before a peer gone without a close held its room until the system's TCP timeout.

The play surface presents the widest gamut and range the surface and display offer: extended range (HDR) with Display P3 on Metal (scRGB EDR), DX12 and Vulkan (scRGB), and WebGPU (a `display-p3` canvas with `toneMapping: extended`), else Display P3 at standard range, else sRGB. `wide` keeps standard range, `srgb` the output as before. Offscreen renderers, captures and reference frames stay sRGB at standard range.
Whether the surface presents Display P3; `hdr` whether it presents extended range.

On an extended-range output ACES, AgX, Khronos PBR Neutral and none keep middle grey where SDR puts it and end at the headroom (RenderOptions.peakNits over paperWhiteNits, 1000 / 203 left out, no more than the display reports) instead of SDR white: emissive, glow, bloom and the sun keep rising past white.

added.member: UI: Display P3 colours and the display media queries
added.summary: On a Display P3 output, CSS colours outside sRGB (`color(display-p3 …)`, a wide `oklch()`, a mix of them) keep their gamut, gamut mapped into P3 by OKLCh chroma reduction instead of into sRGB. `(color-gamut: p3)` and `(dynamic-range: high)` (and `video-dynamic-range`) match where the surface presents them; they were fixed false.

world.restore(save, { session: true }) takes the save's input too (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock: what was held and the tick's edges) instead of keeping the host's, so the world is the one saved, hash and all: what a tool returning to a state needs (og explore). The default still keeps the player's input.

`og run --profile out.cpuprofile` (or `out.md`) samples the game's TypeScript on the native host while it runs and writes a CPU profile whose locations are the game's `src/` files and lines: a `.cpuprofile` for Chrome's and VS Code's profile views, a `.md` as hot-function and call-tree tables to read. Time inside the engine shows on the binding that called it. Not an option of `og run --device`.

added.member: og.story, og.video, og.destruction and og.motion as optional runtime modules
added.summary: Each is a feature of the runtime (story, video, destruction, motion), on by default and in every shipped web variant (publish, publish2d and both lanes modules) and the native host, so a game's calls and saves are unchanged. A build without one links none of that module's crate; its calls answer a refusal naming the feature, and the world it leaves (records in IDL order, systems, state blocks) is the full build's for a game that never uses the module.
Reaches 8000 m (was 500 m): a wood scattered with an impostor is drawn as cards out to the horizon.

og.TerrainScatter's `model` scatters a whole glTF as one copy, every part with its own material: a grown plant's wood and leaves stand and sway together, so three or four species with footprints make a wood. Cooked with an impostor, copies past impostorDistance draw as one card. The world guide (§3) and the models guide (§3) show how.

The time of year: a calendar date (`start`, `speed`), a `latitude` and a climate (`temperature`, `temperatureRange`, `dayRange`). With og.DayNight it sets where the sun rises, how high it climbs and how long the day is in place of `DayNight.tilt` (`sun: false` keeps DayNight's path). A change of `start` plays over `change` seconds, the date running through the days between. Off by default and registered when first named: existing worlds, saves and frames are unchanged.

The time of year now, for gameplay: the date, the season (0 spring to 3 winter, with how far through it), sunrise, sunset and the day's length on og.atmosphere.timeOfDay's clock, the air's temperature, and how far the leaves and the grass are through their year. The probe's `get:og.Season` adds the same fields to the record's (the air's temperature as `temperatureNow`).
The northern equinoxes and solstices as days of the year, for og.Season.start.
A game shader may call the sRGB curve both ways and the luminance of linear light without writing them.
A game shader may ask for the direction from a surface point to the eye (orthographic cameras included) and whether a prepass view depth is the sky.
A game shader may scatter light by the Henyey-Greenstein phase function, and a lit one fade a local light to its range and a spot to its cone as the engine's lights do.
A game shader may call smooth 2D value noise in [0, 1) over the engine's integer hash, on a lattice layer of its choosing.
A game shader may move linear colour to Oklab and back without writing the matrices; a colour outside the gamut (a negative channel) round-trips.

added.member: material shaders: a lit full shader (`type full`)
added.summary: A lit full shader hands its surface to the renderer's one shading entry: it now takes the screen's occlusion, the probe GI, the light volumes and the caustics under water as a built-in material does, its reflection is bent towards the normal by roughness, and the albedo, image-based light and direct light debug views show it.

The 3D fluid's body and lit particles shade through the renderer's one shading entry: both now take the probe GI, the light volumes, the hemisphere light and the caustics under water as a mesh does. The fluid's reflection is the shared image-based specular, added over the body by Fresnel, where it was a mix with the environment at a fixed blur; a glossy fluid reads slightly differently.

The terrain and its stamps take the light around them through the renderer's one shading entry: the light volumes and the probe GI's occlusion of reflections reach the ground, and its reflection is bent towards the normal by roughness as a mesh's is.

Scattered models, their impostors, crowd cards and grass take the light around them through the renderer's one shading entry: the screen-space occlusion and bent normal, the probe GI, the light volumes and the reflection bent by roughness, as a mesh does. Crowd cards also take the screen-space reflections.

A water surface takes the point, spot and rect lights around it (a lamp over a lake or a sea now lights it: its facets mirror the lamp, its body and its foam scatter it back), and gathers the light around it as every lit surface does: the probe GI, the light volumes and the hemisphere light reach its body, its foam and its reflection, so a pool under a roof no longer takes the open sky's light. Its own reflection, glitter and foam are unchanged outdoors.

A box nothing grows in: no og.TerrainScatter copy whose root stands in it and no og.Grass blade, so a house's floor, a paved yard or a slab laid over a terrain no longer has grass and trees growing through it. The box is centred on the entity and follows its whole world transform, rotation and scale included; `size` 0 on any axis clears nothing. Both scatter placers (CPU and GPU) honour it, and moving one places the copies again. Visual only. (Unreal's procedural foliage blocking volume, Unity's detail exclusion.)

added.member: type import: texture { sway clumps | tiers ["map.png"] }
added.summary: The cook cuts a 2D plant's texture into the parts og.Sprite.sway moves, cooked as `<id>#sway`: `clumps` for a broadleaf tree or a bush, `tiers` for a conifer, or the parts of a map image of the texture's size (one flat colour per part, clear where the plant stands still). Drawn at rest the parts are the texture, texel for texel.

A sprite whose texture is cooked with wind parts is drawn as those parts in og.Wind: a tree's wood stands, its clumps of leaves or tiers of branches lean downwind with the gusts and loop as the wind's wave passes, in step with grass and 3D vegetation. Pixel art moves by whole texels and holds each pose (ArtMotion.stepFps, else 10 a second). 0, the default, draws the sprite whole; so do still air, a flipbook, slices, a palette, a material or a uv region. Presentation only.

A node header that holds the conversation on entering each node that has it (DialogueView.held) until og.story.advance runs the node, so another module can pace a story by node; logic nodes without the header run through. Saves keep the hold (story save version 9; older saves still load).
Every hashtag of a choice by name (`#hotspot:knife` is `{ hotspot: "knife" }`), for the game to read.

A loaded dialogue's nodes with their headers and choices, and every node each choice and each node's own steps may jump to: for a flowchart, a test that walks every route, or warming the segments a choice may lead to.
A dialogue node may carry `og-film`, `og-film-chapter` and `og-film-ending` (read by og.film); other `og-` headers still need an `og-topic` bark node.

RenderCaps, what the device can do under the tier, as og-render's Caps: compute, mrt, asyncPipelines, timestamps, indirect, indirectFirstInstance, fragmentStorage and vertexStorage, all false without a renderer.

added.member: og style art: a dress cell lists several selectors
added.summary: A slot's `dress` cell in art-requests.json may be a list of the dressings it goes to alike (`["Panel.frame", "Dialog.panel"]`): the painted cell is packed once and each dressing gets its slice and tone, so a pack's window art dresses its dialogs and its field art its select and stepper without a copied slice going stale when the atlas is packed again.

added.member: fantasy, scifi and cartoon style packs
added.summary: Each pack's palette is now its --seed-* colours (fantasy: crimson, brass, walnut; scifi: cyan with a deeper teal in the light scheme, amber, deep sea; cartoon: sunflower, indigo), from which the default style derives the grounds, inks, accents, statuses and teams in both schemes at the contrast their pairs need, so og.ui.configure's seeds retints a pack. What the derivation cannot express stays on top as art: scifi's cyan rims and highlight, cartoon's saturated sky and indigo grounds and their inks. Text over the scene takes the default's halo. Fantasy's light buttons ink a step deeper brass, its epic tier and selected tab read at 4.5:1.

Light that spreads under the surface before it leaves: skin, wax, marble, jade, milk. `subsurface: 1` softens the shading past the terminator where the surface curves, the channel that travels farthest (`subsurfaceRadius`, metres per channel; the default is skin's) bleeding into the shadow first, and with `thickness` the sun and the lamps behind a thin part come through it. In closed form in the lit pass, on every backend: no extra pass and no texture.

Inline SVG text takes several lines (`<tspan x>` with `y` or `dy`, `dx`/`dy` in user units or `em`), `white-space` (and `xml:space="preserve"`), and `<textPath href startOffset side method spacing>` (or its own `path`) along any path or shape, drawn by og-ui's text on a path (docs/ui.md §3.3). These were refused before.

`marker-start`, `marker-mid` and `marker-end="url(#id)"` draw a `<marker viewBox refX refY markerWidth markerHeight markerUnits orient>` at a shape's vertices (orient auto, auto-start-reverse or an angle; context-fill and context-stroke). `stroke-dasharray` takes any list; it took one dash and one gap before.
`<foreignObject x y width height>` in an inline `<svg>` lays document elements out in its box of user units, clipped and scaled with the view box.

SMIL animation inside the element it animates, with `<mpath>`, begin (clock lists, id.begin/id.end), dur, repeatCount, repeatDur, fill, values, from/to/by, keyTimes, keySplines, calcMode, additive and accumulate. Presentation only, on the UI's tick clock from when the element first shows (kept in widget memory, outside world_hash); an event begin is refused (docs/ui.md §3.3).

A caption file's translations beside it (`narration.zh.srt`, `narration.pt-BR.srt` beside `narration.srt`, each with its own times) cook with the timeline, and the track says the one of the locale the player asked for (og.i18n.setLocale), its language's for a regional tag, else its own. `locale "zh" { captions "…" }` in a caption track names a translation kept elsewhere.

$captions, read by every document like $ui unless a mount binds its own captions: the lines the playing timelines are saying now, a collection of { id, text } keyed by id, in the order of the timelines and of their caption tracks. Each key is a row of its own, so a line that stays is not rebuilt when another joins or goes.
The built-in subtitles screen shows $captions after its own lines, with nothing to pass.

A timeline's `video` track plays footage on an og.VideoPlayer: `track video "tv" { key 0 { video "clips/kitchen.ogt" from 0 speed 1 } }` plays on the entity named `tv`, `track video { … }` on the og.Timeline's own entity. The video's time is `from + (t − key) · speed` at the timeline's time, so seeking a timeline and playing it to the same moment show the same frame, and several segments can share one long file through `from`. Loading the timeline loads its videos; the cook refuses a video it does not have.

GSAP-shaped timelines: `og.tween.timeline(world, { defaults, repeat, yoyo, repeatDelay, paused, timeScale, autoKill })` answers a TweenTimeline whose to, from, fromTo, set, call, addLabel and add chain and take GSAP's position (seconds, `<`, `>`, `+=n`, `-=n`, labels, `label+=n`, `<50%`). Tweens take `stagger` (seconds or `{ each | amount, from: start|center|end|edges|random|index, grid, ease }`), `keyframes`, `repeatDelay` and callbacks; play, pause, resume, reverse, restart, seek, progress, timeScale and kill control it. It renders from its playhead and is world state, restored whole (guide animation §6). og.tween.cancelEntity drops a timeline's tweens of the entity and lets it play on.
A timeline's named callbacks (`onStart`, `onUpdate`, `onComplete`, `onRepeat`, `.call(name)`) as an event a system reads: its timeline, target entity, name, progress and tag.
TweenDesc.to and from, TweenFromDesc.from, TimelineTweenVars.to and from and TweenKeyframe.to are typed as one number or a list (number | number[]), as the engine always read them.

uvRepeat is declared on CylinderGeometryDesc, ConeGeometryDesc, CapsuleGeometryDesc, TorusGeometryDesc, RingGeometryDesc, CircleGeometryDesc and TubeGeometryDesc (default 1 1), as the engine already applied it.
ShapeGeometryDesc.shapes and ExtrudeGeometryDesc.shapes take a list of ShapePoints (og.Shape.extractPoints) and SweepGeometryDesc.section a ShapePoints, as an og.Shape crosses to the engine.

MassTemplateDesc.pivot defaults to 0.5 0.5 and a size component of 0 is the kind's default (text and numbers 24, bars 80 × 8, icons 32, particles 8), as declared in the IDL; og.ui.previewViewport's Viewport.width and height default to 1280 and 720.

added.member: og.nav and og.ai as optional runtime modules
added.summary: Each is a feature of the runtime (nav, ai; ai needs nav), on by default and in every shipped web variant and the native host, so a game's calls and saves are unchanged. A build without one links none of og-nav (nor og-bundle's navmesh loaders) or og-ai: its calls answer a refusal naming the feature (a cooked navmesh is refused, never dropped), and the world it leaves (the og.nav and og.ai systems and their state blocks, the records in IDL order) saves and hashes byte for byte as the full build's for a game that never uses the module.

A screen's root matches `:active-view-transition` from the frame its layer's view transition starts until it ends, so `:active-view-transition .card { … }` styles the screen during the transition. `:active-view-transition-type(slide)` matches when the screen's `@view-transition { types: slide; }` declares one of the types; it now works in any rule, not only before a `::view-transition-*` pseudo-element.

A desc, as og.input's ActionDesc: every field may be left out and takes its default (trigger press, holdMs 500, no toggle, an empty label), so og.ui.defineAction(world, { name: "skip", keys: ["KeyX"], buttons: ["y"] }) is a whole action. Descs that write every field are unchanged.

The UI modules keep the rules of the conventions guide, which gains their lines: a UI Paint's color is a linear Color like any other while colours the UI takes as text or bare numbers are sRGB; opacity names how opaque a thing is in every module; the UI's pointer, gestures and actions use down, justPressed, justReleased and held as og.input does.

The test over every field of the API has no UI member left to rename and keeps two more names: a field named alpha or ending in Alpha is an opacity, and a bool named pressed or released is justPressed or justReleased. The UI's fields in ticks, radians and ratios carry their units (MassTemplateDesc.lifetimeTicks, GestureInfo.rotation, the opacities).
Ready checks with participant responses, game-owned countdown text, changeable local accept/decline intents, closed, loading, empty and disabled states.
Map voting with stable option-id intents, game-owned tallies and winners, visible local selection and per-option disabled reasons.

Spectator HUD with keyed follow intents, current subject, free camera, previous/next and Leave actions; loading never removes the exit. All three support phone text, bounded scrolling and token/part styling.

ARIA on any element: role (checked against og.ui's roles), aria-labelledby and aria-describedby joined to the named elements' text, aria-description, aria-value{min,max,now,text}, and aria-checked, -selected, -expanded, -pressed, -busy, -disabled, -level and -current. A11yNode states gain current.
A style token for the corners of a player's avatar, round (--radius-capsule) in the default style; a style pack squares or softens every avatar by setting it. The base Avatar and Friends read it.
Adds showName (default true) to hide the visible caption when composing an avatar beside a heading, preserving its accessible name, level and status.

A slot of the built-in backpack drags onto another and the bag reports move with { dragged, target }, the two items' keys; the dragged slot springs home and the game reorders, swaps or stacks. A locked item does not drag. A press without a drag reports choose as before.

The base components are redone. Currency is a chip as wide as what it holds: the icon in a socket, the name over the amount, then its capacity, a Full pill and its rate. Steps is a rail of marks, each joined to the next by a reach that fills once the step is done, in a row and in a column alike, with the step's state above its name in its tone; it lies along a row and stands up as a column with `column` or in a container under 480px. Pips sits on one line and takes `tone` (empty is the style's pip colour, a life's red; success, warn, danger, info or primary); a unit eases as it drains, and an unavailable resource's units lose their colour and dim. EmptyState and ErrorState are a recess with their mark on a disc (ErrorState's tinted and ringed in danger, quieter than its action), EmptyState's action is the primary button, and ErrorState's support code is set apart as a chip. ListItem keeps its value over its badge at the row's end while its words keep a measure beside them, and drops them under the words only when a long value would squeeze the name into a column, and a disabled row dims its name. Avatar carries presence as a dot on its rim and in the tone of its words, its level across its foot, and a rim round its picture. ItemSlot shows the time left large over its dimmed icon, an empty slot's plus sits back, and a loading slot shows only its spinner. Spinner always shows its track ring with the arc running round it; a host that holds nothing else while it waits (Avatar, ItemSlot) sizes it to itself through --spinner-size. SkeletonGroup is swept by one band of light across the whole group instead of one per bone. Steps has a `column` fixture and its `error` fixture follows the container; Ribbon has a fixture for every corner, the stamp and a long word.

A card is the frame's own glass a step nearer (--color-card) instead of a grey wash; a role badge is a raised chip of the glass with its rim, so a count or a key holds over a picture; a chosen row on dark glass is the glass a step lighter with the primary on its edge, not a grey slab. New role tokens a pack can set: --pip-ink, --pip-empty-ink and --pip-motion (a counted unit, Pips) and --cell-cooling-opacity (what a cooling cell's icon dims to under its time left). A ribbon's words are bold. More role tokens: --spinner-track and --spinner-ink (the ring a Spinner turns in, in the rim's colour so it shows on glass, in a tile and over the scene, and the arc that runs round it), and --dot-alert-fill and --dot-alert-rim (a failure's mark: a tint of danger ringed in it).

A `<div>` (or other block box) that names `align-items`, `justify-content` or `flex-direction` without `display: flex` is reported as a document warning: "align-items does nothing on a block box; give it display: flex". A browser ignores those properties on a block too.

added.member: UI documents: margin-top, margin-bottom, margin-block, margin
added.summary:
Vertical margins in px or em, with CSS 2 margin collapsing in display:block boxes (adjacent siblings, a parent with its first or last child). HTML's UA margins for

,

    ,
      and

      –

      ; margin:0 resets them. A horizontal margin is 0 or auto only.

`border-shape` (CSS Borders 4 §7): one basic shape strokes the border along its path, over the half-border box by default; two fill the border between them, the outer over the border box and the inner over the padding box by default. The width and colour come from the first side, in block-start, inline-start, block-end, inline-end order, that has a border style. The outer shape becomes the element's shape, so its background, shadows and overflow cut follow it, and its border-radius is ignored. Layout is unchanged.

A table's `border-spacing: <h> [<v>]` (inherited, 0 by default) separates its cells and its outer cells from its padding edge (CSS 2 §17.6.1); `border-collapse: collapse` sets the cells edge to edge. Both were refused. A table now ignores `gap`, as CSS tables do.

Bound CSS custom properties: an element's inline custom property, set from store data, which rules read with var() and children inherit (style:--fill={$hp / $max}). A store change re-resolves that element only; null leaves var()'s fallback.

added.member: UI documents: calc(), min(), max(), clamp()
added.summary: CSS math functions, reduced once their var()s are known (at cook, or when the element resolves): width: calc(var(--fill) * 100%), animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 80ms). Every term of one function takes one unit.

`box-decoration-break` (CSS Fragmentation 3 §5.4) on a text a multi-column break splits: `slice`, the initial value, draws its background, border and shadows as one unbroken box cut at the break, each piece showing its part in its own column; `clone` gives each piece its own whole box, with padding and border at the break taken into the column balancing. A split text drew one box for its first piece only, with a border at the break, and none in the next column.

Every component document under the engine package's src/ui/components/ (its group directories included) is built in: a game's document uses one by the name its <meta name="component"> declares (<StatBar/>, <AbilityBar/>) without copying it. The cook bundles each built-in component the game's documents reach, with its string tables and the files it names, under the reserved id @ui/<path under src/ui> (@ui/components/stat-bar.svelte), as it bundles a look's @styles/; two built-in documents of one name fail the cook. A game document declaring the same component name (what og ui eject writes) wins, and the engine's copy is then not bundled. og ui types reads the built-in components' props and events for the documents that use them.

Every screen document under the engine package's src/ui/screens/ is built in as well: og.load.document(world, "@ui/screens/pause.svelte") loads it without a copy and og.ui.push(world, "pause") shows it, as with a game's own screen. The cook bundles each built-in screen whose id the game's code names as a string literal, with its strings and the components it uses. A game document declaring the same screen name (what og ui eject writes) wins: the engine's is not bundled, and loading its @ui/ id loads the game's copy at ui/<file> instead.

Loading a document also loads every component document it uses, and theirs, once each: the game's own component of a name, else the built-in one. A screen needs only its own og.load.document call; loading a component explicitly as well is harmless. og dev's reload loads a component an edit starts using.
An ejected component replaces the built-in one of its name and loads with the screens that use it; the message no longer asks for a separate og.load.document.

-og-burst in a keyframe takes var() and calc(): -og-burst: 21 var(--size-4xl) var(--gold) var(--motion-duration-breathe). Each animated element resolves the value through its own cascade, so two elements with different custom properties throw different bursts from one @keyframes; a value that is not a count, a radius in px, a colour and a time once resolved fires nothing and is reported. A literal value is read as before.

An <anchor mass>'s keyframes take var() and calc() in translate, scale and opacity (translate: 0 calc(var(--space-3xl) * -1)), resolved through the anchor's cascade; such a keyframe was dropped from the element's timeline before. The built-in damage numbers rise again as they fade, and the celebration's fireworks shells throw their rays again.

A button that is on (<button aria-pressed={on}>: a toggle, a chip) has a look in the default style: --button-selected-fill under --button-selected-ink, the neutral selection, whatever its variant, at rest, hovered and held. Before, the default style left it looking like its off neighbour and each document wrote its own selected state. A style pack sets the two tokens or dresses button[aria-pressed=true]::part(base); a document that draws its own state on a part still wins. Built-in components that mark a button on (the strategy command card's active command, an armed puzzle booster, the rhythm song list's Preview) now show it.

CSS's ::backdrop pseudo-element on a modal <dialog>: `dialog::backdrop { background: … }` fills its scrim, cascading with states, variables and media; the scrim is the part Dialog.backdrop to a style pack. ui.DialogDesc.backdrop for Rust.

Fonts ship as packs, one per script (latin, cyrillic-greek, arabic, hebrew, devanagari, thai, japanese, korean, chinese-simplified, chinese-traditional), each an extension.json of kind font with its faces and licence. `og font list` names them and `og font add <pack>` installs one under assets/fonts/<pack>/.
--lang installs the font pack of each language's script (Chinese by script), with no generated code.

og.i18n chains installed font packs with no code: the locale's own pack, then a pack loaded the first frame its characters are drawn. Pack faces draw from outlines at run time and the web fetches them on demand.

A core select bound by value: literal options under one level of optgroups (disabled options and groups skipped), keyboard, d-pad and pointer picking, typeahead, Escape or B closing, the focus returned to the trigger. A bound list is items={…} values={…}. Parts Dropdown.trigger, .list, .group, .option.

HTML's dialog, two-way open: modal (a scrim taking every press, the focus moved in, trapped and returned, Escape, B or the scrim closing it) or in place (Back closes it while the focus is inside). ui.DialogDesc and Ui::open_dialog for Rust.
A disclosure, two-way open: the summary row toggles it by press, Enter, Space or A; the content is built only while open. Parts Details.root, .summary[open], .content.
HTML's meter beside <progress>: value, min, max, low, high, optimum; the fill is dressed Meter.fill[region=optimum|suboptimum|poor] by HTML's region rules.

HTML's required, minlength, pattern (the whole text, ^(?:p)$; an invalid one is a parse error) and, on a number, min, max and step (default 1, step="any" for none) set :invalid as HTML's valueMissing, tooShort, patternMismatch, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow and stepMismatch. readonly drops every edit but keeps selection, copy and the focus stop.

A field's HTML `type`: password (masked, uncopyable, with a reveal toggle `<id>/Reveal` dressed `<component>.reveal[revealed]`), number (filters typed characters), email, url, tel and search. A number, email or url that is not one is invalid; documents write `<input type="password">` and style it with `:invalid`.
The virtual keyboard a field asks for (HTML `inputmode`); unset, its type's. The web shell gives a one-line field a hidden <input> with it.
A field's autofill hint (HTML `autocomplete`), passed to the page's input.

linear-gradient(), radial-gradient(), conic-gradient() and their repeating- forms take CSS Images 4's colour interpolation method anywhere in their prelude, `in <colour space> [shorter | longer | increasing | decreasing hue]` (`linear-gradient(to right in oklch longer hue, #36c, gold)`): the stops mix in that space, drawn as a piecewise OKLab ramp within the gradient's 8 stops. A gradient without one still mixes in OKLab.

Colour emoji as run-time glyphs: a COLR (v0 or v1) font that ships its file paints each colour glyph when a text first shows it, off the frame, with the cook's painter and the palette its settings name, onto colour pages with silhouette fields for glow and outlines. Skin tones, ZWJ sequences and flags are one glyph each.
The emoji font pack: Noto Color Emoji COLRv1 (SIL OFL 1.1, 5.05 MB), a pack of no language (script Zsye) tried after every text pack. `og font add emoji` installs it.

Colour-blind modes as a player setting: protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia. The whole frame, scene and UI alike, is recoloured after every other effect: corrected by daltonisation (the default) or simulated for checking a screen (UiDesc.colorVisionFilter), at UiDesc.colorVisionStrength. Simulation is Viénot 1999 and Brettel 1997 from libDaltonLens; correction is Fidaner 2005.
The colour vision setting in effect, with its filter and strength.

Document CSS reads the player's colour vision: `(-og-color-vision)` for any mode, `(-og-color-vision: deuteranopia)` for one; a retained mount restyles only the elements that read it when the setting changes.
An <icon> draws a colour token's icon cue (`-og-cue: danger`, a status, rarity, team or damage type), the icon the style pairs with that colour, so a state never rests on colour alone.

`column-height` makes every row of a multi-column container's columns that tall, and the columns past the count wrap into a new row below, `row-gap` apart (`normal`: 1em), each row with its own `column-rule`. `column-wrap: nowrap` keeps them beside instead; `auto` (the default) wraps when a `column-height` is set (CSS Multicol 2 §4.2, §4.4). A row keeps its height when its content is shorter. `columns` takes `/ <column-height>` and resets `column-wrap`.
A text's ::part run takes text-combine-upright: all (or digits) down a vertical line: the run's text is set upright in one em, squeezed across, and breaks as one unit (CSS Writing Modes 4 §9.1).

The engine ships component documents in place of the TS builders, in packages/engine/src/ui/screens: card, confirm, pagination, data-list, key-values, table, tree, calendar, objective-tracker, star-rating, banner, subtitles and notifications, each with its props, actions and a default fixture (docs/ui.md §2). `og ui eject <name>` copies one into a game.

An arena group of built-in components under @ui/components/arena/, used by name like the rpg and shooter ones: ArenaRoster (character selection: cells with portrait or icon, name and role in words, P1–P4 marks with a ready check, locked and taken cells disabled and named; reports choose with the character's key), ArenaDraft (ban and pick phases for two teams, filled, empty, banned and active slots, the team to choose and the turn's HudTimer; reports confirm), ArenaVersus (two sides with portraits, names, champions and ranks, the local player marked; a new reveal id replays the entrance, which reduced motion skips), ArenaScoreboard (two teams under their names and scores, K/D/A and score or score only, the local row marked You, disconnected players dimmed and named), ArenaRoundHud (round n of N, both team scores, the round HudTimer and a Round won / lost / drawn banner) and ArenaLobby (seats with host, ready and not-ready in words, open seats with Invite; reports invite with the seat's key, ready, unready and start). They compute no scores, ranks, outcomes, timers, legality or readiness: the game passes them in. Each names its frames, rows, cells, titles and badges as parts (src/ui/components/arena/README.md).
arena.css dresses the arena components' parts in the pack's brass, soot and crimson, the teams in its --team1 and --team2, from its existing tokens.

A card group of built-in components (src/ui/components/card/, README there): CardFace (a card's cost seal, art, name, type line and rules text), CardHand (the hand, overlapping as it grows and fanned by the game's per-card place; a card the game says is unplayable keeps its mark, offers no Play and never reports play; reports select and play by card key), CardPiles (draw, discard and exhaust counts; reports open by pile key), CardCollection (a deck builder's filter tabs and card grid with owned and in-deck badges; a card the game will not add stays in reach, is marked and says the game's reason, and reports inspect instead of add; reports add, inspect and choosefilter), CardDeckList (the deck's rows with copies, the size against the game's limit, plus and minus per row, each disabled and silent where the game refuses it; reports choose, add, remove and confirm), CardReward (pick one of the game's card or relic offers, or skip; it says so when there is none) and CardRunMap (the run map on the core NodeGraph with visited, current, reachable and out-of-reach rooms and a legend; reports NodeGraph's pick). Each takes the game's data as keyed rows and returns intents with their keys; legality, costs, targets and rewards stay the game's. Every member names its frames, rows, cells and badges as parts with their states as data-* attributes.

card.css dresses the card group's parts in the pack's materials: walnut card plates in rarity-inked brass rims, crimson cost seals, tinted art windows by card type, panel frames for the collection, deck list and run map under the pack's shared heading band, relic seals rimmed by rarity, pile counts and the deck size bar.

A general group of built-in components most games share, used by name like the rpg and shooter groups: Shop (offer tiles with prices in one or more currencies, category tabs, the player's balances, and the game's soldOut, owned, affordable, featured and discount flags; a refused tile keeps the focus, names its verdict and reports nothing; reports buy, choosetab, tabNext/tabPrev and retry), ShopConfirm (the purchase confirmation with the cost and the balance left, as content for a host that owns modality and focus, such as the built-in confirm screen; reports confirm and cancel), Achievements (locked, in progress with a bar, unlocked with its date, hidden until unlocked, tier in words, rarity; reports claim), DailyQuests (rows with progress, reward and the game's refresh countdown; reports claim), DailyRewards (a login calendar of days in the state the game sends, claimed, today, upcoming or missed; today's tile is a button while canClaim holds and reports claim), Chat (channel tabs with unread counts, system, own and others' messages, an input row; reports choosetab and send, and writes the draft back through bind:draft) and Friends (presence in words, requests with accept and decline, invite, add, an empty state). They hold no money or reward logic: the game passes every price, verdict and figure and applies the intents. Each is dressed through named parts (Shop.offer, DailyRewards.day…); the fantasy pack dresses them in general.css. og ui eject general/<name> copies one.

An idle group of built-in components under @ui/components/idle/, used by name like the rpg and racing ones: IdleResources (a chip per currency with its amount and income, the game's formatted strings winning over compacted numbers, a Full badge and loading placeholders), IdleGenerators (producers with owned, yield, level, boost, Auto and a ProgressBar for the running cycle; reports choose, a locked row disabled), IdlePurchases (a ×1/×10/×100/Max radio group, or the game's own wording of each amount, reporting chooseamount, and upgrades with effect, level, count and cost; reports buy only for a row that is affordable and neither maxed nor locked), IdlePrestige (held and gained prestige currency, each bonus now and after the reset, the requirement met or not; reports request, then while the game sets confirming an inline Reset and Cancel, Escape cancelling) and IdleOffline (time away as the game's words or seconds through formatDuration, the haul per currency; reports collect and, when canDouble, double). They compute no income, prices, counts, gains or earnings: the game passes them in. Each names its frames, rows, cells, titles and badges as parts (src/ui/components/idle/README.md).
idle.css dresses the idle components' parts in the pack's brass, leather and crimson, from its existing tokens, and breathes the loading placeholder (still under reduced motion).

A built-in puzzle component (packages/engine/src/ui/components/puzzle/level-path.svelte): a scrolling level path of chapters, each with its name and the stars the game counts, and its levels as round nodes placed across the path where the game says (x), each locked, open, current or done with its stars. Reports choose with the level's key and details (X, pad Y) on the focused level; a locked level is disabled and sends neither. Parts frame, chapter, title, badge, lane, trail, node, number, stars, here and empty.

A built-in puzzle component (puzzle/goals.svelte): the in-level HUD with what limits the level (moves left or a countdown), a Running low warning when the game says so, the goals as icons with what is left of each and a check once met, and the score, all as the game counts them. The goals wrap under the counter and score by the component's own width, as the level path and booster tray tighten theirs. Parts frame, counter, label, figure, warning, goals, goal, count, done and score.

A built-in puzzle component (puzzle/boosters.svelte): the booster tray, each booster with its icon, count and name; one the game will not take now is disabled, locked and worded Unavailable, the armed one is pressed and worded Armed. Reports choose with the booster's key; the game spends, arms or refuses it. Parts frame, booster, count, name, state and empty.

A built-in puzzle component (puzzle/summary.svelte): the end of a level, won or failed, with the level's name, the score on the shared StarBar, the stars the game awarded in words, a New best badge, the game's worded score breakdown and total, and Next (only when the game offers it), Retry and Map (also Escape and pad B), reported as next, retry and menu. Parts frame, band, title, level, stars, earned, record, breakdown, row, rowLabel, rowValue, total, actions, next, retry and menu.

templates/styles/fantasy/puzzle.css dresses the puzzle components through their parts: brass-rimmed seals for levels (crimson for the current one, grey for locked), gold stars, the HUD plates for goals and boosters with the low counter's pulse (dropped under reduced motion), and the pack's iron and crimson buttons on the level summary.

A racing group of built-in components under @ui/components/racing/, used by name like the rpg and shooter ones: RacingTelemetry (speed in the game's units, gear, a rev dial with its redline marked or a compact strip, boost, the shift cue), RacingLapHud (lap n/N, position p/N, current, best and last lap times, the split delta ahead or behind, the final lap, an optional checkpoint HudTimer that turns warn at warnAt seconds, 10 by default), RacingStandings (the running order with gaps, the player's row and pitting, retired and finished badges), RacingBanner (the 3-2-1 countdown, GO, final lap and finish calls; a new call id replays its entrance, which reduced motion skips), RacingGarage (the shown car with arrows and a tile strip, StatBar ratings, owned, locked and driven states, Buy disabled and named Too costly when the game says the car is not affordable; reports choose, select and buy with the car's key, and prev, next and back) and RacingResults (the classification with times, points, the fastest-lap mark, DNF and DSQ; reports continue and retry). They compute no times, gaps, points, prices or unlocks: the game passes them in. Each names its frames, rows, cells, titles and badges as parts (src/ui/components/racing/README.md).
racing.css dresses the racing components' parts in the pack's brass, soot and crimson, from its existing tokens.

A rhythm group of built-in components under @ui/components/rhythm/, used by name like the rpg and shooter ones: RhythmSongSelect (the song list with jacket, artist, BPM and New, Cleared, Locked, Selected and Previewing in words, the selected song's details, loading and error states; reports choose and preview with the song's key, and retry from the error state), RhythmDifficulty (one tile per chart with its tier, level, best grade and score; reports choose), RhythmJudgement (Perfect to Miss with Early or Late and the combo or Combo broken; a new hit id draws the word afresh, so a pack's entrance animation replays), RhythmScoreHud (score, accuracy, a life gauge with Danger and Failed, the song's progress as a ProgressBar) and RhythmResults (grade, Cleared or Failed, score against the old best, Full combo or All perfect, max combo, accuracy and the judgement tally; reports retry and next, Escape and pad B being next). They judge, time and score nothing: the game passes every figure in. Each names its frames, rows, cells, titles and badges as parts (src/ui/components/rhythm/README.md).
rhythm.css dresses the rhythm components' parts in the pack's brass, soot and crimson, from its existing tokens, and pops the judgement in for each hit (a quick fade under reduced motion).

A strategy group of built-in components under @ui/components/strategy/, used by name like the rpg and shooter ones: StrategySelection (the selected units and buildings as portrait cells with counts and health bars, the focused group's name, line, status and StatBar, and its command card: each plate with its <kbd data-action> key cap, a cooldown shade and time, an On mark for a toggle, and when disabled the reason in words; reports choose and command with the row's key), StrategyQueue (the production queue with a ProgressBar and time left per order, stack counts, waiting, paused and blocked words with the reason, count over limit and Queue full; reports cancel with the order's key), StrategyWave (wave n of N or an endless count, the phase in words, the next wave's HudTimer that turns warn at warnAt seconds, 5 by default, the incoming enemies by kind with counts, boss and unscouted marks, and Call early with its reward; reports callEarly) and StrategyTower (the tower's stats with the value after the next upgrade behind an arrow, its upgrade paths with tier of tiers, cost and data-state affordable, unaffordable, locked or maxed, each also a word and the reason when locked, and Sell with the refund; reports upgrade with the path's key and sell). They compute no costs, timing, legality or stats: the game passes every figure and flag in. Each names its frames, rows, cells, titles and badges as parts (src/ui/components/strategy/README.md).
strategy.css dresses the strategy components' parts in the pack's leather, brass, iron and crimson, from its existing tokens.

A <button> holds content: <button class="primary"><icon name="coin"/>Buy<badge>3</badge></button> lays its icon, text and badge out as a centred row inside the button's frame, states and press, and they take the button's ink. A text-only button is unchanged.

color-mix() takes one colour or more (CSS Color 5 §3.3): each is mixed into the mix of those before it by its share of their percentages, normalised as CSS Values 5 §6.1 says, and the colour space may be left out (OKLab). Percentages that are all 0% give a transparent colour instead of a parse error. Two-colour mixes draw as before.

CSS Color 5's contrast-color(<colour>) resolves to white or black, whichever has the greater WCAG 2 ratio on the colour as an opaque ground (white on a tie), so it reads at least 4.58:1 on any ground. It takes any colour, a role included (contrast-color(var(--panel)) is resolved where it is drawn and follows a scheme switch), and nests in color-mix() and relative colours.

A control element takes its inside from a control document: a component document that declares <meta name="control" content="progress"> (a tag with optional attribute tests, as input[type=range]) is instantiated under every element it names. Its props read the host's attributes, :host and :host(...) style the host under the rules written for it where it stands, and an element with part="name" is the host's ::part(name), which a pack's or a document's ::part() rule outranks. The cook bundles a control document when a game's documents have its element.

The engine's @ui/controls/progress.svelte and @ui/controls/meter.svelte draw <progress> and <meter>: track and fill are elements, reached as before through ::part(track) and ::part(fill). A game replaces one with its own control document for the element (og ui eject controls/progress).
A <meter> carries HTML's region of its value as its region attribute (optimum, suboptimum or poor) for its own document's selectors as well as its parts': meter[region=poor] { ... } matches.

A document holds UI state of its own: <meta name="state:open" content="bool"> (number, string or bool, with data-default) gives each instance of the document, and each host of a control document, its own value, read by its name and written with bind: (<details bind:open={open}>). A snapshot carries it, and it goes when the instance does. Use it for what the game has no stake in (a picker open, the tab shown); $state stays refused.
`--switch-knob-shadow` gives a switch's knob a shadow, and `--checkbox-radius` a checkbox's box its radius (by default the field radius).

Every value a style pack restyles a core control with is now a token the default style's rules read, so a pack restyles buttons, checkboxes, radios, switches, tabs, sliders, fields, selects, steppers, details, panels, dialogs, tooltips, HUD frames, slots, badges, meters, the keyboard and the touch controls by setting `:root` values alone: fills, inks, rims and their widths, shadows, border images, corner shapes, type, padding and glass, each per state and variant (`--button-fill`, `--button-primary-hover-image`, `--checkbox-checked-fill`, `--tabs-tab-selected-ink`, `--tooltip-glass`, `--badge-success-fill`, the full list in docs/ui.md §3.1). Role frames take `--frame-glass` and plates `--plate-glass` as their backdrop filter, except a bare frame and one inside another. Each defaults to what the control drew before, so the default style is unchanged.

HTML and CSS for the core controls: a range's list and ticks and labels, -og-fill-origin and disabled; a checkbox caption placed in source order, flex-direction: row-reverse on its label, a description, -og-control-size and disabled on switches and tabs; dialog closedby (HTML defaults: closerequest for a modal, none in place) and appearance: none; aria-invalid on select and input; select::picker(select) { max-height }; object-view-box: inset() and -og-uv on ; as text; data-og-instant settles an element's first entrance.

The built-in conversation shows its line rate characters a second, starting again with each new line, and reports revealed once the line is whole; rate 0 (and left out) shows the line at once as before, and setting 0 finishes a line early. Reduced motion shows the whole line.

count={$n} counted text (-og-count-duration, -og-count-decimals); -og-reveal typewriter text with onrevealed; <select> with -og-select: cycle; <dialog> with -og-spotlight: <id>; <input type="color"> with a picker writing #rrggbb back; the settings screen's tree from $pages and $entries collections.

HTML core controls: a plain <input type="checkbox"> is a check box (indeterminate a dash; switch keeps the switch), <input type="radio" value bind:group> radios, <input type="number"> with -og-stepper: buttons a stepper, <menu> of menu items; onhold (data-hold ms), oncontextmenu (secondary press or long press), ontoggle and onclose fire.
A stat with count: true counts up from 0 as the screen opens, written whole or with its decimals digits after the point (a percent stat as a percent). The other stats show their value as before.
An amount the component formats itself (no value string) counts to each new amount instead of jumping. A formatted value the game passes is shown as it is.

A counter writes its number as a binding's format does, in the UI's language: format="compact" (1.2K), percent (0.62 as 62%), clock, duration, letters and the rest. The count runs through what the format shows, and decimals is then the format's digit count. Without a format it groups thousands as before.
A counter starts its first count at from (a score counting up from 0 as its screen opens). Left out, it shows its value at once and counts only when the value changes, as before.

`cross-fade()` (CSS Images 4 §2.6) is an image wherever a background, mask or border image takes one: `cross-fade(url(a.png) 30%, url(b.png))` draws each image placed as the layer places it, weighted and summed into one image (a colour is a solid image). Omitted percentages share what is left of 100%, a sum over 100% is scaled to it, and under it the rest is transparent. Images of different sizes each keep their own size.

Scroll-triggered animations (CSS Animation Triggers 1): `timeline-trigger: --name view() contain / cover` on an element makes a trigger that activates when its timeline enters the first range and deactivates when it leaves the second; `animation-trigger: --name play-forwards play-backwards` (or play, play-once, pause, reset, replay) makes an animation wait at its start until then, so a card can animate in once it scrolls into view and back out when it leaves. `trigger-scope` keeps a name to a subtree. Trigger states and playback are saved UI state.

Customizable select (HTML `appearance: base-select`): `select { appearance: base-select }` builds the select from its own children instead of the native dropdown.
