Its `<button>` is the trigger, `<selectedcontent>` shows the chosen option's content, and `::picker(select)` is an anchored top-layer popover holding `<option>`s with any content, `<optgroup>`s and `<hr>`s. A press on an option writes its value, fires onchange and closes the picker. The chosen option matches `:checked` and the select matches `:open`. Options may now carry an id and a class.

added.member: CSS alignment-baseline, baseline-shift, baseline-source and dominant-baseline
added.summary: vertical-align is CSS Inline 3's shorthand of alignment-baseline, baseline-shift and baseline-source, and all four properties and dominant-baseline apply to text runs and inline-level boxes. A run aligns its alphabetic, ideographic, central, middle, mathematical, hanging, text-top or text-bottom baseline (`baseline`: its paragraph's dominant-baseline) with the same baseline of the paragraph's text, from each font's BASE table or the baselines CSS Inline 3 Appendix A.2 synthesizes; baseline-shift then raises it by a length, a percentage of its line height, sub or super, or places it on the line box's top, centre or bottom. SVG text's dominant-baseline takes the same font baselines.

added.member: UI: every CSS mix-blend-mode, in documents, style packs and Rive
added.summary: mix-blend-mode takes darken, lighten, color-burn, hard-light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color and luminosity beside the earlier modes; style packs take them as `blend`, Rive's blend modes 16 to 28 convert instead of failing, and og-render's UiBlend gains the variants.
The UI guide explains existing root safe-area padding versus viewport-relative env() values and fixed viewport-page padding, backed by computed output tests.

added.member: UI documents: border, outline and box-shadow
added.summary: Standard CSS borders and outlines on any element: the border and outline shorthands and their longhands (per-side width, style and colour, outline-offset), styles none, hidden, solid, dashed, dotted, double, groove, ridge, inset and outset, and currentColor. A border pads the box (border-box); an outline takes no room, so :focus-visible { outline: … } replaces the core focus ring. box-shadow takes a comma list of [inset] x y [blur [spread]] [colour], outer shadows under the background and inset ones over it.

overflow, overflow-x and overflow-y take visible, hidden, clip, scroll and auto as CSS Overflow 3 defines them (visible beside a non-visible axis computes to auto); auto and scroll scroll that axis, hidden and clip clip the children. scrollbar-width: none hides a scrolling box's bars.

added.member: og ui sheet and og ui review
added.summary: Accept CSS pack directories or discovered names. Pack sheets cover the core controls at desktopHd and phonePortrait, 100% and 150% text, including overlapping scroll captures below the fold. Pack review adds locales. CSS source errors name their file and line; style check reports unresolved URLs and root-token contrast ratios without grading.
The core sheet loads Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Arabic string tables before its document. Locale review renders translated text with the installed locale font packs and mirrors Arabic layout.

CSS `caret-shape: auto | bar | block | underscore` (inherited): a focused field draws its caret as a bar, a block under the next character's advance, or an underscore below it; with no next character the block and underscore take 1ch after the text. A terminal or retro console screen gets its caret without game code.

CJK text is spaced as CSS Text 4 §8.4 and §8.5 say. text-autospace (normal by default) puts an eighth of an ideograph's advance between an ideograph and a Latin letter or digit on one line, never at a line break; replace and French punctuation spacing work too. text-spacing-trim (normal by default: space-start trim-adjacent allow-end) sets fullwidth brackets and punctuation half-width through the font's halt feature at a line's start and end and between punctuation pairs, and allow-end fits a closing bracket on a line it fits only trimmed. Mixed CJK and Latin text and CJK punctuation now lay out a little differently by default; text-autospace: no-autospace and text-spacing-trim: space-all restore the old spacing.

added.member: UI: CSS clip-path rect(), xywh(), shape(), geometry boxes and url(#id)
added.summary: clip-path takes rect() and xywh() with round, CSS Shapes 2's shape() (move, line, hline, vline, curve, smooth, arc, close), a geometry box beside a shape or alone (border-, padding-, content-, margin-, fill-, stroke- and view-box), and url(#id) of an inline SVG <clipPath> in user space or objectBoundingBox units.

added.member: UI documents: every CSS colour function, color-mix(), relative colours, light-dark() and all named colours
added.summary: Document CSS colours take hex with alpha, all 148 named colours, rgb(), hsl(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() and color() over every predefined space, color-mix() with hue methods, relative colours over roles (oklch(from var(--accent) l c calc(h + 180))) and light-dark(). Out-of-gamut colours are gamut mapped as CSS Color 4 says; colours over roles resolve against the active style when drawn.

Each column's ::column::scroll-marker is now a pseudo-element of its own: :target-current, :target-before and :target-after follow its own column, and :hover only the marker under the pointer, so a scroll-marker group can highlight the current column. Before, a column marker took none of these states. A state-dependent `content` on a column marker is not applied.

A multi-column container's columns are ::column pseudo-elements (CSS Multicol 2 §4.8). ::column takes scroll-snap-align, scroll-snap-stop and scroll-margin, so each column is a snap area of its scroll container. ::column::scroll-marker gives each column a marker in the container's ::scroll-marker-group, and pressing one scrolls its column to the view's start. Columns that overflow a multi-column scroll container now scroll into view; before, the container's scrollable width stopped at its box. A column marker does not yet take :target-current, :target-before or :target-after.

A ::before or ::after content's alternative text, the list after / of strings, counter()s and attr()s (CSS Generated Content 3 §1.2), is what the accessibility tree reads in place of what it draws: `content: "★" / "Featured"` reads Featured. An empty one, `/ ""`, marks the content decorative and leaves it unread. The drawn content is unchanged. A / followed by a quote, an image or nothing is refused.

added.member: UI documents: per-corner, elliptical and % border-radius, and corner-shape
added.summary: border-radius takes four corners, the elliptical / form and percentages, with border-<corner>-radius longhands and logical corner names; corner-shape and its longhands take round, squircle, bevel, scoop, notch, square and superellipse(). Backgrounds, borders, outlines, shadows and overflow clips follow the corners. og-render: UiCorner::Css(UiCssCorners) gives a rectangle elliptical radii and a superellipse per corner.

list-style-type and the list-style shorthand take any counter style: the predefined ones, an @counter-style name, symbols(…) (CSS Counter Styles 3 §6.1), or a "string" drawn as the marker. counter() and counters() take symbols(…) too. markerType now holds the CSS value as written (lower-alpha, not lowerAlpha).

CSS `::details-content`: a `<details>` element's content under its summary is one box its rules style (padding, background, border, gap and every other box property over the disclosure's own), including under the details' `[open]`. A codex or settings accordion can frame its revealed panel without wrapping it.

Any box with display: list-item is a list item: it draws a ::marker in its list-style-type, numbered by the list-item counter (CSS Lists 3 §4.6: each one increments it by 1 unless its counter-increment names list-item). An <li> is a list item through the UA sheet's li { display: list-item }, so an <li> set to another display draws no marker.

`<input type="file">` is now HTML's file upload control: a button (`::file-selector-button`, "Choose file…" unless the input has text) with the names chosen beside it ("No file chosen" before any). A press anywhere on the input still sends `filepick`. `::file-selector-button` rules now style the button as they style a `<button>`, where before they were accepted and styled nothing. `field-sizing: fixed` keeps the names at the width "No file chosen" takes.

Moves frames where a document sets them: every font-variant-* keyword, font-feature-settings and font-kerning reach the shaper as OpenType settings with their values (oldstyle and slashed-zero figures, fractions, ligatures off, superior and inferior digits, full-width forms, kern off), not only small caps and tabular figures; settings apply after the variants, and a line is measured with the features it is drawn with.

font-style: oblique <angle> slants a synthesised oblique by its angle (14deg when it names none) instead of the engine's fixed slant; font-synthesis-weight, font-synthesis-style and the font-synthesis shorthand set to none stop a bold or a slant from being synthesised where no face has it.

added.member: UI: CSS isolation and group blending
added.summary: A document element with mix-blend-mode composites with its subtree as one group through the blend (CSS Compositing 1 §3.2), and `isolation: isolate` makes an element a group its descendants' blends stay inside. og-render reads a copy of a UI layer drawn so far for the blends inside it, applies the spec's backdrop alpha, and composites a layer through its UiShape's blend.

Horizontal rich paragraphs hang first opening punctuation, last closing punctuation, and line-end stops and commas with force-end or allow-end. Hanging punctuation is excluded from alignment width; allow-end hangs only when needed to fit, and inline padding prevents hanging.

Custom highlights (CSS Custom Highlight API): `og.ui.setHighlight(name, { ranges, priority })` registers ranges of laid-out text, each from a character of one element to a character of the same element or a later one, by path and offset, and `::highlight(<name>)` styles them with background-color, color, text-decoration and text-shadow, as ::selection is styled. A style reaches the elements under its rule (`:root::highlight(found)` styles them all). Overlays stack by priority under ::target-text and the selection, a tie going to the highlight registered later. It suits search hits, words a tutorial points out, and a spell checker's marks.

added.member: CSS hyphens: auto, hyphenate-character and hyphenate-limit-chars
added.summary: hyphens: auto breaks words at the hyphenation points of the game's language (og.i18n's locale), from hyph-utf8's TeX patterns; a text with no locale set is not hyphenated. The dictionaries ship in the latin (27 languages) and cyrillic-greek (7) font packs, and the cook packs one only when the game declares hyphens: auto and ships a locale of that language; a shipped locale with no dictionary is warned of at cook and breaks only at soft hyphens. hyphenate-character sets what a hyphenated line ends in (a hyphen by default), and hyphenate-limit-chars the fewest characters of a word that hyphenates and of its parts before and after the break (CSS Text 4 §6). manual stays the initial value: only soft hyphens break.

Backgrounds, masks and border images select image-set candidates by viewport density, preserve density-correct intrinsic sizing, filter unsupported types before duplicate resolutions, and discover bare-string asset URLs. Retained documents and button part backgrounds reselect when DPR changes; saved drawings preserve image density.

added.member: UI: CSS pointer-events, touch-action, visibility and every cursor keyword in documents
added.summary: pointer-events none and auto (inherited) and the SVG values on inline SVG shapes, tested on their fill and stroke; touch-action pans and pinch-zoom intersected down the tree; visibility hidden and collapse with visible children inside a hidden parent; cursor takes every CSS UI 4 keyword, and og.ui.Cursor gains contextMenu, cell, verticalText, alias, copy, noDrop, allScroll, resizeCol, resizeRow and the edge and corner resizes. The visible attribute stays.

CSS `interactivity: inert | auto`: `inert` makes an element and its subtree take no input, as the `inert` attribute does, and a declared value overrides that attribute (HTML's `[inert] { interactivity: inert }`).

CSS `interest-delay-start`, `interest-delay-end` and the `interest-delay` shorthand on an `interestfor` control: how long the pointer rests before its hint shows, and how long the hint stays after the pointer and focus leave. `normal` is the style's slow duration to show and its fast duration to leave; a hint used to vanish the frame its control lost interest.

CSS `interpolate-size` (inherited): under `allow-keywords` a `width` or `height` transition between a length and `auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, `fit-content` or `stretch` moves through `calc-size()` instead of jumping, so `height: 0` → `auto` opens smoothly. `numeric-only`, the initial value, keeps the jump.

added.member: UI: CSS background-origin, background-clip (with text), background-attachment and background-blend-mode
added.summary: Background layers take their positioning box, their clip box or the element's glyphs, fixed and local attachment, and a blend mode per layer inside an isolated group; gradient layers take size, position and repeat as tiles of their concrete size.

added.member: UI: CSS border-image and every border-image-* longhand
added.summary: A gradient or url() image cut into nine parts by its slice and drawn over the border box with its widths, outset and repeat (stretch, repeat, round, space) instead of the border lines.

added.member: UI: CSS mask layers, every mask-* longhand and mask-border
added.summary: mask and mask-image take several url() and gradient layers with size, position, repeat, origin, clip, mode and composite; mask-border and its longhands cut by a border image's nine parts.

added.member: og-render UiPaint::GradientImage, UiFit::BorderImage, UiEdge::Space, UiBackground::area, UiImage::luminance and the Porter-Duff UiBlend variants
added.summary: A gradient drawn as an image tile, a CSS border image fit, space repeats, a background's positioning area, luminance images, and SourceIn, SourceOut, DestinationIn and Xor blends for shapes and layer composites.

margin, margin-left/-right, margin-inline (and -start/-end) and margin-block-start/-end take px, em, rem, viewport units, percentages (of the parent's content width, as CSS 2 §8.3 has it), negatives, auto and calc(). In a block's flow auto left and right margins centre or push the box (margin: 0 auto); in a flex line auto margins take the free space and align the item across it; in a grid area they align the item and other margins inset it.

added.member: UI documents: mixed-unit calc(), min(), max(), clamp()
added.summary: A length calc() reduces to a linear sum of %, px and em terms, with rem and vw/vh/vmin/vmax turned into px when the element resolves; layout resolves the percentage against the basis it already has. min(), max() and clamp() over such sums are evaluated at layout. width: calc(100% - 12px) and min(100%, 600px) work, a var() term bound with style:--name moves only its element, and a viewport unit re-resolves on resize.

added.member: UI documents: empty blocks collapse through themselves
added.summary:
An empty block in a block's flow (no padding, auto height, no children but such blocks) and an empty

are 0 tall, and their top and bottom margins collapse with their neighbours' (CSS 2 §8.3.1).

transition-timing-function, animation-timing-function, keyframe timing and og.tween ease text take CSS Easing 2's linear(<number> <percentage>{0,2}, …) with the spec's canonicalisation and extrapolation.
docs/ui.md includes a pinned 454-feature WebDX CSS checklist distinguishing scoped output proofs from missing implementation or proof, with widget part applicability tracked separately.

added.member: CSS display: list-item on text and <summary>
added.summary:
A text-only element such as a

or with display: list-item draws a ::marker too: outside before its first line, or inside as the first run of its text in the ::marker's style.

is a list item in the UA sheet (HTML §15.3.12): its marker is disclosure-closed, or disclosure-open while its
is open, and list-style restyles or removes it. The disclosure-closed and disclosure-open styles draw the theme's disclosure chevron on any list item. The summary is now an element of the details' header, so its own rules (summary, summary::marker, details[open] > summary) style it.
border-block, border-inline, border-block-start/-end, border-inline-start/-end and their -width, -style and -color longhands now work, mapped to the physical sides in horizontal-tb, left to right.

CSS Motion Path: `offset-path` (`path("…")`, `circle([<n>px])` or `ray(<angle> [<size>])`), `offset-distance` (px or % of the path, and it transitions and animates), `offset-rotate` (`auto`, `reverse` and/or an angle), `offset-anchor` and `offset-position` move an element's anchor along a path in its parent's border box, after `translate`/`rotate`/`scale` and before `transform`. Hits and the cursor follow the moved box.

Scroll anchoring (CSS Scroll Anchoring 1): a scroll container scrolled down from its start keeps what it shows in place when content above it grows or shrinks, a chat log or quest list that loads older entries no longer jumps. `overflow-anchor: none` turns it off on a container or keeps a subtree from being the anchor. UI state version 26 saves the anchors; version 25 upgrades with none.
A popover takes `::backdrop`: styled, it covers the page under the open popover (as a modal dialog's does), and closes with it.

On a box element, ::before and ::after are real boxes: display (inline by default), sizes, padding, borders, background, position, transforms, transitions and every other property a <div> takes apply to them, with the generated text inside. They cascade under their element's states, attributes and structural selectors, and never count as its children for :nth-child, :empty or sibling combinators. An idle frame still builds nothing. On a text element they stay styled runs of its text.

added.member: UI documents: ::backdrop and ::picker(select) take every box property
added.summary: dialog::backdrop styles a modal's scrim and select::picker(select) its open list with the full box property set: background, opacity, backdrop-filter, filter, padding, borders, radius, box-shadow and the rest. ::picker(select)'s max-height bounds the rows before they scroll.

Scoped view transitions (CSS View Transitions 2): `og.ui.startViewTransition(path)` starts a view transition on one element, like `element.startViewTransition()`. The `view-transition-name` elements in its subtree morph from where the last frame drew them to where they are now, drawn just after the element and styled by its document's `::view-transition-*` rules, a component's included. Several run at once, beside a screen's. `view-transition-scope: all` keeps the names under an element to its own transitions.

Scroll axis locking (CSS Overflow 5 §4): a drag on a scroll container that scrolls both ways keeps to the axis its first move runs along (within a 2:1 slope of it) until released, so a mostly-vertical swipe through a list no longer drifts sideways; `scroll-axis-lock: none` on a map or a zoomed image lets every drag move freely. UI state version 25 saves the locked axis; version 24 upgrades with none decided.

CSS `scroll-initial-target: nearest`: a scroll container that appears starts scrolled so the first such element in it stands at its view's start (its `scroll-margin` and the container's `scroll-padding` apply), from its first frame. A saga map or a long list can open on the current item without game code; a target added later does not move a container already shown.

Scroll markers and buttons (CSS Overflow 5 §3): `scroll-marker-group: before | after` on a scroll container builds a `::scroll-marker-group` beside it holding each inner element's `::scroll-marker` (a carousel's dots, a chapter list), which scroll their element into view when pressed; `::scroll-button(up | down | left | right | *)` pages the container by 85% of its view and matches `:disabled` at its ends. The marker for the section in view matches `:target-current`, those before and after `:target-before` and `:target-after`; `scroll-target-group: auto` gives `<a href="#id">` links the same states.

added.member: UI: CSS overscroll-behavior, scroll-behavior, scroll-margin, scroll-padding, scroll-snap-stop and the scrollbar properties in documents
added.summary: overscroll-behavior contain and none (and its axes) stop scroll chaining; scroll-behavior smooth glides a scroll into view; scroll-margin* and scroll-padding* (longhands, logical sides, shorthands) apply to snapping and scrolling into view; scroll-snap-stop always stops a fling; scrollbar-width thin draws half-width bars; scrollbar-color paints the thumb and a track; scrollbar-gutter stable [both-edges] keeps the bar's room.

Underlines and overlines break where they would cross a glyph's ink, a line thickness to either side, as CSS Text Decoration 4 §2.10.4 asks: auto (the initial value) skips every script but CJK, all skips CJK too, none draws the line whole. A line-through never breaks. Before, decoration lines ran through descenders.

Decoration lines skip spaces as CSS Text Decoration 4 §2.10.3 asks: by default (start end) a line's leading and trailing spaces are not underlined or struck through, all skips every space and word separator with the letter spacing beside it, none decorates them all. Before, an underline ran under a preserved line's end spaces.

Horizontal paragraph and label roots support text-box-trim, text-box-edge and the text-box shorthand. Trim the first and last lines to cap height, x-height, text or ideographic font edges without changing inter-line spacing; cap alphabetic lets buttons and badges centre their labels optically.

added.member: UI documents: standard CSS font and text properties on elements
added.summary: font-size, font-weight, font-style, line-height, letter-spacing, word-spacing, the font shorthand, font-variant*, font-feature-settings, font-variation-settings, font-kerning, font-synthesis, text-transform (all values), white-space and its longhands, text-wrap, hyphens, word-break, overflow-wrap, text-indent, tab-size, text-justify, text-align left/right/justify, text-align-last, text-decoration with style, colour, thickness and offset, -webkit-text-stroke, paint-order, accent-color, caret-color and color-scheme now work on document elements, inherited as CSS inherits them. font: var(--text-*) stays valid.

overflow-wrap: anywhere and break-word (and word-break: break-word) break a word too wide for its line between its letters once it has a line of its own; anywhere also lowers the text's min-content width to its widest letter.

text-align-last aligns a text's last line and each line a forced break ends (justify-all justifies it too); text-justify takes a justified line's room at its spaces (auto, inter-word), between every two characters (inter-character) or nowhere (none).

text-size-adjust (auto | none | <percentage>, inherited) is accepted instead of warned of as unsupported. It changes nothing: the engine never inflates text, which is the only case the property adjusts (CSS Mobile Text Size Adjustment 1 §2); a player's text scale stays its own setting.

added.member: UI: CSS text-wrap: balance and pretty laid out
added.summary: A wrapping label with text-wrap-style balance takes lines as even as its line count allows; pretty moves a word down so the last line is not one word alone. stable lays out as auto.
A cut label ends in the given string instead of an ellipsis (the `ellipsisText` prop).

Documents accept var(--space-*), var(--size-*), var(--radius-*) and var(--stroke-*) wherever a length is accepted, including border-radius, padding, size bounds, grid tracks, translations and interaction states. References survive cooking and follow the active style when built. Style declarations accept length and colour references, including token aliases; missing references and cycles name the token. Document colour references are checked against the default theme and the game's cooked styles; document cook stamps include those style sources. Rarity, damage, team and series colours can be used as colour tokens.

added.member: UI documents: CSS transform with 3D, perspective and preserve-3d
added.summary: transform takes every CSS function including matrix3d, rotate3d/X/Y/Z, translate3d/Z, scale3d/Z and perspective(); transform-origin takes keywords, lengths and a z; perspective, perspective-origin, transform-style: preserve-3d, backface-visibility and transform-box work. A 3D-transformed element is drawn perspective-correct and hit tested where it is seen. The individual translate, scale and rotate properties stay. Ui::save_state now writes version 22 (a map's projective row); Ui::upgrade_state reads versions 20 and 21.

A document's CSS takes `all: inherit | initial | unset | revert | revert-layer` (CSS Cascade 5 §3.2.1). It sets every property but `direction`, `unicode-bidi` and the custom properties at its place in the block, so a declaration after it wins and one before it loses. Any other value, `var()` included, fails to cook.

A document's CSS takes anchored container queries (CSS Anchor Positioning 2 §2): an anchor-positioned element with `container-type: anchored` answers `@container anchored(fallback: …)` for its descendants with the `position-try-fallbacks` entry it applied: `none` (its own placement), an `@position-try` name and try-tactics matched in order, or a position-area (`top`, `bottom any`), and `anchored(fallback)` for any entry. The descendants restyle on the frame after the applied entry changes.

A document's `width` and `height` (and `inline-size` and `block-size`) take `calc-size(<basis>, <calculation>)` (CSS Values 5). The basis is `auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, `fit-content`, `stretch`, a length or another calc-size(). The calculation is linear in `size`, as in `calc-size(auto, size * 0.5)` or `calc-size(max-content, size + 12px)`, and min and max apply after. og-ui's `Size::CalcSize` and `SizeBasis` carry it. A non-linear calculation, or calc-size() in a min-/max- bound, fails to cook.

`@container card { … }` with only a name applies under an ancestor container named `card`. `@container style()` takes ranges such as `style(--level > 3)`, `style(2 < --n <= 5)` and `style(--gap >= 12px)`. Custom properties and literals are compared once each side reduces to one unit; sides of different types are false (CSS Conditional 5).

`@custom-media --name <media-query-list>;` (also `true` or `false`) names a media query that `@media (--name)` and `@import … (--name)` use (Media Queries 5). A name can be used before it is defined and inside another definition, and its last definition wins. An undefined or self-referring name fails to cook.

Document media queries take `device-width`, `device-height` and `device-aspect-ratio`, with their `min-` and `max-` forms (Media Queries 4). They read the play surface. Also new: `-webkit-device-pixel-ratio` and its `min-`/`max-` forms, which are `resolution` in dppx; `-webkit-transform-3d`, which is 1 since 3D transforms draw; and `device-posture`, `horizontal-viewport-segments` and `vertical-viewport-segments`. No host reports a fold, so those answer `continuous` and 1.

CSS `dynamic-range-limit: standard | constrained | no-limit | dynamic-range-limit-mix()` (CSS Color HDR 1) on a document's root element caps how far over SDR white the frame goes on an extended-range surface. `standard` caps it at SDR white, `constrained` at one stop over (2×), and `no-limit` (the initial value) at the display's headroom. A mix is weighted in stops. The display pass clamps there, and the tone curves roll off to it. Where several documents' roots declare one, the most limiting wins.

A document's CSS takes `@function --name(--param <type>: <default>, …) returns <type> { --local: …; result: …; }` (CSS Custom Functions and Mixins 1) and calls `--name(arg, …)` in any value, a comma-holding argument in braces. A call substitutes as `var()` does: its body is evaluated on the calling element, reading the element's custom properties, the arguments, defaults and locals (a local shadows a parameter), with `@media` and `@supports` inside it. An argument that does not match its type, too many arguments, an unknown function, a self-call or a result that does not match `returns` make the property invalid. A call in a custom property resolves there and is inherited as its result.

A document's CSS takes `if(<condition>: <value>; …; else: <value>)` (CSS Values 5 §8.3): the value of the first branch whose condition holds, or nothing (the property unset) when none does. Conditions are `media(…)`, `supports(…)` and `style(…)` tests of the element's custom properties, joined by `not`, `and` and `or`. It substitutes as `var()` does: a custom property's `if()` resolves where the property is computed and its children inherit that branch, and a `media()` test resolves again when the viewport or preferences change. A malformed branch or test fails when the document is defined.

A document's CSS math takes `progress(no-clamp? value, start, end)` (CSS Values 5 §5), the value's place between start and end as a number clamped to [0, 1] unless `no-clamp`, and `random(key?, min, max, step?)` (§9.1). random() draws from a hash of its random cache name: by default the element, the property and its place in the value, shared by a `--name` key, scoped by `element-scoped`, `property-scoped` or `property-index-scoped`, or set by `fixed <number>`. A value is the same each time the element resolves and on every host. random() with a step, and progress(), take arguments in one unit.

A document's CSS takes `random-item(<key>, item, …)` (CSS Values 5 §9.2): it substitutes, as `var()` does, the item `floor(R × N)` of its random base value R, an item in braces (`{Times, serif}`) taken whole. A random function's key now names the property it is written in (a shorthand's, such as `margin` or `transition`, before it expands) and its place among the declaration's random functions (§9.4.1), and its cache name includes the document (the mount), so a shared `--name` draws apart in another mount. `progress()` of lengths that mix `%` with px, times a length (`calc(progress(50%, 0px, 200px) * 100px)`), reads its basis at layout.

A document's CSS takes `sibling-index()` and `sibling-count()` (CSS Values 5 §8.1): an element's place among its parent's children, from 1, and their count, as integers in any value or math (`transition-delay: calc(sibling-index() * 50ms)`). Inserting, removing or moving a row restyles its siblings on that frame. A document that uses neither pays nothing for them.

`@supports` takes CSS Conditional 5's `at-rule(@name)`, `named-feature(name)` and `env(name)`. `at-rule()` is true for the at-rules a document can use (not `@charset` or `@page`). `named-feature()` is true for `gamut-mapping`. `env()` is true for the safe-area and `-og-hud-inset-*` variables. `@import … supports(…)` now takes these too.

A text run (`::part` or HTML's `<sub>`/`<sup>`) and an inline-level box take baseline, sub, super, text-top, text-bottom, middle, top, bottom, lengths and percentages (CSS 2.1 §10.8); a moved run grows its line. `<sub>` and `<sup>` are inline markup, a size smaller.

CSS vertical form controls: a range input, a `<progress>` and a `<meter>` under `writing-mode: vertical-lr` or `vertical-rl` stand up, their `height` the track's length, with the value running top to bottom, or bottom to top under `direction: rtl` (`sideways-lr` the reverse). A press or drag reads the pointer down the track. A mixer's faders or a vertical health gauge are one CSS line.
word-spacing adds its length after each space and no-break space of a text, which was parsed but never laid out.
Loading currency balances compose the shared Spinner as well as their localized Loading label, matching Avatar and ItemSlot without exposing stale amounts. The spinner has its own restylable part.

A reusable currency/resource pill at @ui/components/base/currency.svelte: compact or game-formatted balances, optional capacity and income, explicit Full, Loading and Unavailable states, wrapping phone text and independently restylable parts. Read-only; the game owns the economy.

added.member: UI documents: <input type="date">, time, datetime-local, month, week
added.summary: A pad-friendly picker of og-ui steppers, one per part, bound by value in HTML's format, within min and max and on the step grid from min; a part past its end carries into the next. Required or out-of-range values are :invalid and hold a form's submit back. Before this they were refused.

A visual UI debugger in development builds: the inspector's UI view (F1, third tab, or inspect:ui[:<path>]) picks an element of the game's UI and shows its box model, its layout boundaries, its computed styles with the file:line each was written on, the style rules that dress it and its bindings, and draws its margin, border, padding and content boxes over the game. Layout bounds outlines every element. In Rust: Ui::debug_pick, Ui::debug_element, og_ui::debug_overlay (docs/ui.md 6.4).
dump_ui:motion[:path] writes the elements in visual states or animating alone, as dump_ui:layers writes the layer stack.

The default style is redesigned as smoked glass with lit edges, in four materials: glass frames and plates, recesses (cells, wells, fields, tracks), raised faces (buttons, knobs, keys, the chosen tab) and light in the primary for what is chosen, focused or active. New tokens a pack can set: --color-glass*, --color-plate-*, --color-rim*, --color-lit, --color-shade*, --color-tile*, --color-raised-*, --color-glow*, --color-select-*, --shadow-panel/plate/raise/raise-hover/sunk/held, and the roles' --raise-shadow, --held-shadow, --sunk-shadow, --cell-scene-* (a cell that stands over the scene), --cell-marked-shadow and --well-alert-fill. Disabled checkboxes, radios and fields go flat (--checkbox-disabled-fill, --field-disabled-fill), and the accent badge is light in the primary (--badge-primary-fill).

transition:, in:, out: and animate:flip accept motion: 'ui' | 'panel' | 'emphasis' | 'playful' | 'enter' | 'exit' to use the style's duration and easing at playback instead of literal timing. Geometry and transition delays still apply; mixing a motion token with duration or easing is refused.

`@media (display-state: fullscreen)` matches, as `display-mode: fullscreen` does: the play surface fills its display. `normal`, `maximized` and `minimized` never match; the bare `(display-state)` is true.

background and background-image take url() layers beside gradients: an atlas icon by name or a texture by its asset handle, each with a position, size and repeat (CSS Backgrounds 3), and background-size, background-position and background-repeat as comma lists over the layers. border-radius and clip-path cut them.
An image fill sized (cover, contain, given or auto from the texture's own size), placed and repeated per axis (repeat, no-repeat, space, round) as a CSS background layer.

added.member: UI documents: filter and backdrop-filter functions
added.summary: filter takes contrast(), invert(), sepia(), opacity() and drop-shadow() beside blur(), brightness(), grayscale(), hue-rotate() and saturate(), applied in the order written; drop-shadow() follows the alpha of what is drawn, not the box. backdrop-filter takes the same set over the backdrop.
Layer materials for a CSS colour matrix (over sRGB-encoded straight colour, clamped) and a drop shadow of the layer's alpha, and a colour matrix over a backdrop.

added.member: UI documents: CSS gradients, mask-image, clip-path, filter, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode, text-shadow, -og-material
added.summary: Document CSS takes linear, radial and conic gradients (and repeating ones) in background, mask-image gradients, clip-path basic shapes and path() cut by analytic coverage with either fill rule, filter blur and colour adjustment, backdrop-filter glass, mix-blend-mode, text-shadow, and -og-material for og-render's built-in layer materials. Geometry resolves against the placed box; an idle element builds nothing.

A <ground> is laid as a decal against the depth prepass: it follows the terrain's height under it within a quarter of its shorter side of its plane, surfaces standing across the plane fade it, nearer geometry hides it, and it falls back to the plane where the scene lies behind it. It is drawn with the camera among it (a corner behind the camera) instead of skipped. A moving camera still costs no bindings and no reconciling.

A projected layer's drape, in place of the unreleased UiLayer.quad: the affine map from a screen point and its view depth to the layer's rect and the plane's normal (UiDrape::new from a view-projection), with the corners that size its target when all are in front. A frame with one runs the depth prepass. The ui-ground reference is now draped over a heightfield with a pillar.

A box laid flat in the world at an entity or point, drawn by the UI onto the plane in perspective under the screen's elements (selection rings, range markers, decals). A moving camera moves only its quad: no bindings, no reconciling, no relevelling. Inert; not drawn behind the camera.

A layer composited onto a screen quadrilateral through the projective map (square_to_quad), its target sized from the size it is seen at, capped at UI_QUAD_LAYER_MAX. New reference: og-tests ui-ground.
Explicit model paths, keyed each expressions with empty branches, named snippets and render references, and conditional scoped style rules for the retained document adapter.

A keyed each of <anchor mass="name" value max> compiles to a mass template (a number, or a bar with max) whose timeline is the element's CSS animation keyframes (translate, scale, opacity). A row with an animation spawns one instance when it appears; one without stands with its row, pushed every tick with nothing built.

-og-burst in a @keyframes step fires a burst from the element. -og-emitter emits particles while the element stands. -og-meta draws a vignette or tint overlay at the element's opacity. The engine keeps emitters and overlays registered every tick, so a retained element builds nothing. Reduced motion silences bursts and emitters.

added.member: UI documents: drag and drop and Pointer Events
added.summary: draggable="true" with data-drag-type, and ondragstart, ondragend, ondragover and ondrop (drop targets filter by data-accept); onpointerdown, onpointermove, onpointerup and onwheel on any element. Events bubble to the nearest handler and carry { dragged, target } row keys and { x, y } in the handler's box (wheel: deltaX, deltaY).

added.member: UI documents: onhold, oncontextmenu, onrevealed, ontoggle, onclose
added.summary: Parsed as handlers; the controls that fire them land with the capabilities work (holdButton, menus, typewriter text, popovers, dialogs).

Scrolling boxes snap a released drag, a fling or a stopped wheel onto their areas' snap positions (mandatory or proximity). A modal dialog with -og-sheet-detents is a bottom sheet that drags onto its detents and closes when swiped down, writing open back.

<use href> draws a copy of a symbol (its viewBox fitted by preserveAspectRatio), group or shape that inherits the use's presentation attributes; clip-path and mask cut groups and shapes (a mask of one gradient-filled shape fades); a <pattern> fill tiles its shapes; <image href> draws an atlas image icon or a render texture in its rect; <title> names its parent for assistive technology and binds. Rect, circle and ellipse clips are native; a clip to paths draws uncut with a warning.
With a view box, the sub-rect its non-path shape, clip and paints fill, in view-box units.

<text x y dx dy font-size font-weight font-style text-anchor dominant-baseline fill> inside an <svg> is one line shaped by og-ui's text, its anchor placed on the point fitted into the svg's box and scaled with the view box (hit tests and accessibility bounds too, right to left where the view box shows it); its content binds, and <tspan> runs take font-weight, font-style, text-decoration and fill. A <pattern> fill on a path is cut to the path.

An out-of-flow element placed at a point of its parent's view box, laid out unscaled and scaled by the fit about its anchor (layout's own channel beside flip, gesture and custom; not the sampled transform).
A <clipPath>'s shapes cut by their clip-rule, nonzero or evenodd (a mask's by fill-rule), so an evenodd ring clips its hole; one clip's shapes take one rule.

<joystick action>, <dpad action> and <button data-og-touch> are input sources of og-input actions: their laid-out rects become the action map's zones, sampled from the touches that started on them in the tick (a stick from its centre past data-dead-zone, a d-pad eight ways, a button while held). @media takes pointer, any-pointer, hover and any-hover.

On-screen control zones (ControlZone: an action, a stick, pad or button kind, a rect in surface CSS px) feed actions as one more binding; session state like the surface, kept across a restore and outside the world hash.

A camera's render target in the layout (the native scene viewport): src names the target, camera-orbit, camera-target and field-of-view (model-viewer's names) place its camera, bind:clientWidth and bind:clientHeight write its laid-out size, and its pointer events carry the ray into its scene.

A box held over an entity or world point (the native world anchor): offset, occlusion, declutter, clamp="edge", priority, max-distance and scale-at. Placed every tick; its subtree is built again only when a binding it reads changes.

The native world panel in a document: laid out at its CSS size, drawn into the render target src names, shown on a quad size world units across at an entity or point, turned by rotation. Pointer rays that meet the quad reach its controls (onclick, focus, Enter).

added.member: UI: {#each} over a list held in a row
added.summary: Inside an {#each}, {#each row.cells as cell, i (cell.id)} reads a list held in a row field: an array of objects keyed by a nonempty string field of each item. Its rows follow the list when the holding field is patched (new keys are made, missing ones go, kept ones move), the index alias reads the item's place, and bind: on a nested row's field writes the holding row. Before, an each read only a $name collection or a prop bound to one.
{#each $items as item, i (item.id)} names the row's position i (from 0), which follows a move, insert or remove in both immediate and mounted documents. A key that uses the position is refused.

Number inputs retain the text field's height, raw string, validation, selection, clipboard and readonly behavior while offering side-by-side increment/decrement buttons with 24px desktop and 44px phone/touch widths. Up/Down preserves editing focus; Shift arrows and Shift-click use the larger step. Spinner options support wrapping and unfocused display formatting without rewriting the editing value.

`element(#id)` (CSS Images 4 §2.7) is a background image: the document's first drawn element of that id, drawn live in each tile the layer places at the element's border box size (background-size, -position and -repeat as for any image), without its own transform or its ancestors' opacity and clips. An element that holds the image (itself, an ancestor, or a cycle of element() images) draws nothing. A hash in a CSS value now takes `-` and `_`, so `element(#hud-map)` names `hud-map`.

Emphasis marks take their side from the content language, as CSS Text Decoration 4's default sheet does: under horizontal Chinese text (lang="zh", or a Chinese locale at the root), over Japanese and Korean; an author's text-emphasis-position still wins.

`exportparts` on a control written inside a control document (CSS Shadow Parts §4.2): `<progress exportparts="fill: bar-fill">` in a meter's control document makes the bar's fill the meter's `::part(bar-fill)`, so a page or a style pack reaches it from outside. A rule reaching a part through an export ranks one shadow boundary further out, over the holding document's own rule for it. Written anywhere else, or on a component instance, it is refused.

shooter.css dresses the shooter components' new parts: the vitals plate in the ammunition's brass rim (CombatHud.vitals), the keyline on both edges of the circle reticle's ring (Crosshair.ring), the magazine strip in gold on a brass track (Ammo.magazine, Ammo.track), the weapon's name and the reload's words in letter-spaced small caps (Ammo.weapon, Ammo.label, Ammo.prompt), and the killfeed's headshot mark in gold (Killfeed.headshot). The low magazine and the empty prompt keep --warn and --danger.

shooter.css dresses the shooter components' parts: the crosshair's marks and hit confirmations, each with a dark keyline so the reticle reads over a bright sky and a dark ground; opaque lamp-black plates in a brass rim for the ammunition and the killfeed rows, with the names in their side's ink and the player's rows under a gold edge; the fire mode on a crimson tag; the loadout's categories under crimson bands and its slots as soot plates, hovered, pressed, focused, equipped, selected, locked, and locked while selected.

added.member: UI: feImage href="#id" draws the element mounted
added.summary: The element an <feImage href="#id"> draws is mounted again where the filter is, in every document: its bound attributes follow their stores, and the {#if} and {#each} blocks and the components inside it are built. It reads what the filtered element can read (its stores, its {#each} row, its component's props); an element that reads a row the filtered element is not in draws nothing and warns. The image is a picture: nothing in it takes input, sends an event, writes a store or runs a use: action, and it is not a child of the filtered element for selectors.

field-sizing: content also sizes a select to the option it shows, a file input to the names chosen, and text inputs and textareas in vertical writing modes along their inline axis (height), a line wide. Under the default fixed sizing a file input keeps its default label's width and cuts a longer chosen name with an ellipsis.

Text inputs and textareas support field-sizing: content. Their displayed value or placeholder determines intrinsic size; explicit CSS dimensions and min/max constraints still apply. Textareas wrap and grow instead of keeping their rows height. The default fixed sizing is unchanged.
Whether the host opens a file picker for a document's <input type="file">; false on the web and natively today.
Parses with accept, multiple and bind:value; built as a button sending a filepick event only where og.ui.filePicker is true, otherwise not built with a frame warning (it was refused at parse).

`filter(<image>, <filter functions>)` (Filter Effects 1 §12) is an image wherever a background, mask or border image takes one: `filter(url(a.png), grayscale(1) blur(2px))` draws the image through the same functions the `filter` property takes, in order, without filtering the element. It works inside `cross-fade()`, and a `filter()` of a `filter()` applies both lists. `url(#id)` references are refused.

added.member: UI: feImage href="#id" draws whatever the element draws
added.summary: An feImage of an element now builds the element as <use> builds it, so gradients, patterns, text, images, groups and nested <use> all draw into the filter's input, not only literal shapes with solid paint.

added.member: UI: backdrop-filter reads what is really under the element, url(#id) included
added.summary: backdrop-filter's functions and url(#id) now run in order as one SVG filter graph over a capture of what is under the element where its composite draws: the screen, or the group it is drawn in (the backdrop root). og-render's UiLayer::backdrop captures it; the blur is an exact Gaussian rather than the glass pyramid, so a backdrop with no blur is sharp.

feConvolveMatrix and the lighting primitives read kernelUnitLength. feImage takes an element of the document by href="#id", drawn as <use> would draw it in the filtered element's user space (og-render's UiFilterOp::Layer).

A data-hold element draws a fill from its start edge across the share of the hold its press has reached, over its background and under its content; button::-og-hold { background } colours it (::-og-hold is a pseudo-element box, as ::backdrop is). Enter, Space or a pad's A held while it has the focus hold it, and so does its data-action's input.

added.member: UI document <input type=checkbox switch data-on data-off>
added.summary: A switch's on and off words are its value for a screen reader and the probe.

With -og-stepper: buttons, -og-stepper-wrap: wrap goes past max to min, -og-stepper-large-step sets what a held button's repeats move by, and data-format writes the value through an ICU message over value in the UI's locale ({value, number} m, {value, number, compact}, {value, plural, =0 {Off} other {#}}), checked when the document is parsed.
A search box draws HTML's clear button at its end while it has text (`<id>/Clear`, dressed `<component>.clear`); a press empties it.
-og-select-filter: on puts a filter field atop the open list, off keeps it away, auto (the default) shows it past 10 options; data-filter-placeholder is what it shows while empty.

added.member: UI document <tabs icons badges>, tabPrev and tabNext
added.summary: icons and badges (a list each, one per tab) draw an icon before a tab's label and a count badge after it. The tabPrev and tabNext actions (Q and E, LB and RB) step through a document's tabs, wrapping.
HTML's exclusive accordion: of the disclosures in a mount sharing a literal name, one is open at once; opening one closes the others the next tick and writes their open state back.

`og ui eject hold-button` (a hold-to-confirm button with its holding words and hint) and `og ui eject action-hints` (the action bar: a <kbd data-action> glyph and hint per action, a hold row filling as its action is held).

added.member: UI document popover placement (position-area, insets, position-try-fallbacks on a popover)
added.summary: An open popover is placed by CSS anchor positioning against its implicit anchor, the control whose popovertarget or interestfor opened it: position-area picks the side and alignment, an inset (left: 8px beside a right-hand popover) offsets it, and position-try-fallbacks and @position-try flip it inside the safe area. A popover with none of them still hangs under its control, above it where there is more room.

A popover's ::-og-arrow { width; background } draws a square turned 45° across the edge facing its anchor, over the anchor's middle where the box allows, and hides while no side faces it. Its colour defaults to the popover's background.
contextmenu="id" on an element opens popover id at the point of a secondary press or long press on it; that zero-size point is its anchor, so position-area and fallbacks place it there.

packages/engine/src/ui/components/menu.svelte (commands, checks, radios, separators, headers, shortcuts and a drill-in submenu) and tooltip-card.svelte (rarity title and pips, art slot, stat rows with deltas, a comparison card, footer and action hints). Put them in a popover, or eject them with og ui eject menu and og ui eject tooltip-card.

A short tab set can opt into fitting its track: padding compresses first, then proportional tabs wrap labels to two lines and finally ellipsize, keeping their full accessible names. Without fit, long sets still scroll; fill keeps its existing equal-width behavior. Icon-only tabs accept an aria-labels string list.

`flex-wrap: balance` (CSS Flexbox 2): a wrapping flex container breaks its items into lines as even as the breaks allow, the longest line as short as it can be, through Taffy's balanced line breaking. `flex-flow` takes it too, and the element's `wrapBalance` prop sets it.

A design token for one CSS px at 100 % text, grown by the player's text scale (`calc(1rem / 14)`), so a part that grows with the text as a whole sizes itself as `calc(48 * var(--font-step-px))`. AbilitySlot and AbilityBar read it instead of a literal rem.

Enter in a form's single-line text field submits the form as a press of its first submit button would: the same validation and action, and nothing while that button is disabled or when the form has no submit button.

A document link `href="#id"` now scrolls the element with that id into view, as HTML's "scroll to the fragment" does: its `scroll-margin` box to the start of each scroller around it, inside the scroller's `scroll-padding` (and the least move across). A text fragment that matches nothing scrolls to its id the same way, and a matched passage's centring respects `scroll-padding`. A help page's table of contents now takes the reader to the section.

A flex container draws `column-rule` and `row-rule` too: a rule between the items of each line, as tall as the line, and one between lines across its content box (CSS Gap Decorations 1; `rule-break` acts as `none` there). The `rule-inset` family (`[column-|row-]rule-inset[-cap|-junction][-start|-end]`) moves a rule's ends in from the items beside them, a cap's at the box's edge or where the rule stops and a junction's where it goes on past a crossing gap, by a px length or a percentage of the gap that end meets; negative values extend it (§3.3).

added.member: UI CSS column-rule, row-rule, rule, column-rule-break, row-rule-break, rule-break
added.summary: A grid draws `column-rule` and `row-rule` (and the `rule` shorthands) centred in its gaps, from its first track's start to its last one's end (CSS Gap Decorations 1). `*-rule-break: normal` (the default) runs a rule through crossing gaps and stops it where an item spans its gap, `intersection` stops it at every crossing gap, and `none` runs it end to end. Row rules draw over column rules. Multi-column rules are unchanged. Flex containers, `rule-inset`, `rule-visibility-items` and lists of rule values are not supported yet.
A gradient takes up to 128 stops instead of 8: CSS linear-, radial- and conic-gradient() (and their repeating forms), a style's paint entries, SVG gradients and the draw API's ui.Gradient.

`display: grid-lanes` (and `inline-grid-lanes`) packs a box's items into its column tracks, each into the lane filled least (CSS Grid 3, masonry). `fit-tolerance` (`normal` = 1em, a px or em length, or `infinite`) treats lanes that close as tied, and a tie goes to the first lane after the last item's, so items keep their reading order across lanes.

A grid track size takes calc(), min(), max() and clamp() of px and %, resolved against the grid's own size, so repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(240px, 100%), 1fr)) shrinks its tile to a container narrower than one instead of overflowing it.
`:heading` selects every `<h1>` to `<h6>` and `:heading(1, 2)` those of the listed levels, in a document's and a style pack's rules. Before, both were refused as unsupported pseudo-classes.

Inside a component, `:host` selects the instance, whose box is the component's root: `:host { padding: 8px; --accent: red }` styles that box, and `:host(<compound>)` reads the instance: `:host([tone=warn])` the prop the instance passes (absent while null or false), `:host(.wide)` a word of its `class`, `:host(:hover)` and other states the root's live state, `:host(:nth-child(2))` its place among its siblings. `:host(…) .inner` and `:host > .child` select inside it. Before, `:host` was refused and `:host(…)` matched nothing. `:host.wide` and `:host:hover` are refused with `:host(.wide)` and `:host(:hover)` as the fix.

`<Card class="wide"/>` (or `class={…}`) passes the component's `class` prop, which a component declares (`<meta name="prop:class" content="string">`) to read in `:host(.wide)` or its markup. Before, a class on an instance was read and dropped.

HTML's table elements take their display from the UA stylesheet (table, table-caption, table-header-group, table-row-group, table-footer-group, table-row, table-cell), so a plain <table> lays out as a table with no author CSS; cells get padding: 1px, <th> is bold and centred and the caption centred, as in HTML's UA stylesheet.

Tables with HTML's content model, roles (table, row, cell, columnheader, rowheader by scope or HTML's auto rule) and colspan and rowspan as the cells' colspan and rowspan props, which CSS table layout reads; the first caption names the table.

added.member: UI documents: <form onsubmit onreset>, <fieldset disabled> with <legend>, <figure> with <figcaption>, <output for>
added.summary: A button in a form sends the form's onsubmit action (type reset: onreset); a disabled fieldset disables its controls but those in its first legend, which names the group; a figcaption names its figure; an output is a polite status text.
HTML text tags map to the text element (<text> stays the core name); headings carry role heading with aria-level and HTML's type steps; inline formatting and <a href> style runs of one paragraph.
A link: a click sends a `link` event named by its href through the document's events (immediate and mounted), with a link node in the accessibility tree.
A generic box laid out by CSS display (block by default, flex, grid, none); landmarks take their roles (navigation, main, banner, contentinfo, complementary, article, region for a named section).

Non-virtual lists with CSS markers: list-style-type (none, disc, circle, square, decimal, lower/upper-alpha, lower/upper-roman), list-style-position, the list-style shorthand, <ol start reversed>, <li value>. Numbers come from the structural selectors' sibling index, so keyed reorders and inserts renumber.
A plain checkbox is a toggle; <label for=id> joins a checkbox as its caption and names any other control. A label with neither a wrapped checkbox nor for is refused.
A heading's level, 1 to 6 (aria-level).

Role tokens for a meter over the scene: --bar-skew, --bar-well, --bar-rim, --bar-gloss, --bar-ghost, --bar-ghost-motion, --bar-pending, --bar-critical-rim, --bar-notch, --bar-shield, --bar-danger, --bar-figure-weight and --bar-figure-stretch. StatBar wears them: it leans forward in a dark well with one lit rim, a loss leaves a warm ghost that holds 450 ms and drains in 350 ms, healing on its way is striped, and under the critical mark the rim glows in danger and pulses.

`<iframe src="news.svelte">` embeds another document of the game inside a box: the cook bundles it with its embedder, the iframe's other attributes are its props, and its events reach the game as a component's do. It is a separate cascade, as an iframe's document is: no rule of the embedder matches inside, no selector inside sees the page around it, and nothing is inherited across its edge; the style pack and colour scheme still apply. The box is 300 × 150 px by default, and `frame-sizing: content-height` (or `content-width`, `content-block-size`, `content-inline-size`) sizes it to the document's content when that document declares `<meta name="responsive-embedded-sizing">`. A URL `src` is refused for now. See the `frames` guide.

Remote `<iframe>`s are on demand. `og build --publish` ships the engine with them only to a game whose project.ogt lists `frames`; every other game downloads none of their code (the document fetch, the frame budgets, the nesting walk, frame messages). The new capability query `og.ui.remoteFrames(world)` answers whether this engine shows them, the same on both hosts: true only for a game that lists `frames`. Where it answers false, a remote `src` is refused when its document loads and `og.ui.frameMessages` stays empty. Local `<iframe src="x.svelte">` frames work in every game.

`<iframe src="https://events.example.com/og/event.svelte">` shows a document another origin serves, such as an event page on the game's CDN. project.ogt's new `frames "https://events.example.com"` lists the origins it may come from (none by default); the cook refuses any other, and og-build.json's new `frames` carries the list for the page's CSP. `crossorigin`, `integrity` and `referrerpolicy` apply as url()'s request modifiers. The engine fetches the `.svelte` source on both hosts, with its relative images and nested frames beside it (at most 3 deep), and executors wait for it. A remote document reads only its props and `$ui`, uses only the engine's built-in components, and stays within 256 KiB, 4,096 nodes and 64 images; otherwise it shows nothing and warns. Its events never reach docEvents: read them from the new `og.ui.frameMessages(world)`, each with the origin it came from. See the `frames` guide.

`image-orientation` (CSS Images 3 §5.1) is inherited and takes `from-image`, the initial value, and `none`. Under `from-image`, a UI image (``, art, a background or a border image) whose source carries an EXIF orientation (a phone photo saved as JPEG, PNG or WebP) is drawn upright, and its natural width and height are those of the turned image. Under `none`, its pixels are drawn as stored. The cook keeps the orientation beside the texels, which stay as stored, and the turn is applied when the image is drawn. Sprites and materials sample the texels as stored.

Inline , and among a text's words; styled by any text element's ::part(name), which now also takes font-size, line-height and letter-spacing (the rich-text [size=…] of the markup, as CSS); MessageFormat 2 markup ({#b}…{/b}, {#i}, {#u}, {#s}, {#br/}) in translated strings.

An inline element inside a text (a `<span>`, `<b>`, `<a>` and so on) draws its `background`, `border`, `border-radius` and `box-shadow` on each line it wraps onto, under its words (CSS 2 §10.8). Under `box-decoration-break: slice`, the initial value, the box is drawn as if unbroken and cut at the line breaks, so its start edge shows on its first line and its end edge on its last; under `clone` each line gets a whole box. An element that only decorates its box, with no text style of its own, now becomes an inline element node too. Its text decorated nothing before.
`display: ruby`, `ruby-base`, `ruby-text`, `ruby-base-container` and `ruby-text-container` on any inline element of a text, from a rule or an inline style, lay it out as CSS Ruby 1 does.

A text's inline elements that style its words are nodes under it (kind `inline` in the probe), each with its fragments, one per line it has words on, and its box their union; the pointer over an inline link's words sets its `<a>`'s `:hover` and `:active` (and focus its `:focus`), which its CSS styles in place of the built-in hover ink.

An inline element of a text takes room for its margin, border and padding before its first character and after its last (CSS 2 §10.3.1), on the lines holding those edges; its fragments are its border boxes, grown by its border and padding across the line without growing the line. Under `box-decoration-break: clone` every line it is on holds both edges and breaks with room for them. Down a vertical line its edges take room along the column.

<svg viewBox> with <g>, <path>, <rect>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polyline>, <polygon>, gradients and <stop> in documents; every attribute binds, SVG's presentation properties are attributes or CSS and inherit, the view box fits the box as xMidYMid meet with strokes and dashes scaled, pathLength makes stroke-dashoffset a fraction. Each shape is one retained element drawn as an analytic path: a changed attribute draws that shape again, nothing else.

Style props, as in Svelte: --name="value" or --name={expr} on a component instance is a custom property its root inherits, so the component's own rules win, null sets nothing, and a component whose root is another component hands it on. style:--name stays the element's spelling; each is refused on the other with the right one named.
Adds restylable item slots with rarity, count, cooldown, selection and unavailable states, plus avatars with portrait fallback, level, presence and loading states.

<kbd> is a keycap, and <kbd data-action="jump"> the action's glyph on the device used last, rebuilt when the device changes; data-og-rebind bind:value captures the next key. Every document reads the engine's $ui store: device, coarsePointer and the top layer's action bar.
A cooked vector's strokes take stroke-dashoffset (it was refused), and its stroke outlines are kurbo's stroke expansion: offset curves, joins and caps as SVG draws them.
An icon's path data takes arcs (A and a), which were refused; every icon path is read by the same SVG path parser as documents and vectors.

Live regions: aria-live (polite, assertive, off), aria-atomic and role (status, log, alert) on document elements. A screen reader announces what enters or changes in a region once, from the tree its host last sent, and nothing for the first tree or a restore. Native hosts speak through AccessKit, and the web mirror speaks the frame answer's announce list, in publish builds too. A11yNode.live is the region's setting (docs/ui.md, Live regions).
A live region that announces as it appears (an alert, a toast); another region that enters with its content says nothing until it changes.
A live region that announces its whole text when any of it changes (aria-atomic, or its role's: status and alert).

Shared CLDR decimal grouping, fraction precision, signs and native digits on both hosts; messages and core data, feedback and HUD components use the same formatter. formatCompact accepts optional fraction precision. DateStyle adds monthYear, monthName, weekday and weekdayShort; DurationStyle adds clock and narrow short cooldown labels. pseudo/en-XA expand formatting, and ar-XB also uses RTL direction and isolation.

`margin-trim: block | block-start | block-end` on a block container drops its first in-flow block child's top margin and its last child's bottom margin (CSS Box 4 §3.3), so a list's padding alone sets the room at its edges.
Shared parameterized and named curves on the GPU through deduplicated 4097-sample lookup tables, preserving discontinuous step timing.

--measure-xs to --measure-3xl (200px to 960px) are the widths of panels, columns and tracks: how wide a block of content runs before it wraps or scrolls. Built-in components size their blocks from them, so a style pack widens or narrows all of them by setting tokens.

`:playing`, `:paused`, `:muted` and `:seeking` match a `<video>` or `<audio>` by its own state: `video:paused` while its `paused` is true and `video:playing` once it is false, `:muted` with its `muted`, `:seeking` from a `currentTime` write until the seek reaches the player. `:buffering`, `:stalled` and `:volume-locked` parse and never match. Before, all were refused.

A mounted document reads its props bare, as an instance does: with <meta name="prop:objective" content="string">, {objective} at the mount's root is the mount's store of that name, and a prop the mount leaves out reads its default. A document that declares no props reads every bare name that way, as a pushed screen reads its viewmodel's fields.

added.member: UI documents: components and snippets in mounted documents
added.summary: A capitalised tag instantiates a component document in a scope.mount: its props are the user's expressions read in the user's context (bind: writes back), snippets inside the instance and its other children (`children`) are content rendered by {@render name()} in the context they were written in; {#each} iterates a collection passed as a prop.
A fourth argument passes content by reference: a name the document renders with {@render name()}, mapped to a document (its root) or `document#snippet`.

added.member: UI documents: mounted screens are layers
added.summary: A `type screen` document mounted with scope.mount is a layer of the stack while it is mounted: its data-layer, data-pause, data-back and data-focus apply, its bindings read the mount's stores, Back or a pop trigger unmounts it, and snapshots carry it. Its root's path is `scope:id/<root id>`.
The store-driven mount that shows a layer, `scope:id`; empty for a pushed screen.

CSS View Transitions for a screen's layer: @view-transition { navigation: auto } cross-fades the layer as it joins and leaves the stack (the UA's fade-in and fade-out); ::view-transition-new(root) and ::view-transition-old(root) take animation with the document's @keyframes, ::view-transition-group(root) and -image-pair(root) their inherited timing, and types gate :active-view-transition-type() rules. The engine's covers are built-in keyframes -og-iris, -og-dissolve, -og-wipe and -og-slide (-from-right/top/bottom); ::view-transition background-color is their colour.

Add restylable base documents for empty and recoverable error states, selectable icon/title/value rows and progress steps. Each exposes token-based layouts, named parts, typed defaults, stable keyed intents, disabled and loading states where applicable, responsive overflow and review fixtures.

Add keyed full, fractional and depleted resource pips; boss health with named current/completed/upcoming phases and invulnerable/defeated/loading states; and game-driven combo count, fractional multiplier and remaining-window displays. Parts and tokens support style packs; labels wrap at phone widths.

Add signed pickup logs with keyed entries, wrapping names/details and loading/empty states, and supplied FPS, fractional frame time, ping and packet-loss readings with distinct unknown and connection states. Games own feed expiry and measurement thresholds.

Add restylable progression and update panels with game-owned facts: free/premium reward claims, sealed and revealed rewards, keyed inbox attachments and message actions, and expandable news. Include localized states, disabled/loading/error/empty recovery and desktop/phone fixtures.

added.member: UI: expression index and number lists
added.summary: A document's expressions take an index (`items[i]`, `row['key']`, a string's character) and `numbers(text)`, a number list as SVG writes one (`numbers(view)[2]` is a viewBox's width). A component can size from a viewBox string without the game splitting it.

A full-screen overlay element: vignette [<colour>], tint <colour> or material <material>, drawn at the element's opacity and never taking input; og.load.document loads the ui-material asset its effect names.

A document's text input that a pad gives the focus opens an on-screen keyboard docked at the screen's bottom: letters with shift and caps, symbols, a number pad, and with `lang="ja"` the kana table with composition. Its keys edit the bound value; `type` and `inputmode` pick the layout, `enterkeyhint` labels Done, `inputmode="none"` opens none (docs/ui.md §2.3). The document form of the onScreenKeyboard builder.

`overflow-clip-margin: <visual-box> || <length>` lets what an `overflow: clip` or `contain: paint` box draws reach that far past its padding edge (or the `border-box` or `content-box` it names) before it is cut (CSS Overflow 4 §3.2). It was refused.

A built-in style pack, loaded with og.load.style(world, "@styles/cartoon") or a look's ui "cartoon": a casual cartoon dress with bright candy colours on a sky ground, one thick dark outline around every control, frame and tile, chunky rounded buttons that stand on a raised bottom edge and sink onto it when pressed, bold rounded type (Lilita One and Fredoka, with ZCOOL KuaiLe for Chinese), soft drop shadows and springy motion with a prefers-reduced-motion branch. It has a dark and a light scheme, dresses every core control, the ten built-in component groups, the ungrouped components and the built-in screens, and sets the rarity colours (--common to --mythic), the long durations, --opacity-wash and --button-selected-*. Only base.css writes values, so a variant restyles it by setting tokens.
`Celebration.stage` names the level-up row that holds `Celebration.title` and `Celebration.value`, so a style pack can stack or space the word and the level.

New tokens `--slider-bubble-ink` (default `--ink-inverse`) and `--checkbox-mark-ink` (default `--on-primary`): a slider's value bubble draws its text, and a checkbox its tick, in their part's `color` (`input[type=range]::part(bubble)`, `input[type=checkbox]::part(mark)`), so a style pack sets the ink to suit its plates.

New role tokens `--frame-corner-shape`, `--plate-corner-shape`, `--row-corner-shape`, `--cell-corner-shape`, `--badge-corner-shape` and `--well-corner-shape` (default `round`): the default style's role rules set `corner-shape` from them, so a style pack chamfers or scoops every frame or cell by setting a token.

A heading's `::part(flourish)` draws its CSS box (`background`, `border`, `box-shadow`…) beside the heading's first line, as `::before` and `::after` boxes are, sized by its `width` and `height` and kept a small gap from the text, so a style pack without an ornament atlas can frame its headings.

Marks an atlas's cells as full-colour pictures (item art): ``, rich text's `[icon=]` and every other icon drawn from it keep their own colours, as an `` does, whatever the icon's `color`. Without it the cells stay masks drawn in the icon's `color`, as a CSS `mask-image` over `currentColor` is, so a light scheme's dark ink no longer turns item art into silhouettes once the atlas says what it holds.

The radial menu names its item button `RadialMenu.item`, so a style pack reaches each wedge's button with `button::part(RadialMenu\.item)` and clears or dresses the plate its `button::part(base)` rule gives it. The component draws no plate on it itself.
`select::part(option):checked` matches the chosen option of an open select, as HTML's selected `<option>` matches `:checked`.

The pack's glass blurs the scene behind it: panels, dialogs, tooltips and role frames take `--scifi-glass-blur` over a thinner frost, and HUD plates and `.hud` frames take the lighter `--scifi-plate-blur` over a denser frost that keeps their captions readable over a bright sky. World tags, per-value bars and the small chips of a busy HUD stay on solid glass and do not blur.

shooter.css dresses the shooter components' new parts: the vitals plate as the ammunition's cut glass plate (CombatHud.vitals), the keyline on both edges of the circle reticle's ring (Crosshair.ring), the magazine strip lit cyan on a hairline track (Ammo.magazine, Ammo.track), the weapon's name and the reload's words in condensed capitals (Ammo.weapon, Ammo.label, Ammo.prompt), and the killfeed's headshot mark in amber (Killfeed.headshot). The low magazine and the empty prompt keep --warn and --danger.

A second built-in style pack: dark translucent glass, thin glowing cyan rims, chamfered frames with corner brackets, scan lines, condensed technical type, an amber accent for what is chosen, and quick motion without overshoot, in a dark and a light scheme. It dresses every core control, the ten component groups, the ungrouped components and the built-in screens. Load it with og.load.style(world, "@styles/scifi"), or name it in a look (ui "scifi").

Parts with CSS keyframes repaint even when their semantic host is unchanged. Paint reuse now accounts for active animations as well as transitions and does not reuse volatile node commands. Finished or removed animations return to cached commands. Progress fills advance through alternate iterations and replay the same opacity after restoring presentation state.

A built-in control's parts are a shadow tree under its element, so a ::part() rule can read where that element stands in its document, as in a browser: `.shop button::part(base)`, `#Bag > li:first-child button::part(base)`. This works in a document's <style> and in a style pack, and the part restyles when an ancestor's class or the element's place changes. Before, a ::part() selector had to be one compound.

added.member: UI part reflection and og style check
added.summary: UI reflection exposes built-in host, part and state declarations through documentSchema, the probe and the generated UI catalogue. og style check validates selectors against the same declarations and accepts explicit custom parts from Svelte markup and custom-element hosts. Button part constructors use the reflected lowercase host while retaining legacy StylePart recognition. Default CSS no longer advertises part selectors that no widget emits.

HTML tooltips and popovers: title on any element is its tooltip and description; popover (auto, manual, hint) shows an element in a layer against the control that opened it; popovertarget/popovertargetaction toggle it on a press, interestfor shows a hint while its control is hovered or focused.

`position-visibility` takes `anchors-valid` (hidden while an anchor its placement reads is missing) and any combination of `anchors-valid`, `anchors-visible` and `no-overflow` (CSS Anchor Positioning 1 §4.1); `anchors-visible` stays the default. `no-overflow` together with a clipped anchor now hides on either condition. `anchors-visible` now also hides when a box between the anchor and the anchored element clips it out (`overflow: hidden` or `clip`, paint containment), not only a scroll container.

Player profiles at @ui/components/meta/profile.svelte compose the shared Avatar and Spinner, with identity, presence, rank, game-formatted stats, private/empty/error/loading states and keyed game-owned actions. Phone content scrolls separately from the actions; pending and disabled actions show their state and reason without dispatching.

A component's prop that its user leaves out reads its type's zero value ("", 0, false, [] with no rows, {}, null for any) unless its <meta name="prop:…"> gives a data-default, so <StatBar /> or <AbilityBar /> builds with no props and a game passes only what it shows; the generated .d.ts marks those props optional. A screen pushed without a prop holds its default too, so og.ui.screenVm answers every prop (typed ScreenValues<S>, whose fields are all present) where it answered null for one the push left out. A {#each} over a list prop left out iterates no rows. data-required marks a prop its user must pass; a mount or push leaving it out is refused with an error naming the instance and the prop.

The built-in components declare a default wherever the zero value would draw something wrong: a meter's max is 1, a "negative is none" figure (an ultimate's charge, a timer, a reload, a nameplate's health, a waypoint's distance) is -1, a world mark's at is "0 0 0", a word prop takes its neutral word (StatBar kind health, Crosshair shape cross and hit none, RacingBanner kind none), and the values their docs named (InteractionPrompt maxDistance 6, Nameplate 80, StatBar low 0.3 and critical 0.15, AmmoCounter low 0.25, Minimap size 160, SplitView ratio 0.5). None is data-required.

added.member: state pseudo-classes after a box pseudo-element
added.summary: `dialog::backdrop:hover`, `select::picker(select):hover` and `::details-content:hover` are accepted and read the pseudo-element's own state: the pointer on the scrim, not on the dialog. `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled` and `:enabled` may follow `::backdrop`, `::picker(select)`, `::details-content`, `::-og-hold` and `::-og-arrow`. Before, any pseudo-class after a pseudo-element was refused.
