The scroll-marker pseudo-classes parse, on an element (`a:target-current`) and after a box pseudo-element. They match what `Ui::set_selector_state` marks; nothing marks an element yet, so they match nothing until scroll markers land.

`pseudo=` in a control document (docs/ui.md §2.4): an element declared `pseudo="details-content"` is its host's standard pseudo-element, so the host's document and the style pack style it as `details::details-content`, `select::picker(select)`, `select::picker-icon`, `option::checkmark`, `dialog::backdrop` or `input::file-selector-button`, one shadow boundary in from the host (over the control document's own rule for it). A state after it reads the element's own state (`input::file-selector-button:hover` is the pointer on the button). The names are apart from `part=`. `pseudo=` is refused outside a control document, on a host HTML does not give that pseudo-element, twice for one name, bound, or on a component instance; a control document's own `:host::backdrop` rule is refused with `pseudo=` as its fix.

og.ui.screenVm(screen) returns the screen's values as they are now: what was pushed, with what the screen's controls wrote through bind:, and each value the screen reads that the push left out (its prop's default, else its type's zero value: "", 0, false, [], {}, or null for a store that is no prop). It is null once the screen has left the stack.

Add press, hold and mash prompts with game-supplied time and completion bars, accessible input hints, stable keyed respond intents and distinct waiting, disabled, success, failure and expired states. Pointer and keyboard holds cancel on early release; the game owns deadlines and outcomes. Parts and shared tokens support restyling.

Quiet and ghost buttons, which are text on the surface rather than plates, take inks of their own: `--button-quiet-ink`, `--button-quiet-hover-ink`, `--button-quiet-pressed-ink`, `--button-ghost-hover-ink` and `--button-ghost-pressed-ink`. Unset, they fall back to `--button-ink`, `--button-hover-ink` and `--button-pressed-ink` as before, so the default style is unchanged.

added.member: UI document CSS env(-og-hud-inset-top | right | bottom | left)
added.summary: The HUD band's insets: env(safe-area-inset-*) (the host's covered region folded in) with the left and right insets grown alike until the area between them is at most UiDesc.hudMaxAspect times its height wide. A HUD document placed at them (`position: fixed; right: calc(env(-og-hud-inset-right) + 24px)`) stays clear of Back and, on a 21:9 or 32:9 ultrawide, sits in the centred band the toasts use. A change of the surface or of hudMaxAspect re-resolves what reads them.

A range input with `low` and `high` is a range slider: two knobs on one track and the fill between them, each its own focus stop, a press taking the nearer knob, and CSS `-og-min-gap` keeping them apart; both values are written back. The document form of the rangeSlider builder (docs/ui.md §2).

A text input's `list` names a `<datalist>` whose options, or whose bound `items={$names}`, are suggestions listed under the field while it has the focus, filtered by its text with prefix matches first; choosing one writes it to the field. The document form of the searchBox builder (docs/ui.md §2).

A flex or grid container's `reading-flow` sets the order Tab and Shift+Tab move through its items in, and the accessibility tree's focus order (CSS Display 4 §3): `flex-visual` by where the items are, `flex-flow` and `grid-order` by `order`, `grid-rows` and `grid-columns` by row or column, `source-order` by the source. Each item's `reading-order` comes first. `normal` (the default) keeps the source order. Pointer hits and arrow moves are unchanged.
`input::part(frame):hover` and `textarea::part(frame):hover` match while the pointer is over a text field, as `:hover` does on a browser's field.

added.member: UI documents: a remote url() image's EXIF orientation
added.summary: An http(s) url() image turned by its EXIF orientation draws upright under image-orientation: from-image, as a package image does; natively, image-orientation: none draws it as stored. On the web the browser's decoder turns it before the engine sees it.

added.member: UI documents and style packs: url() of http(s) images
added.summary: A url() in a document, an inline style or a style pack may name an http:// or https:// PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image (background, mask and border images, image-set()), fetched at run time in CORS mode on both hosts and drawn once it lands; until then its layer draws nothing, and a refused or failed image is one warning naming the URL and the reason. CSS's request modifiers cross-origin(), integrity() and referrer-policy() apply. Native executors wait for every image a document named before drawing, so captures do not depend on the network, and og.loading.idle is false while one is fetched. The screens guide's §3 Images on a CDN.

A .riv's embedded images now convert (docs/ui.md §11.2): each cooks to its own texture, `<file>.riv#image<n>`, which og.load.document binds when it loads the artboard. An image draws at its pixel size about its origin, follows its node's transform and opacity, and is listed as an element. A hosted image, or one with a blend mode other than normal, is a cook error naming the asset.

A .riv's text now converts (docs/ui.md §11.2): runs in their styles' fonts, sizes, line heights, letter spacing and fill and stroke paints; auto, width and fixed sizing; alignment, vertical alignment and origin; wrapping; overflow visible, hidden, clipped, ellipsis, fit and fit font size; and keyed words, fonts, sizes and boxes. Each font a text uses cooks beside the artboard as `<file>.riv#font<n>` with only the characters its runs show (run-time glyphs, more characters and referenced fonts' files by the import settings' `font <name> { … }`), and is bound when og.load.document loads the artboard. Text is laid out as rive-runtime lays it out and shaped and drawn by og-ui's text. Rive features the import does not convert stay cook errors naming the asset and feature.

Mounted documents keep their render nodes between ticks: a tick writes again only the elements whose bindings, styles, structure, interaction or widget motion changed, and the rest stay in the tree without being visited (an idle tick evaluates no binding and writes no element; one changed label writes one element).

The CSS-wide keyword `revert-rule` rolls a property back to what it is without the keyword's own rule: `button.quiet { background: revert-rule }` shows the background the rules below give. It works on custom properties and as a `var()` fallback. Before, the value was refused.

added.member: og ui sheet and og ui review
added.summary: A pack is named as a game names it: `og ui sheet fantasy` or `og ui sheet @styles/fantasy` (a bundled pack, or the project's `assets/styles/<name>`), and `--style` takes the same forms. `og ui --help` and the screens guide say so; a group's sheet is still named by its group.

A dot role part with data-tone (success, danger, warn, info, primary) now fills with that tone. The overlay layout primitive now stacks its other children as a column, so a scroller inside it is bounded while a fade or badge is anchored over it.

A document element's `part` takes a list of names, as in HTML (`part="Bag.portrait Bag.picture"`): `::part()` reaches it by any of them, the document's own `[part~="Bag.portrait"]` by one, and it wears the role of its last name. Every name is in the document's `parts` line.

Three new roles: `name` (`--name-font/size/tracking/transform/ink/shadow/selected-ink`), `picture` (`--picture-fill/rim/rim-width/radius/shadow`) and `tab`, which wears the core tabs' `--tabs-tab-*` and `--tabs-font/tracking/transform`. The name and picture hooks are unset by default, so the components' own look stands until a pack sets them.

Built-in components' shared parts (frame, band, title, row, cell, badge, well, figure, label) are dressed once by the default style from role tokens (--frame-*, --band-*, --title-*, --row-*, --cell-*), so a style pack restyles all of them by setting tokens. class hud makes a frame a HUD plate and class bare leaves it undressed. --font-step-* are type sizes in em that follow the player's text scale.

Adds token-styled crafting requirements and batch controls, buy/sell inspection with game-owned prices and restrictions, keyed loot collection, and scrollable conversation history with earlier lines and replay/stop intents. Loading spinners, pending-action guards, failure messages and explicit empty states remain readable at phone and desktop sizes; named parts expose each panel for style packs.
Adds optional History, Skip and Auto controls with game-owned permissions and automatic-advance state; controls remain hidden by default.
A ruby's base takes its text's emphasis marks, placed outside its annotations on that side as CSS Text Decoration 4 §3.4 says, and its line grows for them; annotations take none.

Ruby follows CSS Ruby 1's box model: <rb> columns pair with <rt>s one by one, <rtc> adds another level (its bare words spanning the bases), nested <ruby> stacks its annotation past the inner one's, and a text's ::part spans take display: ruby, ruby-base, ruby-text, ruby-base-container, ruby-text-container and none. ruby-position: alternate puts each level on the other side of the one before, and inter-character stands the annotation upright in a column right of its base.

Documents lay out HTML ruby (<ruby>, <rb>, <rt>, <rp>) inside text as CSS Ruby 1 does: the annotation at half the base's size over or under it (ruby-position), spread by ruby-align, hanging over the text beside it by up to one character under ruby-overhang, the line growing where its leading cannot hold it; across and down vertical lines.

text-emphasis, text-emphasis-style, -color and -position draw CSS Text Decoration 4's emphasis marks: one per character but punctuation and separators, at half the text's size over or under it, right or left of it in vertical text; the shapes are drawn, so every face has them.

text-combine-upright: digits combines each run of up to its count of ASCII digits into one upright em (CSS Writing Modes 4 §9.1), not only a text that is all digits; a combined run takes no letter-spacing. glyph-orientation-vertical (auto, 0deg, 90deg) is read as text-orientation.

Every built-in screen reads its declared props bare ({title}, bind:open={open}), as the built-in components do, so each serves both as a pushed or mounted screen and as an instance (<Confirm title=... />). They read them as $name before; what a screen shows from the same values is unchanged. $toasts and $captions stay: they are the engine's stores, not props. An ejected screen written with $name keeps working.

A look's `uiSeeds { primary "#rrggbb" … }` block gives the UI its seed colours with its style, so the UI's palette matches the scene; applying a look with a `ui` line replaces the last seeds (none without the block). anime-cel-3d, cinematic-realism, faceted-low-poly, inked-comic-3d, low-resolution-3d, minimal-geometric and pixel, whose `ui` is the default style, set seeds from their scenes.

The seed colours the UI's palette is derived from (UiSeeds: primary, accent, neutral, danger, warn, success, info, team), over the style's. Calling og.ui.configure with new seeds at run time (a faction, the time of day) restyles the whole UI from the next tick.

A style pack sets the palette with seed tokens on :root (`--seed-primary`, `--seed-accent`, `--seed-neutral`, `--seed-danger`, `--seed-warn`, `--seed-success`, `--seed-info`, `--seed-team`), any CSS colour, once for both schemes; the default stylesheet derives every colour token from them as relative colours that resolve when drawn. `--team1` to `--team8` are stylesheet tokens, read back into UiTheme.tokens.team, and `--well-rim` is the `--color-well-rim` token.
Type selectors match a tag case-insensitively, as HTML's do.

shape-outside: url(<file>) wraps lines around the alpha channel of a texture stretched over the float's content box, holding the pixels greater than the new shape-image-threshold (0 by default; number or percentage); shape-margin expands it. The host reads the alpha on the CPU as the document loads (any texture natively, a lossless kind pixel texture on the web); a float whose image it cannot read keeps its box, with a note.
New og-ui host call giving a texture asset path its CPU alpha (ImageAlpha); UiDocument::shape_images lists the paths a document's shape-outside names.

Expand float exclusion contours by a non-negative CSS length or percentage with round joins, clipped to the float margin box. Percentages resolve against the containing block inline size; dynamic changes update neighbouring lines in both document builders.

Basic shapes and reference boxes shorten inline lines around floats without changing float placement, clearance or block formatting context avoidance. Changes to fixed-size float contours invalidate neighbouring layout in both builders. Shape-margin and image alpha contours remain unsupported; the CSS inventory records the proved syntax and remaining gaps.

The default style has layout primitives, after Every Layout, that every document can use and a style pack retunes through tokens. data-layout asks for a stack, row, cluster, sidebar, switcher, grid, cover, center, ratio, shell, scroll list or overlay (its children placed with data-anchor), and data-gap (none, hair, tight, loose, wide) spaces the children by a step of the layout scale (--layout-gap-*). Sidebar, switcher and grid wrap by their own container's width (the grid is repeat(auto-fill, minmax(--layout-tile, 1fr))), and a shell is the container a component's @container rules read. CardCollection, Friends and EmptyState use them.

The default style owns a shared set of keyframes (og-fade-in, og-fade-out, og-rise-in, og-drop-in, og-pop-in, og-stamp-in, og-beat, og-pulse, og-spin, og-ping, og-shimmer) every document can name. A part asks for one by meaning with data-motion (enter, exit, pop, stamp, beat, pulse, spin, ping, shimmer), timed by the role tokens --<name>-motion from motion.css; a pack retunes a token or redefines the keyframes. Interactive role parts (row, cell, card, tab, badge) ease between hover, press and selection (--change-motion), and a cell gives under a press (--cell-pressed-scale). Under prefers-reduced-motion every data-motion but spin stops. Spinner, StatBar and ProgressBar use them.

added.member: More shared roles, motions and layout marks
added.summary: The default style dresses more role parts from tokens: tag (text over the scene), fade (a scroller's edge cue, placed with data-anchor=bottom-edge or top-edge), former (a struck former price), ribbon (ink is the contrast of its toned fill), skeleton and its shimmering sheen, divider, grip, notch, zone (a toned rim and wash, hatched for danger) and sweep (a cooldown veil). An SVG shape named track, fill, sweep, series, area, gridline, link or tail strokes and fills from role tokens. glyph (a stroked SVG mark) strokes in its text's colour, a picture with data-muted sets back, data-tone takes primary, a mass anchor's fill draws in --fill-color, and figure takes --figure-size and --figure-weight, and figures and badges use tabular numerals. aria-pressed counts as selected; data-shape gives cells and dots a shape, data-down dims a row, cell, card or frame, a disabled one dims its picture and icons, and a fill with data-ghost trails a loss. data-motion adds float (a figure flying off its anchor) and change (ease between states, now including opacity, translate and rotate), a scroll or cluster primitive with data-from=end starts at its end, and data-fade-ends (x or y) fades a window's ends to clear.

New roles the default style dresses from tokens a style pack sets once: card (a rimmed surface holding one thing, --card-*), headline and caption (a card's or row's name and its supporting words, --headline-*, --caption-*), dot (a small round mark, --dot-*), track and fill (a meter's groove and its full part, --track-*, --fill-color, --fill-gloss), and badge's --badge-pad and --badge-text. data-tone takes success, danger, warn and info (--tone-*), and a fill in a tone takes its colour. A role's selected state also follows any aria-current but false (a step's aria-current=step). News, Steps and StatBar wear them; Pips' filled layer is the part full and PassTrack's reward strip the part rewards, so neither wears a role it is not.
Shared cubic Bezier and step timing functions, CSS keyword parsing, deterministic fixed-iteration evaluation, and lossless timeline and snapshot payloads. Named GSAP codes are unchanged.

added.member: og ui sheet components, screens and world
added.summary: Three review sheets cover what no group owns: `components` (the ungrouped built-in components on a HUD, a panels and a states page), `screens` (every built-in screen on its own page, its states through `--states`) and `world` (nameplates, loot labels, damage numbers, overhead bars, prompts, waypoints, selection rings and the other world-anchored components over a 3D scene). Each renders in fantasy, scifi and default.

More parts for a style pack to dress: CombatHud.vitals (the plate behind the health bar), Crosshair.ring (the circle shape's ring), Ammo.track (the tracks of the magazine strip and the reload bar), Ammo.magazine[low] (the magazine strip's fill), Ammo.weapon, Ammo.label (the reload's label), Ammo.prompt (the empty magazine's prompt) and Killfeed.headshot (the headshot mark, an og-icon). The group's README lists every part with its qualifiers.

`::slotted(<compound>)` in a component's sheet selects the top-level elements of the content rendered at its `{@render}` sites, from the element around the site: `.body::slotted(p) { margin: 0 }`, or bare `::slotted(p)` for every site. The rule ranks under the rules of the document that wrote the content, as CSS ranks a shadow tree's rules on slotted content, and `!important` reverses that. A component instance passed as content is selected by its root's tag, classes and attributes, and there the rule wins over the component's own rules for its root. Before, `::slotted()` was refused.

`:has-slotted` matches the element around a `{@render}` site while content passed to the component (elements or component instances) is rendered there, and not for the component's own fallback snippet: `.footer:has-slotted { padding: 8px }`. Before, it was refused.

Split screen: player="k" (ElementProps.player, Props::player) makes an element's subtree player k's region. Pad k's focus moves only inside it, its first move lands at its centre, and controls outside every region stay the pads' without one (docs/ui.md 2.5).
The split screen region a control was pressed or clicked in; null outside every region.

Mount loaded UI documents with named store inputs over the binary host protocol, without per-element TypeScript calls. Mounts preserve keyed identities, subscribe to inputs until unmount or disposal, and restore presentation state against current code registrations.

Typed Unicode-scalar attribute ranges feed the shared paragraph shaper directly, without markup conversion. Overlapping part declarations inherit independently, colour tokens follow the active style, unknown attributes and zero-length markers remain metadata, and wave, shake and pulse reuse checkpointed tick motion and reduced-motion handling. TextSpan is generated for stores on both hosts; rendering is exposed through the Svelte text spans binding, not a new TypeScript UI builder.

A style pack's core-control state sheet (docs/ui.md §6.2) covers the whole control set: four pages (controls, fields, surfaces, overlays), every button variant, tab, checkbox, switch, radio, text field, select, stepper and range in rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible, selected, disabled and selected+disabled, with the type, frames, slots, dialog, disclosures, meters and badges they sit on; each page fits a 390 × 844 phone by touch, where hover and focus have no column.

added.member: og.ui style tokens (document and style CSS `:root`)
added.summary: Every value the built-in controls draw with is now a CSS variable a style sets in `:root`, and the controls read them back: motion durations (`--motion-duration-*`), easings (`--motion-easing-out`, `--motion-easing-exit`) and the named transitions' springs (`--motion-named-ui-duration`, `-bounce`, likewise panel, emphasis, playful, enter, exit); control states (`--state-hover-wash`, `--state-press-scale`, `--state-control-press-scale`, `--state-lift`, `--state-disabled-opacity`, `--state-touch-disabled-opacity`, the focus and player rings); each input's densities (`--density-compact-*`, `--density-pad-*`, `--density-touch-*`) and the input's own as `--control-sm`, `--control-md`, `--control-lg`, `--row`, `--header`, `--gutter`, `--section`, with `--touch-target`; sizes and strokes (`--size-*`, `--stroke-edge`); shadows (`--shadow-*`: the design language's per scheme and the controls' `--shadow-sheen`, `-well`, `-pressed`, `-groove`, `-fill-sheen`, `-minimap`, `-slot-selected`, `-tab-selected`); glass (`--glass-blur-thick`, `--glass-blur-regular`, `--glass-saturation`); and the engine colours `--color-track`, `--color-minimap`, `--color-minimap-edge`, `--color-slot-selected-edge`. Each core control has its own tokens, `--<control>-<property>`: `--button-*`, `--field-*`, `--checkbox-*`, `--radio-*` and `--radio-card-*`, `--switch-*`, `--slider-*`, `--segmented-pad-ratio`, `--tabs-radius`, `--chip-radius`, `--dropdown-*`, `--menu-open-duration`, `--details-icon`, `--modal-width`, `--panel-*`, `--hud-radius`, `--slot-*`, `--meter-*`, `--keyboard-*`, `--joystick-size`, `--dpad-size`, `--action-size` and `--state-press-duration`. The defaults are the values drawn before, so no frame moves (docs/ui.md §3.1).

{#key expr} makes its content again (new elements, their entrances playing) when expr changes; {@const name = expr} names an expression inside a block; {#await $load}…{:then value}…{:catch error}…{/await} shows its branches by the settled record a store holds ({ status: "pending" | "fulfilled" | "rejected", value, reason }). Nothing is awaited in the tick (docs/ui.md §2).

added.member: UI documents: prop defaults and <script> with $derived
added.summary: A prop's metadata may give its default (<meta name="prop:gold" content="number" data-default="0">): a component user who leaves the prop out reads it, and the generated .d.ts marks it optional. A document's <script lang="ts"> may name pure expressions with $derived(expr) or $derived.by(() => expr). $props() is refused with a diagnostic naming the metadata form; $state, $effect, imports, functions and other statements are refused with a diagnostic pointing to a TS system.

added.member: UI documents: transition:, in:, out: and animate:flip
added.summary: Svelte's fade, fly, slide, scale and blur with their duration, delay, easing (svelte/easing's names) and own params map onto the element's enter and exit presence, crossfade's key onto its shared-element key, and animate:flip onto its layout motion. Presentation only.

added.member: UI documents: style:prop={value}, style:prop|important and style="…"
added.summary: An element's own declarations for any supported property, bound or literal; they win over every stylesheet rule but an !important one, and |important wins over that too.

bind:this={name} names the element (its id; the name reads as that id, for popovertarget, anchorTo and #name selectors). use:name={params} sends DocEvents of kind "use" with value { phase: "create" | "update" | "destroy", params } when the element is made, its params change and it goes, for the game's handler.

<svelte:window onresize={action} bind:innerWidth={w} bind:innerHeight={h}/> sends an event when the screen's size changes and names its size; <svelte:element this={tag}> is that tag, or for a bound tag the text or block tag it names. The $ui store gains width and height. <svelte:document>, <svelte:boundary> and the Svelte 4 elements are refused with the reason.
Svelte's draw on an SVG shape strokes it on (or off) over the outline's length, with duration, delay and easing (default cubicInOut). speed is refused: give duration.

added.member: UI: SVG <filter> through CSS filter: url(#id) and the SVG filter attribute
added.summary: An inline SVG <filter> and its primitives (feGaussianBlur, feOffset, feFlood, feComposite, feMerge, feBlend, feColorMatrix, feComponentTransfer, feMorphology, feDisplacementMap, feTurbulence, feDropShadow, feImage, feTile, feConvolveMatrix, feDiffuseLighting and feSpecularLighting with distant, point and spot lights) now draw, with their in/in2/result graph, filter region, filterUnits, primitiveUnits, subregions and color-interpolation-filters. CSS filter takes url(#id) mixed with the filter functions in order; a <g> or shape takes filter="url(#id)". backdrop-filter: url(#id) is not drawn yet and warns.

A role part on a team (`data-team="a"` or `"b"`: a frame, plate, band, title, row, cell, badge, well, figure, label or heading) wears `--team1` or `--team2` as its ink and rim, so a pack colours every team part by setting the two tokens. The arena kit's team headings now take their team's colour in the default style too.

`text-indent` (with `hanging` and `each-line`) and `line-break` (`auto`, `loose`, `normal`, `strict`, `anywhere`) now lay out (CSS Text 3 §8.1, §5.3). A text that sets either is laid out by Parley: its indent is room at the start of its first line, or of every line but the first under `hanging`, or after each forced break too under `each-line`. Lines break around that room, a fitting box grows by it, and `text-align` aligns the rest. `line-break` sets how strictly CJK punctuation and small kana may break, and `anywhere` breaks inside words. `text-indent` used to be accepted and ignored, and `line-break` was refused. Atlas-only and pixel faces, which Parley cannot shape, are not indented.

Text on a path (CSS -og-text-path in documents, SVG 2 textPath layout): path("<SVG path data>") or circle([r]), -og-text-path-offset in px or % of the path, text-align as the anchor, -og-text-path-side: right to run it backwards. Each grapheme is turned to the path with its baseline on it; what runs off an open path is dropped and a circle wraps. An element with no size is as large as its path. CSS offset-path still moves the element itself.

$toasts, read by every document like $ui: the toasts up, oldest first, each { id, text, tone, leaving }. In a row of it, onclick={dismissToast} dismisses that toast; the engine answers it and the game never sees the event.
The built-in notifications screen shows $toasts after its own items: each arrives and leaves with the motion tokens, takes its tone's stripe, and a press dismisses it.

The default style sets more surfaces as tokens, so a component or a pack names a value instead of writing one: --size-3xl to --size-7xl, --opacity-faint/dim/muted/soft, --filter-locked and --filter-spent, --font-leading-*, --font-tracking-*, --font-weight-*, --motion-easing-in-out and --motion-scale-press/swell/pop/shrink/breathe.

Durations longer than a transition, for loops and long plays: --motion-duration-turn (800ms), -pulse (1000ms), -flare (1040ms), -ping (1200ms), -sweep (1400ms), -breathe (1600ms), -sheen (2000ms), -drift (2400ms), -fanfare (2560ms) and -orbit (6000ms). The built-in components' spinners, pings, sweeps and celebration plays take them in place of multiples of --motion-duration-slow, at the lengths they had; a style retimes them by setting the token.

The six rarity colours are tokens of the default style: --common, --uncommon, --rare, --epic, --legendary and --mythic, each the status colour a rarity borrowed before (--line-strong, --success, --info, --xp, --warn, --danger). A style that names its own still wins, and var(--rare) needs no fallback. A loot label's common tier wears --common as its rim, and its name stays the scene's ink.
--opacity-wash (0.25): how much of a colour a soft wash lays over what is under it. A chart's area and the celebration's rays take it.

A built-in on-screen pad: <TouchControls move="move" actions={$actions} /> puts a stick (or a d-pad with pad) at the start side and ActionButtons at the end side, the first nearest the corner, with an optional second stick (look). Each control is an input source of the og-input action it names, so the game reads the same actions as from keys or a pad. It shows only where the primary pointer is a finger unless always is set; disabled stops every control feeding.

A document's `translate` takes percentages of the element's own box, as CSS's does: `translate: -50% -50%` centres a map marker or a compass mark on the point a game projects, for the probe, the pointer and the paint. A px `translate` that wins the cascade replaces an earlier percentage. States and dressings keep px.

The built-in tutorial points at an element: target is its id in any document under the screen. The screen dims around it, the element stays lit and takes its presses while the dimmed rest takes none, and the card stands against it in place of x and y. Empty (and left out) dims nothing, as before.

Selectable read-only text (CSS `user-select` in documents): `text` selects by press and drag, a double press a word, a triple press a line, a long press on a touch screen a word; `all` takes the whole element; drags run across elements in tree order. Ctrl or Cmd+C copies to the host's clipboard with wrapped lines rejoined as their source had them. Off by default and under controls.
The probe's UI dump carries the player's text selection: its text and each end's path and character, null with none. UI state version 20 saves it; versions 11 to 19 upgrade with nothing selected.

`:user-valid` matches a form control whose value the player changed and its constraints accept, the counterpart of `:user-invalid` (`input:user-valid { border-color: var(--good) }`). An untouched control matches neither.

A document plays an og.VideoPlayer (its frame as the element's picture) or og.AudioSource entity from a store, with Svelte's bind:paused, bind:currentTime, bind:duration, bind:volume, bind:muted, bind:ended and autoplay, loop, poster and controls. A literal src is refused: spawn the player in a system and bind its entity.
The recorded intent a document's <video> or <audio> sends its player (play, pause, seek, gain, loop), applied by og.video at the next tick. Registered lazily, once a document with one loads.

added.member: UI: CSS shared-element view transitions (view-transition-name, view-transition-class)
added.summary: Elements named with view-transition-name (a name, auto or match-element) morph across a screen's view transition: the old element's frozen drawing and the new live element cross-fade with plus-lighter in a ::view-transition-group that moves from the old box to the new one. ::view-transition-group, -image-pair, -old and -new take (name), (*), (.class) and (name.class) with view-transition-class, cascaded by the spec's specificity, with the UA's default animations and author @keyframes. A name on two elements skips the transition with a warning; reduced motion skips it unless the style keeps motion.

`orphans` and `widows` (inherited positive integers, 2 by default) set the fewest lines of a text a column break leaves before and after it in a multi-column box (CSS Fragmentation 3 §4.4). Before, the break always kept two lines on each side.

The built-in world map draws its map zoom times the box (1 when left out) and moved by panX and panY in CSS px; markers keep their size. It reports zoom (the wheel, with deltaY), pinch (two touches, with scale), and grab, pan and release (a press, its moves and its end, with x and y in the map's box). The game keeps the zoom and the pan and sets them back; a page that passes none of the three draws as before.
A cast's spell name spans the cast bar and is inked `--ink-on-warn` over the part the cast has filled and `--ink` past it, so it reads over both; a name longer than the bar ends in an ellipsis.

Tokens `--tag-halo`, `--tag-fill`, `--tag-pad` and `--tag-radius` dress the text built-in components draw over the scene (a nameplate's name and subtitle, a waypoint's label and distance, a status grid's time left): an outline by default, and a ground of their own where a pack sets one, so they read over a bright sky.

`zoom` (CSS Viewport 1 §4) makes a box and its subtree that many times larger, and its parent makes room for it: its size, padding, margins and text, and every length under it, grow by the factor; a percentage or `auto` does not. Zooms nest by multiplying, a percentage is its hundredth, and 0 is 1. The subtree is drawn scaled from the box's top left, so its transforms act inside the zoom. A zoomed box starts its own float context.

The effect-packs guide lists each effect's measured size (metres), anchor (ground or centre), peak GPU milliseconds and draw calls beside its length, with the device they were measured on, so `og api find` answers what an effect looks like in size and what it costs before it is installed.

added.member: effect-packs guide: a section per category
added.summary: The generated `effect-packs` guide ends with one section per effect category (level up, heal, portal, fire, ...), listing that category's effects in every pack, so `og api find "level up"` answers with the level-up effects. og.Beam takes the aliases laser beam, laser, LineRenderer, tether and lightning bolt.

A composed effect whose decal draws a region of og.RenderSettings.decalAtlas while no atlas is set (so the decal is a square of its colour) is warned of in the engine's log, once per effect. og vfx preview prints the warnings of its run that name each effect, and its --json records carry them as warnings.

The share of a composed effect instance's particles that are born, 0 to 1 (default 1): 0.5 draws half the sparks and smoke of the same effect, each emitter thinned by its own pick, as an emitter's own emission line does. A distant or smaller fire costs less without a second file. Its glows, meshes, trails, lights and decals are unchanged.

Turns the hue of everything a composed effect instance draws, in radians about the grey axis, after its tint (default 0): the same fire drawn blue for ice (about 3.1) or green for poison, white, grey and black unchanged. Its particles and meshes turn their whole drawn colour, textures included; its trails', beams', lights' and decals' colours turn, and a coloured trail, beam or decal texture keeps its own colours.

added.member: effect packs: effekseer-starter and pixel-scenario bundled, ten effekseer-<contributor> packs downloadable
added.summary: The engine bundles two vfx packs in packages/engine/extensions/: effekseer-starter (38 Effekseer sample effects from nine contributors, type vfx: fire, explosions, hits, slashes, heals, buffs, level-ups, projectiles, impacts, portals, weather, ambient) and pixel-scenario (42 Pixel VFX Forge effects, type vfx2d). The ten per-contributor Effekseer packs (285 effects) are in packages/vfx-packs/ and ship with each release as vfx/<pack>.tar.gz. `og vfx add <pack>` installs any of them into assets/vfx/<pack>/; a game carries a pack only once it is installed. Every pack lists each file's sha256, CC0 or custom licence, source and credit in assets.json, with previews and cost sheets under preview/. `og api find` searches them: the generated `effect-packs` guide (`og api show effect-packs`) lists each pack's tags, keywords and effects.

A composed effect declares up to 4 numbers the game sets per instance (`param <name> <default>`), and an element reads one with `when <param>` (it plays only while the value is above 0: a critical hit's extra burst) or `amount <param>` (it multiplies an emitter's share of particles born, a mesh's, glow's, decal's or flipbook's size, a trail's or beam's width, a light's intensity, a shake's trauma or a sound's volume). og.Vfx.params and og.vfx.spawn's params give the values in the order declared, a value left out taking its default; og.vfx.info lists the names, and a spawn with more than 4 is refused.

`--quality low|medium|high` plays the effects with that graphics preset applied (og.render.applyQuality), as a player who picked it sees them: the frames, the measured size and the milliseconds, alone or `--together`, are at that preset.

together.json also holds the CPU's milliseconds (`cpu`: the frame's and each render pass's, over the empty stage, at the run's peak and typical frame) beside the GPU's: what recording the effects' draws and particle dispatches costs, which the GPU rows do not show.

`og vfx preview <effect.ogt>...` plays each effect of a project (type vfx, or type vfx2d in a 2D project) alone on a dark stage and reports it without a scene written for it: six frames in time order, the impact frame among them, tiled into og-out/vfx-preview/<effect>.png with the camera placed by the box the effect was measured to cover; its length, impact time, measured size and anchor (ground or centre), draw calls, particle slots and its peak GPU milliseconds over an empty frame, printed and written to <effect>.json. `--decal-atlas <texture>` sets the stage's decal atlas for effects with decals; `--no-cost` skips the timed run.

added.member: og vfx add <pack>, downloadable effect packs
added.summary: An effect pack that is neither a directory nor bundled with the engine (packages/engine/extensions/) nor installed is downloaded from the running engine's release: `og vfx add <pack> [project] [--any-engine]` fetches <downloads>/<version>/SHA256SUMS and its minisign signature, verifies it with the engine's release key (the launcher's), checks manifest.json and vfx/<pack>.tar.gz against the signed sums, unpacks it with regular files only, no `..`, absolute paths or links and a size cap, and installs it into assets/vfx/<pack>/ as a local directory is. A failed check refuses, naming it, and leaves nothing behind. $ORIGIN_ENGINE_DOWNLOADS (default https://origingame.ai/downloads/engine) and $ORIGIN_ENGINE_PUBKEY are the launcher's. Each release carries one vfx/<pack>.tar.gz per packages/vfx-packs/<pack>/ (deterministic, without preview/), listed in SHA256SUMS and in manifest.json's new `vfx` section ({url, sha256, size, version, minEngine}); no engine archive carries them.

`loudness <lufs>` normalises a video's sound to that integrated loudness with ffmpeg's loudnorm (EBU R128), −16 to 0 (typically −16 for streaming, −14 louder), so clips a generative model made at different levels all play at one target; off by default.
`aiGenerated true` marks footage made by a generative model; VideoInfo.aiGenerated carries it, so a game or store labels AI content.

`og video edges <path> [--out <dir>]` writes the first and last frame of a clip as PNG (`<stem>.first.png`, `<stem>.last.png`): the last frame is the seed an image-to-video model continues from for the next clip, the first checks a cut joins. `path` is a media file or a `type video` .ogt (whose source and maxSeconds it reads).

A streamed video's player with `wait` holds the engine's clock on the web while it plays and its frame is not decoded yet (its chunk still downloading, or decoding behind), so the picture and its sound never part on a slow connection: the world ticks later instead. Off by default; executors always wait for each frame. Leave it off in a lockstep game.
A stream's seconds per chunk (`chunk 6` by default, rounded to whole key frame intervals): what a player downloads at a time.

A streamed video (`stream true`) now also cooks an HEVC rendition of the same frames and key frames by default (ffmpeg's libx265), and an H.264 one with `renditions h264` or `renditions hevc h264` (libx264); `renditions none` leaves them out. A browser whose WebCodecs decodes no AV1 but decodes HEVC or H.264, such as Safari on an iPhone or Mac without AV1 hardware, plays that rendition in place of the AV1, at full size and in hardware where the device has it, instead of the 720p software decoder. Only one copy is fetched. An ffmpeg without libx265 cooks no default rendition and says so; og doctor reports the encoders.
The codecs streams decode in on this host, preferred first (`av1`, `hevc`, `h264`).

The shape of a region on its entity: a box along the entity's axes or a sphere about it, with a fade past its surface. og.ReverbZone and og.StreamCell take their extent from it, so regions are placed, turned, scaled and faded the same way and one entity can be several regions of one shape.

og.Buoyancy floats whatever its entity is, not only a dynamic rigid body: an og.Ragdoll's bones while it is limp and an og.CharacterController are lifted by the water they displace, slowed against the moving water and carried by its flow (a river's current, a wave's orbit), on an og.Water or an og.WaterSurface. Both count as density 1, so the default floats them half under; `submerged` is written for each and a ragdoll with it crossing the surface is an og.Splash. Only an entity that already had og.Buoyancy beside an og.Ragdoll or an og.CharacterController (where it did nothing) steps differently.

Every og.Water is crossed like an og.WaterSurface: a body or character whose centre crosses a lake's level, a sea's waves or a river's course is an og.Splash, without an og.WaterSurface on the entity. Which side each body near a water is on is world state, saved and restored with the simulation.

It answers for every og.Water: a lake without a `wind` answers its level and a river its course (both were refused), a sea its waves as before, each with the waves bodies raised on an og.WaterSurface on the same entity. An og.Water drawn over a mesh (`geometry`) is still refused.

A hull floats on a river as on a lake or a sea, and cuts the water it sits in on all three. An og.Water alone still lifts only og.Buoyancy bodies; og.WaterSurface and og.WaterLine keep lifting every body's box by their `buoyancy`.

The water at a point: of every og.Water, og.WaterSurface and og.WaterLine over it, the one whose surface stands highest, with the point's depth under it and the water's velocity, acceleration and surface normal there (og.WaterPoint); null over no water. It answers inside a system (reading og.Water and og.Transform) as between ticks, from the function the simulation floats bodies on.

The underwater view has depth: the water's light falls off with depth (brighter looking up than down, darker the deeper the eye), the sun comes down in moving shafts as strong as `caustics` (0: none), split into fine pencils of light, and the surface from below shows the sky and the sun inside Snell's window as the surface bends them, its rim broken into shards by a lake's capillary ripples (blurred where a pixel cannot hold them), and mirrors the water outside it. Some 0.8 ms at 720p on an Apple M4 Pro (7.8 to 8.6 ms, 7.9 to 9.3 ms looking up the shafts, a debug build).

A lake's caustics are the light its ripples focus (1 / |det(I + kH)| of ten travelling ripples, as a sea's are its waves'), in place of a cell pattern: a net of bright lines whose cells grow with depth, fading to their mean where a pixel holds whole cells, and as bright as the sun that makes them (the old lines clipped to white). `causticsScale` is the ripples' fineness. Frames with a lake's caustics move; a sea's do not.

Wakes are drawn on every og.Water, not a sea alone: a body that cuts a lake or a river bends its reflections with its bow wave and Kelvin wake and leaves foam along its sides and astern (the surface stays flat: a sea's alone rises with them). One 64 m square round the camera serves the water being cut, and rests two minutes after the last cut; a water nothing cuts costs nothing. An entity with og.WaterSurface too draws its own ripples instead.

The watercolour wash thinned with water: the pigment over watercolorPaper is that much less dense, so a lit scene's heavy darks lift towards the paper, hues keep and the paper stays the paper. 0 (the default) leaves the frame as lit. The watercolor-wash look sets 0.4, so its frames are paler than before.

added.member: og build --assets and project.ogt publish { assets }
added.summary: A web build can boot its cooked package from an asset base on another origin, such as a CDN: og build --assets <https url> (or publish { assets "<url>" }) writes the base and the manifest's integrity into the page and og-build.json's assets { base, origin }. The cook writes each cooked file's sha384 integrity into cooked/.cook.ogt, and the web loader fetches every file against it, so a changed file fails to load. The assets guide's §3 A package on a CDN; docs/web-export.md §Asset base.
`model.taken`: the tick each of the last 256 batches was taken at, and the tick it was due at.

The web shell tells its page when a playing video player with `wait` holds the clock for its frame (true) and lets it go (false), so the page shows a loading sign; the frame answer carries `buffering`.

Select Yarn's first, best, best-least-viewed or random-best-least-viewed strategy, or the engine's conditional-first weighted strategy. Strategy, view counts and all random draws use checkpointed story state.
Rust cook-time Yarn compiler, extracted base strings through i18n, conditional weighted line groups on the story RNG fork, and save-safe choices and detours.

fixed.summary: A switch whose knob all but vanishes into the track it is on (contrast under 1.5:1, the neutral default style's white on white) turns the inverse ink while on, so the knob and its tick read. A dropdown's rows are inset a step beyond the focus ring's reach, so a focused end row's ring keeps the list's ground round it and no longer stands for the list's edge.

Ground snapping holds only a controller that was grounded at the start of its move (down slopes and steps), as rapier's own controller does: one falling from a jump or off a ledge now lands where it meets the ground instead of being pulled down to ground within snapDistance in one tick (up to 0.2 m at once by default, a visible drop at every landing).
A `type ui-material`'s `source` is read relative to the material file first, then from assets/, so a material installed with a kit keeps finding its WGSL.
The UI state saves which finger holds each touch control (version 16); a save at version 15 upgrades on load.
Ejecting a kit document copied the whole kit beside it (its TypeScript, manifest, skill and review sheet); it now copies the document with its companion documents and assets only.

On a phone in portrait the conversation's caption and choices traded room every tick and the caption rose over the tools; the choices now take a fixed share of the room. A resource bar laid in the flow folds to its box, not to the screen.

A restored grid or navmesh keeps the edit count its agents planned on. A restore rebuilds a mesh's obstacles, areas and links (or a grid's costs) with edits of its own, so its count only matched the saved paths by chance, and when it did not every agent planned again on the tick after a load (the same motion, a different world hash). The count is now set back from the saved paths; a nav edited after its newest path was planned also writes its count in the og.nav trailer (tag 4), so a path that was stale at the save is stale after it. A state whose paths are current saves byte for byte as before.

A save holds the names given since the last tick began: an entity named by world.spawn between ticks (GameDesc.start, a command) and then saved, or named by a system and saved by a later system in the same tick, restores with its name instead of losing it for good (a restore drops the names still queued for the world). A name given in a system now goes into the world when that system returns, with its spawn, so the world hash of that tick includes it (it used to from the next tick on).

An engine upgrade no longer refuses or resets a player's save: the engine migrates its own state in a save from an older build before the restore checks it (a table of steps by what moved and its version; og.ui's state block 9 -> 11, so a save from 0.7.7 restores without migrate, its game data, engine components and og.Rng record for record as this build runs the game).

The 512 KiB cap stays, measured against a 5,000-entity world (half physics bodies): 437 KiB, about 100 ms to save and 65 ms to restore natively; a slot's two banks are the platform's 1 MiB a player and game. A text over the cap is refused pointing at selections. Saves are og-save:2: (with the game's save version); og-save:1: saves still read, as version 1.

A save restores without `migrate` when an engine type (og.* component, resource or event) only gained fields since it was written: every saved field is still there with its type, and each added field takes its declared default from the IDL (og.RenderSettings' new fields in every save of the build before), never zero by accident. A removed, renamed or retyped engine field still needs an engine migration; a game's own types stay strict, refused naming the fields.

fixed.member: World.despawn/get/set/insert/remove/has/alive/nameOf, every API call taking an Entity, SpawnDesc.parent, world.spawn in a system
fixed.summary: A value that is not an entity number (null from world.find, undefined, a Result) is thrown naming the call and parameter on both hosts (`world.set: entity is null (world.find returns null when no entity has the name)`), not napi's conversion error natively or a coercion to 0 on the web; a non-number SpawnDesc.parent is refused instead of ignored; a dead handle is refused as `world.despawn: no live entity has the handle N`, with the hint `Archetype.entities holds (index, generation) pairs; use a.entity(i) for a handle` (and one engine log line per system and call) for a bare index; world.spawn's undeclared og.Parent or og.Transform write says spawn wrote it (`... (world.spawn with parent writes og.Parent; add og.Parent to the system's writes)`).

og-game (166 KB, 27 chapters) is an entry point of 40 KB; rendering, physics, 2D, animation and lockstep are the new skills og-render, og-physics, og-2d, og-anim and og-net, performance and video out are og-build, generators and type model og-model, looks og-taste. The API wiki is no longer mounted under og-game: every skill names og api show <module> for its modules, and api.ogt names the skill that teaches each module.

Keys held when the window loses focus or the page is hidden are released, and the pads come to rest with the keys they map to (the next poll sends a pad still held); nothing released them before, so a key could stay down in the game after an alt-tab.

A type whose layout changed since the save is compared only when the save holds data of it (a component row, a resource value or an event): a type it holds none of takes this build's layout, since nothing of it can be misread, so adding a field to a type a save never used (Model.variant) no longer refuses that save without migrate. Types the save holds data of are checked as before.

Automatic quality no longer cycles between two rungs on the GPU-time path: a rung that falls back within VERIFY_FRAMES waits twice as long before it is tried again and is given up after MAX_FAILURES, and the rung above is predicted with the measured spread added (meridian-loop at 2560x1600 stepped 1.6 to 1.7 and back every 30 s in Chrome and Edge).

A lockstep room no longer stalls for good when the room loses an input message: every input message carries all of the sender's inputs its peers have not acknowledged (each carries the sender's confirmed tick) and a peer waiting at a boundary sends them again. The lockstep wire version is 2: a peer on an older engine has its start refused with the reason instead of desyncing (G2-7).

fixed.member: lockstep: inputs overtaking a seat change
fixed.summary: An input message (sent unreliably) that overtook the reliable `admit` it followed let a peer confirm the new seat's first tick without it, so a late joiner's world could differ; input messages now name the seat changes their sender knows and wait for the resend otherwise. In rollback an admit's seat starts after every input the authority already sent.

fixed.member: og-net relay client: a stopped and resumed process
fixed.summary: A signal interrupting the client's socket read or write (a process stopped and resumed, a laptop waking) no longer counts as a lost connection.

A cooked font now carries U+00A0, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F and U+205F even when its file lacks them (or its charset leaves them out): empty glyphs with the font's own advance, else the width Unicode gives the space (the space's for U+00A0; en and em quads and spaces in em; figure and punctuation spaces as `0` and `.`; thin spaces and U+202F about a third of an em, never wider than the space; the hair space a tenth). They used to take no width, so CLDR's "3:05 PM" (U+202F before PM) drew as "3:05PM" and fr's "1 234" as "1234". The font's cook stamp moves ("font 2"), so every font re-cooks once; the blob layout and type hash are unchanged, and a requested `chars` space the file lacks is no longer reported missing.

A text drawing a character its face lacks (its atlas, and its file at run time) is warned of the same with or without a renderer, once per face and character, on the tick that drew it: og-ui reads each frame's texts against each face's metrics, og.render.text and og.render.floatingText are read when queued. Before, only a frame a GPU drew warned, so a run whose adapter request failed missed it (ui-kit's settings-saved, one run in five), and a character a second face lacked was never named.

An element's draw paints over its background, as documented: a rim stroked with setDraw on an element with a background drew under the background quad and showed only at the corners its radius left uncovered.

Moves frames: under 4x MSAA a sprite's or tile's uv is interpolated at a covered sample (centroid) instead of the pixel centre, so an edge pixel no longer reads the next cell of its atlas; a tilemap's rows had a faint seam in the colour of the neighbouring tile (top-down's path tiles). One sample per pixel draws as before.

Component catalogue sections now have stable identities keyed by kind instead of enum position, so inserting or reordering kinds no longer changes saved guide references or API search results. Restored the existing control sections after inline elements were added.
The doc states its sense: the heading of the camera from the orbited point, from +Z towards +X (unchanged).

fixed: The angle rule is stated on the units: radians for every rotation, heading, yaw, joint or steering limit, arc, uv rotation and cone (a half-angle); degrees for a field of view (the full angle), slopes, the sky's angles, camera roll, and the angles of post effects, styles and the art contract. The physics guide no longer says every angle is in radians (maxSlope is degrees).

fixed.summary: The docs list og.platform's error codes again, and which of them are retryable.
The docs list every method a host can answer again.

UI motion, widgets and style curves use the deterministic shared timing evaluator; style steps no longer become linear transitions. Style roles remain indirection, and CSS keeps its own authored timing vocabulary.

minimal-geometric's ground no longer draws as a checkerboard of triangles: its facets are the cook's (facetAngle 8), each one colour and one normal, and the preset no longer sets MaterialStyle.flatShading, whose per-triangle normals put neighbouring triangles in different toon bands. Geometry built at run time is shaded smooth under it unless its material sets flatShading.

After the probe's report is taken (assertions(true)) and the world restored to a tick whose number comes again, og.assert's sometimes, reachable and each sites are reported to the new report again; they were taken for already heard of when the restored tick's number matched the last call's, so a replay in the same engine missed them.

The mixer took about 9 % of a core to render 32 busy voices (16 streamed stereo QOA loops at assorted pitches, 16 resident ones) with the windowed-sinc resampler: one serial chain of adds per voice frame and per-frame bookkeeping. A voice now renders in runs of 64 frames: their source positions, the history filled once from the decoded block, eight frames' taps summed side by side with SSE (the same order everywhere else, so every host renders the same samples), then the filter, panner and ramp. The same mix takes about 4 %. Pitched or resampled voices move by rounding only: at most -138 dBFS dry, about -96 dBFS (one 16-bit step) once bus effects carry it; unpitched voices at the output's rate and the linear resampler are unchanged, bit for bit.

A world restored from a snapshot or a save no longer wakes the sleeping bodies of a joint with breakForce or breakTorque: the save now carries the two, so the restored world goes on tick for tick as the one it was saved from (a rollback, a rejoin and a loaded save had left it for the ticks the pair took to fall asleep again). Saves of worlds without a breakable joint are byte for byte what they were.
The TypeScript runtime now exports the declared setHighlight and remoteFrames operations through the existing host ABI.

fixed: The native watch loop announces probe readiness after installing its bundle watcher, so the first edit made on readiness is observed.

fixed.summary: A scene entity's source line is now cooked into the scene blob (a `lines` table, left out of publish cooks), so the web host answers `scenes/main.ogt:5` as the native host does instead of the bare scene id. A prefab instance's nodes name the line where the instance is placed. The cooker version moves to r15, so projects re-cook once.
timeline's screen changes are recorded on both hosts: the runtime's UI hook passed the layer stack through to the probe, and before this it reported none.

A renderer destroyed after drawing a single frame no longer waits for its full lit pipeline variants: they now start compiling in the background after the renderer's second frame instead of its first, so one that draws a single frame (a test, a screenshot tool) never starts them. On the L4 a terrain scene's renderer waited about 3.0 s at destruction. A renderer that draws on still compiles them from its second frame, and still waits for any it is compiling when destroyed, so no compile is left running when the process exits.

Clouds take og.Fog as the sky behind them does (the fog 5 km out, by Fog.sky's share); they took a mesh's distance fog and drew as flat fog-coloured cut-outs against a clear sky. Scenes with clouds and distance fog move: far clouds keep their light and shade.
An opaque cloud hides the sun's disc; a hundredth of it drew through as a bright circle on the cloud.

In a frame with a depth prepass (ambient occlusion and the other effects that read depth), the cloud march skips the parts of the sky that surfaces cover, so a view that looks at the ground or a wall no longer pays for clouds it cannot see (a fully covered view 6.1 ms to 3.8 ms at 720p on an Apple M4 Pro). An open sky costs the same.

The main camera's clouds are marched at half the frame's size each way and drawn over the sky at the frame's own size, so a cloudy sky costs about half as much of the frame (a fair sky 10.3 ms to 5.7 ms, a sunset 12.5 ms to 6.2 ms at 720p on an Apple M4 Pro). Cloud edges are a little softer and the march's dither grain is gone; meshes against the sky stay as sharp. Probes, mirrors, views and a live sky's capture march at their own pixels as before.

Under an overcast the sky's strip above the horizon no longer marches the cloud deck four extra times at every pixel: the grey those marches gave is the same for every pixel, so it is made once a frame, with the same pixels. A storm sky over the sea costs about 40% less of the frame (36 ms to 21 ms at 720p on an Apple M4 Pro), a live sky's capture about 45% less.
Clouds drift the way `wind` and og.Wind blow, as rain, grass and cloth go. Before, they drifted the opposite way.
The clouds stand over the world: walking or flying under them passes them overhead. Before, they followed the camera, the same sky over every place.
The clouds keep their shapes as the clock runs. Before, every cloud changed shape in one frame each time the wind had carried them four times `scale` (every 50 minutes at the default wind and scale).

A native game that exits while a pipeline variant is still compiling in the background no longer crashes (SIGSEGV) or hangs at exit on NVIDIA's Linux driver when the shader cache is cold: the exit now waits for the running compiles before the driver's compiler is torn down.

Quoted component props use the component's declared type, not a same-named native attribute's type. Inbox selected="welcome" and boolean selected props work without renaming; native numeric tabs attributes retain their meaning.

A shadowed point or spot light's contact shadows are traced only over the pixels its range reaches, not the whole screen, with the same pixels. A light whose range covers the view costs what it did; one that covers part of it costs in proportion.

Moves frames; re-cooks everything (cooker r16): the base colour texture of a glTF material that tests its alpha (`alphaMode` `MASK`, or a `type model`'s `alphaTest`) gets mips that keep its coverage. Each level is the one before sampled bilinearly at the texel centre (a 2×2 box on even sizes, the two centre taps on odd ones, clamped at the edges: WebGL's `generateMipmap`), and a level that keeps fewer texels at or above the material's `alphaCutoff` than the first level does has its alpha raised until it keeps as many. basisu's own filter spread a leaf card's alpha over the transparent texels around it, so its minified levels fell under the cut-off and the card thinned out and vanished with distance (a 1024×384 bamboo spray had no texel left from its 4×1 level down). The cut-off is taken in the texture's alpha, as the renderer tests it times the material's `baseColorFactor` alpha: 255 × `alphaCutoff` / that factor, rounded up. A material with no such byte keeps the encoder's mips: a cut-off of 0 or less, a factor under the cut-off, or a mesh drawn with it whose vertex colour (`COLOR_0`) alpha falls under 1 somewhere, so materials whose vertex alpha varies keep today's mips. Every other texture keeps the same levels. One image under an alpha-tested and another material, or under two whose cut-offs come to different bytes, now cooks as that many textures.

An edit made in the same timestamp tick as the cook before it (4 ms on ext4, up to 2 s on FAT) that kept the file's length left its size and times as they were, so the next cook, and og cook --watch and og dev's reload, reused the old result. A source or cooked file last written in the tick a cook saw it in is now compared by content on the next cook. Cooked bytes are unchanged; a .og/cook-index written by an earlier version is rebuilt on the first cook.

fixed: Cooking UASTC textures skips encoder candidates whose exact error lower bound cannot beat the current result, reducing cold model-cook time without changing encoded output or quality settings.

Angles wrap into (-π, π] the same way everywhere (og_core::math::wrap_angle): og.motion's turn towards a heading, an agent's wander angle and a nav agent's yaw step. og.motion wrapped through atan2(sin, cos), which rounded differently, so a turning agent's heading can differ in its last bits and a replay recorded before this may step differently.

og.CameraRail's inline points and a spline emitter's shape follow og-core's one Catmull-Rom (og_core::math::catmull_rom, the cubic og.path evaluates): the same curve, computed in another order, so a rail camera's position can differ in its last bits and a replay recorded before this may step differently.

og bake projection: the grey clay a view is painted over is encoded with the sRGB curve, as every other image the engine writes; it used a 2.2 power, which left its mid tones about two codes darker (0.5 linear was 186, now 188).

A tileset's numbers in .ogt text are refused when they are not finite (such as 1e39, past f32), as timelines, effects and 2D rigs already refuse them; a 2D rig's, a vfx colour's and a timeline's line errors now read the same way (`line N: `key` takes a number`, `must be finite`, `takes true or false`, `takes a colour: r g b [a]`).
Lightning: a strike's bolt and branches are drawn from og-core's seeded stream instead of an inline xorshift, so each strike number has a new shape (still the same shape every time for that number).

A timeline's transform and quaternion field tracks turn with og-core's one deterministic slerp (og_core::math::quat_slerp, what og.motion, the virtual cameras and render interpolation use). The timeline had its own, which fell back to a normalised lerp below a 1.8° turn and took the angle from atan2: a rotation played by a timeline can differ in its last bits, so a replay recorded before this may step differently.

fixed.summary: A crash from a system that throws names the tick it threw in. A frame that caught up after a slow one stepped several ticks, and the report named the tick the previous frame had reached, a few ticks early.

Creation in a checkout reads the source catalogue instead of an outdated packed copy, so --no-prompt selects core default after the UI reset. Interactive creation skips fields with only one available choice.
A crowd's members draw the model's cooked levels of detail by distance, as the model's unposed instances do; every member drew the full mesh. A far crowd costs a fraction of what it did.

A GPU crowd member whose world transform mirrors the model (a negative scale on one axis, as a character flipped by scale.x = -1) draws from outside, lit and shadowed as an unmirrored one. Before, a crowd's draws ignored the mirror and a front-sided member showed its far faces from inside. Mirrored and unmirrored members of one model draw as two crowds.

Skinned meshes and crowds cost less on the GPU: a vertex reads only the joints that weigh on it, so a rigidly bound part reads one joint (and a baked clip's two frames of it) instead of four. 50,000 walkers draw in 16.4 ms a frame instead of 20.9 ms on an M4 Pro; the picture is unchanged.
Every colour a document or style file reads takes all four CSS hex forms, #rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb and #rrggbbaa: column-rule-color: #e33 and other paint properties no longer refuse the short forms.

fixed.member: UI document scoped CSS (vertical-align on inline-level boxes)
fixed.summary: An inline-block (or other inline-level box) with a vertical-align other than baseline is placed by layout while heights are computed, and its line box grows to hold it (CSS 2.1 §10.8), instead of being moved only where it is drawn and overflowing its line. The boxes after its line move down with it.

fixed.member: UI: inline-blocks in a vertical line
fixed.summary: Inline-level boxes in a `vertical-rl` or `vertical-lr` line run down the line and sit on its central baseline; they were stacked on one spot at the line's end.

fixed.member: UI: vertical rich text breaks by vertical advances
fixed.summary: A vertical rich paragraph's lines break by what each unit takes down the column (upright clusters at their vertical advances, sideways runs at their widths). They broke by horizontal widths, so upright Latin and mixed lines ran past their box.

fixed.member: UI: background-clip on a background colour alone
fixed.summary: A background colour with no image now takes background-clip (padding-box, content-box); it was drawn over the whole border box.

Layout change: a `stretch` box with margins across a centred or end-aligned flex line is sized to the line less its margins (calc(100% - margins)), clamped by its max size, and then aligned with the line. It was laid out at the line's start when a max size clamped it.

fixed.member: UI: CSS scrollbar-color and scroll-snap-stop in documents
fixed.summary: scrollbar-color inherits, as CSS Scrollbars 1 says, so a colour on a panel paints the scrollers inside it; scroll-snap-stop always also stops a wheel when it settles, not only a fling: it settles no farther than the first such area past where the wheel started.

A float among a block's inline content is placed at the top of the line it comes on when it fits beside what that line already holds, else at the next line's top (CSS 2.1 §9.5.1), instead of at the block's top. This holds in vertical writing modes as well.

A block-level box among inline lines beside a float is a block of its own (CSS 2 §9.2.1.1). It spans the line box, and its content flows around the float. One that starts a formatting context of its own is still fitted beside the float.

A rich-text paragraph beside a float is shaped once and broken against each line's room. Bidi and soft hyphens now see the whole paragraph, where before the paragraph was reshaped from the spans left on every line.
A shared element's old and new images leave out the shared elements inside it, as the spec captures them: each of those is drawn only by its own group, and no longer twice.

A modal dialog directly under the root, and a spotlight dialog, no longer give their place in the tree the key of the layer that draws them: the probe lists that place as <id>~place and the layer as <id>, so each key names one element and the bounded frame's index holds both. An element's entrance (-og-enter) is remembered from the tick it was first seen, so a restored snapshot matches the frame that wrote it.

fixed.member: UI: currentColor and light-dark() in documents
fixed.summary: currentColor is the element's own color, declared or inherited, in a background, a gradient's stops, a box shadow, a filter and color itself (whose currentColor is the inherited colour); it was the style's ink outside borders and outlines. light-dark() takes the element's used colour scheme: color-scheme: light or dark on it or an ancestor forces it, and light dark or none keeps the style's. It took the style's scheme everywhere.

fixed.member: UI: physical sides under a right-to-left surface
fixed.summary: In a right-to-left surface a document's `left`, `right`, `margin-left`, `padding-right`, `text-align: left`, `justify-content: right` and transforms stay on the side they name; before, the whole-surface mirror turned them round with the logical ones. The surface mirror still lays out documents that are right to left as a whole.
font-size-adjust scales a face's extents with its size, so its baseline sits where the adjusted face's does, and x_height() and cap_height() report a scaled face's own.

Text at a computed weight of 600 or more whose face is lighter than 600 is drawn with a synthesised bold, as browsers draw it, in plain and rich text alike (rich text synthesised only from 700, and plain text from a face more than 100 lighter). The synthesised bold replaces the style's textWeight thickening instead of adding to it. Semibold headings and buttons in a style without a semibold face now read bold; a style that wants its own thickening sets font-synthesis-weight: none.

An Emoji_Presentation character a text face has (⌚, ⭐) now draws in the colour emoji face when the text's fonts have one, and U+FE0F after a character such as © draws it in colour, as browsers do; font-variant-emoji: text keeps it in the text face.

A document's plain text at a bold weight (700 or more) whose family has no face within 100 of it is drawn thickened, as a rich text's bold span already was, instead of in the regular face; font-synthesis-weight: none keeps it regular.
@container scroll-state(stuck: top | right | bottom | left | block-start…) now matches a position: sticky container held to that edge of its scrollport; before, only stuck: none matched.
Destroying an engine now closes what its host opened for it: the audio output, the probe socket, the room link and the renderer's records. They were held until the process or the page ended.

An f32 field is compared with its declared bounds at f32 precision. A field set to its own minimum or maximum (og.Water.depthFade at 0.01, which its f32 holds as 0.0099999998) no longer breaks "in range" on every tick, so `og run` no longer exits with status 1 for it. A value past a bound by more than the f32's rounding still breaks it.

A material's shader parameter change is one write: its new values, the ones the frame before drew and the number of the frame it is drawn in. previous_shader_params() (motion vectors) reads the previous values in that frame only, so the parameters' motion stops on the next frame, also while the game is paused, with nothing written then. Before, the frame after each change wrote the previous values again on every changed material and ran the per-frame material pass for it. Frames do not change.

A scatter's chunks share one key of what placed them, hashed once a frame, instead of each chunk cloning the scatter's parameters, layers and tiles into two keys and hashing them up to four times every frame. Keys still compare by value, so what is built and drawn does not change. A garden of 1072 cells: scatter prepare 258 -> 102 ms per 10 s, of which hashing 148 -> 29 ms.

The static shadow cache keeps each instance's hash across frames and hashes again only the instances that moved or changed (their transform, sway, own material, or their mesh's or material's revision), instead of hashing every sorted instance every frame. The hash is unchanged, so every decision of the cache is the one a full pass gives. Frames do not change. A garden of 1072 cells: the per-frame hashing 127 -> 0 ms per 10 s, keeping the hashes 24 ms.

A render pass on the web draws with the browser's own draw methods. Before, every page replaced GPURenderPassEncoder's draw, drawIndexed, drawIndirect and drawIndexedIndirect with wrappers that checked for a skipped stand-in pipeline, so every draw of every frame went through one. Now only a pass whose setPipeline skips a stand-in that is not made yet drops its draws, until its next made pipeline. What is drawn and skipped does not change. A garden of 1072 cells, 8.9k draws a frame: 0.17-0.42 ms less engine Worker time a frame.

A ray's answer is written as text directly instead of being built as a JSON object per hit and formatted. The text is byte-identical: the same keys in the same order, the same digits, null for a value that is not finite. A garden with about sixty casts a tick: 0.44 of castRay's 1.23 ms a tick on the web.

Decoding a cooked model's meshopt-compressed vertices is faster, most of all on the web: the delta decode takes its element width as a constant, so its loops unroll without a bounds check per byte. The bytes decoded do not change. 268 cooked cells of a 1072-cell garden decode in 0.71 of the time; the garden's web cell load spends about 1.8 s less decoding.

A cascade drawn over its cached static casters finds which batches are dynamic from a table built once a frame, one load per batch, instead of a binary search asked twice per batch and cascade. The same batches are drawn. Frames do not change. A garden of 1072 cells (about 3,500 batches), web, from a profile: 66.5 of the 111 ms per 10 s that the cascades' lists took.

A frame makes a pipeline job only for a pipeline that is neither made nor queued. Before, every frame made a job for every batch and pass (cloning the device, layouts and shader module and boxing the builder) and dropped it when the pipeline was already held, on every frame after the load. What is compiled does not change.

Extracting the terrain components (og.Terrain, og.TerrainScatter, og.TerrainStamp, og.GrassType, og.Grass, og.GrassPusher) and the atmosphere ones (og.WindMotor, og.Water and its kin, og.Fluid2D, og.Fluid3D, og.Rope, og.Cloth, og.SoftBody) keeps the JSON of each row whose bytes did not change since the last frame, instead of decoding every row and dropping it every frame. What is extracted does not change. A garden of 1072 cells, web, from a profile: terrain 60 and atmosphere 38 ms per 10 s, about half of each in decoding.

A key code's place in og.Input's key sets is found by a binary search of the codes, built once, instead of a scan of the 106-code table; the UI's input read asks it about 300 times a tick. The answers do not change. A garden at its gate, web, from a profile: 28 of the UI input read's 38 ms per 10 s.

Under a fixed shadow box every receiver is compared towards the light by the game's shadowBias again, as three.js compares and as the field says. Since the closed-receiver rule (a closed, single-sided receiver compared a quarter of the depth bias past its own depth), a box's closed receivers were compared a quarter of shadowBias past themselves instead, so a ground under a 0.18 m bias shadowed itself at noon. Frames move only in games that set shadowBox; the cascades keep the closed-receiver rule.

fixed.member: rendering: clustered meshes in a frame culled on the CPU
fixed.summary: Under the default culling a clustered mesh takes the meshlet path only in a frame that is culled on the GPU anyway (from 16,384 instances, or for GPU crowds). Every cooked model has clusters, so before this one clustered batch turned GPU culling on for a whole frame of any size, the path that costs a small frame more than the CPU culling it replaces. In a smaller frame clustered meshes now draw on the per-instance path, culled on the CPU, at the level og-runtime picks, as Culling::Cpu already drew them. A garden of about 3,000 instances: 10,393 draws -> 4,688 and the native render median 40.6 -> 27.1 ms, with frames byte-identical to the meshlet path's. Culling::Gpu is unchanged.

fixed.member: models sharing a glTF material (og.render.updateMaterial, material shaders and their parameters)
fixed.summary: Each model's copy of a shared glTF material batches with the others again whenever the game has given them the same edit. Before, the first edit of a copy (a value, a material shader or a shader parameter) parted it from the others for good, so a game that edits every model's materials (seasons, alpha to coverage, a shader) drew each model in a batch of its own. Now an edit that leaves the copies drawing the same (equal values, the same shader with equal parameters) joins them, in either order, and one that makes them differ parts them. A model loaded after the game edited the copies loaded before it (one loaded while the game runs, as a web boot loads cell by cell) joins them from the edit that makes it alike. Each copy keeps its own values and parameters, so an edit of one never shows on another. In the frame a copy's or its original's shader parameters change, the two draw apart, so each one's motion vectors (previous_shader_params) read its own previous parameters; they batch again from the next frame. A garden of 1072 cells: native draws at the gate 4688 -> 3271, web 4687 -> 3270.

fixed.member: material shaders' vertex_offset in the prepass
fixed.summary: The depth prepass runs a material shader's vertex_offset hook for the frame before (the motion vectors' previous position) only in a frame whose motion vectors something reads: TAA or a temporal upscaler, motion blur, screen-space reflections, screen-space GI or a custom post pass. Before, it ran the hook twice per vertex in every frame. Frames do not change. A garden whose wind sways every plant: native GPU prepass 7.1 -> 5.3 ms at the gate.

A glyph cooked both by its code point and by its glyph id (every face is shaped, so each charset glyph is cooked twice) is one image in the atlas, both rows at it, instead of two. Fonts re-cook once (stamp "font 9", including embedded Rive fonts).
