Text over a nine-slice, a border image, a pattern or a cover, contain, none or scale-down image is read on what that layer draws under it, placed as og-render places it (og-draw's UiImage::place and UiGradientImage::place, ui.wgsl's image_uv); such pairs were reported `unchecked`, their ratio leaving the layer out (fantasy's 152). The `unchecked` ground kind is gone.

A button that is a chosen radio (`role="radio" aria-checked="true"`, such as a quantity among ×1/×10/Max buttons or a segment) wears the default style's selection, as a button with `aria-pressed="true"` does: --button-selected-fill under --button-selected-ink, in every variant, at rest, hovered and held. It was drawn as a plain button, so the chosen one did not show.

`background-clip: text` cuts the background to the text of the element and of all its descendants (CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.1), drawn where the background is, under that text; it cut only to the element's own text, so a box whose text sat in child elements drew no background at all.

fixed.member: CSS relative colours in a stylesheet
fixed.summary: A relative colour whose channel uses math (`background: oklch(from var(--accent) l c calc(h + 180))`) no longer fails the declaration with "calc() does not take 'h'": the channel keywords are the colour's to resolve.
A colour whose alpha is `none` (`rgb(0 0 0 / none)`) draws transparent, as CSS Color 4 treats a missing component as zero; it drew opaque.
A space or punctuation after an emoji takes a text face's glyph instead of the emoji face's 1.25 em space.

`color` inherits between document elements, as in CSS: text under an element that declares it (`
…
`, a class, a role rule such as a frame's `--ink`) takes that colour, however deep, and follows it when it changes. Before, text that declared no colour drew the palette's ink. A `
A value written as #rgba now reads as that colour with its alpha dropped, as CSS reads it. It used to read as black.

The health bar has a length on desktop: the vitals plate is --measure-sm wide (within the safe area). It hugged its content, and a StatBar takes its container's width, so the bar drew 0 px wide and only the icon and the figure showed.

fixed.member: <dialog modal>, popover and -og-spotlight in a mounted document
fixed.summary: A container inside a modal dialog, a popover or a spotlight's callout now shows its content in a mounted (retained) document; before, its children were dropped from the first frame (a modal's footer of buttons showed empty), because they were named apart from the top-layer node they are built under.

An ancestor's ground counts under a text only where its box covers the text: a hotkey placed under its slot (RpgActionBar) is over the scene and takes the tag treatment, in every style (it read 1.0–1.36:1 under the packs).

ModeSelect's unselected and locked cards and SaveLoad's unselected slots dim their art, not their words, which keep their ink; StatusGrid's expiring buff blinks its icon, not its stack count; MinimapView's north mark wears --tag-halo instead of a soft offset shadow (3.73:1 on its bezel).
A locked cell ([data-locked=true]) keeps its words' ink, as it is still read (a locked card's rules); only a disabled one takes --ink-disabled. It keeps the empty cell's shadow.

Text over glass (a backdrop: -og-material glass, backdrop-filter) is read on what the glass makes of a black and a white scene, as og-render composes it; it was read as bare text on the scene (OverlayBar's names at 1.36–1.48:1).

fixed: Built-in UI name and dependency lookup now reads a generated package manifest instead of parsing every built-in document. UI type generation parses only the built-ins it needs.

fixed.summary: A component's prop may share a name with a property one tag owns (count, which is <og-counter>'s value) or with a renamed HTML attribute (hidden): on a component it is passed as the prop under its own name. On any other element it is still refused with the tag to write.

fixed.member: AbilityBar, AbilitySlot, ActionButton, Cooldown, HeroButton, HoldButton, RadialMenu, TouchControls, OverlayBar, StatBar
fixed.summary: HUD controls use HTML with CSS while retaining ids, parts and input contracts. Optional cooldowns, costs and hints occupy no blank space; labels stay visible when a hold has no alternate wording, and long confirmation labels wrap. Primary touch labels use their contrasting foreground and twin-stick actions wrap within phone width. Radial commands announce the current choice and show its label when no detail is supplied; the RadialMenu.well surface hook stops the scene halo at the centre. Overlay legends have explicit spacing and their choices scroll within the available width. Stat bars fill the slot supplied by their container.

HUD instruments use HTML with CSS and keep every existing id and part. StatBar's shield, healing and value layers are contained by their own tracks, orb values stay centered above contained liquid, and progress labels share the ring's center. Timers distinguish the caption from the numeric readout with consistent spacing and numeric typography. Optional labels and rings occupy no space when absent.

Compass edges fade as a sliding window, with the heading in a separately spaced readout below. A minimap without a texture shows a visible grid rather than an apparently blank surface. New Compass.readout and Minimap.grid parts let style packs restyle these pieces.

Navigation documents use HTML with CSS and retain their ids and parts. Map markers and rotating map content belong to their own positioned viewports. The compass centers its heading in the actual available width on a phone and separates objective icons and distances from the cardinal directions. Optional labels, textures and distances leave no blank space.

fixed.member: RacingTelemetry, RacingLapHud, RacingStandings, RacingBanner, RacingGarage, RacingResults
fixed.summary: Racing components use HTML with CSS and retain their parts, ids, intents and keyed replay. Telemetry has visible token-colored gauge tracks and centered speed and gear, optional readouts occupy no blank space, garage names wrap, and classification badges no longer squeeze the driver's name on a phone. Default review pages now load a readable font.

fixed.member: ShooterAmmoCounter, ShooterCombatHud, ShooterCrosshair, ShooterDamageDirection, ShooterKillfeed, ShooterLoadout
fixed.summary: Shooter components use HTML with CSS while retaining ids, parts and intents. Ammo and reload layers stay in their tracks, optional readouts leave no empty space, and a token-based reticle keyline keeps the aim visible against bright scenes. Loadout columns and the review sheet's non-shrinking footer remain usable at phone width.

fixed.member: DamageNumbers, OverheadBars, Nameplate, SelectionRing, Telegraph, PathLine, PlacementGhost, InteractionPrompt, LootLabel, SpeechBubble
fixed.summary: In-world documents retain their semantic anchors and ground projections while expressing their boxes in HTML with CSS. Nameplate health, shield and cast layers stay inside their tracks; placement grids and reach previews are contained by their footprint. Optional labels and shape branches occupy no blank space. Speech and interaction text use explicit spacing, loot counts have a distinct numeric readout, and overhead health bars follow the style's health token. All existing parts and ids remain available to style packs.

fixed.member: CardFace, CardCollection, CardDeckList, CardHand, CardPiles, CardReward, CardRunMap, NodeGraph
fixed.summary: Card components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditional content. Card faces have two-line names, start-aligned rules and inset art wells; collection counts sit below cards instead of on their art, and phone collections use two readable columns. Deck size has a contained meter with a danger fill above the limit, pile counts have a solid ground, relics have an icon well, narrow rewards scroll as readable cards and map legends have a spaced surface. NodeGraph positions its graph inside its own well rather than the screen, keeping the run map visible. Existing ids, parts and intents are retained.

fixed.member: ActionHints, Celebration, Ribbon, SkeletonGroup, Spinner, SplitView, StarBar, StatusGrid
fixed.summary: Feedback components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditionals while retaining their HUD halo hooks and style-pack parts. Loading skeleton shapes have explicit layouts; split panes fit phone widths and scroll their content; score stars sit above a separate inset track, with the final threshold inside the bar, and status countdown overlays measure against their own holders. Long action hints wrap inside the viewport and long ribbon labels ellipsize instead of spilling across the band. SplitView retains its game-owned ratio and raw resize intents.

fixed.member: Achievements, Chat, DailyQuests, DailyRewards, Friends, Shop, ShopConfirm
fixed.summary: General components use HTML-with-CSS roots, conditional optional content and bounded CSS scrollers. Names, descriptions and rewards have consistent spacing and readable hierarchy in the default style; reward calendars switch to four columns before narrow day states collide. Loading indicators remain visible, and existing ids, parts and keyed intents are preserved. The review sheet includes default-style desktop and phone pages.

fixed.member: Breadcrumbs, Carousel, Chart, DataGrid, Menu, TooltipCard
fixed.summary: Panel components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditional optional content. Tooltip comparisons wrap inside phone viewports, chart layers are contained in their plot, grid text is start-aligned with numeric cells end-aligned, and carousel page dots stay in their own control row. Empty charts and carousels explain their state. Breadcrumbs expose the current page and reverse separators in RTL. Carousel navigation remains game-owned intents, disabled only with fewer than two pages. Existing ids, parts and virtualised list markup are preserved; isolated sheet fixtures expose individual panel states for review.
Keeps unavailable booster words and counts readable while dimming only their art, uses the shared opaque-surface halo reset, and labels the puzzle review sheet's empty board explicitly.
Keeps booster and summary panel text crisp without scene halos, and gives the scrolling score breakdown a fading edge above its actions.

Improves the default puzzle kit with stronger counter hierarchy, visible completion checks and earned stars, current-level and armed-booster emphasis, readable count badges, quieter disabled states and a separated score total. Uses HTML and token-based CSS, with conditional optional content and phone-sized booster cards. Review sheets now include the default style.

fixed.member: ui.RpgBackpack, ui.RpgQuestDetail, ui.RpgVitals, ui.RpgParty, ui.RpgEnemyInfo, ui.RpgWorldMap, ui.RpgItemCard, ui.RpgQuestTracker
fixed.summary: Wraps backpack categories, tightens quest spacing to expose rewards, grounds bar values on contrasting plates, distinguishes quest diamonds from waypoint dots, keeps item actions beside their content, and makes completed HUD objectives legible.

Improves the default RPG kit with visible health, mana and carry fills; grounded shortcut and quantity badges; clearer selected, acting and down states; quest progress marks; separated attributes and rewards; quieter supporting text; and readable phone tab spacing. Converts optional content and scrollers to HTML with token-based CSS. Default-style review sheets now keep desktop panels inside the viewport and give all phone equipment slots room above the stats.

Moves frames: arena documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. The default look gives roster choices two readable phone columns, quieter role labels, distinct draft and lobby row surfaces, stronger versus names, and larger match scores. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: idle documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Default resource figures, generator names and prestige gains have clearer hierarchy; upgrade prices and states have their own column, earnings have quiet row surfaces, and the reset confirmation is more distinct. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: rhythm documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Default chart ratings, judgement calls, combo counts, grades and scores have clearer hierarchy; song details have a quiet surface, missing jackets have a music-icon fallback, and secondary metadata recedes. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: roster, generator and purchase scrollers show a stationary token-based bottom fade so partially visible phone rows read as scrollable, not broken. The idle review sheet adds an isolated bounded Welcome back page to show both claim actions entirely on phone; its combined reset page still scrolls between panels. The rhythm phone HUD gives song progress its own padded strip instead of straddling the playfield background.

Moves frames: strategy documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Selection health fills measure against their own positioned tracks; cooldown text no longer covers command icons. Production rows, tower stats and upgrade paths have clearer grouping, wave counts have clearer hierarchy, and phone actions wrap their text. Tower upgrade paths scroll within the height given, keeping long descriptions and disabled buy controls reachable above Sell. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Repeating unchanged UI configuration retains mounted styles and text measurements. Loading or replacing a CSS texture or its shape-outside alpha updates only elements referencing that asset, rather than invalidating the whole UI; a late alpha now updates its float without another style change.

A call that keeps the style in effect (a scheme, a text scale, reduced motion) no longer installs it again, and one that returns to the default style takes the default stylesheet as already read. Before, every call without a style read the whole default stylesheet again.

Confirm stays whole on a phone at 150 % text: the question and the actions keep their place and what follows scrolls between them; the actions share a line and fill it, take a line each (the confirming one first) where both do not fit, and a long action wraps inside its button. The question is one type step smaller on a phone, and on a phone on its side the dialog widens with what it holds. The document declares an overflow fixture.

An element that reads its container's size (a container query or cq units) and has a child reading it too now takes its queried values on the first frame: settlement could resolve the child first and leave the element as the unmeasured build made it, so a card hand's slots drew 0×0 for a frame and the first focus landed on the one card that had a box.

A container variant that stops matching while its element is laid out (a box whose width follows its height by `aspect`, a block narrowed beside floats) no longer leaves its arrangement, grid columns, `hidden` and animatable values applied: they follow the inline size the element ends the layout with, as its box already did.

fixed.member: UI CSS position: absolute, position: fixed
fixed.summary: A document's absolutely positioned element is now placed against its nearest positioned ancestor (or a `<stack>`), else the document's outermost box, as CSS does (CSS Position 3 §2.1); it used to be placed in its parent's box whether or not the parent was positioned. A fixed element under a transformed ancestor, one whose `will-change` names a transform or filter, or one with `contain: layout` or `paint` is placed against that ancestor's box (CSS Transforms 1 §3, CSS Containment 2 §3.2), not the viewport. Give the intended parent `position: relative` where an absolute child relied on the old placement.

A control with an accent-color draws what sits on the accent in contrast-color() of it: a check mark on a navy accent in the dark scheme was the scheme's near-black on-primary ink (1.4:1) and now reads at least 4.58:1 on any accent. The fill of a checked box, a switch that is on, a chosen radio, a range's track and a progress bar take the accent as before.

A switch that is on keeps its knob readable on a light track: when the knob would vanish on the filled track (a light primary or accent-color), it takes whichever of the scheme's ink and inverse ink reads more on the track. In the light scheme a gold accent left a white knob, and the gold tick on it, at 1.35:1; it is now the dark ink.

A background layer's image or gradient tile is read where og-render draws it (its background-size, -position, -repeat and -origin): fantasy's 58 px filigree corners were read stretched over each frame, under every text in it. A pair over an image the check does not sample (nine-slice, border image, pattern, cover, contain) is reported over "unchecked" instead of a ratio that leaves its look out.

The default ink on a warn fill (Nameplate's cast name on its bar) is contrast-color(var(--warn)), so it reads 4.5:1 or more on any warn a style gives without its own --ink-on-warn (it was --ink-inverse).

An element's style attribute (and style: directive) takes the inherited text properties a <style> rule takes, such as accent-color, caret-color, color-scheme, text-wrap-style and -webkit-text-fill-color; they were refused as unsupported.

The default style's tag halo (--tag-halo, on a nameplate's name, a waypoint's label and a status grid's time left) is an outline: eight unblurred copies of the glyphs 1–1.5 px round them in the ink's inverse, with no drop. The blurred halo with a 1 px drop covered at most half at the glyphs' edge, read 1.09:1 over a white sky and drew an embossed second copy under each label; the outline reads 12.3:1 there (16.7:1 for the light scheme's dark ink over a black scene). Packs that set --tag-halo keep theirs.
The +n tile's count reads over the scene: it takes the figure ink and the tag halo, like an effect's time left. In muted ink, bare on the cell's translucent fill, it read 1.5:1 over a bright sky.

A slider or a <details> resized by a container query draws its new size in that frame: the slider's knob is placed by layout at its value instead of from last frame's track, and the disclosure's root takes the queried width as its summary row does.

revert-layer in a rule that reaches an element from another document (a ::part() rule on a control document's part) rolls back that document's layers only and then falls to the element's own document, instead of also discarding the element's own rules.

A separator is drawn by the default style's hr rule (a --stroke-hairline line in currentColor, --line by default; vertical stands it up) instead of by og-ui, so hr { color; block-size } and any other rule for hr restyle it as CSS does.
A slot now draws the `--slot-shadow` a pack sets; a later rule had cleared it. It is none by default, and a component cell keeps the well shadow it drew, so the default style is unchanged.

A `var()` whose value is `revert` or `revert-layer` rolls the cascade back as the keyword written would (CSS Variables 2 §3): `background: var(--fill, revert-layer)` keeps the layers below until `--fill` is set, instead of being refused as an invalid colour and leaving the property unset.

A control a component names for a role (`<button part="Bag.cell">`, any part ending in `.frame`, `.cell`, `.row`, `.badge` and the other roles) wears its role and the role's tokens alone, as `appearance: none` gives a browser's button its page's look: `button::part(base)` and the control's other own-part rules no longer paint their plate, padding or border image over it. A part named for no role (`Shop.buy`) keeps its control's dress. A control's focus ring is its `focus` part alone and never draws the base's fill, border or border image again over the focused control.

A control a document builds styles its parts as itself from the tick it is built: a rebuilt <button> no longer matched its parts against the enclosing element (a <column part=…>) for that tick, so a focused primary button in a screen no longer switched between two looks on alternate ticks and rebuilt itself while nothing changed.

A font whose face has tabular figures (`tnum`) now cooks them into its atlas without a `features tnum` line, since the default style turns tabular numerals on for its figures and badges. A struck price or a value with inline markup in such a face draws tabular digits that hold their width, and the cook no longer warns about its proportional figures. Fonts re-cook once with this version.

A retained document no longer stops building when a store hides a list row in the same refresh as a change among that row's children; a <select> without <option>s keeps its bound items; screens that declare props may read the engine's $ui store.
A counter styled with a CSS text property (font, letter-spacing and the like, its own or inherited) or named as a part shows its number; it showed nothing.
A counter lands on its value exactly; a value past 16,777,216 was rounded to a float and shown a few units off.

A transition or keyframe animation between `anchor()` insets, or between `anchor-size()` sizes, moves through the lengths they resolve to (CSS Anchor Positioning 1), following an anchor that moves meanwhile, instead of jumping from one anchor to the other. An inset and an anchor size also take `calc()` of weighted terms added, `calc(0.5 * anchor(--a right) + 0.5 * anchor(--b right))`.

fixed.member: CSS vertical-align on an inline block
fixed.summary: An inline block aligns by its last baseline (baseline-source: auto, CSS 2.1 §10.8.1): a two-line inline block beside text sits with its second line on the text's baseline, not its first. baseline-source: first keeps the first. A table cell's vertical-align: text-top and text-bottom place its content at the start and end.
They now blend sRGB-encoded values, as CSS Compositing does, instead of linear light; mid-tones under them are lighter than before.

Bound false HTML boolean attributes are absent from attribute selectors in both document builders; true values are present with an empty string. Data and ARIA false values remain selector-visible. Retained :default follows the checked attribute's presence.
Linear and radial gradient colour stops accept reduced calc() sums of percentages and pixels, including mask-image fades with a fixed pixel tail.
A display: block box with an auto width fills its block parent's content width, as in CSS block flow, instead of shrinking to its content.

fixed.member: UI: CSS clip-path cuts the element's own shadows and borders
fixed.summary: As CSS has it, clip-path now cuts the element's box shadows, borders and outline with its background and children; before, only the background and children were cut. A `#` inside parentheses in a declaration (`url(#id)`) is no longer read as a comment.

Document landed lexical CSS variables, cascade and selector semantics, native layout settlement, and bounded missing-art placeholders. Keep CSS queries, motion completion, sibling and structural selectors, and retained mounting explicitly pending.

counter-reset: reversed(name) with no value starts where CSS Lists 3 says, from the increments and the first counter-set in its scope, so items that count down by one end at 1; it started at 0 and counted below it. Its readers take the start from the tick after the scope is counted.

Resolve cursors over noninteractive boxes in paint order, including inherited values, URL images, transforms, overflow clipping and pointer-events. Passive boxes no longer expose an unrelated underlying control's cursor. Held controls retain their cursor and passive boxes gain no input handlers.

An element's clip-path now bounds where its cursor and its descendants' apply: outside any basic shape, path() or shape() by its fill rule, or a url(#id) <clipPath>, the cursor is that of what lies beneath.

fixed.member: UI: dashed borders on round corners
fixed.summary: A uniform dashed border or outline is dashed side by side with a dash on every corner; the pattern no longer laps the outline and leaves its remainder as a thick arc on the top-left corner.

Load and register document CSS texture assets, including imported stylesheets and inline styles, on initial load and document reload. Inline URLs resolve beside the document. Cooked SVG files supply mask images and cursor pixels without manual texture loading.

A text's pseudo-element styles draw: ::first-letter, ::first-line, ::before and ::after colours, fonts and decorations were replaced by the element's plain style once its CSS fields applied. ::first-letter takes the first letter, number or symbol with the Unicode punctuation around it (“¿Q, (1)) and a base with its combining marks, as CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §2.2 says; it took only ASCII punctuation before a single character.

Blends that read the destination inside a UI layer (a filtered, masked or material ancestor) draw instead of being dropped; a layer's composite honours its blend instead of drawing normal; multiply over a layer's transparent pixels no longer darkens them, and screen and plus-lighter keep the layer's alpha.

::selection and ::target-text follow highlight inheritance (CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §3.5), as ::highlight() does. Each property the text's own element leaves unset comes from the nearest ancestor's rule that sets it, background-color included, so `div::selection { color: red }` now styles the selection in the paragraphs inside that div.
Accept valid MIME parameters in type() descriptors and discard malformed descriptors before resolution deduplication. Asset discovery and rendering use the same selection rules.
Preserve quoted strings during math-function discovery and scan Unicode at character boundaries, avoiding a panic on non-ASCII MIME parameters and accidental evaluation of literal calc() text.
Preserve percentage slice and automatic-width metadata through the renderer instead of clamping it away; automatic widths account for image-set density.

Inline !important declarations, including Svelte style:prop|important, outrank stylesheet !important declarations across cascade layers. Removing a bound inline value restores the underlying declaration.

Moves frames: a justified line ends at its box's edge. Each glyph after a widened space was moved by the extra room twice (by the pen and again by its offset), so a justified line ran past its box by its free room.

fixed.member: UI: a background gradient on an element with a border
fixed.summary: It is placed in the padding box and repeats under the border, as CSS's background-origin default does, instead of stretching over the border box.
Repeating radial and conic gradients repeat the interval between their first and last stops, including negative positions; coincident stops render their CSS average colour.
counter(list-item) in a <ul>'s ::marker or ::before reads the item's number; it read 0 unless the list was numbered.

fixed: Review missing-art fallback slots at natural wide, tall, full-bleed and icon sizes rather than square cells.

fixed.summary: A document whose CSS rule body holds a character of more than one byte (`--icon: é`) no longer crashes its parse.

New parts measure before entering the layout cache. Retained content preserves logical IDs while attaching under its physical part box. Settled animations reuse paint, and removing and reinserting a host retires its parts.
An empty field's placeholder keeps its `::placeholder` colour (else the style's placeholder ink) when the field sets its own `color`; the field's colour inked the placeholder before.

A popover opens and closes as HTML's top layer does. Closed, it keeps no style, so it opens from its `@starting-style` and shows from the frame `:popover-open` matches, one tick after the press, instead of transitioning from its closed style. Its own `opacity`, `transform`, transitions and animations now move its shown layer, not an empty placeholder. Closing with an `allow-discrete` transition of `overlay` or `display` keeps it shown, inert, until that transition ends while its closed style transitions in, where it vanished at once. An open popover keeps its anchor across `restoreState`.

data-og-instant settles the first @starting-style entrance for channel and computed values. Whitespace no longer makes a discrete display exit disappear halfway through; retained display exits retire their render subtree on completion.

fixed.member: Widget part placement in right-to-left frames
fixed.summary: A widget part's own placement is no longer mirrored a second time in a right-to-left frame: a switch's knob stays on its track. Part boxes keep their widget's enter and exit presence.
Evaluate resolution descriptors through the shared CSS math engine: calc(), min(), max() and clamp() accept mixed x, dppx, dpi and dpcm units for document and widget-part images.

Non-repeating CSS gradients preserve stops outside 0..100%; translate:none clears percentage and length offsets; hidden masked boxes preserve subtree layer pairing without painting; column flex items derive auto cross sizes from their final flexed height and aspect ratio.
Built-in CSS packs may reference SVG images inside art/ subdirectories, just like other relative asset directories.
Select popup parts retain their markup host's selector attributes and document stylesheet without changing independent popovers. Part inspection includes persistent part boxes.

Button text uses the host's installed font-family, with part-local font overrides taking precedence. Divider color reaches the drawn rule. Tab indicators retain their layout motion. Persistent content boxes retain host interaction states and focus radii, and select borders preserve default text positions.

A text length in em or a percentage (line-height: 200%, letter-spacing: 0.5em, text-indent, tab-size) resolves against the element's own font-size even when its rule declares that size after it, as CSS computes it; it took the parent's size before.

Moves frames: a CSS text stroke is centred on the glyphs' edge over the fill at its width, as browsers draw it (it ran wholly outside the edge), takes color rather than -webkit-text-fill-color when it names no colour, and paint-order: stroke paints it under the fill so only its outer half shows.

CSS `touch-action` is read from the element a touch lands on (intersected with its ancestors), as Pointer Events 3 says, not from the scroll container the drag moves: `touch-action: pan-y` on a card inside a two-axis scroller now keeps its drag vertical. UI state is version 24 (version 23 upgrades with no touch in progress).

text-underline-position: under puts the underline at the font's descent, clear of every descender, with text-underline-offset measured from there; text-underline-offset: from-font and text-decoration-thickness: from-font take the font's own post underline position and thickness.

Boolean media features follow Media Queries 4 §2.4.4: a feature matches unless its value is 0, `none` or a value it names false. `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` now matches in both schemes, where it used to match in neither. `@media (hover)` and `(any-hover)` no longer match on a coarse pointer, whose `hover` is `none`.

`initial` on `direction`, `unicode-bidi`, `writing-mode`, `text-orientation` and `text-combine-upright` now gives the property's initial value (`ltr`, `normal`, `horizontal-tb`, `mixed`, `none`). It used to keep the parent's value, as `inherit` does: `direction: initial` under an rtl parent stayed rtl.

A document's `ex`, `cap`, `rex` and `rcap` now read the body face's own x-height and cap height (OS/2) instead of 0.5em and the ascent. `ch` and `ic` use the advance of the face's `0` and 水, and fall back to CSS Values 4's 0.5em and 1em when the face lacks the glyph. They used to take the .notdef advance.

A `box-sizing: content-box` size written as `round()`, `mod()`, `rem()`, `abs()` or `hypot()` adds its padding once to the result; it used to add it to each argument, so `round(down, 60%, 50px)` also moved its step.

A custom property registered with `@property` and a `<length>` syntax now computes to px where it is set, so `--gap: 2em` is the setting element's em and its children inherit those pixels. Children used to re-read `2em` at their own font size.

Transition and animation longhands and the `transition` and `animation` shorthands take math their element resolves (viewport and font units, `env()`, `random()`, the tree-counting functions): the value is checked when the element resolves, as a `var()` is, instead of being refused when the document is defined.

white-space: pre, pre-wrap, pre-line and break-spaces (and white-space-collapse) keep the spaces, tabs and line breaks a document's literal text was written with: the text was HTML-collapsed when the document was read, so they had nothing left to keep. pre-wrap may break after a run of spaces, break-spaces after each one, and a tab advances to the next tab-size column.
The capacity readout uses its strings table, so locales can translate the separator and built-in component documents cook without an untranslated-text warning.

Moves frames: adds pinned Lucide fallback vectors for apple, bomb, crown, drop, fire, gear, gem, heart, home, key, leaf, pause, potion, shield and sword, so built-in documents and their sample data draw these icons without a game atlas. Game-supplied icons still win.

Built-in UI icon names now have on-demand vector fallbacks when neither the game's atlas nor fallbackIcons supplies them, including check, lock, close and all three chevrons. Game-supplied icons retain precedence.

Moves frames: default-style games with no font use the licensed Instrument Sans variable outlines in every UI role, ahead of locale fallback faces. The cook ships no atlas and loads the separate face only when needed; games without UI documents carry no default face. A game's own font and other fonts' cook settings remain unchanged.

font-weight and font-stretch now select a role font's wght and wdth axes, including fonts supplied through UiDesc.font. Real supported bold is not synthesised; explicit @font-face descriptor ranges still constrain selection.

fixed: og dev regenerates UI types and restarts source checks when a .svelte document changes, instead of watching the obsolete .ogt document extension.

fixed.summary: A disabled control's input-action handler (`ondetails`, `onconfirm`, …) no longer fires: pressing X over a disabled Track button sent `track` although a tap sent nothing. A `<fieldset disabled>`'s controls are silent too.

Moves frames: disabled text inputs and textareas now expose their disabled frame and text state, reject editing and leave the focus order. Adds field-disabled-ink, field-disabled-shadow and checkbox-disabled-shadow style hooks, including radio rings.

The built-in ProgressBar is HTML with CSS: its track is the fill's and buffer's containing block, so the fill starts at the track's edge and is exactly its value's share of the track (it was measured against the screen), and the label row and the sheen are built only when shown ({#if}). Its parts are unchanged.
The graph fits its container: it is at most as wide and as tall as the space it is given, so CardRunMap and film-flowchart on a 390-wide phone no longer lay their rooms out past the screen's edge.

The 33 built-in screens are written in HTML with CSS instead of the engine's layout tags (row, column, stack, grid, text, spacer, scroll, panel): their element ids and parts are unchanged, so ::part() and #id rules still reach them, but a rule selecting an engine tag inside a screen (pause column, main-menu stack) no longer matches. film-choices draws no empty quick-time bar on a choice without one, and notifications keep clear of the HUD insets on a phone.

blur() is CSS's standard deviation (it was taken as the layer blur's radius, half as soft), grayscale(), saturate(), brightness() and hue-rotate() use Filter Effects' matrices over sRGB-encoded colour (they mixed in linear light), and blur() with a colour function draws both (the colour function replaced the blur). backdrop-filter's saturate() and brightness() are the same matrices. Reference frames css-paint-1280 and css-paint-390 moved.
Loading an unchanged document again reuses its definition instead of reparsing it; changed cooked documents still reload.

fixed: UI resource bindings reuse their last reflected value until the resource is written, while following removal, reinsertion, restores and TimeScale changes.

fixed.summary: A document is read once, against the style `og.ui.configure` selected. Before, loading a document under a style parsed its text three times, and every `og.ui.configure` call (a scheme or text-scale change included) parsed every loaded document again. Select the style before loading documents; when a later `og.ui.configure` changes the style, the loaded documents are read again, once each.

fixed: Editing a style pack no longer recooks unrelated UI documents; document stamps still track their own sources, imported stylesheets and referenced files.

fixed.summary: A masked or material layer of an element drawn through a view box composited through its unfitted shape; it now uses the fitted geometry, and a gradient mask in view-box units is fitted as a fill gradient is.
An element inside an anchor's world layer holds no slot of its own; a binding change writes the anchor again in its place.

fixed.member: og-ui: retained elements inside an <anchor> or <panel world>
fixed.summary: A document's world layer is keyed by the element's own path, so the nodes in it carry the keys and paths the retained document gives them: presses and focus reach them, a patch writes the changed element in place (it wrote the whole anchor before), and an anchor or panel may be its document's root. Probe paths inside an anchor now include its document's path.
What a toned dot holds (a check, a cross, a number) now takes the readable contrast of the dot's fill instead of the tone itself, which had made it invisible on the fill.

Gives unselected recipe and stock options a quiet default row surface while preserving the shared hover, pressed, selected and disabled treatments. Documents the loot review fixture's all-or-nothing Take all policy and how games can instead offer partial collection.
Retained frames remove expired particle bursts instead of replaying their last cached drawing. Frame-owned effects invalidate their drawing once more when they disappear.

CSS font-family retains its ordered named-family list through inheritance and rich spans. Missing glyphs use the next matching named face before generic and locale fallbacks, without replacing primary-font glyphs.
UI check and preview report overflow from the measured frame instead of replaying stale tick-0 layout warnings. Other runtime diagnostics remain visible.

AbilitySlot and AbilityBar slots are dark wells in a brass rim, as the rpg action bar's skills are. They wore the painted button plate, whose padding squeezed the well into a black column down the slot's middle with the cost and charges badges stacked over the icon; the icon now reads across the whole slot and each badge sits on its own small plate in a faint brass rim.

A painted button draws its plate alone. The pack set none of the default style's button shadow hooks, so the default's raised shadow, the primary's glow and the danger variant's inset ring drew the button's rectangle around the plate's pointed ends: a rose rectangle round a danger button (Confirm's Quit), a dark one behind a primary (GameOver's Revive). The pack now sets --button-base-shadow, -hover-shadow, -base-pressed-shadow, -primary-shadow, -danger-shadow, -selected-shadow and -disabled-shadow to none.

A button that a component names as a part wears the component's dress and no longer the core button's plate. controls.css keeps the core controls in a layer of their own (fantasy-controls) under the pack's other files, so a rule that names a component part wins whatever its file's place in the lexical order or the specificity of the core button's state rules. Before, the arena roster's cells and the card collection's cells (their files sort before controls.css) showed the plate's brass ends behind them and cut their names short, and button.secondary::part(base) repainted the rim of every named button (the racing garage's tiles, the loadout's slots) as the plate's border image in every state; that rule is removed. The roster's cells and the garage's tiles also keep the component's padding, not the core button's 24 px a side.

A focused button draws a focus ring only. The focus part wears the button's base rules, so a focused button that a component names as a part drew the core plate over its content; the ring's rules now stand outside the controls' layer and clear the plate.

A primary button written as variant="primary" wears the primary's ink (--on-primary) at rest. The rule named only the class, which a variant does not set on the host, so its label took the default button's gold, under 4.5:1 on the crimson plate.

MinimapView's glass is a dark well in a brass rim instead of the painted button plate, whose gold ends drew bands across the top and bottom of the map; the north mark stands on a small lamp-black plate in the label face, so it reads over any map.

The crosshair draws under a style pack. Its line width was a variable named --line, which is also the palette's rule colour: a pack's :root sets that on the component's root, above the component's own layer, so in any pack the arms, the dot, the ring and the hit ticks had no size. The variable is now --weight; a game that set --line on a Crosshair to change its line sets --weight.
components.css dresses the speech bubble's tail (SpeechBubble.tail) in the frame's lamp-black foot with a brass rim, so the bubble points at its speaker again.

A text field without `bind:value` keeps what the player types, as an HTML input does. Before, it dropped the text every frame, so the field stayed empty and `:invalid`, `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` never saw the typed value. The typed value is carried by a UI snapshot.

A figure role part inside a button (IdlePurchases' cost in Buy) takes the button's ink from the first frame, with no pack and with a pack set before the document mounts, as it already did after a restyle. `--figure-ink: currentColor` on a button is now one of og's user-agent declarations (beside HTML's `button { text-align: center }`), so every document has it, whether or not a pack is loaded, and a style's own rule for a button still wins over it. Before, a game that set its pack before mounting, and the default style, drew the cost in the frame's figure ink on the primary plate (1.12:1 by default, 2.04:1 under scifi).

A figure role part inside a button (a cost inside Buy: `part="IdlePurchases.cost IdlePurchases.figure"`) takes the button's ink instead of `--figure-ink`, as its plate's other content does: the default style sets `--figure-ink: currentColor` on `button`, so a pack's figure ink stays off its plates. Before, a cost on a primary plate wore the figure ink (2.04:1 under scifi).
`color: currentcolor` (directly or through `var()`) inherits, as CSS Color 4 says: the element takes its parent's colour, and a button's content its ink. Before, it took the style's ink.

A style's rules for a document element that names a part (`[part$=".figure"]`) read the custom properties the element inherits from its document (`button { --figure-ink: … }`), as `var()` reads an element's computed values. Before, they read only the root's.

A dressing whose only change is `fill none` now clears the control's own fill: a pack's `Button::base.quiet:disabled { -og-fill: none }` keeps a disabled quiet button clear. Before, a dressing that drew nothing was skipped and the control's fill stayed.

A film no longer fails as a malformed script when its steps land at sums such as 0.1 + 0.2 (each timed step is written to four decimals) or when a capture in `--at` comes before a later step (the script is put in time order).

fixed.member: UI: backdrop-filter inside a world panel, a ground or a 3D plane
fixed.summary: A backdrop drawn inside a world panel's, a <ground>'s or a 3D plane's layer now reads what that layer has drawn so far, planned on the layer's own pixels, instead of drawing nothing.

fixed.member: UI: wide blurs and turned morphology are exact
fixed.summary: A blur wider than about 42 device px now reads every texel (split into passes that compose to the exact Gaussian) instead of stepping between texels; a morphology under a rotation takes every texel its segment crosses instead of the nearest one each device px.

A renderer no longer compiles the UI filter pipeline (every SVG and CSS filter primitive in one shader) when it is made: the pipeline compiles the first time a UI layer draws with a filter, as the UI's other pipelines do. With an empty Metal shader cache on an Apple M4 Pro, a scene's setup and first frame take 1.27 s instead of 1.71–1.83 s (the terrain scene), 0.89 s instead of 1.28–1.31 s (glTF) and 0.93–0.96 s instead of 1.33–1.37 s (materials). The picture is unchanged; a game whose first frame draws a filtered UI layer waits for it then instead.

fixed.member: UI: SVG filters run in the element's own space
fixed.summary: A blur, morphology, lighting, subregion, tile, image and turbulence of a turned, skewed or scaled element now run along the element's axes instead of the screen's.

Scroll containers whose content fits no longer swallow taps or drag starts intended for a parent control. Overflowing containers still drag-scroll; wheel routing and overscroll boundaries are unchanged.

A `position: fixed` element keeps its static position on an axis with no inset (CSS 2.1 §10.3.7 and §10.6.4): with `bottom: 10px` alone it stays across where its parent's flow would have put it (centred in a flex column with `align-items: center`, at the end of a row with `justify-content: flex-end`, under the sibling before it in a block). It stood at the screen's left edge (or its top, with no vertical inset). A fixed element written with one inset that relied on the edge now needs the other inset (`left: 0`).

Backpack, ItemCard and RpgCharacter's fixtures name built-in glyphs (sword, apple, potion) instead of the rpg sheet's painted art ids, so their review states draw an icon in a project with no icon atlas.

A control's focus ring now follows the control's corners and their shape, as a CSS outline follows its box: a button a pack bevels with `--button-corner-shape` rings bevelled instead of round. `--button-focus-radius` and `--button-focus-corner-shape` give the ring its own corners. Unset, the default style draws the same ring.
A button with aria-disabled no longer sends its click, tap, double tap or long press; it stays focusable, as documented.

A submit button no longer sends the form's onsubmit action while one of its text fields is :invalid; the first invalid field takes the focus instead, as HTML's constraint validation does. novalidate on the form or formnovalidate on the button skips the check; disabled and read-only fields are not validated.

GameOver centres through the cover primitive, so a panel taller than the screen starts at the safe top and its title is never cut; on a phone on its side the line, the score and the stats sit beside the offer or the actions and the whole screen shows without scrolling.

CSS font-family preserves generic families at their authored positions instead of discarding all named families after the first generic. Quoted generic names remain named families, including in inherited text, spans and widget parts. An unrendered generic no longer adds synthetic bold to a later real heavy face.

fixed.member: Arena, idle, rhythm and strategy components
fixed.summary: The 23 genre components now take their surfaces, text hierarchy, meter fills, scroll fades and cooldown shades from shared role tokens, and their shapes and reveal motion from shared layout and motion primitives. Style packs can dress these parts consistently without component-specific look rules. Existing states, actions and part names remain available.

A `-og-material: glass …` surface now takes any `backdrop-filter` chain. Blurs followed by colour functions still fold into the glass backdrop. Any other chain (a colour function before a blur, colour functions that need clamping between them, `drop-shadow()` or `url()`) runs as the staged backdrop filter in order, and the glass draws over its result without filtering again. Such a chain used to be refused with a warning and drew no filter.

Global pack selectors match ancestors across component boundaries and restyle retained descendants when those ancestors change. Document styles remain component-scoped; minimap frame masks now receive their wrapper-qualified pack rules.

fixed.member: UI: gradients that leave the output's gamut
fixed.summary: Moves frames where a gradient's mix leaves the gamut (a hue turned `in oklch`, a wide stop): each pixel is gamut mapped into the output's gamut by OKLCh chroma reduction (CSS Color 4 §13.2), keeping its lightness and hue, instead of clipped per channel, which turned both and left a crease along the ramp. On a Display P3 output the mix keeps P3's range; on sRGB it stays inside sRGB. Gradients inside the gamut draw as before.

Moves frames: a gradient mixed in another space (`linear-gradient(to right in hsl longer hue, red, red)`, `in oklch`, `in lch`) follows that mix to within an eighth of a just-noticeable difference, so a long hue sweep or a P3/oklch ramp no longer shows bands where its 8 stops were joined.

Moves frames slightly: every gradient's dither is triangular noise of one code value of the output either way (it was half a code value, uniform), so a dark or shallow ramp has an even grain instead of clean stripes where it lands on a code. It follows the output's bit depth.

A masonry grid now breaks ties between lanes within 1em of the shortest by the auto-placement cursor, as grid-lanes does, instead of always taking the strictly shortest lane; items can move to an earlier lane.
The default style's grid primitive shrinks its tile (--layout-tile) to a container narrower than one instead of overflowing it.

Moves frames: a ground's texts and badges draw over every ground's other drawing. Grounds were composited in tree order in one band, so a ring or line laid after a ground covered its label (on the world sheet, PlacementGhost's range ring and the path's dashes crossed PathLine's "12 m · 2 AP").

A child of a ground or a world panel placed by percent insets or by anchor positioning (an overlay's data-anchor=center, top: 50%) vanished with everything in it: once placed, it was laid out again cut to the screen, while its layer lies off it. It is now cut as its layer is, so a placement ghost's centred footprint, a panel's centred badge and the like draw.

A halo a document drawn over the scene sets on its root (`text-shadow: var(--tag-halo)`, inherited) now stops at a surface with a fill of its own: a `<button>`, a `<badge>` and a frame (except a `.bare` one), band, row, cell, badge, well or tab part reset `text-shadow` in the default style, so text on a HUD's panels and buttons is no longer outlined. A rule a document writes for the element still wins.
A hidden backface and the children composited into its layer no longer intercept the pointer. Front-facing planes and visible backfaces remain interactive.

fixed.member: UI documents: aria-label on fields and other controls
fixed.summary: The name prop (aria-label) now names every element in the accessibility tree; fields ignored it.

BossBar wears the HUD bar (--bar-*): a leaning danger bar in a dark well, a ghost that holds and drains after a hit, a gate cut into the bar at each phase boundary, the info tone while invulnerable and a pulsing danger rim under a quarter. It stands over the scene on the halo instead of a plate, its phases are a line of chips under the bar, and its loading state shows a spinner.
ProgressBar wears the HUD bar (--bar-*): a thin leaning bar in a dark well with a lit fill, its words in the scene's opaque ink and its figure bold and tabular; the track grows with the text scale.

The shield lies along the top of the bar it guards and draws nothing when broken (an empty shield drew a dark strip above the bar), and the track grows with the text scale, so a value inside it is not cut at 150 % text.
A press on the built-in hud-editor screen's dock reaches the dock's buttons again: HUD edit mode no longer takes it for a customisable element under the dock.

Use the shared Spinner alongside loading labels in resource pips and pickup feeds, with loading parts for style packs. Connecting performance fixtures show unavailable samples rather than invented zero readings; measured zero remains distinct and is covered separately.

AbilityBar, AbilitySlot, Cooldown and StatusGrid cells stand over the scene as sockets in plates instead of flat tiles; a cost the player cannot pay washes its well from the foot instead of filling it; StatBar's shield is a tab of its plate, and its dark gloss band (the part StatBar.sheen) is gone, the fill's own gloss replacing it; RadialMenu's disc takes the HUD ground.

fixed.member: UI built-ins: HUD, world, shooter, racing
fixed.summary: Dress HUD instruments, world labels and maps, shooter panels and racing readouts through shared role tokens, state tones and motion. Layout primitives place their children and keep the component sheet's round timer clear of the HP value and compass clear of the resource bars. Buff stacks and timers have their own rows below their icons. Custom orb glass, premium and round action controls, keylined crosshairs, split-ink casts, celebrations and keyed exit motion remain unchanged pending shared mechanisms.

An icon that declares no color now takes its parent's, as an SVG icon in a page draws in currentColor: a step's check in its success tone, an icon in a danger label in danger. An icon that declares its own colour keeps it, and og-icon::part(image) still restyles it.

The chosen buy amount (×1, ×10, ×100, Max) shows as selected. Each amount button was also named the figure role (`IdlePurchases.amount IdlePurchases.figure`), and a control named for a role wears that role alone, so it lost the button's selected look. It is now `IdlePurchases.amount` only, with the figure font set on it; `::part(IdlePurchases.figure)` no longer reaches the amount buttons.

fixed: An idle UI screen no longer rebuilds or repaints anything each tick. A focused or hovered control is written again when its focus or hover changes, not every tick while it lasts (a tooltip's or an interest delay counts, a text field's caret blinks, a pressed control follows the pointer). A closed or open popover, a scroll container with scroll markers or buttons and a `::first-line` text are built again only when what they show changes. Inline SVG and other element draws, rich text without moving spans and a scroller's bars keep last tick's paint while they are unchanged, and a styled part's draw is kept while its style, size and ground are.

fixed.summary:
A change to an inherited value (a custom property, a text property) reaches what reads it through elements that only hand it down: toggling a class that sets `--x` on a container restyles a `

` under a plain `

` inside it. Before, the `

` kept the value its first build read.
A wrapped inline link is hit on its words' fragment on each line (their content area), no longer on the rectangle around all its lines, which took presses on the words before and after it.
Miter joints no longer leave a half-covered seam on the bisector (visible at every joint of a flattened curve), and a closed line that ends at its start no longer draws a miter spike there.
Gives loading slots and avatars distinct spinner parts, keeps inset unavailable labels inside a consistent slot silhouette, and shows nonempty avatar frame keys with a restylable token ring.

ItemSlot grows with the player's text scale (96px at 100% text), so its key, count and Locked or Unavailable chip keep their room around the icon at 150% text instead of being cut by the slot. A game's `--item-slot-size` is still taken as given; in a slot narrower than its state word, the word ends in an ellipsis inside its chip.

fixed.member: UI CSS justify-self, justify-items in a block
fixed.summary: `justify-self` and `justify-items` now align a block container's block-level children in its inline axis (CSS Box Alignment 3 §6.1.1); an `auto` width aligned anything but `normal` or `stretch` shrinks to `fit-content`. They used to apply only in grids, so such a child stayed at the start.

A badge or <kbd> cap reads its ground through its ancestors' CSS background layers (a gradient face, a background colour set with layers) as well as their fills, so its ink holds 4.5:1 there: HeroButton's E cap on the default style's light primary face read 1.16:1 dark and 1.23:1 light, now 4.74:1 and 4.64:1.

Moves frames: a keycap inside a button keeps the ink it picks to read on its own cap; the button's content ink no longer restamps it. On a primary button the cap's glyph wore the button's on-primary ink on the cap (scifi's draft Confirm X and rhythm results Next Esc, 2.51:1 dark and 1.94:1 light; now 4.62 and 4.60).
A keyframes name is its highest cascade layer's definition (CSS Cascade 5), not the last read: a pack's og-pack keyframes win over the default style's og-default ones whichever is read first.

SVG path data, arcs, flattening, dashes and cubic-to-quadratic conversion are kurbo's in documents' inline <svg>, clip-path: path(), -og-text-path, cooked vectors and icons, one path model instead of three hand-written parsers. A dash list's dash that runs across a closed shape's start is one dash, not two cut at the seam; a gradient in objectBoundingBox units spans the shape's curves, not their control points; and path data errors name what is wrong in one wording everywhere. A zero-length dash due exactly at an open path's end draws no dot.

`lang` and `dir` are HTML global attributes, so `:lang()` and `:dir()` read them on every element (`
`, `

`). Before, any element except a field refused them ("lang does not apply to box"). A field's `lang` still picks its on-screen keyboard.

fixed: Resizing single-level UI layers reuse render targets in 64-pixel buckets instead of allocating a texture for each pixel-size change. Composites and SVG filters read only the used rectangle, preserving the layer's pixel grid and edge sampling. Mipmapped Blur and DropShadow targets keep exact sizes because padding would change their downsampled pixels.

fixed.summary: UI documents lay out as a browser lays out the same CSS: CSS Flexbox, Grid and block flow (margin collapsing, floats, clearance) now run on Taffy 0.15.1 in place of the engine's own approximation, on both hosts. Where the two differed, the CSS answer now holds. Flex items shrink in proportion to their flex basis. A border-box size is never smaller than its padding and border. An aspect ratio carries a size the parent decides (a stretched or flexed side) to the other axis. A wrapping column's lines stretch under align-content: normal. A box with size containment is sized as if empty, then by contain-intrinsic-size. An absolutely positioned box centred by its insets keeps its own width instead of its column's. align-items: end keeps the writing mode's end under wrap-reverse. A box in another writing mode starts a formatting context of its own, so its floats stay inside it. Text, line boxes beside floats, shape-outside, tables, multi-column, writing modes and anchored boxes keep og-ui's layout, now fed by the CSS core.

A right-to-left box (`dir="rtl"`, `direction: rtl`) lays its flex lines, grid columns, block flow and floats out from the right as CSS `direction` does, instead of being laid out left to right and mirrored afterwards. Its floats, `clear` and `shape-outside` contours keep the sides they name.

align-content on a block container shifts its content as one in the block axis (CSS Box Alignment 3 §5.1.1): `align-content: end` on a tall block sits its children at its bottom, and any value but `normal` starts a formatting context of its own. A flow-root, a multi-column box or a box in another writing mode now starts a context of its own the way Taffy's block layout does, and keeps its baseline: a flow-root in a baseline-aligned row aligns by its first line instead of its bottom edge.

`line-clamp: N` now keeps a text's first N lines and sizes its box to them without `text-overflow: ellipsis` as well (CSS Overflow 4 §4.1: `max-lines` with `block-ellipsis: auto`). It used to cut nothing unless the ellipsis was set, so the box stayed as tall as all its lines.
The web mirror announces what og-ui's live regions say instead of only the status and alert nodes that appear, so an in-place status change is heard and the page and the native tree agree.

The menu's column is centred while it fits and scrolls when it is taller than the screen (justify-content: safe center; overflow-y: auto); on a short screen its last buttons were cut off at the bottom edge with no way to reach them.

Colours inside mask and mask-image are classified as coverage data rather than visible look literals. Structural gradient masks may use colour stops directly; lengths, durations and asset URLs still require tokens, as do visible colours in backgrounds and other paint declarations.
Document standard media conditions and remove the obsolete named-breakpoint example. Keep container-query runtime support explicitly pending.

Root tokens, theme reads and widget-part styles now survive viewport resizes while their media-query answers stay unchanged. Breakpoint and density changes, inline media conditions, conditional CSS functions and viewport-unit lengths still refresh their dependent styles. Document roots inherit the computed theme tokens without re-inlining them.

A <video> or <audio> in a mounted document reads its player every frame: bind:currentTime, bind:paused and bind:ended follow the media while nothing else changes. They were read only on a frame some other value rebuilt the element, so a clip's end reached the game late or never.
The back row's and a submenu row's chevrons are the engine's chevronLeft and chevronRight icons, line glyphs like the menu's other icons, instead of a heavier inline mark.
Menu's entry labels start at the row's start, after the icon or check, instead of centring between it and the shortcut as a button's text does.
A UI text whose face lacks every one of its glyphs (so it measured no width) reached the renderer and is counted; it was dropped before drawing and the count stayed 0.

Elements that animate their transform or opacity cost less per tick. Their draws no longer copy the theme, the passes over moved nodes take them in drawing order without a heap, and the draw levels of moved commands are found again without allocating. A dense menu with 40 cards springing in scale and opacity spends 0.39 ms a tick instead of 0.48 ms on Windows.

A named font's mixed-script fallback chain skips unrendered generic-role placeholders, so locale font glyphs beside Latin digits are emitted instead of silently disappearing. Measurement-only fonts retain their fallback metrics.
A part named on a built-in control (part="slot" on a button) adds to the control's own part instead of replacing it: `button::part(base)` rules still dress the button.

Authored native-frame backgrounds replace the default material's matching colour and image layers, including transparent and background-image:none. Colour-only overrides retain the material's images; authored SVG and custom drawing content are preserved.

NodeGraph fits its `view` in its well as an SVG viewBox does under `xMidYMid meet`: the graph scales to the most that holds it (with a node's width to spare at each edge) and stands in the middle, so CardRunMap's map spans its panel instead of a small patch of it. Nodes keep their size. A caption stands centred under its node on a chip of the well, so a path runs under it, not through it; a diamond's caption turns back about the node's middle instead of standing beside it; a locked node dims its icon and mutes its caption instead of thinning the whole node.

Moves frames: nowrap text styled as rich paragraphs, including trimmed headings, now ellipsizes at its final flex-item width. Overflow hidden and clip also cut a text leaf's own line instead of only its children.

A number input's spin buttons draw as control cells: the default style gives input[type=number]::part(button) the button plate, border, hover and press, where they drew as bare chevrons beside 1 px divider bars, and they sit inside the field's border, flush with its end. A style pack restyles them through that part.

A document's number input steps by the decimals written: with step="0.1" and data-large-step="0.3" a shift-press writes "0.3", not "0.30000000447034836". A number written in a document's markup keeps its decimal value where the engine reads it at full precision (a number input's min, max, step and large step).

A selector reads an element's own facts the same way whether it is lowered when the document is parsed or matched on the mounted tree. An HTML type selector matches caselessly everywhere (`DIV#x` selects `<div id="x">`; before, it did only in a structural selector), and `:state(name)` is on for `state:name` with any true value but the word "false" (`state:on=""` is off, as a bound empty string already was; before, a literal empty value turned it on).

`details[open]` and `dialog[open]` follow the element's open state as HTML reflects it, however it changed: the player toggling it, a `bind:open` store, or the player closing one written `open`. Before, `[open]` read only the written attribute, so a bound or toggled element never matched and a closed literal one still did. An unbound element's toggled state is now carried by a UI snapshot.

fixed.member: CSS order: painting and hit testing
fixed.summary: Flex and grid items now paint and are hit in order-modified document order (CSS Flexbox 1 §5.4, CSS Grid 2 §9): an item that `order` moves ahead paints under the siblings it now precedes, and where items overlap the one drawn on top takes the pointer. Before, they painted and were hit in document order whatever their `order`. Tab and Shift+Tab still follow the document (or the container's `reading-flow`), and `reading-flow: source-order` now ranks by the document rather than by `order`.
An outer box-shadow is drawn outside its border box only, as CSS specifies: a transparent or translucent box no longer shows its own shadow through itself.

A box with `overflow: hidden`, `auto` or `scroll` (on either axis), or with `contain: layout` or `paint`, now starts a block formatting context of its own (CSS Overflow 3 §3, CSS Display 3 §2.3): its first child's top margin stays inside it instead of collapsing through and moving the box down. `overflow: clip` still lets margins collapse. Layouts that relied on the margin escaping an `overflow: hidden` box move.
`overflow: overlay` (and on `overflow-x` and `overflow-y`) now cooks as the legacy alias of `auto` (CSS Overflow 3 §3.1) instead of failing as not an overflow.

fixed: A frame whose UI is the same as the last one (between two ticks, or on an idle screen) no longer rebuilds, sorts and uploads the UI overlay: the renderer keeps the overlay it built and its tables on the device while the UI frame, its anchored elements' shifts, the target size and the fonts and textures it reads are unchanged. A UI with mass elements, or an overlay that also carries screen text, is built every frame as before.

fixed.member: UI: Display P3 colours in documents
fixed.summary: On a Display P3 output a document's colours outside sRGB (`background: color(display-p3 1 0 0)`, a wide `oklch()`, in a stylesheet or a `style` attribute) now keep their gamut through the UI's style, so they draw in P3. They were gamut mapped into sRGB when the document built, so only gradients and colours a host drew directly kept their range. On an sRGB output nothing changes.

Loading a UI document no longer reads the whole style sheet again. A style pack's CSS over the default style (or the default style's role rules, without a pack) is tokenized, its selectors parsed and its rule bodies lowered once, and every document shares the result; only matching the document's own elements is left. A small document's parse takes 0.46 ms instead of 2.9 ms under the default style and 8.6 ms instead of 35.6 ms under the fantasy pack (release build, Linux).

The hero button tells the engine its variant: primary for its default and premium tones, secondary and danger for theirs. A style pack can now tell a secondary hero button from the default one in `button.secondary::part(HeroButton\.base)` and `button.primary::part(HeroButton\.base)`; before, every hero button was a variant-less (secondary) button, so the default tone matched `.secondary` too.

A node graph's hex node is cut by its corners (`corner-shape: bevel` on a 25% / 50% radius) instead of a `clip-path`, so it no longer clips its own caption below it (the card run map's Event and Treasure), and its rim follows the hexagon. The graph's well sizes as a box does, across and down its container (no less than a graph's height), instead of a fixed 420 × 288, so it no longer overflows a phone.

A `<kbd>` keycap draws its text in the font-family its element computes, as a browser draws a `<kbd>`. Under a style pack that brings its faces through `@font-face`, keycaps inside buttons (action hints, the hero button's key, a loadout's Back and Equip) drew as empty blocks.

`<kbd data-action>` naming an action the game defined with `og.input.defineAction`, and no UI action, shows that action's binding on the device used last. It drew the raw action name (`interact` on an InteractionPrompt).
A `<kbd data-og-rebind bind:value>` shows the key it holds (`Space`, then the key the player captured), not the action's default glyph or name.

A style pack's or a document's `:root[data-scheme=light]` rules now apply under the light scheme (`og.ui.configure(world, { scheme: "light" })`). Before, every document's root matched the pack's `:root` block but never its `data-scheme` blocks, so a pack's light palette could not be reached while the engine's own inks turned light.
A modal `<dialog>` in the top layer is `dialog::part(panel)` (with `:open`) as a dialog opened in place is, so a style pack's panel rule dresses it (the confirm screen drew a flat surface).
`font-family` on a part whose element is its own text (`badge::part(base)`, a keycap) reaches that text, as the part's colour and size already did.

A style that brings its faces only through `@font-face` backs the body, display, mono and rounded roles with the families its `--font-body`, `--font-display`, `--font-mono` and `--font-rounded` name, wherever `UiDesc` gives a role no font. Text a widget draws in a role (a radio's, checkbox's or switch's label, a select's value, a range's bubble, a badge, a tab, damage numbers) drew nothing under such a style.

A CSS `filter` function list on an inline SVG element (`drop-shadow()`, `blur()`…, as in `[part="DamageDirection.arc"] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px …) }`) now draws, as it does on a CSS box. Before, an SVG shape read only the `filter="url(#id)"` attribute and dropped the rule's value without a warning. A rule's `filter` overrides the attribute.

A hero button's secondary tone wears the core button's glass instead of the primary's lit face, a radial menu's wedges are a control's glass, lit when chosen, and no longer carry the core button plate, and under the light scheme, which now applies, the character sheet's figure is not faded. The pack cuts its frames, plates and cells through the role corner-shape tokens and names the slider bubble's and the checkbox tick's inks, where rules stood in for them; its README drops the engine gaps now fixed, the light scheme among them.

The content of a primary button written as variant="primary" wears the primary's ink (--on-primary). The rule named only the class, which a variant does not set on the host, so an icon inside the button took the default button's cyan on the lit cyan plate.

Inks the component, screen and world review sheets showed too close to their ground now read: a data grid's headings on its lit band take the full ink; the rare, epic and mythic colours are lighter, so an item's title or loot name in them reads; --health and the vitals bar's mana are deeper, so the white figures on the health orb and the vitals bars read, and the vitals bars light only their tip; a loot label is a tag on the scene plate with its rarity's rim instead of the core button's lit face; a nameplate's cast bar is a deep amber, so the spell's name reads on it; a status effect's time sits on the scene plate, so it reads over a bright sky; and the scene plate and the role wells are more opaque (0.95), so text on them reads over a bright scene.

An element whose transform or opacity animates no longer has its whole subtree painted again each tick: each element's draw commands are kept apart from where the frame places them (its map, opacity and clip) and placed again. A dense menu with 40 cards springing in scale and opacity spends 0.55 ms a tick instead of 1.05 ms on Windows. A faded element's styled text now fades its shadows, outline and gradient fill with it.

Shadowed interfaces use fewer painter levels without changing their look: font-to-shape crossings reuse the renderer's existing order, and ordinary round-rectangle shadows use conservative shader-derived Y bounds. Real overlaps retain their ordering, including after retained updates and raster-scale changes.

Built-in panels, shops, progression, social and card documents now take their surfaces, typography, state colours and motion from shared role parts and tokens, and their layout from shared primitives. Existing component parts, inputs and intents remain available. Style packs can retune these families together; overlapping hand cards keep an opaque role fill, and loading rows use shared skeleton shimmer.

fixed.member: Word moves and double presses in text (text fields, areas, user-select text)
fixed.summary: Words come from ICU's segmenter with its dictionaries: Ctrl or Alt with the arrows (Option on a Mac), word deletes and a double press stop at the words of Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Chinese and Japanese, which are written without spaces, where they stepped a cluster or a character at a time.

The caret, the selection and what Backspace and Delete remove come from Parley's editor over the text as it is laid out: ← and → step a grapheme cluster on screen, through a right-to-left run from the side they enter it; ↑ and ↓ keep the caret's column; a press lands on the cluster drawn under it in every face. Backspace removes one character of a cluster (an accent, a Thai tone mark, an Indic vowel sign) as platform text fields do, and a whole emoji or line break; Delete removes the cluster after the caret.

Moves frames: its lines break as labels do (UAX #14), so Thai breaks between words and Chinese and Japanese between characters, where an area broke only at spaces (or mid-word when a word was wider than the line).

Parsing a UI document matches each rule against its elements by node index rather than by searching the element list, and reads each rule's selector once rather than once per element. The 148 built-in documents parse in 370 ms rather than 493 ms without a style pack, and in 1056 ms rather than 1282 ms under fantasy (release, x86-64).

A part whose border colour a transition covers, set through a `border` shorthand (`border: 2px solid var(--rim)`) while a competing rule writes `border-color`, no longer flashes the text colour for the length of the transition after the two rules stop competing: the transition now reads the colour the shorthand gives, so it moves between the two rim colours instead of to `currentColor`. Affected a ghost button, a select trigger after hover, and a hovered checked checkbox under a pack or game that mixed the two forms.

fixed.member: UI: the cost of resolving a control's parts
fixed.summary: A part of a control (a field's caret, a slider's thumb, a date input's segments) resolved the `:root` cascade of the installed part CSS again on every read, several times a part each frame. The UI now keeps that cascade for the installed style and the media context it matched under, and computes it again when the part CSS, the style pack, the theme tokens or the media context change. A `transition` or `animation` shorthand written with `var()` is expanded once for each substituted text, not once for each of its longhands on every read. No cascade result changes: every kept value equalled a fresh one across the og-ui and og-runtime suites.

A ::part run (and ::before/::after content) takes the first family in its font-family list that a loaded document's @font-face declares, then the generic family, as an element does; it no longer takes the first named family whether or not any face declares it.

A control's parts weigh the style's rules for the control over what the control only inherits from its document, as CSS weighs a rule for an element over an inherited value: a primary button in a frame (or any element whose role sets the ink) draws its text in --on-primary where it drew the frame's ink on the primary plate, in a document with a style: binding. What a document declares on the control itself (.buy { color: … }) still wins over the style.

An element named a part keeps the flex-wrap: wrap-reverse, row-gap, column-gap, align-content, justify-items, column-count, contain, resize and safe alignment its document declares. The part's values cleared whichever of them they did not set, so a wrap-reverse part stacked its lines from the top with no gap between them.

A control's text inside a part now inherits the font family, size, weight, letter spacing, word spacing, text transform and colour the part declares, as CSS inheritance gives them: a tab's label takes `tabs::part(tab)`'s (`--tabs-font`, `--tabs-transform`, `--tabs-tracking`, `--tabs-tab-ink`), a select's value `select::part(trigger)`'s and a date stepper's value its frame's (`--field-font`), and a details summary its label type. Before, only a part whose box was its own text (a button's label, a number field's value) took them. A nested part's own declarations win inside it, and a component document's content keeps its own cascade.

A tick of UI that did not change costs a fraction of what it did, with the same values: an element that sets a custom property no longer copies its style's whole token table (an element's custom properties are the shared table and a small layer of what it sets over it), and a part's style is kept from tick to tick while its part, host, document, theme and transition state are the ones it was resolved from, instead of being cascaded again each time it is drawn. A part whose transition or animation runs is still resolved every tick.

Restyling many controls at once costs less: a control part resolved while building is reused when it is painted under the same theme, and asked again in the same build before its transition state is committed, instead of resolving again each time. When the 40 cards of a dense menu change class in one tick, the end of that tick takes 13 ms instead of 21 on Windows.
