A frame of documents styled by a style pack costs a fraction of what it did, with the same values: a component's part rules are merged with the pack's once per document instead of for every part each frame, a part looks only at the rules that can match it, an element no longer copies its inherited custom properties to carry an unchanged value, and the second frame after a mount no longer restyles every element the first frame styled.

A focused or hovered control built again each tick no longer recomputes its parts' text style: it is kept with the part's style for each type step. An idle leaderboard screen spends 0.28 ms a tick instead of 0.32 ms on Windows, and every library screen about 0.04 ms less.
A running part transition reuses its retained cascade and updates only motion instead of resolving the unchanged cascade again each frame.

Missing artwork uses a quiet token surface and a small square-fit mark instead of stretching a disc across the slot. Core-screen references now use supplied art and populated settings, creator-tools and HUD-editor content, with separate missing-art coverage for every slot kind.

Moves frames: polygon() points now accept calc() mixing percentages and pixel offsets. Each coordinate resolves against its reference box's used axis, preserving fixed-size notches and corners when the box resizes.

Moves frames: positioned descendant text and icons retain their containing block's inherited scroll clip when laid out at their resolved position. Viewport-fixed content still escapes the scroll chain.

<og-icon> with an empty icon name draws no icon and no longer warns that '' is in neither the icon atlas nor the fallback icons. StatBar with shieldMax 0 no longer warns that its shield width is invalid.

A pushed screen is built the way a mounted document is, so it resolves only the elements whose values changed and keeps its elements' state across frames. A dropdown or tooltip a layer opens is ordered just above that layer.

The safe-area insets now clear the host's covered region (Viewport.covered, a published page's Back): it is folded into the one edge whose inset clears it for the least surface, the left inset on a landscape or desktop surface and the top one on a portrait phone, so a HUD document placed at the insets never draws under Back. A change of the covered region re-resolves what reads them.

A popover is a raised panel again (--panel-raised and the panel radius; a hint the tooltip's), as a browser's popover has its own canvas: one without a CSS background no longer draws its text straight over the page. Its CSS overrides that box.
A context menu, opened at a point, draws no ::-og-arrow: its corner sits at the point, as a desktop's and a game's context menus do.
A <menu>'s buttons (its menu items) each span the menu, so a context menu's rows are as wide as each other instead of their labels' widths.

A document <button> places its label by its CSS text-align instead of always centring it. HTML's user-agent rule `button { text-align: center }` keeps it centred by default, so it does not inherit its parent's alignment.
A <menu>'s buttons (its menu items, a context menu's rows) put their labels at the start, as a desktop's menus do.

A document's t() text, its i18n keys and its controls' item keys are pseudo-localised too (accented, 40 % longer, in brackets), not only og.i18n.t's: the pseudo cells run in og-i18n's pseudo-locale, which lengthens every translated text alike, instead of wrapping og.i18n.t in process. og.i18n.t under the pseudo-locale (`og run --locale pseudo`) is lengthened the same way.

A character a fallback face of the font chain draws takes that face's vertical form (vert, vrt2) in a vertical line instead of always turning: vertical_run shapes each stretch of a mixed text with the face that draws it. The cook keeps every face's vertical forms of its characters in its atlas (font stamp 8; fonts re-cook).

fixed.member: UI document ::selection on vertical rich text
fixed.summary: Vertical rich text draws ::selection's text-decoration and text-shadow over the selected stretch, not only its color, and cuts its own glyphs there instead of drawing the selected ones again on top, so a translucent selection color no longer blends with the text's ink.

Moves frames: a range input's keyboard and gamepad focus ring follows its moving knob instead of its full input reach. Focus outlines follow the painted part's dimensions and corners, including CSS-sized knobs.

A ratio box that does not set --layout-ratio is now square (1) instead of 16 / 9, as a portrait, a jacket or an icon's box is. ArenaRoster's portraits are square again. A box meant to be wide sets --layout-ratio: 16 / 9 on itself.

An absolutely positioned text element in centred text (inside a `<button>`, or under `text-align: center`) shrinks to fit its text, as CSS sizes a positioned box, instead of taking its column's width. AbilitySlot's cost and charge badges and AbilityBar's cost no longer span the slot and cover its icon.

A cook counts the built-in style pack and built-in UI documents it bundles among its inputs: after an edit to a pack's CSS (or to a built-in component) the next `og cook`, `og ui preview` or `og ui review` cooks it again. It kept the project's cooked/ while the project's own files were unchanged, so a pack edit did not show until the sheet was copied afresh.

Text sized by the type ramp's tokens (`font: var(--text-sm)`, `font-size: var(--type-sm-size)`) follows `UiDesc.textScale`, as text sized in em and the widgets' own text already did. Under a 150 % text scale a core `StatBar`'s "64 / 100" stayed at its 100 % size.

Typed custom properties compute math before syntax checking and substitution, so a registered percentage calculated from a 0..1 value paints the correct gradient stop instead of resetting to its initial value. Universal properties retain their original tokens.

fixed.member: UI documents: a remote url() image's EXIF orientation on the web
fixed.summary: On the web, image-orientation: none now draws a remote JPEG, PNG or WebP as its file stores it, as natively; before, the browser's decoder had already turned it upright. from-image is unchanged.

fixed.member: og-render: UiClip with a path or polyline geometry
fixed.summary: A UiClip of a Path or Polyline was ignored (its children drew uncut); it now cuts by the path fill's analytic coverage and fill rule (a polyline by its polygon, even-odd), so SVG <clipPath> and <mask> of paths, polygons and turned shapes cut correctly.

A frame that restyles document elements into a state they had before (a card lifted and set down, a row hovered and left) costs about a quarter less: each element keeps the cascades and text styles of its last two states and reuses one whose inputs are unchanged.

Toggling a class on many controls no longer stalls a frame. A control's part styles are kept for each state its element returns to, not only the last one, and the parse of computed transitions and declarations is kept by its text. In a dense menu where 40 cards change class every 12 ticks, the slowest ticks (p95) take 7 ms instead of 30 ms on Windows.

A frame that restyles many document elements at once (a menu switching its phase) costs about 15% less: an element restyled re-walks only the inherited values that changed, or every one when what it declares changes.
A frame that restyles many document elements at once (a class toggled on every card of a shop) costs about 15% less: an element is rebuilt from its kept style without copying it.

On a short landscape phone the result's line and the XP gained share a line and the stats close up, so every stat of a three-stat result shows before the page scrolls at 150 % text (the third was cut by the page's lower edge); the rewards follow under a shorter scroll fade.

An active screen reader receives only the nodes that changed: the native bridge reads the accessibility records the frame logged as changed (written or repainted nodes, their ancestors and next sibling, focus, scroll offsets) instead of rebuilding the whole tree each tick, and the whole tree only when nodes entered or left it. An idle tick reads nothing. The main, banner, contentinfo, complementary and article roles now reach AccessKit.

Finishing a frame no longer walks every node: the drawing order and each node's features (motion, drags, matches, anchors, groups, recognisers, scrollers, scopes, parts) are kept across frames and made again only where the trees changed shape, and each node's map, opacity, inertness, scopes and hits are made again only where they may have changed and below wherever they did. An idle frame's finish no longer grows with the size of the tree.

A frame lays out only the paths to what changed: the nodes written again, the parents of written and removed ones, layers, scroll containers and container-query readers, and their ancestors. A clean subtree is reached only when it gets another size, place or clip. Baseline rows and anchored, screen-placed and resized-box elements are laid out whole every frame, so what the frame moves after layout is never applied twice. Missing glyphs are read only from newly painted commands, and kept text measurements are swept when the cache doubles instead of every frame.

A frame that changes a few commands at the top of its draw list levels, bakes and scales only those, and levels again only the commands they overlapped or now overlap; it compares only the commands not kept in place, instead of baking, levelling and scaling the whole list. Subtrees kept where they stood last frame move their commands out of last frame's list instead of copying them. A changed list shape, a change inside a layer, or a change to an eighth of the list levels the frame afresh as before.

The motion pass visits only the animated elements a frame may change (written, laid out, entered, or still moving last tick: a channel off its target or waiting out a delay, a play, a CSS animation, a layout motion), not every element that declares a transition, state group or animation; a settled element keeps its values unvisited. What it forgets is read from those elements, the elements that left the trees and the widget channels stepped lately, instead of scanning all motion state, so an idle screen of animated elements does no motion work. `LayoutStats.animated` counts the elements visited.

Painting a frame judges only the nodes whose drawing may have changed (written, laid out, moved, restyled, or drawn again on their own every frame: game draws, rich text, exits, match keys, glitches, scroll fades and focus rings) and the subtrees under any that changed; every other subtree keeps last frame's commands without being compared, and a frame that keeps every tree takes last frame's list instead of copying it.
A heading's level (`<h1>`…`<h6>`, `aria-level`) reaches native screen readers through AccessKit.

A scroll of a retained list writes, copies and levels only what it changes. It writes and copies only the rows it brings in, and drops the paint marks of rows it let go (630 to 940 stale marks a tick). The rows it keeps move their commands with the scroll and keep their painter levels, because rows moved exactly still overlap what they overlapped. Only the rows it brings in, rows clipped otherwise at the edge, what lies across the moved rows' edge and what a dropped row overlapped are levelled again. Before, every command was levelled afresh.

A list whose rows in view change no longer repaints every element on the screen: the filler height it keeps for the rows after them was compared as drawing, so on each scroll tick that brought a row in the list and everything under it painted afresh.

Edges snapped to device pixels are also held to a multiple of 1/256 CSS px (less than 1/512 px off the device grid). At ratios such as 1.25, 1.5 and 3 a device pixel is no exact f32. Now a scrolled row's moved commands equal painting it there, and a fling there keeps the bounded scroll. Nothing moves at 1, 2 and 4. At 1.5, edge pixels change by at most 12/255 (widget set RMSE 0.00038).

The accessibility tree, the probe's element list, overlaps, dense and sideways regions and the motion dump are no longer made while a frame is drawn: each is made from the finished frame the first time it is asked for that tick. A retained node that was not written again draws its last commands while its geometry and sampled style are unchanged, so an idle tick lays out and paints nothing.

Document native binding scheduling, stable keyed mount identities, virtualization, lifecycle and row-key actions. Keep TypeScript mount wiring, builder removal, stable render slots, bounded layout and paint, lazy diagnostics and performance after-numbers explicitly pending.

A subtree that only moved since it was painted (a scrolled list's rows: the same size, clip, opacity and style, no transform) copies its last commands moved as far, with their clips where they were, instead of painting again: a scroll paints only the rows it brings in.

A subtree that paints as last frame copies its commands whole, and a frame whose trees and overlays all paint as last frame keeps last frame's draw items without baking or levelling them again. Subtrees below a focus ring's owner, ghosts' parents, world-marked, frozen, glitching and scrolling-with-bars nodes, and parents whose children changed are drawn again. A virtual list's rows with no input on them are kept as they stand when the list scrolls: only the rows the scroll brings in are written. What is on screen is found through a persistent index of the frame's trees instead of a map rebuilt every frame.

fixed.member: og ui check and og ui review contrast
fixed.summary: Contrast is read where the text draws: over the line box of its drawn run, against the composited pixels behind its glyphs, as a WCAG tool reads a rendered page. Right-aligned figures in wide cells and text on stacked translucent panels, gradients, scanlines or border-image plates no longer read about 1:1 when they read 8:1. Text on translucent grounds is measured when the stacked grounds, composited, cover at least half of what is behind it, and inside scroll containers too; a lone faint tint is still over the scene.

fixed.member: og ui check and og ui review contrast
fixed.summary: A lone narrow figure (a "1" in a quantity column, its run under 6 px wide) is read on its own line, as wider text is, instead of across its whole cell: on a scanlined plate it no longer reads about 1.3:1 when it reads 10:1.

Reviews of one sheet in different styles (`--style fantasy` and `--style scifi`) run at once from one checkout: each style list stages its own copy of the sheet under .og/review instead of removing the other run's copy while it renders.

A rich paragraph's line boxes are Parley's (CSS 2 §10.8): every line holds the paragraph's strut, its own text's line height and font size, so a line of smaller spans keeps the paragraph's line height; `vertical-align` on a span or inline icon is placed by the same line box, and lines beside floats break at each line's room in one pass over the shaped paragraph. A line used to take only its tallest span's height, the strut counting only when a span had a `vertical-align`.

On a mounted document, an element hidden by a store (`hidden={$closed}`, `display: none` from a class) is shown again when the store changes back; before, it stayed gone. A hidden element that was built keeps its subtree, as the web keeps a hidden element's DOM, so hiding and showing it change one element. A Rive frame plays on without rebuilding its element every frame: an idle frame builds nothing.
The window edge mask is now data-fade-ends (x or y); as data-edge it collided with a sheet's dock edge and was refused.

A style pack's `:root` custom properties are declared once, at the root, and every document inherits their values, as a component's root inherits in a browser instead of matching the page's `:root` again. A token an ancestor sets (`
`) now reaches inside the component; before, the component's root declared the pack's value again over it. A pack's other `:root` declarations (`font-family`, `color`) still apply to every document's root. Parsing a document under a pack no longer copies the pack's several hundred tokens onto it: the 148 built-in documents parse in 494 ms under fantasy, from 1056 ms (release, x86-64).

A `corner-shape: round` beside one `border-radius` (the default style's role rules since the `--*-corner-shape` tokens) is the plain corner again. It had made every role box a CSS-corner box, which left a dressed table row's fill undrawn: the default style's selected or current row (a scoreboard's own player) showed no highlight.

A declared action's handler inside an `{#each}` row (`ondetails={equip}` on each row) takes the action only while the focus is within that row, so it acts for the focused row with its row key; before, every row's handler fired at once. A handler outside the rows still takes the action wherever the focus is, and an exclusive `<details name>` group still closes its other members.

NodeGraph stands its graph in the middle of its well, as an SVG viewBox's xMidYMid does, and zooms about that middle. Since the well stretches over its container, the graph sat in its top-left corner (CardRunMap's map in a corner of an empty panel).

A table's rows and row groups are in the UI tree's orders, so what reads them (their CSS decor, a part's dressing) reaches them. A table row given a corner shape other than round (`--row-corner-shape: bevel`, `scoop`, `notch`, `squircle`, `square`) drew no fill at all, so the arena scoreboard lost the local player's highlight.

fixed: The RPG review sheet supplies localized Quest and Camp labels for the shared Compass in all four review locales.

fixed.summary: Crosshair's arms and hit mark and AmmoCounter's magazine fill transition with the defined motion tokens (--motion-ui-duration and --motion-ui-easing, the spring pair for the mark's scale); they named --motion-ui and --motion-emphasis, which no style defines, so they did not animate and warned every frame.

Separates quest reward text from its scenery, adds a fade cue to the combat log scroller, moves cooldown readouts away from item icons, and keeps narrow conversations reachable with wrapping and scrolling.

A style rule that sets a property by a binding (#Card { top: bind(y) }) works in a mounted document and follows the bound value. Mounting such a document stopped the engine with "compiled property input".

Cover and center primitives use safe centring, covers scroll overflow, and modal panels stay within the safe surface even when author sizes are larger. Modal content has a whole-panel scroll fallback; an explicit shell and scroll body keep title and actions fixed.

Moves frames: a background image layer counts as the ground under a text only where it paints, placed as og-render places it: an image in a plate's corner (a filigree) no longer makes the whole plate an authored ground, so text on the plate's thin fill takes the style's --tag-halo over the scene (fantasy's done quest step on its HUD plate read 2.3:1 over a bright sky).

The default tag halo is in contrast-color(currentColor), the text's own ink: black round pale or gold ink, white round dark or navy ink (it was --ink-inverse, the same as a light text's ink in the light scheme). currentColor inside a colour function in text-shadow is the element's colour.
A text whose element cuts a gradient to it (background-clip: text) is read in that gradient, once; it was read as white, the glyph mask og-ui draws it through.

Their inks follow the palette and the packs where they sat on a ground they did not follow: StrategyTower's cost on an affordable path is --on-primary, Ribbon's text is contrast-color() of its tone with the tag outline, Calibration's step badges take the accent and neutral tones, WorldMap's legend is a scene plate in --scene-ink.

The HUD components and screens drawn over the scene (the ability bar, minimap, compass, timers, meters, the genre HUDs, subtitles, objectives and banners) write `text-shadow: var(--tag-halo)` on their root, so every text in them takes the style's tag outline.

Leaderboard ranks size to their formatted text without wrapping. Results use explicit per-stat number/percent presentation through the string table instead of rounding every stat to an integer. Calibration shows one offset value with units; slider documents expose show-value for adjacent readouts.

The action rows of Calibration, Pagination, Leaderboard, FilmFlowchart, Settings, SaveLoad, Card, ModeSelect and Tutorial wrap at 150 % text instead of running off a phone's screen; Calibration centres through the cover primitive, and a CreatorTools panel title ends in an ellipsis instead of widening its panel.

The eyebrow over the main menu's News card and over the loading screen's tip takes --highlight, the emphasised ink, instead of --primary, the primary action's fill, which a pack may make too deep to read as text (fantasy's crimson read 2.1:1 on its panel).

fixed.member: ui screens (calendar, notifications, pagination, star-rating, tree)
fixed.summary: Moves frames: their `<og-icon>`s draw their glyphs. They named the glyph with `name=`, which on an `<og-icon>` element is what a screen reader calls it (only an icon inline in text takes its glyph from `name`), so the previous and next chevrons, the close cross, the stars and the tree's twisty drew nothing and were announced as "chevronLeft" and the like. They now write `icon=`; each button keeps its own `aria-label`.

Calendar, CreatorTools and Credits fit a phone at 150% text: the calendar's seven columns share its header's width and shrink with it, and a marked day wears the style's marked cell (--cell-marked-shadow); CreatorTools' tabs wrap inside the screen; Credits' Back button has its own bar above the roll instead of overlapping the logo.
Anchor selection visits the slots with positive vertical scroll offsets instead of scanning every UI slot, retaining the previous slot order and anchor rules. Layout and drawing are unchanged.
A scroll container restyled by a container query keeps the room for its scroll bar beside its content in the frame it restyles and after; it was dropped until the element was built again.

A box with `overflow-y: auto` or `scroll` and no `overflow-x` of its own now keeps its vertical bar's gutter (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`, and the room the bar takes while its content overflows), so the bar no longer draws over the content's right edge. CSS computes that box's `overflow-x` to `auto`, which og-ui read as a two-way scroller whose bars draw over its content. Content in such boxes is narrower by the bar's room.

Moves frames: an accented control's primary, hover, press and on-primary are the style's derivation of the accent as its --seed-primary (its tokens re-read with that seed), not the accent as given with no hover or press step. In the default style an accent in the mid-lightness band where neither ink reads is held out of it, as a seed is (OKLCH 0.6 is drawn at 0.74 with black on it).

Moves frames: --color-accent-fg (--on-primary, a primary button's label) is contrast-color(var(--color-accent)): exact black or white, at least 4.58:1 on the primary and on its hover and press, instead of #111113 and #fafafd.

A status badge's ink reads 4.5:1 on its own tone wash whatever the seeds: the light scheme's danger, warn, success and info are derived darker (WCAG luminance at most 0.088, was 0.148) and the dark scheme's lighter (at least 0.45, was 0.3), so the default Warning, Success and Info badges read 5.25, 5.32 and 5.26 (were 3.70, 3.92 and 4.21). The faint ink (`--ink-faint`) is a step darker in the light scheme and reads 4.5:1 on a control's fill, and the dark scheme's `--xp` (the epic tier) is #c86ff5 and reads 4.5:1 on a raised surface.

A game's seeds win over a style pack's own (`:root { --seed-primary: … }`) everywhere the palette is drawn, as they are documented to: every document's root is a `:root` the pack's rules match again, and it now carries the root's theme tokens there too. A document drew with the pack's seeds, so og.ui.configure's `seeds` did not retint a pack that sets its own.

fixed: Preserve authored tags and selector attributes in UI documents, including classes not referenced by the document's current stylesheet, for retained mount matching.

fixed.summary: align-items and align-self take `self-start` and `self-end` as the item's own writing mode's sides (CSS Box Alignment 3 §4.3): a right-to-left item in a left-to-right column sits at the right under `self-start`. They used to read as `start` and `end`, the container's sides.
A keyframes rule that gives scale only at its start (a stamp or pop) now ends at no scaling on an element with no scale of its own, instead of warning that none is not a number and not playing.
A text decoration with no colour of its own (currentColor) now takes the colour of the element that declares it, as CSS Text Decoration says, instead of the text it is drawn across.

fixed: og ui sheet reuses its incremental cook cache across invocations. Built-in style-sheet pages share one engine and renderer per breakpoint, locale and style, switching page and text scale in place and drawing only captures.

fixed.summary: Desktop cells are captured at 1920×1080 (desktopHd), the frame size docs/ui.md §6.2 sets for kit and pack references; they were 1280×720.
The core-control state sheet draws in the pack's own fonts and icons (it kept the sheet's default font over them) and sets its display and heading samples in the pack's display face.

The state sheet's controls page lays out like its fields page, a row per control and a captioned box per state, seven abreast on a desktop and two on a phone, so every page fits 390 px at 150 % text with no word broken and no toggle running into the next box.

fixed.member: og ui sheet components, screens and world
fixed.summary: The screens sheet draws pagination's, the calendar's and the tree's chevrons instead of warning on every cell; the components sheet's HUD page stacks into a scrolling column on a phone instead of laying the minimap over the vitals; the world sheet frames its scene for a portrait phone, so its units and their tags stay on the screen; StatusGrid's overflow fixture no longer has more time left than its duration.

The group review sheets ship with the engine package in `sheets/` (without their references), so `og ui sheet arena` and `og ui review arena --style fantasy` run on an installed engine instead of failing to find the sheet. No game's cook bundles a sheet.

The shooter components' text follows the player's text scale (UiDesc.textScale). Their sizes were type ramp steps written as font: var(--text-<step>), which a document resolves in px; they are now steps in em of the surrounding text (--font-step-*), so a style pack that sets those steps also sets these sizes. The StatBar inside CombatHud is a core component and keeps its size.
A phone on its side shows the three newest rows, as an upright phone does. It showed every row, which covered the upper corner of the play area.
Oversized strokes on small synthetic-bold text clamp to the distance field's remaining reach instead of painting tinted glyph rectangles.

An element a snippet renders in a mounted document keeps the elements written inside it. Its node was held without the snippet's name, so the engine released its children every frame: a <row id="Foot"> in {#snippet card()} drew empty. Its path is <parent>/card/Foot, as docs/ui.md gives it.

The tail takes --panel, the colour the default frame is filled with, instead of --frame-fill: a frame fill is a background, and a style pack's may be layers of images and gradients that no shape can take, so the tail drew nothing under such a pack. A pack whose frame is not one colour dresses the SpeechBubble.tail part.

A box with a `z-index` now paints, and is hit, in its nearest ancestor that makes a stacking context, not only among its siblings (CSS 2 Appendix E). A positive level lifts it over its parent's later siblings, and a negative one puts it under its parent's own background. A parent keeps its children's levels inside it when it has a level of its own, opacity under 1, a transform, a filter, a mask, a clip-path, a blend mode, `isolation: isolate`, a `will-change` naming one of those, or paint containment. Scroll containers, shaped overflow clips, dressed parts and game draws also keep their children's levels inside them.

An unlit star takes --ink-faint, the faintest ink that still reads, instead of --well, a ground that vanished on a dark one (the "none" state drew three near-black stars on the default style's dark ground).

`stepper::part(frame)` exposes `:disabled`, the state the stepper already gives its frame, so a style can dress a disabled stepper's field; the default style no longer writes a `:hover` rule for the frame, which never hovers (its value and buttons do). A pack generated by `og style new` passes `og style check` again.

Store writes send the mutation and first reactive poll in one host call, with synchronous errors and subscriptions unchanged. Own writable and collection reads avoid temporary subscriptions; readable and derived reads retain their start/stop lifecycle. Binary patches use a growable byte buffer, and derived values are encoded once.

A whole number written to a UI store reaches the document as an integer, so integer fields take it: `<text spans={$spans}>` no longer drops its text when a span's position or length comes from a script.
Unit tray portraits keep their square ratio after the shared-layout conversion, restoring full-size centered fallback icons on desktop and phone.

Boxes the `stretch` migration missed or that read differently under CSS sizing now lay out as designed at phone and container-query widths: Calibration's dead-zone slider shares its row with its label instead of overflowing it, RpgQuestTracker's step text no longer runs past its row, the Achievements title wraps the summary below it on a narrow panel instead of being squeezed to a few pixels, and the film chapter and gallery cards share each row evenly on a phone (two across in portrait, four in landscape) instead of each taking its title's width.

A style pack is read once. Its sheets are read once for both its `::part()` rules and the rules it gives a document's elements, and the default style's CSS, which every pack sits on, is read once in the process. Before, loading a style read the pack and the whole default style twice, and the default style a third time for the UI.
Built-in style discovery excludes tests, references and captures directories at every depth while retaining nested art assets.

A forced interaction state (hover, pressed, focused) reaches a document element's :hover, :active, :focus and :focus-visible rules and its control's drawing, on any number of elements at once, as the pointer's and the focus's do; it never clicks, and a text field forced to focus shows it without taking the keyboard.
A document mounted from TypeScript reads the engine's $ui store as a natively mounted one does: <kbd data-action> glyphs and $ui.device no longer warn `mount has no input store 'ui'`.

Svelte's blur now blurs the subtree through CSS filter: blur()'s layer from amount px (default 5), not opacity only. Presence and state values take the new props blur (CSS px) and draw (0 drawn whole, 1 hidden).
An inline SVG shape's fill or stroke of currentColor now takes the element's CSS color, inherited from its ancestors (a data-tone, a role's ink, an explicit color), instead of always the style's ink.

The overlay primitive's top, bottom and center anchors now centre their child by its own size, so a label, icon or SVG can be anchored; they no longer give the child a flex display, which only a box accepts.

Switch knob defaults, tick size and stroke, and selection travel now settle from the measured CSS track and knob boxes, including percentage dimensions and retained restyles. Same-instance and fresh-instance checkpoint restore preserve the derived geometry. Default widget and core-document reference frames are unchanged.

Moves frames: native equal-width tabs measure their natural text independently of clipping and pixel snapping, so narrow tab tracks settle instead of repeatedly growing and shrinking. Shorter labels can still shrink the track.
The state sheet's tabs move to the fields page, where a two-tab bar fits a phone cell by touch, and its disclosures sit in a panel as an accordion.

Moves frames: fitted tabs wrap between words, never inside an overwide word. Each overflowing line ellipsizes independently while the full accessible label remains intact. Plain text now respects overflow-wrap: normal; anywhere and break-word retain emergency breaks.

tabular-nums on a rich text (a struck price, a value with inline markup) in a face whose atlas was cooked without `features tnum` drew no digits, only the punctuation and decoration: the shaped paragraph drew the face's tabular forms, which the atlas lacks. Such a text is now laid out run by run and draws its digits from the atlas, as a plain label does. The built-in figure role's prices and progress values show their numbers again.

Team inks (`--team1` to `--team8`) keep 4.5:1 on every ground they are drawn on, whatever the seeds: the page, its subtle ground, panels, raised panels, a hovered row and a cell's or badge's control wash, in both schemes. Light teams now sit at or under luminance 0.108 and dark teams at or over 0.447; the default light team1 is #0041fd (was #005ee0, about 4.0:1 on tinted light grounds). A selected row on a team keeps the selected ink (`--ink-selected`), its team in its rim, since the selection ground is too light for a dark team ink. Teams 1 to 6 still hold 0.1 apart in OKLab under every colour vision; teams 7 and 8 now hold 0.05.

The team colours stay apart under every colour vision. Teams 1 to 6 (`--team1` to `--team6`, UiTheme.tokens.team) are six fixed colours per scheme, vermilion, yellow, bluish green, blue, violet and reddish purple, alternately lighter and darker, at least 0.1 apart in OKLab under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (og style check's simulation) and 4.5:1 on the grounds, whatever the seeds. The team seed (`--seed-team`, UiSeeds.team) picks the first, the nearest by hue, and the rest follow in Okabe-Ito order: the default blue seed gives blue, vermilion, bluish green, yellow, reddish purple and violet. Teams 7 and 8 are fixed and hold 0.07: past six sides, give each a shape, a pattern or an icon as well. The default dark team2 and team3 were 0.009 apart under deuteranopia.

The team colours (`--team1` to `--team8`, UiTheme.tokens.team) read 4.5:1 as text on the grounds and surfaces whatever the seeds, as the default style's role parts on a team (`data-team=a|b`) use them as ink: the light scheme's are derived darker (WCAG luminance at most 0.135, was 0.245) and the dark scheme's lighter (at least 0.31, was 0.195). The default light team1 and team2 are #2e62c9 and #be3333 (were #3d7eff and #f74545, 3.73 and 3.56 on white).

Text declarations and font shorthands accept root-relative lengths before per-element unit conversion. rem uses the body type step and follows player text scale instead of inheriting the parent font size.

Under a style pack, text sized by the type ramp's tokens (`font: var(--text-caption)`) follows `UiDesc.textScale` again. A pack's sheet sets the ramp again on every document's root, at its authored px, so only the default style grew it: AbilitySlot's percent stayed 13 px at 150 % under fantasy, scifi and cartoon. A type length set in px now grows wherever it is set.

`text-shadow` inherits, as CSS Text Decoration 3 defines it: a shadow written on a box reaches every text inside it, its `currentColor` read as each text's own ink, so `text-shadow: var(--tag-halo)` on a HUD's root outlines all its texts. Before, it reached only the element it was written on. A title or a figure takes its style's `--title-shadow` or `--figure-shadow` when the style sets one and inherits otherwise; the default style sets neither.

fixed.member: UI: the cost of beginning a frame
fixed.summary: Every frame's begin read the theme from the `:root` tokens again: a full root cascade and a parse of every colour, length and type step, about 1.6 ms a frame with no UI on screen. The UI now keeps that reading for the theme it started from and the media context, and reads again when the part CSS, the style pack, the theme, the fonts or the media context change. No theme value changes: every kept theme equalled a fresh one across the og-ui and og-runtime suites.

Comparison rows accept optional added/removed facts, show translated presence words and restylable data-change hooks without fake deltas, mute removed values and wrap long names in desktop and stacked phone layouts.

A touch button with elements inside it (a face, an icon, as the built-in ActionButton has) feeds its own action where it stands. Its zone was taken from the element before it, so in a row of such buttons each fed the next one's action and the first fed none.

fixed.member: CSS: cascade order of a <button>'s plate
fixed.summary: A rule ranks by its tree context before its layer, as CSS Cascade 5 §6.1 says. A button's own box declarations (background, border, padding, corners, box-shadow) are its plate's: above the style's ::part() rules and below its document's own ::part() rule. !important now reverses that order, as in CSS. A style's !important plate declaration beats the button's own declaration, and a button's own !important beats its document's ::part() rule. Before, the button's own plate beat every style rule whatever its importance, and lost to every document ::part() rule. No default style, style pack or built-in component uses !important on these properties, so no frame moves.

A Tree row is indented by the body type's size per level (--type-body-size) at every width, so the step grows with the player's text scale (21 px at 150 % text where a phone had 12 px, which read as no hierarchy beside 21 px names), and the indent stops growing after four levels so a deep row keeps room for its name. The overflow fixture is a tree a game could flatten: Camera is open over the rows it holds, and a closed row (Audio) follows.

A Tree name longer than its row wraps inside it (inside a word too, for an identifier) instead of running off the screen; a leaf lines up with the rows that open, the selected row's highlight ends at the row, the chevron of a row that opens shows in every style pack (a pack's button padding left it no width), and the indent step is smaller on a phone. The document declares an overflow fixture.
A typewriter's accessible name is its whole text from the first tick; a screen reader was given the part shown so far, changing every tick.

A typewriter styled with a CSS text property (text-transform, white-space and the like, its own or inherited) reveals its text at its rate; it showed the whole text from the first tick. It cuts its source before CSS transforms it, so a character a transform lengthens (ß in capitals) appears whole.

A UI text clipped out of view no longer reaches the renderer on every frame as if its face lacked its glyphs: only a text that measured no width goes on without bounds. A screen of 1,000 labels with 360 in view sent all 1,000 to be recorded on every idle tick (idle 0.047 ms, record 0.032; now 0.027 and 0.013).

A document `<button variant="primary">` (or `danger`, `ghost`, `quiet`, `secondary`) is that class for a style's host rules as it is for its parts, so `button.primary { color: … }` inks its label where `button.primary::part(base)` already dressed its plate. Before, a pack set on a mounted document drew a variant button's label in the plain `--button-ink`. A bound variant is that class only while it holds that word.

A document element's style warnings (a missing token, a value invalid at computed-value time, an -og-burst keyframe whose var() does not resolve) are in every frame's warnings while they hold, not only in the frame the element was styled again; they go when the element is styled without them or leaves. An `<svg width="0" height="0">` holding only `<defs>` no longer warns that its viewBox has no size: only a viewBox the author wrote is checked.
Call early stays on one line on a phone while a long early-call reward wraps within the button.
Numbers spawned on one tick over one target stand apart as a stack, clear of its nameplate and of the numbers still rising, instead of drawn over each other where none reads.

World tags declutter by everything they draw (a targeted nameplate's scaled frame, a name wider than its plate), keep a gap from each other instead of touching, and keep clear of the text a ground draws (a PathLine's badge), so no tag covers another.

fixed.member: UI world anchors and damage numbers
fixed.summary: Crowded world labels find the same decluttered positions without allocating and sorting every pair of candidate coordinates. Unchanged world-layer boxes retain their CSS layout while the camera moves; projection and interaction still update each tick.

Moves frames: a decluttered tag stays on the screen and clear of the tags placed before it. Each takes the nearest spot a gap off the tags near it (a stack straight above first, then straight below, then any way) that is inside the safe area and within its reach, and fades out while none is; only a Rust `contain` anchor was kept on the screen, so a crowd of nameplates and speech bubbles climbed past the screen's top.

Moves frames: a ground draws what overflows its box, as any CSS box's overflow shows. It was laid out clipped to its box and drawn only over its box's quad, so PathLine's badge past the path's end was cut to the room left in the box ("12 m · 2 AP" read "12"). A world panel drawn into its render target is still cut to the target.
Moves frames: two prompts over nearby things stand apart (it declutters by shifting, the nearer keeping its place); they were drawn one over the other.
The north mark stands on the map inside the bezel instead of over the bezel's top edge.
An effect with more seconds left than its duration (refreshed or extended) draws no sweep; its negative dash was refused with a warning and the sweep covered the whole tile.
An effect's time left wears the pack's tag tokens; the component's own shadow no longer overrides what a pack sets.

Under flex-wrap: wrap-reverse, align-items and align-self: start and end are the writing mode's sides again (end is the bottom of a row's line), as CSS has them; they were laid out as flex-start and flex-end, on the reversed side. flex-start and flex-end still follow the reversed lines, and so does an alignment left unwritten. A container that wrote flex-start to get the bottom keeps its layout.

Moves frames: headings laid out on more than one line no longer draw side flourishes beside their first line, regardless of alignment or style pack. Single-line headings retain their flourishes, including smaller headings with explicitly sized flourish parts.
`z-index: auto`, the property's initial value, now cooks instead of failing as "not a number". It is stack level 0, so a later `auto` undoes an earlier rule's level (CSS 2 §9.9.1).

`min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0` now lift a flex item's automatic minimum (CSS Flexbox 1 §4.5), so a sharing item (`flex: 1`) shrinks below its content, as browsers do. The zero used to be folded into the size's range, where 0 means no minimum, and the item stayed floored at its content's width.

fixed.member: og vfx import: sprite size of unevenly scaled and generated nodes
fixed.summary: A sprite or mesh whose scale differs per axis is drawn at its axes' mean, not its longest axis, also when that size is constant over its life (the flat curve was taken as 1); and the generator's own scale, and that of the single nodes below it, now reach the drawn node's size and motion, as Effekseer binds them. Converted effects draw at Effekseer's sizes: AndrewFM01's actionLines_radial2 draws its 2000 lines as 0.8 m quads, not 4.5 m ones (GPU cost +109 ms to +7 ms on an M4 Pro), and Pierre02's LossOfBlood goes from +54 ms to +36 ms. 163 of the 285 converted samples and 25 of effekseer-starter's 38 effects change size; their pack files, previews and cost sheets are regenerated. Moves no reference frame.

Every CPU-simulated particle system, sub-emitter, CPU trail and effect mesh now writes its drawn slots into one vertex buffer the frame shares, in one write, instead of a write to a buffer of its own each (wgpu makes and frees a staging buffer per write), and an effect material's check no longer formats a name for each of its custom values every frame. With twenty starter effects on screen (og vfx preview --together, release, on a CPU Vulkan), the particle renderer's prepare fell from 38 % to 30 % of the render call's CPU samples and queue writes from 25 % to 16 %. Frames do not change.

fixed.member: og vfx import: texture names that differ only in case
fixed.summary: Two effects imported into one folder that name the same texture in different case (`Star.png`, `star.png`) now share one copy under the first name, or get distinct names when their bytes differ, so every id names its file as it is spelt on disk on case-sensitive and case-insensitive file systems alike.
A composed effect's flipbook sprite turns with the instance's hue, as its other elements do; it took only the tint.

A composed effect's `sound` element stopped the run on the tick it was due ("'og.AudioSource.pan' default: the value is a number, got null"): its source was spawned without og.AudioSource's defaults. It now plays on a source that is a child of the effect and goes with it at its end.

A tinted composed effect no longer adds a copy of each of its emitters to the renderer for every tint it is drawn with (copies that were never freed, one per distinct tint); the tint is the particle system's own, and draws exactly as before.

A streamed video is no longer downloaded whole when it loads. The cook splits each stream (and each rendition) into chunks from a key frame on; nothing is fetched until a player wants its frames, a playing player's chunks arrive up to four seconds ahead of it, and chunks no player needs are let go. A game can load all its footage in GameDesc.start and pays only for what plays; a paused player at a segment's start fetches and decodes just its first chunk. Re-cook to get chunked streams (og cook does it on its own); dump_stream lists each stream's chunks.
Names the codec this host plays the stream in (`av1`, `hevc` or `h264`) instead of always `av1`.

A voxelised model keeps its surface's height: each surface point fills the cube half an edge inside it, so the cubes' faces lie within half an edge of the surface on either side. Before, a point filled the cube it lay in, and every upward face rose a whole cube: a ground at y = 0 became a slab one cube thick above it, and with the cube edge doubled past the face budget it rose over the props standing on it. Voxelised models re-cook (conform-mesh-v4).

A voxelised model past its face budget keeps its cube edge and the cook warns, where before the edge doubled until the budget was met: a rolling ground at 0.1 m became steps 1.6 m high, walls over the scene. The greedy mesher already merges every coplanar face of one colour. Only a model wider than 256 cubes is still voxelised coarser. Voxelised models re-cook (conform-mesh-v5).

A model voxelised under a mirrored node keeps counter-clockwise triangles that agree with their normals; it was wound the other way, which only drew right while the renderer ignored mirroring. Voxelised models re-cook.

A lake seen from below breaks the rim of Snell's window into irregular shards of mixed sizes, as ripples do: the ripples drawn there are sixteen wavelets 5 to 39 cm long with unrelated directions, where six fixed ones drew the shards in regular rows. Rendering only.

A lake's and a river's bank foam and ripple foam are lit as a sea's foam and a fall's white water: the sun's share is Lambert's, its irradiance over pi. It was three times too bright in the sun and clipped to flat white. Frames with such foam in sunlight get darker foam (up to 53 levels on an Apple M4 Pro); shaded foam, a fall's and a sea's are unchanged.

A lake's wind waves no longer draw a regular grid (an egg crate with the sun's glints in rows): the surface detail is sixteen plane waves of unrelated lengths and directions about one heading, a short-crested field as a breeze makes, where four fixed cosines crossed at a right angle. Their slope variance is as before, so reflections and highlights keep their strength. Rendering only.

The light shafts under water are the sun's light in the water itself, drawn as a volume: lit through the same wave focusing that draws the caustics (each shaft ends in the bright line it draws on the bed), running parallel along the refracted sun, and shadowed by whatever stands in the water. They replace straight beams fanned about the sun's place on screen, which no wave shaped and nothing shadowed. They take og.Water.caustics' strength as before, and need RenderQuality.volumetricFog (off at low quality, where the water's light is even). Rendering only.

A planar reflection draws what grows on the terrain: og.TerrainScatter's copies with their impostors, the crowds' cards and og.Grass. Before, a mirror drew the meshes, the terrain and the sky, so a lake's shore stood in it bare, without its woods and reeds.

A planar reflection keeps the fog under volumetric fog: the mirror is fogged by the same fog unlit. Before, a scene with Fog.volumetric drew its mirror without any fog, so hills in mist stood clear in the water.

A gale's sea had almost no foam: its foam levels lie far out in the tail of the surface's folding, and the fixed gain reached a tenth to a fifth of full. The gain now follows how close the surface lies under each level, so a 20 m/s sea carries whitecaps and a breeze's sea gains a few. Over the shoals the least gain holds, so the surf zone does not whiten to the beach. Old foam stays open at its rim and in its body instead of filling its patch flat, and spray puffs are broken clouds of droplets, not even discs. At dusk and at night foam and spray are as bright as the sky lights them: they took the twilight's fourfold lift of the image-based light, which the sea's mirror already left out, and glowed white on a dark sea.

The paint pass reads its structure tensor from nine Sobel windows of four bilinear taps and, where a stroke is at least 1.5 pixels across, its Kuwahara taps as 2 x 2 blocks, instead of every pixel of both windows. A forest at 1280 x 720 with paintRadius 3 on an Apple M4 Pro: paint 7.8 -> 2.0 ms. Painted frames differ slightly (strokes over fine texture are a little softer).

A wash's rim pools only where there is pigment: the side of a boundary on the paper or a pale wash (the sky behind branches) no longer gets a grey line. 2D art painted by the cook is re-cooked with the same rule.

Web releases ship wasm-bindgen output directly, without a Binaryen pass, including the AV1 fallback. Engine modules are larger before compression and slightly larger over Brotli; the per-download 16 MiB Brotli budget is unchanged.
Both physics profiles' shared-memory web lanes modules can grow to 4 GiB instead of 2 GiB where the browser allows, matching the single-threaded wasm32 ceiling.

On the web, og.motion's poses no longer depend on when the GPU's readbacks arrive: each batch is taken at its due tick, as natively, and a tick whose step needs a batch that is not back is held until it is (the engine Worker goes on drawing and the page on taking input). The web's jump clip keeps one frame past the drawn one, as natively, instead of a measured latency's worth.

A snapshot steps og.motion to its tick first, as a capture does, so its presentation hash is the tick's whether or not a frame was drawn; on the web its `presentation` is empty, and a capture is null, while that step waits for the GPU (ask again).

fixed.member: og render (web) and the Worker's renderFrame
fixed.summary: The web host's display-frame readback returned no bytes: wgpu's web backend lists only RENDER_ATTACHMENT among a canvas's usages, so the surface was configured without COPY_SRC and keeping frames was refused. The canvas is now configured with COPY_SRC, which WebGPU allows on every device.
A vortex leans vegetation counter-clockwise seen from above, as its description says; it turned clockwise.

fixed.member: number arguments (every binding that reads a float field)
fixed.summary: A NaN passed in a number field now reaches the engine as NaN instead of reading as the field's default (the wire writes NaN as null), so og.render.light2dAt and every binding that checks finiteness refuse it again. An absent field still takes its default; integer, boolean and string fields are unchanged.

added.member: og.PointerLock, og.Pointers.movement, PointerInput.movementX/movementY, og.PointerMove.movementX/movementY, InjectedInput pointerLock, mouse_move and pointer_lock actions
added.summary: Mouse-look: og.Pointers.movement is the mouse's relative movement this tick (movementX/Y of pointer 0's events summed, zero next tick); og.PointerLock { wanted, locked } lets a game ask for the pointer lock, which the web shell requests on the next press on the canvas, exits when wanted goes false and reports back from pointerlockchange (absolute positions held while locked). Injected pointer events and og.PointerMove carry movementX/Y (0 when omitted); the command channel's mouse_move:dx,dy and pointer_lock:on|off script them. Native runs are headless and never lock. Off by default; the simulation of existing games is unchanged.

og cook takes .mp3, .ogg (Vorbis) and .flac sounds beside .wav: decoded to 16-bit PCM in the cook (pure Rust, symphonia; no ffmpeg or afconvert) and encoded to QOA like a WAV, chunked and streamed the same way, under the source's asset id (audio/theme.mp3, audio/theme.mp3#chunk3). An undecodable file is refused naming the file and its format. The cook only: the runtime and the wasm are unchanged.

fixed.summary: The built-in look presets and style assets (og_cook look STYLES, BUILTINS) are statics, so og carries each CJK font once instead of twice (about 9.7 MB less per platform).
"What works" says the cited examples/* games live in the GitHub repository, not the installed package, and that the archetypes are installed (og new --archetype).

added.member: og api find / og api show
added.summary: Look the API up one entry at a time: og api find <words> lists the reference entries matching the words (name, module, first sentence, then field and parameter docs), one line each; og api show <name> prints one entry in full (signature, fields with defaults, ranges and units, doc) without its IDL source. Both read the wiki of the installed engine package. og-core §7 and og-game §25 teach them.

added.member: UI style fonts cjk and cjkDisplay
added.summary: A style's fonts block takes cjk and cjkDisplay, Simplified Chinese companions that set a label's Chinese beside the role's Latin face, ahead of the locale's fonts. Every built-in style names one matched to its Latin (templates/styles/cjk: Noto Sans SC, Noto Serif SC, ZCOOL KuaiLe, Fusion Pixel; OFL), cooked in only for a game with a zh string table, rendered at run time.

added.member: UI style tone <part> r g b a
added.summary: The frame art's centre colour (og cook measures it from the atlas when a style does not set it): a button's label ink, and the ground any widget reads through it, are judged against it at 7:1.
og.ui: warns when a control is laid out past the screen's edge with no scroll container to bring it back, naming it and by how much.

fixed: Button labels read on what is drawn: a game's primaryColor over a dark neon or scifi body keeps a light label, and a mid-scale colour (crimson) moves away from its ink as little as it takes. The accent highlight now follows the game's primary and reads 5:1 on its wash. Games on a built-in style look different.
A centred or end-aligned label in a column takes the column's width (it sat at the start in a box as wide as its text).

The neon style: its glow marks the button and the title only (no panel, HUD or number glow; tighter tube halos, a fainter grid), and its numbers are Chakra Petch SemiBold (Orbitron read 0 as Ø and 1 as 7).
AnchorDesc.margin's doc says it insets every edge; no IDL member added or removed.

added.summary: With the variable set (Origin Runner sets it when Origin Desktop draws the Session's engine), og run and og dev show their frames in the desktop window through shared GPU memory and render at the size the window asks for; without it nothing changes.

fixed: level-texturing's texture-level.ts paints with gemini-nano-banana-2.1 by default (qwen-image-2.1-pro stays one --model away); its http provider sends Qwen's seed and prompt_extend only to Qwen models and the view's size to the others, which Gemini's route requires; a resumed run keeps its model.

added: MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness (0 to 1, 0 off): where the sun does not reach (the toon ramp's dark band, the side turned away, a cast shadow) a lit surface loses that share of the sun and of the ambient light, so 1 draws shadows as solid black masses; local lights, emissive and shadowTint still show. RenderCapabilities.stylise names it shadowDarkness.

The cook paints a model's own colour textures with the look's Stylise paint fields in texel space (Kuwahara along the edges, bleed, pigment pooling, canvas grain), as it paints 2D sprites, when the project's look has an art contract that conforms models; textures no model claims, normal and data maps are not painted. Painted 3D textures re-cook and their frames change (painterly-3d, sculpted-clay, paper-craft on their samples).

The cook holds a model that says `conform character` (its type model text, or a glTF's import settings) to ArtShape.characterFaces, as a skinned one, and og style check judges it so; a type model past its face budget is built again with fewer segments before it is decimated.

MaterialStyle.surface (MaterialSurface none, clay, paper, plastic), surfaceStrength and surfaceScale: a made surface on every lit standard material (normal detail, colour grain, wrapped light and roughness in the mesh's own space), none by default; the sculpted-clay, paper-craft and miniature-diorama presets set it and their frames change.
fixed: The heavy-ink-shadows preset draws its shadows as solid black ink (MaterialStyle.shadowDarkness 1; shadowTint at amount 0 had no effect, and posterize never reaches black because the ambient light lifts every shadow), with a near-black sky, a blood-red haze and muted colour. Its frames change.

The low-resolution-3d preset ends its draw distance in a short dark fog the colour of its sky (the clear colour), so the 240-line frame reads as early-console 3D; its vertex snapping and affine texturing were already drawn. Its frames change.

MaterialStyle.surface no longer draws black blots where a mesh's shading normal lies in its face (a smooth silhouette or a rim turning away): the bump fades out there and the normal stays, instead of a NaN the post effects spread. Rumpus Isle's look sets surface none to keep its own colours under miniature-diorama.

The cook's mesh conformance (ArtShape.normals flat) drops faces thinner than the position grid and keeps flat normals on lathe poles and on voxelised parts turned by their placement; conformed models re-cook (model desc conform-mesh-v3).
RenderScene::set_shader_param writes a changed parameter into the material's uniform in place and keeps its bind group, instead of rebuilding both; frames are unchanged.

Stylise.dither and ArtPalette.dither bayer4 and bayer8 use the dispersed Bayer matrix; they drew a quadrant-clustered one whose tones showed as blocks of the matrix's size. Frames and cook-conformed textures dithered with them change; bayer2 does not.
The rubber-hose-animation and gothic-contour presets no longer posterize: per-channel steps turned their sepia and blue-grey art into olive, pink and violet bands. Their frames change.

breaking.change: A project whose look (project.ogt look, or one extending a preset) sets art blocks now cooks its assets conformed to them: 2D art to the pixel grid, the palette and the line (and, with stream A3, models, mesh textures and clips to the shape, texel and motion contract). Frames of such a game change. With stream A4 such a project (one naming its look in project.ogt) also draws under the contract's runtime defaults: cleanEdge pixel-art rotation, the line on sprites the cook did not line, ArtCamera's preset on an applied look, ArtMotion.stepFps as the animation step. At run time, a look with art blocks also sets the camera from ArtCamera when applied, defaults Sprite.outline from ArtLine, draws pixel art through cleanEdge under ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge, and defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps from ArtMotion.stepFps, which changes the ticks of a game whose animation drives play (rubber-hose-animation, sculpted-clay).
breaking.fix: Keep it (the style is the point), or opt an asset out with conform off in its import settings or project.ogt conform { off ... }, or set the preset's art blocks to zero in the game's look. At run time: a player whose own AnimationPlayer.stepFps is above 0 keeps it, and ArtMotion { stepFps 0 } in the game's look turns the default off; the camera preset is applied with the look, before GameDesc.start, so camera code in start or later wins.

added.summary: New resource (module art): the palette the assets' texels sit on: colors, strict, maxColors, rampSteps, accents, dither; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the pixel grid of 2D art: unit, logicalHeight, spriteSizes, rotation, rotationSteps, snap; no constraint at zero.
New resource: texel density on 3D surfaces: density, maxSize, filter, mips; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the shape language of models: propFaces, characterFaces, normals, normalAngle, bevel, voxel, silhouette; no constraint at zero.
New resource: the line the assets carry: width, color, place, distanceFalloff; no line at width 0.
New resource: stepFps, maxFrames, squash; no constraint at zero.
New resource: projection, fixedAngle, pitch, yaw, fovMin, fovMax, pixelPerfect; no constraint at zero.
New enum: free, nearest, cleanEdge, prerotated.
New enum: any, nearest, linear.
New enum: any, full, none.
New enum: any, smooth, flat, angle.
New enum: outside, inside, both.
New enum: any, perspective, orthographic.
Left out or empty, project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" line is applied when it has one; the two naming different looks is refused. A project without the line runs as before.
Names the art resources a look sets too.
Inside a system, an art resource the system does not declare among its writes is left as it is instead of refusing the look.
A look's blocks include the seven art resources, checked against their records as the frame's are; the 37 presets carry their catalogue style's values.
project.ogt's look "looks/<id>.ogt" names the look whose art contract the cook reads before any asset cooks; create writes it beside GameDesc.look.
The brush the cook draws a 2D line with (og.ArtBrush); diamond at zero.
New enum: diamond, circle, square.

The cook conforms sprites, flipbooks, tile sets and UI images to the look's art contract (pixel grid, 1-bit alpha, Oklab palette with dither, line, prerotated cells, painted 2D) and writes <id>#index for palette swaps; conform off and project.ogt conform { off } opt out; og cook --report lists every change. Byte-identical without a contract.

Knowledge (scripts/brief.ts) and @origingame/create-game: artBrief(look, kind, subject, options?) compiles the flattened look and its catalogue entry into the request for one asset: prompt, references, generator parameters; readLook(dir) and presetLook(slug) read a look from disk. A public contract (docs/art.md §2.2).

og style check [project] [--title|--play|--results <commands>] [--size WxH] [--no-frames] [--critic] [--json]: every cooked asset measured against the look's art contract (palette hit rate within ΔE00 2, colours, pixel grid and half pixels, line, texel size, filter and mips, faces against the budget, flat-normal share, texel density and spread), every opt-out listed, and the title, play and results frames (project.ogt's screens block) measured; --critic prints the catalogue's three checks and the frames only. og doctor --project has a style line; og build --publish prints it as warnings, never refusing.

A pixel outline this many logical pixels wide (0 to 4), drawn by the sprite shader from the texture's alpha; 0 is none, or under the project's art contract the look's ArtLine.width for a texture the cook did not line.
The outline's linear colour; at its default, the art contract's ArtLine.color.
A palette swap: the sprite draws its texture's index texture (the cook's <id>#index) through a row of this palette texture of N rows; 0 is none.
The row of Sprite.palette drawn.
A palette swap of every tile layer through a row of this palette texture; 0 is none.
The row of Tilemap.palette drawn.

Under project.ogt's look (stream A4): ArtPixels.rotation cleanEdge draws pixel-art textures through the new cleanEdge sampler (og-render TextureFilter::CleanEdge), ArtLine defaults Sprite.outline, ArtCamera sets the camera's projection, angle and field of view when a look is applied and pixelPerfect snaps the 2D camera by logical pixels, ArtMotion.stepFps defaults AnimationPlayer.stepFps, and a strict ArtPalette tints the UI's icons to their nearest palette colour. Without the look line nothing changes.

added: Knowledge: the craft skills architecture-discipline, component-forge, level-texturing (with scripts/texture-level.ts), localization, recipe-craft and visual-acceptance move from origin-agent into the knowledge package under the same names, free of platform tools and pointing to the og-* skills and the wiki for the API; texture-level.ts's providers are handoff (default), http (an OpenAI-compatible image endpoint) and dashscope, and runs that say agent or gateway resume.

Knowledge: payload(roots) and defaultRoots(pkg?) of knowledge/scripts/lib.ts, with the PayloadFile and Roots shapes, are a public contract beside installed, mount and summary: the platform reads the knowledge straight from the installed package with payload(installed(dir).roots). Nothing about them changed.

fixed: og check on a TypeScript install that bun x left incomplete (tsgo, where tsrs has no package): instead of tsgo's Go panic or Cannot find global type errors, it names the incomplete directory and the fix (delete it or bun pm cache rm, then rerun); og doctor reports it as broken.

The knowledge package's scripts/mount.ts CLI mounts into an origin-agent checkout's knowledge/, where the platform's knowledge moved from OriginGame's packages/game-knowledge/production; installed, mount and summary are unchanged.

og-ui glass on WebGL2 in Chrome and Edge on Windows blurs as on metal, WebGPU and DX12: each pyramid level took its tap spacing from textureDimensions of a view whose base mip level is that level, which ANGLE on D3D11 answers with level 2b's size for base level b, so the blur was about twice as wide. Each level of the glass pyramid and of a view's glow chain now takes the size it reads from a uniform; native frames are unchanged.

WebGL2 starts about four times faster on Windows (ANGLE on D3D11): programs link in the background with KHR_parallel_shader_compile, read when a pass first draws with them, and the GL tier's lit programs leave the rect-light (LTC) code out until a scene has a rect light. fx-showcase's cold first frame went from 30.4-31.7 s to 7.0-7.5 s in Chrome 155 and from 30.3-31.2 s to 7.6-7.7 s in Edge 155; WebGPU, metal and DX12 are unchanged and no frame moved. The trade-off: on WebGL2, a scene that gets its first rect light during play links its lit programs again at that moment (about 5 to 8 s on ANGLE D3D11, waited for by the next lit frame); to pay it at load instead, put an og.RectLight in the first scene (one at intensity 0 counts).

added.summary: og bake projection init|plan|prepare|project|holes|export --run <dir>: a gray level glb painted from planned views by an image model the caller runs, projected into one texture and exported as a textured glb, on the CPU.

fixed: A NavAgent with faceMovement turns the same on every host: its turn was glam's slerp on the host's sinf and drifted by up to 16 ulp between Windows and Linux for the ticks of a turn; it is now a yaw step through og-core's deterministic math, so the turning ticks' quaternions move by an ulp on every host.
og.terrain.sample's slope is computed with og-core's deterministic acos instead of the host's.

camera.worldToScreen and camera.screenToRay, which a system may call inside the tick, answer the same bits on every host: their perspective is built with og-core's sin/cos (not glam's host-libm perspective), now pinned by a test, and glam's perspective constructors are refused in the simulation crates.

added.summary: og upgrade [project] [--to <v>] [--json]: moves project.ogt's engine pin and package.json's dependency, applies the codemods of the versions crossed and lists what needs a hand edit; exit 0 done, 3 manual edits, 1 failed.

og replay record and og replay compare: a game's per-tick world hashes recorded with one engine version and replayed with another; the first divergent tick and the entities, components and fields that differ.
og doctor --json: the checks as one object, with pin { pinned, installed, compatible }.
This file, in the package: each version's kind, whether the simulation changed, its breaks with their fixes, additions and fixes.
Zoom, spin and directional blurs of the frame with screenBlurStrength, screenBlurCenter, screenBlurAngle and screenBlurSamples; off at none or strength 0.
Resource that sways og.TerrainScatter copies (strength, direction, speed, gust); visual only, off at strength 0.
How much og.Wind sways a scatter: 1 as it blows, 0 still.
Barrel or pincushion distortion with lensDistortionCenter; off at 0.
Variant neutral (Khronos PBR Neutral), appended; existing indices unchanged.

Colour adjustments after the LUT: temperature, tint, brightness, contrast, balanceShadows, balanceMidtones, balanceHighlights, preserveLuminosity, hue, saturation, vibrance, grayscale, invert, threshold; each off at 0.
